reallife_guide_start: Real Life Overhaul {version} adds everyday life to the city of Big Ambitions: a camera behind your character, cars that drive like their kind, accidents, crime and police, jobs and careers, a home and a family, people to know, a city economy and government, and much more for your businesses. Each part can be switched off by itself on the options page. # Getting the mod and keeping it up to date - The mod's home is its page on the Steam Workshop. Subscribe there and Steam installs it and keeps it up to date. An update arrives through Steam: close the game while it downloads, and the new version runs the next time the game starts. - Without the Workshop, every version is also on the mod's GitHub page, under Releases, as a setup and a zip. Run each new version's setup yourself; it keeps your saves and your options. - Use one copy, not both. With the Workshop copy switched on in the game's Mods menu and a copy from GitHub in the game's ModsLocal folder as well, the game loads neither and lists both as failed. - Keep Big Ambitions on the current build of Steam's public branch: this version of the mod is made for Build {game_build}. On an older build some of its apps and features do not work, and the mod says so in the main menu. - The first time you load a save with mods, the game offers to keep a backup and plays a copy marked (Modded). That is the game's own step. # First steps - Out of doors the camera sits behind you and the mouse looks around. {key_free_cursor} gives you the mouse cursor back for clicking and takes it again; {key_camera_toggle} switches to the game's own camera. - Your phone has new apps and contacts. The mod's apps are in folders on the phone's home screen, after the game's own: click a folder to open it, and turn the page with the mouse wheel or the More apps button. Each contact can be called. - Things you do at a place, such as a shift, a class or a session, are started by clicking the desk, station or door at that place, in the game's own panel, as at a job of the game's. An app says where to go and can set the way there. # The options page - Open the game's Options and choose the Mods tab. The mod's page starts with a search box, then its ten groups. The first, 'Start here', has the button for this Guide, the presets, reset, export and import, and Report a bug. - Type two letters or more in the search box to find options by a word in their name or their feature's. # The Mod settings app - Your phone has an app called Mod settings, with the same options as the Mods tab. It looks like the game's help (F1), in dark colours, and also opens from 'Open the mod's settings on your phone' under 'Start here'. - The list on the left has the ten groups: click one to open it, then a section to show it on the right. The round arrows at the top go back and forward. - Each option has its name, a short line about it and its control at the right: a switch for on and off, a slider for a number, a list to choose from, or a button for something it does. Click a key's button, then press the new key. - A greyed row says what it needs first. A change is made at once and saved, as on the Mods tab. - 'Search' finds an option in any group by a word of it. 'Presets' under 'Start here' names the preset in use, or the one your choices are nearest, and lists the options that differ from it. The test tools are the last group while 'Show test tools' is on. # Presets - A preset sets how much happens to you. The mod starts on Standard. Relaxed leaves you nearly alone; Realistic and Hardcore bring more incidents and more police. The preset now is {preset}, and the page 'Presets' lists what each one sets. # This Guide - It is an app on your phone, called Guide. It also opens from the button 'Open the Guide on your phone' on the options page (when you close the menu), from the contact 'Real Life Overhaul Guide' (there while 'The mod's phone contacts' is on) and from the notice you are shown once for each new version. - The tab 'Pages' lists the pages, one per feature. Click one and the tab 'Reading' shows its text, a line to a row; scroll with the mouse wheel. 'All pages' on the left goes back to the list. - Every page of the mod's apps ends with a line 'Guide' that names the page here which explains it. - Prices, fines and keys on these pages are read from the mod when a page is opened, so they are the ones in force. - 'What's new' lists what changed in each version, and 'Troubleshooting' what to do when something goes wrong. # Groups and sections - The mod's options are in ten groups, from 'Start here' to 'Troubleshooting'. A group opens to its sections, and one is open at a time. - Each button says how many of its switches are on. - Rest the pointer on a row for a sentence about it. 'About this section' opens its page in this Guide. - A greyed row says what it needs: switch that on first. - The search box at the top finds a row by any word, and shows the group and section it is in. # The mod's keys, as you have them now - Change them on the options page under 'Controls'. The performance and development keys do nothing while 'Developer diagnostics' is off. {controls}
reallife_guide_presets: A preset sets a group of options in one go. The four buttons are on the options page under 'Start here', Presets, and in the Mod settings app, which also names the preset your choices are nearest. The preset in use now is {preset}; it reads 'Custom' as soon as one of the options below differs from all four. - Relaxed: little is done to you. No crime against you, no police stops, arrests or pursuits, and your record does not count. Your own crashes cost nothing and do not hurt, and traffic cannot knock you down. No illness, no prison, no driving licence needed, no fuel use or breakdowns, weather without effects, relationships that do not fade and no arguments at home. Your businesses get only the opportunities, the rivals are gentle and the money rules are at their gentlest. Incidents are rarer, rent from buildings you let is higher and jobs pay {preset_pay_relaxed} of their usual rate. (Hitting a person with your car still costs the fine for it.) - Standard: the values the mod ships with. - Realistic: everything on, with more incidents and police, more trouble for your businesses, harder rivals, stricter money rules, a busier Flare feed and more faults in the city. Job pay is unchanged. - Hardcore: everything on at the strict end: incidents frequent, police about most of the time, heavy car handling, ruthless rivals, the strictest money rules, less rent and a nicer place earning less. The longest prison term is {preset_prison_hardcore} days and jobs pay {preset_pay_hardcore} of their usual rate. - The fines are the same in all four. No preset switches on Permadeath: there is no permanent death unless you switch it on yourself. A preset touches only the options in the table below. Camera, visuals, clothes, keys, performance and Permadeath stay yours. You are asked first, with how many options it changes, and your settings are written to settings_before_preset.txt in {folder} (resetting and loading your choices write it too). To undo a preset, rename that file to settings.txt and press Load my choices from the file. Changes take effect at once; something already going on plays out under the old values. # What each preset sets
reallife_guide_camera_about: A camera behind your character on foot, and behind the car when you drive.
reallife_guide_camera: # On foot - The camera follows behind you. With Mouse look on, the mouse turns the camera and the cursor is hidden; a small dot marks the middle of the screen. You can look up as far as the tops of the buildings. - {key_camera_toggle} switches between this camera and the game's own, on foot and in the car. {key_free_cursor} frees the cursor and locks it again. - The mouse wheel still zooms. With Third-person camera indoors too on, the camera works inside as well and is pulled in front of walls. - Mouse look works on a bicycle, a motorbike or a scooter and with a hand truck too. - Mouse look switches itself off while a menu, the map, a shop window, a list or a dialogue is open, and while the game is not the active window. - {key_interact} (or {key_interact_alt} while the game shows no prompt of its own) near a door or your own car takes you in the way a click would: opening hours and entrance fees apply. The door must be within {enter_door} m, the car within {enter_car} m. During one of the mod's jobs the key opens no door: click the building instead. Enter buildings and vehicles with the interact key switches this off. # In the car - A chase camera sits behind the car. The mouse looks around, up to the skyline too, and once you are moving the view swings back behind the car shortly after you stop moving the mouse. - Hold {key_look_behind} to look behind. - In garages and car parks, and when you use the game's own look-back, the game's cameras take over. - If Empire Motors uses the same key for its car view, its view is kept off so that one press does one thing. # The game's own camera moments - Placing items, the interior designer, previews, the subway, the mini games and the game's other set views use the game's own cameras. This camera stands aside for them and comes back afterwards. # Map markers - The game's place markers are put at the correct edge of the screen when what they mark is behind the camera. # Other camera mods - While another mod drives the camera, this mod's camera, mouse look and chase camera stand aside. They come back shortly after the other mod lets the camera go. - A message names the mod once in a session, and the camera's rows on the options page name it for as long as it has the camera. The camera key shows the message again. # Known limits - The chase camera's mouse look is off while the game's own 'vehicle mouse input' setting is on.
reallife_guide_character_about: Your character drawn in the game's detailed version in the city, and clothes and shoes made for the mod.
reallife_guide_character: # What it does - In the city the game draws a simplified player. With Detailed player character in the city on, the mod hides it and draws the detailed character the game uses in character creation and the shop mirror instead, moving exactly as you do. If you wear something the detailed set does not have, your normal body is shown while you wear it. - Fuller hair and beards gives hair and beards a finish with depth, and sharpens their textures. Hair keeps its own colour under any light. With a lamp behind or beside your head, dark hair stays dark: the glow and the shine of hair follow its colour and stay below the brightness of lit skin. With it off you see the game's own hair, which glows orange against a lamp whatever its colour. - Finer skin up close gives your skin a fine grain and a calmer shine when the camera is close. - Softer light in character creation and shops gives character creation and the previews at the hairdresser, the clothing store and the plastic surgeon a fill light and a rim light. - The mod's clothes, shoes and fuller scalp puts a hair-coloured scalp under your hair, so it does not look thin from a distance, and lets you wear the mod's clothes: T-shirts, a bomber jacket, jeans, chinos, suit trousers, a pencil skirt, a summer dress and an evening dress in up to {clothes_colours} colours and prints, and court trainers, runners, cap-toe derbies, laced boots and penny loafers in several colours each. # How to wear the new clothes - In character creation the starter pieces are in the game's own Torso, Legs and Feet lists, after the game's pieces, tagged RLO. - In a save, the Real Life Overhaul rack in a clothing store opens the game's clothes screen with every piece and its price, {clothes_least} to {clothes_most}. Pick what you want and press the screen's Save to buy it. - What you own is in your wardrobe's Change clothes, colour by colour, after the game's own pieces. A change is kept when you press Save. - The options page has them too, under Your character and home, in Clothes (men) or Clothes (women): a garment, then its colour. The first entry of each list is Game's own, which shows whatever the game has you wearing. - With Clothes must be bought on (it is on in a new game), you can wear only the pieces you have bought. What you chose in character creation is yours. The rack itself needs Clothes rack in clothing stores on. - Your picks are kept with the save. They are drawn over the game's clothes; choosing another piece of that kind in one of the game's own screens takes the mod's piece off. # Checking your hair - The test tools of the options page have four entries for hair. One writes to Player.log what each layer of your hair is made of. One stands a strong lamp behind your head for a short while, and one hangs a copy of the nearest street lamp over it, so you can turn the camera round and look at your hair in the light. One switches the hair finish off and on, to compare it with the game's own hair. # Known limits - The clothes need the mod's files. If they are missing, the new looks are left out and the game's look stays. - If the detailed character cannot be matched to your character, the mod says so once in Player.log and shows the game's own character until the next load.
reallife_guide_citylife_about: People at work and going about their day on the pavements near you.
reallife_guide_citylife: # What you see - Workers: street sweepers, window cleaners, a road crew, a repair worker kneeling at a toolbox, people handing out leaflets, a fundraiser with a clipboard, a painter on a ladder, a gardener, a postman on his round, a courier with a sack truck. - Everyday people: friends talking, two friends on a bench, smokers, people on the phone or on a coffee break, somebody eating lunch from a carton or on a doorstep with a mug, tourists with a map or a camera, joggers, a newspaper reader, a traveller with a suitcase, a pushchair, a driver leaning on a parked car, a doorman, a chess table, tai chi in the morning, a queue outside a door at night, a few people watching one of the game's street performers, umbrellas in the rain. - A coffee cart ({city_coffee_from} to {city_coffee_to}) and a hot-dog cart ({city_hotdog_from} to {city_hotdog_to}) with customers who walk up, queue, are served and walk off. - {city_count} different activities in all, each with its own hours. At most {city_sites} of them are out at once with {city_people} people in all, set up 45 to 95 m from you and taken away only where you are not looking, or once you are far off. # What you can do - Buy a coffee at the coffee cart: on foot, stand at its counter and press {key_interact}. It costs {coffee_price} and gives a little energy. The first time at a cart a notification says how. Coming back to the same cart can be how you meet somebody (see Social life). - The street chess player of Leisure is one of these people, so street chess needs this feature on. - Otherwise they are there to be seen. With 'People you hit fall and can be hurt' on, drive into them and they fall like anyone else, with the same consequences. # When it is quiet - Nothing new comes out between 02:00 and 05:00, and only one activity at a time before 07:00 and after 22:00. Activities already out finish their time. - While an accident or a crime is going on, and in a thunderstorm, nothing new starts. - In the rain everybody is taken in except the people with umbrellas, and they go when it stops. - Going indoors or skipping time clears the street; nothing appears in the first moments after a load. - How much is going on, and which kinds of people (at work, or everyday), are options below. # Known limits - It needs the mod's animation and model files. An activity whose animation or model is missing does not start.
reallife_guide_crime_about: Crime that happens near you, crime against you, and the police stopping you for your own driving.
reallife_guide_crime: # Crime near you (option: 'Crime near you') - Now and then something happens close by: a foot chase, a snatch, a mugging, graffiti, a car break-in, a traffic stop, a shoplifter, a hold-up and more, {crime_count} kinds in all. The game's marker shows where. How often crime happens sets how often. - One thing at a time: no crime starts during an accident or while the police have business with you. - You can watch, walk away, or call 911 (the first choice names what is going on): an officer is sent, and if it ends in an arrest you get the 'Did the right thing' mood. - Somebody running for it can be stopped: stay within arm's reach of them. An officer comes, sometimes they try to break free once, and you are thanked, now and then with a reward of {crime_reward_least} to {crime_reward_most}. - In your own shop you can confront a thief with {key_interact}. - The first 911 calls about nothing in a day are let off with a warning. After that each one costs {fine_wasted_call}, and with the option Arrests for serious offences on, {law_wasted_calls} in one day put you in a holding cell. # Crime against you (option: 'Crimes against you') - Pickpocket: takes {pick_share} of your cash, from {pick_least} to {pick_most}. Catch them and you get it back. If you did not feel it, you find out later. - Mugging, on foot late at night: hand over {mug_share} ({mug_least} to {mug_most}), or refuse: half the time they run, half the time you lose {mug_refused_share} ({mug_least} to {mug_refused_most}) and are hurt. Walking away before they reach you, or getting into a car, also works. - Neither happens while you carry less than {crime_cash_least}. - Hold-up in your own shop: the robber empties the till, {holdup_share} of what the shop takes in a day ({holdup_least} to {holdup_most}). It comes out of your money, as the game keeps one purse for you and your businesses, and shows in the shop's books as theft. - Out of your sight: a break-in at one of your shops overnight (stock, and a repair bill of {breakin_least} to {breakin_most}; good security prevents most), your parked car broken into (repair up to {car_repair_most}), a scam call (hang up and it costs nothing; give the details and you may lose up to {scam_most}). - A pickpocket or mugger leaves you alone for a couple of days after the last one; break-ins, car break-ins and scam calls each rest for several days. # Being pulled over (option: 'Police stop you for traffic offences') - What counts: running a red light, speeding, driving on the pavement, driving against the traffic. Speeding means more than {speed_margin} km/h over the limit ({speed_limit} km/h where the road does not say) for {speed_seconds} seconds. - It only matters if somebody sees it. A patrol car happens to be near {seen_redlight} of the time for a red light, {seen_speeding} for speeding (twice that from {speed_gross} km/h) and {seen_reckless} for reckless driving. How often crime happens, the city's traffic enforcement policy, police patrols in your district and a long record all make that likelier. An officer on foot with a clear view sees much more, though less far in rain, mist and the dark. With the option Police off, nothing you do at the wheel is seen. - A patrol car then comes up behind you with its lights on. Stop within {stop_seconds} seconds and stay stopped: an officer walks up and writes the ticket. - Fines: red light {fine_redlight}, speeding {fine_speeding}, reckless or wrong side {fine_reckless}. Each kind is charged once per stop. After {leisure_tipsy_from} drinks or more, any stop adds {fine_drunk} for driving after drinking. - If you drive on, it is a pursuit. Lose them (out of their sight for {pursuit_unseen} seconds, or {pursuit_far} m ahead) and you pay no fine, but your car is known for the rest of the day: any other offence is seen for certain, speeding far more often, and the fines are half as much again. - If they catch you: the fines, plus {fine_fleeing} for fleeing and {fine_fleeing_step} for every quarter minute it lasted, at most {fine_fleeing_most}, and you are arrested and held at the nearest police station (see the Guide page Police stations, custody and your record). With Arrests end in a holding cell off, {custody_min} to {custody_max} hours pass and you are let go where you stood. - On foot, crossing on red or walking in the road in front of an officer earns a shout and, {jaywalk_chance} of the time, a fine of {fine_jaywalk}. With a long record there is no warning, only the fine. - Fines are charged in full, even if that takes you below zero. # Known limits - A pickpocket or a mugger cannot be reported to 911. - The crimes on this page never kill you unless you switch Permadeath on. Refusing a mugger can injure you, and with Permadeath on, after a first warning, it can end your life.
reallife_guide_driving_about: Each car you drive gets the acceleration and top speed of its kind, an eased throttle, a little more weight and roll, and a speedometer.
reallife_guide_driving: # What changes - In the game every car has the same engine and gearbox and is held back by a limiter. With Realistic car performance on, the car you drive (never traffic, and never another player's car in Going Public) is given a 0 to 100 km/h time and a top speed for its kind, and air drag instead of a limiter: it pulls hard at first, steadily to 100 km/h and builds slowly to its top speed. - Examples (0 to 100 km/h in seconds, top speed in km/h): {car_examples}. Bicycles and motorbikes have figures of their own (see Custom shop and two-wheelers); scooters and hand trucks are left alone. - Top speed (% of each car's own) and Acceleration (% of each car's own) scale those figures. - Smooth throttle: the throttle key eases the pedal down over {throttle_rise} s and lifts in {throttle_fall} s, so a tap pulls away gently. An analogue trigger keeps its own feel. - Hold {key_gentle_throttle} to keep the pedal at {gentle_throttle} at most. - With Car handling off, the brakes are the game's own, made for its slower cars, so a car needs a long way to stop from the new top speeds. With it on, see below. - The speedometer shows km/h or mph, following the game's units setting. Speedometer when driving switches it off. - Everything changed on a car is put back when you get out, change car or switch the option off. # Car handling - The car you drive (never traffic, the bus or another player's car) keeps the game's own grip, steering, springs and anti-roll bars, and carries a little more weight for its kind: up to {handling_mass_most} kg more on a truck, little or none on a small car. Every corner the game's car takes at a speed, it takes too. - After a kerb or a bump the body swings once and settles. - The body leans a little more in bends, the nose dips a little more as you brake and the tail sinks as you pull away. - Past the very limit the tyres give a little: a car thrown sideways slides on rather than gripping harder, and a tall van or truck slides before it would tip. - The brakes build over {handling_brake_rise} s as you hold the key and stop the car about as hard as the game's own, without locking: the game's ABS keeps the wheels turning, so you can still steer. - Light is almost exactly the game's own, Full (the default) adds a little weight, roll and give, Heavy more of each. Off (the game's own) is the game's own handling. - The custom shop's springs, tyres, brakes and weight work on top of it: sports springs are stiffer, grippier tyres slide later, a lighter car keeps its ride height, and stronger brakes stop the car shorter as far as its tyres hold. The shop shows the stopping distance the car really has. # Measure this car - Measure this car's speed and acceleration on the options page times a real run: press it, stand still, then hold full throttle on a straight, empty road for as long as the message says. A message gives 0 to 50 km/h, 0 to 100 km/h, the speed reached and the car's target. # After a hospital trip - Your car is brought to a kerb space near where you come out, or towed to a repair shop, for {tow_fee}. # Known limits - A car from another mod is placed by its own data (weight, cargo room, the game's top speed) into one of the kinds above. - A car the sums cannot be done for (no combustion engine or no automatic gearbox) is left as the game made it, with a line in Player.log. - Faster cars mean the police notice speed only when it is well over the limit for a while: see Crime and police stops. - A car with more than two axles, or wheels of another kind, keeps the game's own handling.
reallife_guide_jobs_about: Seven jobs you do yourself on the street, paid when the work is done.
reallife_guide_jobs: # How to get one - Call the Gig Line on your phone, or walk up to a help-wanted board beside the door of a few service buildings, on foot and with no job on. At a plain board the game's panel has Read the board; at an employer's office it has Speak to the office (see Careers), where the boss's Show me the gig board gives the same list. Each button shows its key. - You are told each job's pay, your level and how much of it is left today: I'll take it, or What else is there?. To stop, call the Gig Line again and choose I'm done for now: work done so far is paid. - The Gig Line contact is there only while 'The mod's phone contacts' is on, read when a save is loaded. The boards work without it. # When a gig is refused - Not indoors, during one of the game's own missions (the delivery van, food deliveries), on the casino boat or the subway, or while one of the game's panels or a time skip is open. - Not with energy below {job_min_energy}, while that job will not have you back, once its amount for the day is done, or on a day it has nothing on ("Nothing in that today"). - Ride-hail also wants a reference, a clean record and the taxi endorsement (see The rules). A driving job with no car near you and too little cash for the van is refused. - Flyers, cleaning, shelves, the cart and busking are done on foot, and the cart and the busker need room on the pavement. Cleaning and shelves need a client near you: somebody else's business that is open and stays open long enough for the walk and the work (for shelves, a shop with customers). With none, try another street, or in opening hours. # The jobs - A unit is one piece of the work: a flyer taken, an eighth of a floor cleaned, a box shelved, a customer served, a song, a parcel delivered, a fare. - Every job shows its figures in a copy of the game's job panel at the top right. What you can do is a button on the game's panel over the place of work; each shows its key and can be clicked. - Where a job has Let time pass, it hands the rest of the shift to the game's clock, as the game's own job does: its panel shows the time remaining, the game's skip button and Stop. The clock pays {skip_share} of the usual pay for each unit it does, with no tips and no bonus, and takes the game minutes each job says below. Stop at any time and carry on by hand. {job_table} - The list gives each job's usual figures at the start's prices; all pay follows the city's prices. - Flyers: you are dressed as a canvasser and have about seven minutes for the bundle, on a pitch round where you took the job. The panel stands over whoever is in reach with Offer a flyer. People take one more often at a higher level and on a busy street; a flyer on a busy street pays more, and the whole bundle handed out by hand adds a bonus. With nobody in reach the panel over you has Let time pass: {skip_minutes_flyers} game minutes a flyer. - Cleaner: you wear the cleaner's uniform. A client's floor is dirty with the game's own dirt, the same as in your own shop: Go in at the door, take the mop (it is put in your hands, or Take the mop) and click the dirty patches until the game's cleanliness reads 100%. You have about five and a half minutes, more for a client further off. You are paid by the share of the dirt you took off: the whole fee at 100%, the share done if you leave or time runs out, and half or more is a shift done. Let time pass cleans the rest: {skip_minutes_cleaner} game minutes for each eighth of the floor, and the room really is clean afterwards. - Shelf stocker: carry boxes from the kerb to a shop's shelves: Pick up at the pile, Go in at the door, Put on the shelf at the shelf. The whole delivery by hand adds a bonus. Let time pass at the pile: {skip_minutes_stocker} game minutes a box. - Drinks cart: see "Working the drinks cart" below. - Busker: walk on to your pitch; you are turned to face the street and kept there. The panel has the three songs (the harder ones call for quicker strums and pay more), then Strum each time a strum is called for. Leaving the pitch mid-song loses that song. More has Step away (after {busker_abandon} seconds away the set is packed up and what is in the case is kept) and Let time pass: {skip_minutes_busker} game minutes a song, paying {skip_share} of what a song usually brings in here and now, taking {busker_average} of the strums to be in time. Tips only, more where people are about, most at lunch and from 16:00 to 21:00, least at night. With the police and police presence on, an officer may move you on after a couple of songs. - Courier: the panel over each place has the button for it: Collect the parcels, Load the car, Take a parcel from the car, then Hand over the parcel or Leave the parcel at the door. Every door delivered with a quarter of the time still left brings a bonus, and some people tip. There is no Let time pass: the car would have to be moved. - Heavy loads: with a heavy goods licence (any licence while driving licences are off), the courier's page of the Gig Line also has Got anything heavier? and then I'll take the load: freight in a heavy truck, {lic_heavy_load_pay} more a drop and on the distance, with {job_heavy_time} more time. It takes your own heavy truck within 60 m, or one hired for {job_truck_fee} a day (less a van's fee already paid that day). - Ride-hail: pick up fares and drive them smoothly: the tip follows the passenger's comfort, which the job panel shows, and a very rough ride costs part of the fare. {taxi_misses} missed fares end the shift, and so does a passenger left sitting alone in the car too long. It ends when the day's fares run out. There is no Let time pass. With Ride fares: easier passengers on, passengers mind hard stops, bumps and speeding less. # No two shifts alike - What a gig pays and how big it is are drawn once, from the day, the hour and the gig. Ask again in the same hour and you get the same offer; the Gig Line says it. - The client is tight, fair or generous: {gig_client_low} to {gig_client_high} of the usual fee. A busy day pays {gig_busy_fee}, another day {gig_normal_fee}, so the average is the usual fee. On average {gig_busy_per_day} of the gigs are busy each day, and {gig_closed_per_day} a day have nothing on. - The size varies round the usual number of units, as the list above says. Pay is for the work done, so a bigger shift pays more. - Flyers, the cart and the busker can meet a quiet street ({gig_quiet} of the usual crowd) or a rush ({gig_rush}). - Small events are each said in a notification. A big tipper turns up in {gig_tipper_chance} of the shifts of the cart, busker, courier, ride-hail and shelf stocker, and tips {gig_tipper_low} to {gig_tipper_high} units of pay. On flyers, cleaning and shelves a client adds a speed bonus in {gig_speed_chance} of the shifts, {gig_speed_low} to {gig_speed_high} units of pay, if you finish by hand within {gig_speed_time} of the time. A difficult customer, in {gig_redo_chance} of the cart and cleaning shifts, sends a drink back or finds a patch you missed. - Bad weather pays more on every gig but cleaning when the weather option is on: {gig_rain_pay} more in rain, {gig_storm_pay} in a storm, {gig_spell_pay} in a heat wave or a cold snap and {gig_ice_pay} on ice. - The usual fee is the average of a shift played well in fair weather, with its tips and bonus. Employers' shifts, booked sets and the test buttons have none of this: an employer pays by your rank there (see Careers), and a booked set pays the venue's fee and tips {gig_set_tips} more. # The rules - Levels: {job_levels} per job. Each level above the first pays {job_level_bonus} more. The 'Job pay' option scales everything. - If you run businesses of your own (ones that take money), every job pays {job_owner_cut} less for each, down to {job_owner_floor} of the usual pay. The pay the Gig Line and the employers quote already includes this. - Ride-hail wants a reference (level {job_reference_level} in any job), no police stop on a job in the last {job_clean_days} days and, while driving licences are switched on, a taxi endorsement from a driving school. - A driving job needs a car of yours within 60 m, or the one you are driving. With none you are given a hired van for {job_van_fee} a day, charged once however many shifts; it is taken back when the shift is over and you are out of it. Parking tickets on it are waived. A van still out must be brought back before new driving work, and a wrecked van ends the shift without a strike. - On a driving job a crash costs {job_crash_cut} of that unit's pay and a police stop {job_stop_cut}; on the courier's round both are twice that. A pay slip never goes below zero. - Giving up with most of the work undone is a failed shift: flyers with under a third handed out (unless you offered at least ten), cleaning, shelves, the cart or parcels with under half done, ride-hail with a passenger aboard. Busking never fails. {job_strikes} failed shifts in a job and it lets you go for {job_sacked_days} days. A good shift takes a strike off, and a doctor's sick note turns a failed shift into no strike. - Work uses energy and trains a skill through the game's own systems: customer service on flyers, shelves, the cart and ride-hail, cleaning on the cleaner's floors, delivery driving on the courier's round; busking trains none. It never takes your energy below 12, and an exhausted player's shift ends. A good shift lifts your mood, a strike lowers it. - A shift ends by itself, paid, if you sleep, are taken to hospital or into custody, take one of the game's missions, or walk into a building that is not the client's. A client that closes calls it off without a strike and pays what was done. - A job in progress does not carry on after a load: loading a save made during a shift pays what you were owed at once and ends the shift, with nothing held against you. - Each week you worked ends with a notification of the shifts and the earnings. - Booked sets: from busker level {gig_set_level}, with Careers on, the Work contact's Something else asks Any booked sets going? on a day without a rota shift. One a day, at a venue near you marked on the map: walk up to its front to play, and the venue pays its fee if you play at least half. # Working the drinks cart - The cart is set up on the pavement beside you and is solid. Walk on to your place behind it (an arrow points at it): you are turned to face the customers, put in the vendor's uniform and kept there, and your own clothes come back when the shift ends. - The job's panel at the top right shows customers served, walk-offs out of three, takings and tips, and the time. - A panel over the cart shows each order and the customer's patience, with a button for each of the three drinks. The right drink within {vendor_quick} seconds earns a full tip; a wrong one costs the customer {vendor_wrong} seconds of patience; a customer kept {vendor_patience} seconds walks off, and one left {job_cart_wait} seconds in the queue gives up. Three walk-offs end the shift. Everyone served with no walk-offs adds a bonus. - Let time pass works as on the other jobs: the clock takes {vendor_minutes_each} game minutes a customer and pays {vendor_skip_share} of a customer's pay, with no tips and no bonus. Stop at any time and serve the rest by hand. - Call out calls to the people walking past within {vendor_hawk_within} m. Each one is tempted, annoyed or takes no notice, shown by the game's faces over their heads. For each tempted one a customer more comes to the cart, up to {vendor_hawk_extra} more than the shift's own number and never past the day's amount of a gig. It can be used again after {vendor_hawk_cooldown} seconds. - A passer-by is more easily tempted at lunch and from 16:00 to 21:00, on a busy pavement and with a higher customer service skill, and less easily at night, while customers already wait at the cart, and when you have just called out. Each call in the last {vendor_hawk_fade} seconds raises the share who are annoyed. With three such calls and the police and police presence switched on, an officer may warn you; the second warning ends calling out for the shift. - Step away lets you walk again. Customers go on waiting, and after {vendor_abandon} seconds away from the cart the shift is given up. Walk back on to your place to carry on. - When the shift ends the pay slip is one of the game's notifications: what the work paid, the tips, any bonus and, for an employer, the basic wage.
reallife_guide_job_row: {name}: {pay} a unit{metre}{size}, at most {daily} units a day, a level every {level} units
reallife_guide_job_need_car: ; needs a car (yours or a hired van)
reallife_guide_life_about: Small things that happen to you, a cold now and then, and people to call.
reallife_guide_life:
# Random events
- Every so often something happens (the frequency option is roughly the number of events per game week): a message on screen, a text from Alex or Mom, or a question with two answers. There are {life_count} of them, and none repeats in a save until all that fit your situation have been seen.
- They move small amounts of money, energy, hunger or mood, and a few give you a cold or a minor injury. A loss never puts you in debt, and questions are never asked while you drive.
- Nothing happens while you sleep, sit in a menu or a dialogue, or are otherwise busy.

# Being sick
- A cold lowers your mood and drains a little extra energy for a day or two.
- Call Dr. Patel while you are sick: a phone consultation costs {doctor_fee} and cures it. So does a hospital stay. With Home life and health on, the doctor's desk in a hospital or clinic also diagnoses and treats what your way of life brings on (see Home life and health).

# The phone
- Emergency Services (911): the first answer names what is going on near you (a traffic accident, a theft, a robbery, a dangerous driver, a crime in progress or a fire), or ask for an ambulance for yourself ({ambulance_fee}, plus the game's own hospital bill). If you were driving, your car is brought near the hospital afterwards for {tow_fee}.
- Alex and Mom can each be called once a day for a better mood. They also text you as part of events. With Social life on, they are two of the people in your life and their calls are as described on the Social life page.

# Moods
- The mod adds its own entries to the game's happiness list (Feeling sick, Injured, Lucky day, Got robbed and so on). They wear off after a few hours to three days.

# Known limits
- The contacts appear only while 'The mod's phone contacts' is on, and that option is read when a save is loaded.
reallife_guide_people_about: Officers on the beat, a patrol car at the kerb, and the crews at accident and crime scenes.
reallife_guide_people:
# What you see
- One or two officers walking a beat near you, a patrol car parked at the kerb with its crew beside it for a few minutes, an officer at a junction.
- At scenes: drivers who get out, paramedics with a stretcher, officers who put up tape, direct traffic and take statements. Officers and paramedics wear one uniform each with their equipment.

# What it needs
- Everything here needs 'Police' (Crime and police stops) and 'People at accidents and on the street' on.
- 'Police on the streets' sets how many officers are about: at 0 there are no patrol cars and no foot patrols. 'How often officers patrol' sets how often a new foot patrol starts, and foot patrols also need 'Officers on foot patrol near you'.
- In a Going Public session where the traffic is shared, the patrol options stand aside: the patrol cars are the traffic's.

# Why it matters
- An officer on foot near you is a witness: within about 30 m to your crossing on red or walking in the road, and within about 60 m, with a clear view, to what you do at the wheel (less in fog or rain). See Crime and police stops.
- A parked patrol car within {horn_officer} m sees a horn used in anger, and patrols notice reckless drivers.
- At an accident you did not cause you can walk up to help (within about 9 m, on foot), once, for the 'Did the right thing' mood.

# Limits the mod keeps to
- Officers, crews and the people at scenes are at most {pool_people} at once, and at most {pool_presence} of them are there only to be seen. An accident or crime scene takes those first, so a parked patrol car may stand empty for a while.
- They appear and leave where you are not looking, and they walk wherever they go.
reallife_guide_phone_about: Contacts you can call, and a modern look for the phone.
reallife_guide_phone: # Contacts - Emergency Services (911): report an accident, a crime or a fire near you, or call an ambulance for yourself ({ambulance_fee}). A call with nothing to report gets a warning at first, then a fine of {fine_wasted_call} if you keep calling that day. - Dr. Patel: a phone consultation when you are sick ({doctor_fee}). - Alex and Mom: a chat once a day each, for your mood. - Gig Line: the jobs (it needs Jobs from the Gig Line on as well). - Real Life Overhaul Guide: opens this guide. - Most other features add a contact of their own, described on that feature's page. - The contacts and their messages are kept in your save by the game, like its own contacts. - Every contact the mod adds has a picture from the game itself: a person's face from the game's portrait camera, and an organisation's logo from the game's own logo shapes. - The Contacts app has a button for each group of the mod's contacts, beside the game's own categories: Family, Friends and people, Work and careers, Services and trades, Money and banks, City and government, and Other. Each button shows the unread messages of its group, and pointing at it says how many contacts it holds. Press a button to see only that group, and press it again to see all. The game's own contacts stay in the game's own categories. 'Groups in the Contacts app' turns this off. - The Search contacts box at the top of Contacts shows only the contacts whose name or description has every word you type, from every group. # The phone's look - With Modern phone look on, the phone has a modern body, a wallpaper, a clock and a status bar. A photo from the Gallery can be the wallpaper. Phone cases bought in the game keep working. Switching it off puts the game's phone back at once. # Notifications - With The mod's notifications carry their own picture and colour on, each notification from the mod shows a picture of its kind on an indigo disc, where it pops up and in the game's notification list: the road, the police, health, money, property, work, your businesses, the tech sector, news, family and friends, and anything else. The game's own notifications look as they always did. The mod's notifications already in a save get their picture too. - When you wake from a sleep, the morning summary says how long you slept and how you feel. With The night's news in the morning summary on, the city's news that came while you slept (the weather, city policies, works next door, what is on, your papers) comes in it, in one notification or two, not as a pile in the minute you wake. - Some notifications have a switch of their own. Switched off, what they tell of still happens and is still in its app: the city's requests, protests, contract offers (for your own work and your tech firms' clients), a better credit rating (a worse one is always told), accidents, Flare, the morning's papers, dividends, the rate decision ahead, online orders waiting with nobody on shift, and the recruitment office. # Known limits - The mod's phone contacts is read when a save is loaded: switching it on or off takes effect on the next load. It covers every contact the mod adds. Switching it off does not delete contacts already in a save; Prepare this save for removing the mod does.
reallife_guide_ragdoll_about: People hit by a car fall as bodies with weight, and may be hurt or killed.
reallife_guide_ragdoll: # When you hit someone - Below {hit_knock} km/h they are knocked over, get up after a few seconds and walk off angry. From {hit_knock} to {hit_injury} km/h they stay down, hurt. Above that they may die, the more likely the faster you were going, and from {hit_deadly} km/h most do. - On a bicycle or a motorbike you only knock people over. - Someone who stays down becomes an accident scene: an ambulance and a patrol car come, and the casualty is taken away. - You have the same choice as after hitting a car: stop within {crash_stop_seconds} seconds and stay near, or drive off. With Police chase you after a hit-and-run off it is always settled as if you had stopped. - Stopped: {fine_injury} for an injury, {fine_death} for a death; with Arrests for serious offences on, a death also means arrest on the spot. Fled and caught: {fine_injury_run} and {fine_death_run}. Got away: {fine_injury_escaped} and {fine_death_escaped}, billed some hours later. When a summons follows, the case takes this bill: a dismissed case owes nothing, and a conviction's sentence covers it, the damages included. A death weighs on your mood for days. - At the roadside the police take at most {fine_cash_share} of your cash, or {roadside_least} if that is more. The rest of the fine goes to court with the case, or is not collected. A fine billed later is charged in full. # When traffic hits you (option: Traffic can knock you down on foot) - On foot in the road you can be knocked down: shaken at low speed, injured from {knock_injury} km/h, and taken to hospital from {knock_hospital} km/h. You lie for a few seconds and get up where you landed. You are never killed unless you switch Permadeath on (see its page), and cannot be hit again for a few seconds. # Pedestrians hit by traffic (option: Traffic can hit pedestrians near you) - Now and then a traffic car hits a pedestrian near you, and an ambulance and the police come; a driver who stopped is questioned and given a ticket, and one who drives off is chased and arrested if caught. How often follows How often accidents happen (1 to 10). # Limits the mod keeps to - At most {ragdoll_max} people are falling with full physics at once; up to {ragdoll_still} more lie still. When more go down, the one who has lain longest makes room.
reallife_guide_traffic_about: Accidents among the game's own traffic, the emergency response to them, and what your own crashes cost.
reallife_guide_traffic: # Accidents near you - Now and then there is an accident near you: one car or two, three in a severe one; minor, moderate or severe (a severe one may roll a car). An orange marker shows where and how far. - Notifications about accidents and A waypoint to each accident can each be switched off: the accidents still happen, without the messages and their sound, or without the marker and its route. - With Reckless drivers cause the accidents on, it happens where a driver went wrong, often in view (see Horn and reckless drivers). With it off, it is set up a little way off, out of your way. - With Police on a patrol car always comes. An ambulance comes for moderate and severe ones, and for those the road is closed with tape, barriers and cones. Crews work, the casualty leaves on a stretcher, and the scene clears within a few minutes. - An officer on traffic duty stands by the tape and waves cars on through the lane left open. An ambulance, a fire engine or a patrol car with its lights on coming up that lane, or an ambulance leaving round the wrecks, is waved through: the officer steps out of its way until it is past. - A driver who stays and calls for help is not arrested. Once the officers have had a look, one of them questions the driver who caused it and writes them a ticket. A driver lying hurt goes with the ambulance instead. - Some drivers run for it and are chased. One who is caught is arrested at the roadside and taken away in the patrol car. - You can walk up to help, or call 911 and report it, which sends the units at once. Both earn the Did the right thing mood. - A road the mod closed is opened again whichever way the scene ends. - With A tow truck takes the wrecks away on, a car too damaged to drive is not simply gone when the scene clears. A tow truck comes for it (the message that the road is open says how long it will be), stands ahead of it, lowers its bed and winches it up, and drives off with it. It needs a lane beside the wreck's running the same way and a straight stretch ahead; where there is none, or the wreck is out of reach, it goes as before. One truck works at a time, so the wrecks of a severe crash wait their turn. # Your own crashes (option: Your crashes cost money and can injure you) - Hitting a traffic car at {crash_from} km/h or more costs damages from {crash_least} to {crash_most} by the speed of the impact. Harder hits injure you; the hardest end in hospital. A reckless driver who runs into you is at fault, and you pay nothing. - With Police chase you after a hit-and-run on you have {crash_stop_seconds} seconds to stop near the crash. Stop, and you pay the damages only. - Drive off and a patrol car comes after you, at up to {pursuit_least} to {pursuit_most} km/h depending on your car ({pursuit_stock} km/h while Realistic car performance is off), with a second one after {pursuit_backup} seconds. Caught: damages plus {fine_caught}, and you are arrested: with Arrests end in a holding cell on, {law_hitrun_least} to {law_hitrun_most} hours in a holding cell. Got away: damages plus {fine_escaped}, billed some hours later (the bill is kept in your save). - If a person was hurt, the larger fines under Ragdolls and people hit by cars apply instead. # How often - At the default setting of How often accidents happen (1 to 10) there is about one accident near you for every {accident_hours} game hours you spend in the street, taken over the whole day in fair weather. At your setting it is one in {accident_hours_now}: at the lowest setting one in {accident_hours_least}, at the highest one in {accident_hours_most}. - The road is quietest in the small hours and busiest in the late afternoon. Mist, rain, storms, ice and snow bring more accidents. At night more of the drivers you see are reckless, and some of them are drunk. - Traffic hits a pedestrian about {ped_share} as often as cars collide, and no accident has a second one close behind it. # When the traffic stops - If the game's traffic stops adding cars and the streets empty, the mod notices within seconds and puts the traffic right by itself. # Options - How often accidents happen (1 to 10) also sets how often traffic hits a pedestrian. - Sirens on emergency vehicles and People at accidents and on the street are read when a unit or a scene starts; one already out keeps what it had. # Known limits - One incident of any kind at a time. A scene that is running when you switch its option off plays to its end. - As a guest in a Going Public session the accidents, tow trucks, police and chases stand aside: the traffic is the host's.
reallife_guide_visuals_about: Colour grading and detail distance for the whole picture.
reallife_guide_visuals: # What it does - Colour saturation and Contrast are added on top of the game's picture and cost nothing. At 0 each is the game's own; both start a little above it. - Bloom at 0 leaves the game's own bloom alone; raising it costs frames. - Detail distance above 100% keeps detailed models for longer and costs frames. - Switching Picture adjustments off puts the game's picture back at once, and the game's own detail distance. - The rows for your character under the same heading (the detailed character, fuller hair, finer skin and softer light) are described on the Character and wardrobe page.
reallife_guide_keys_about: Every key the mod listens to, and how to change it.
reallife_guide_keys: # The mod's keys, as you have them now {controls} # Changing a key - Options page, Controls, Keys: click a line, then press the new key. Hold Shift, Ctrl or Alt with it for a combination, or press one of those keys alone and let go to use it by itself. Esc keeps the old key, and so does waiting a few seconds without pressing one. The left mouse button and gamepad buttons are not offered. - The Mod settings app on your phone has the same lines: click a key's button, then press the new key. - A key the game itself uses is allowed; the line then says which of the game's actions shares it. With Empire Motors on, the line also says when that mod acts on the same key. - Reset the mod's keys puts all of them back. Reset every option and key under 'Start here' does too, and so does the game's own reset of its options. # Keys for developer diagnostics - The three keys for the performance measurements and the character report are under Troubleshooting, in 'Measuring performance'. They only work while 'Developer diagnostics' is switched on, on the options page. While it is off those keys do nothing. # Fixed keys - Photo mode has keys of its own while it is open. A notification names them, and so does the page 'Leisure, clothes and photo mode'. - In jobs, classes and the mod's other activities, the choices are buttons on the panel: click them. - While one of the mod's messages on the options page is open, or while you type in the options page's search box, none of the mod's keys does anything. # The game's own keys - The mod changes none of them. Its interact key ({key_interact}) is the game's own interact key unless you change one of them; the second one ({key_interact_alt}) only acts while the game shows no prompt of its own.
reallife_guide_performance_about: Small changes to how the base game draws the city, shadow and detail settings, and the tools to measure them on your computer.
reallife_guide_performance: # The switches (options page, Performance, 'Faster frames') - On by default, with nothing to see: the refraction effect is off outdoors, where nothing uses it; the sky's reflection and its light on things are refreshed every 2 seconds instead of every frame; street lamps that are off no longer keep their lights switched on; the mod's own bus stops, station fronts, signs, boards and kiosks are not drawn beyond 200 m, as the game does for its street furniture. - Off by default: scenery more than 1.3 km away is not drawn; people, cars and small things are drawn only within 300 m in every direction; street furniture and parked cars are not drawn beyond 200 m. The last one can be seen: they appear at 200 m instead of 300 m. Textures can be kept whole in the graphics card's memory, which spares the processor some work: it takes effect only on a card where all of them take less than half its memory. - Each switch puts back exactly what it changed when it is turned off. One that meets something unexpected says so once in Player.log and stays off until the city is loaded again. - No gain is promised: what a switch saves depends on your computer. The tools below measure it. # Shadows and detail (options page, Performance) - 'Sun shadow distance' is how far the sun's shadows reach, as a share of the game's distance. Shorter is faster: fewer things cast shadows, and shadows end nearer you. - 'Sun shadow cascades' is how many pieces the sun's shadows are drawn in: fewer is faster with softer shadows near you. It is as the game has it until you choose. - 'Detailed models distance' is how far away things keep their detailed models, as a share of the game's. Lower is faster, with simpler models nearer you; 100% is the game's own. - Bloom and detail distance, under 'Picture', cost frames above the game's own and say so in their labels. # Stutters - A long frame on walking into or out of a building is the game's own, behind its black screen, and so is the moment it takes to save and the pause right after midnight while it frees memory. The mod does its own larger work behind that black screen, and prepares its code for midnight a little after a save loads, so the first midnight of a session no longer stutters. 'Troubleshooting' says how to record a stutter for a report. # Measuring on your computer - Two buttons under Troubleshooting, in 'Measuring performance'. 'Measure performance for 10 seconds' writes RealLifeOverhaul_perf_(time).txt: where the time of a frame goes and what is in the city around you, with a screenshot in the folder RealLifeOverhaul_shots. - 'Run the performance test (about 3 minutes)' switches each item off and on in turn, several times, and writes the table RealLifeOverhaul_bench_(time).txt. It needs you on foot in the street; stand still and leave the mouse alone. Parts of the picture and of the interface go and come back while it runs. - After pressing a button, close the menu: the measurement starts two seconds later. - The keys {key_perf_probe} and {key_perf_bench} start the same two measurements, but only while 'Developer diagnostics' is switched on. While it is off they do nothing. - The files are in {data}, next to Player.log. # What the mod itself costs - Apart from the camera, the mod's features work on timers, not every frame, and wait while nothing is going on. Options that cost frames (bloom, detail distance) are off or neutral by default and say so in their label.
reallife_guide_savetools_about: What the mod leaves in a save, and how to take it out again.
reallife_guide_savetools:
# What the mod puts into a save
- Its own data: what it remembers about this save (life events seen, illness, fines owed, job and career progress, your licence and record, the people you know, the city government and so on) and the mod version.
- Its moods in the happiness list. The game cannot load a mood it does not know, so the mod takes its moods out every time the game saves and puts them back a moment later.
- Its phone contacts with their messages, and its lines in the notification list.
- Bank entries for fines, fees and job pay.
- Businesses of its own kinds: tech firms, academies, bank branches, ice cream parlours, tea bars and tobacconists.
- During a job with a hired van: that van, which is one of the game's own job vans.
- A report for companion tools such as Big Copilot: selected settings, businesses, ordinary hourly pay and credit accounts. It does not change play, send anything over the internet or make forecasts, and it is left out during a Going Public session.

# Removing the mod
1. Press "Prepare this save for removing the mod" in each save you want to keep.
2. Quit to the main menu and unsubscribe from the mod, or switch it off under Mods.
3. Restart the game.

# What "Prepare this save for removing the mod" does
- It makes two backup copies of the save's files first, and stops if either fails: one in a folder RealLifeOverhaul_backup_(date and time) inside the save's own folder, one under backups in {folder}. The game deletes a save's folder whole when you delete the character or its last save; the second copy is out of its reach.
- It then ends everything the mod has going and stops the mod's features until a save is loaded again. It makes each business of the mod's own kinds the game's nearest kind (a tech firm a web development agency, an academy a recruitment office, a bank branch a gift shop, an ice cream parlour a fast food restaurant, a tea bar a coffee shop, a tobacconist a liquor store), takes the ready-made designs out of the game's design folder, removes the moods, contacts, notification lines and data listed above, saves under the same name and lists what it did. The list is also written to {folder}.
- If a business of yours is in a shop the mod made an office, the question names it: without the mod that building is a shop again. Start the business again in one of the game's own offices, or close it, first.
- Bank entries stay, because the money really moved; without the mod they are listed by a code, not a name. A hired job van still in the save also stays: the game removes a job van with no job by itself once the save is loaded again.
- The game must have been saved once under a name, and saving must be allowed where you are. You must be on foot, and not in the middle of a hospital trip, police custody, sleep, an activity, a subway ride or a trip on the casino boat.
- Every save you make before you load again is kept clean as well.
- It works on the save that is loaded, one at a time. There is no button for all saves at once.

# Reset the mod's data in this save
- Ends what is going on, takes the mod's moods off and removes its stored data, and keeps the mod running: as if the mod had just been added to this save. Contacts and their messages stay. A backup copy is made first, unless the game has never been saved; the save file itself is not changed until you save, so loading without saving goes back.

# Put back missing contacts and moods
- Puts back the mod's phone contacts that have gone missing and makes sure the game knows the mod's moods. It then lists each contact: on the phone, put back, or not there because its feature or 'The mod's phone contacts' is switched off.

# After every load
- The mod checks the save for things another version of it left behind, and brings data from an older version up to date. Moods this version does not have are removed, with a line in Player.log for each; anything else it does not recognise is kept.

# The mod's own files
- Settings files, save-tool reports and the second backup copies: {folder}. Performance reports and diagnostic files: {data}. None of them is needed to play.
- Options and key choices are kept by the game with its own settings, not in a save.
reallife_guide_diagnostics_about: Detailed lines in Player.log, the diagnostic keys, and the test buttons.
reallife_guide_diagnostics: # Developer diagnostics - Off unless you switch it on (options page, Troubleshooting, Diagnostics). While it is off the mod writes only warnings, errors and the few lines a report needs to Player.log, and the three diagnostic keys do nothing. - Switch it on to report a problem: the mod's features then also write what they are doing to Player.log, a line per step and never a line per frame, with a line a minute on how the game runs, one for each frame that takes far too long and one for each click. - While it is on, {key_perf_probe} and {key_perf_bench} start the two measurements of 'Measuring performance' (see 'Performance'), and {key_character_report} writes a report of the characters on screen. The files are in {data}. None of this changes anything in the game. # Test tools - 'Show test tools' is off unless you switch it on. It puts 'Test tools' under Troubleshooting on the options page and at the end of the Mod settings app, with every feature's test buttons: an accident, a crime, a job, a life event and so on, started where you stand. A test that cannot start says why. It also shows the 'Car handling tuning' sliders. - Some tests have real effects (a fine if you stop for the test patrol car, stock lost in the test break-in). # The other buttons - Check the mod's set-up looks through the options, the presets and the pages of this Guide for anything that does not fit together, and lists it. It changes nothing. - What a game update switched off lists any part of the mod that is off after a game update or repeated errors, with the game's build and the one this version is made for (see 'Troubleshooting'). - What changed in this version opens this Guide on 'What's new'.
reallife_guide_trouble: # The mod's apps do nothing, or the mod says the game needs updating - Real Life Overhaul {version} is made for Build {game_build} of Big Ambitions, the current build on Steam's public branch. On an older build some of its apps and features do not work, and the mod says so in the main menu and when a save is loaded. Player.log names your build near its top, in the line that begins 'Loaded Big Ambitions'. - To update the game in Steam: in the Library, right-click Big Ambitions and choose Properties. Under Betas, set Beta Participation to None. Then, under Installed Files, choose Verify integrity of game files. # The mod is missing, or the game says it failed to load - Use one copy. The Workshop copy, switched on in the game's Mods menu, and a copy from GitHub in the ModsLocal folder together make the game load neither: its Mods menu names both as failed, for a duplicate assembly name. Switch the Workshop copy off or unsubscribe, or delete the RealLifeOverhaul folder from ModsLocal, and start the game again. - A copy from GitHub loads only from ModsLocal\RealLifeOverhaul with RealLifeOverhaul.dll directly inside, not one folder deeper. The setup puts it there for you. - A Workshop update arrives when Steam has downloaded it and the game starts again. The mod's version is at the top of this Guide's 'What's new'. # My tech firm's staff do nothing - See 'Tech sector', which sets a firm up step by step. Staff work only in hours on a shift, at a workstation, while the firm is open and has its internet. The firm's page in the Tech app says who worked yesterday and, if nobody did, why. # No employer offers me a job - See 'Professional jobs'. A new player has no skills or qualifications yet. The first page of the Career app, Professions, names your first step, most often a short course in the Campus app. # The Stocks app will not let me buy more of a company - You may hold at most {mkt_holding} of a listed company's shares, counting your open orders for it. Change it with 'The most of a company you may hold' on the options page, under Money, 'Large investors': 10%, 25%, 50% or no limit. Your own listed company stays at 10%. # The camera jumps or fights itself - Another camera mod may be on as well. While it drives the camera, this mod's camera, mouse look and chase camera stand aside by themselves, and a message names the other mod. If the picture still shakes, switch one of the two off under Mods, and send Player.log: it has a line that starts with 'Camera:' for each time the camera was given up or taken back. # The mouse cursor is gone - Mouse look hides it. Press {key_free_cursor} to get it back (and again to return to mouse look), or {key_camera_toggle} for the game's own camera. # A key does nothing, or does two things - Look at 'Controls' in this Guide for the keys as you have them, and at 'Controls' on the options page: a line says when the game uses the same key. - {key_perf_probe}, {key_perf_bench} and {key_character_report} are diagnostic keys. They do nothing unless 'Developer diagnostics' is on. # Something of the mod's is stuck on the street - Switch its feature off and on again, or, with 'Show test tools' on, use the feature's clear or stop test button if it has one. 'Reset the mod's data in this save' ends everything at once. Loading the save also clears it: nothing the mod puts on the street is saved. # Frame rate - See 'Performance'. If in doubt, set bloom to 0 and detail distance to 100% under Performance, 'Picture', lower the sun shadow distance under 'Shadows and detail', and switch off 'Detailed player character in the city' under 'Looks and hair'. # Where the files are - The game's log is Player.log in {data}. The game moves the one before to Player-prev.log when it starts. The mod's lines begin [Mod:Real Life Overhaul] (or [Mod:RealLifeOverhaul] for a copy from GitHub in the ModsLocal folder). - Performance reports, diagnostic files and the folder RealLifeOverhaul_shots with their screenshots are in the same place. - Settings files, save-tool reports and bug reports are in {folder}. - Backups of a save are inside that save's own folder under SaveGames, and again under backups in {folder}. # Reporting a problem - Switch on 'Developer diagnostics' (options page, Diagnostics) and make the problem happen again, so that Player.log has the detail. - Say what you were doing and what you expected, and attach Player.log from that session (it is overwritten when the game starts again). - For a frame-rate problem, press {key_perf_probe} while it is happening and attach the report it writes. - Export your settings (options page) and attach settings.txt. - Mention the mod version, {version}, your game's build, and which other mods are on. # Going back - 'Reset every option and key' puts the mod as it came. To remove the mod, see 'Save tools'.
reallife_guide_credits:
# The mod
- Real Life Overhaul {version}.
- Big Ambitions is made by Hovgaard Games. This mod is not made or endorsed by them.

# What is in the mod's files
- The mod's own code and texts.
- Clothes and shoes, hair textures, the props in the streets and buildings, and the animations of the city's people, all made for this mod by its own scripts and in Blender.
- No model, texture, animation or sound of Big Ambitions is in the files, and no third-party model, motion capture or animation library.
- The clothes were shaped around measurements of the game's character. The animations were made to the joint positions and bone names of the game's street character, so that they fit its people. These are measurements: nothing of the game's was copied.
- The lettering on signs and tape is drawn with the font Aileron Regular by Sora Sagano (CC0 1.0).
- 'THE DAILY POST' and 'QUICK BITE' on models are names made up for the mod.
- Recorded car sounds, real recordings from Freesound.org: the sports engine from "Audi R8 Idling Reving Backfire" by Jonas_Jocys and the V8 from "Chev350 Raw" by lonemonk, both CC BY 4.0; the rest public domain (CC0 1.0). Sounds/SOURCES.md in the mod's folder lists every file. The mod's code makes the sirens and the city sounds itself.

# Tools used (none of them is in the mod's files)
- Blender, Unity 2022.3, UnityPy, Pillow, NumPy and the .NET SDK.

# Licence
- The mod is open source under the MIT licence. Ask the author before you reuse its code, texts, models or animations.

reallife_lic_grandfather_both: Driving now needs a licence. You own vehicles, so you have a car and a commercial licence, valid {days} days. The Licensing Office is in your contacts.
