reallife_law_desk_hint: Click what you want. {key}: leave the desk.
reallife_law_desk_greeting: Desk sergeant: "{precinct}. What can I do for you?"
reallife_law_desk_greeting_friend: Desk sergeant: "Good to see you again. {precinct}, at your service. What do you need?"
reallife_law_desk_greeting_known: The desk sergeant looks you up and down. "You again. {precinct}. Make it quick."
reallife_law_desk_greeting_wanted: The desk sergeant puts the pen down. "We have been looking for you. You can hand yourself in right here, and it will go a lot easier on you: half the time."
reallife_law_desk_report: Report a crime or an accident
reallife_law_desk_report_taken: "Got it. A unit is on its way, and I have your statement. Thank you for coming in: it will be remembered."
reallife_law_desk_report_known: "We know about that one already; officers are dealing with it. Thank you all the same."
reallife_law_desk_report_nothing: "Nothing has come in from around here, and there is nothing I can send a car to. If you see something, come back or call 911."
reallife_law_desk_fines_paid: "{amount}, paid in full. Here is your receipt; that is the end of it."
reallife_law_desk_fines_short: "You do not have enough on you to settle that. It will be taken when it falls due."
reallife_law_desk_impound: Collect your car from the pound: {amount}
reallife_law_desk_impound_none: Collect a car from the pound (none of yours is held)
reallife_law_desk_impound_short: "The impound fee is {amount}. Come back when you have it; the car is not going anywhere."
reallife_law_desk_impound_outside: "I will have it brought round. It will be at the kerb when you step outside; the fee is taken then."
reallife_law_desk_impound_done: "It is on its way round from the pound now."
reallife_law_desk_impound_here: Your car is already parked near the police station: nothing to pay.
reallife_law_desk_impound_gone: The pound no longer has your car: it is not in the city any more.
reallife_law_desk_licence: Apply for a licence or permit
reallife_law_desk_paper: Ask for a police report on {what}: {amount}
reallife_law_desk_paper_none: Ask for a police report (nothing has happened to you lately)
reallife_law_desk_paper_done: "Here is your report, reference {reference}. Your insurer will ask for that number."
reallife_law_desk_turnin_refused: The sergeant cannot take you in just now. Try again in a moment.
reallife_law_turnin_notice: You handed yourself in. Charge: {charges}. For coming in yourself: {hours} hours in a holding cell at the {precinct}.
reallife_law_desk_hours_line: "The front desk is open day and night. Nobody in the holding cells gets visitors: they are with us two days at the most, and a lawyer or bail gets them out sooner. Fines, reports and the pound are all dealt with here."
reallife_law_released_desk: Signed out at the {precinct} front desk. Hours held: {hours}. Fines and damages paid: {amount}. On your record.
reallife_law_released_desk_bail: Bail of {bail} posted. Signed out at the {precinct} front desk. Hours held: {hours}. On your record.
reallife_law_impound_held: Your car is at the police pound. Any police station's front desk brings it round: {amount}.
reallife_justice_sentence_jail_served: Hours already spent in a cell that count as served: {hours}.
reallife_crime_pullover_drunk: Police lights behind you: your car has been wandering across the road. Pull over and stop.
reallife_wiring_cv_charged: Criminal record: a case is before the court.
reallife_wiring_travel_warrant: I can't book that. There is a warrant out in your name: you would be stopped at the first check. Sort it out at the courthouse first.
reallife_wiring_travel_court: I can't book that. You have a court matter that falls inside those dates, and nobody leaves town over one.
reallife_news_story_fire: FIRE CREWS CALLED OUT. The fire service was called to a blaze in the city. The street was closed while crews brought it under control.
reallife_news_story_acquitted: COURT: ACQUITTED. A defendant walked free from the city court yesterday after the case against them failed.
reallife_news_story_convicted: COURT: GUILTY. The city court handed down a conviction and sentence yesterday.
reallife_news_story_prison: COURT: PRISON. A defendant was sent to prison by the city court yesterday.
reallife_guide_home_about: Hygiene, stress and a tidy flat; cooking, sleep, fitness, illness and the doctor.
reallife_guide_home: # What it adds - Three light needs beside the game's own: hygiene, stress and how tidy your home is. Three more bars hang under the game's energy, hunger and happiness bars at home, or when one runs low. A need left low costs you mood and, in time, your health. - At home, click a cooker (the game says "Click to cook" when you point at one), or click a fridge and choose Cook a meal in its panel. A list opens with the dishes you can make right now from what is in this home's fridges: for each one the portions, the time, how much a portion fills and exactly which items it uses. Dishes that are one ingredient short are listed with their button switched off and what is missing. The first entry changes the size (normal, double, family size), which makes more portions where the fridges hold enough. - Choose a dish and you walk to the cooker and cook it. The food leaves the fridge when the cooking starts, so stopping early wastes it. You eat one portion and the rest are put by as leftovers, which the same list reheats later. Cooked food fills more than its ingredients eaten as they are, and a meal can burn, more often when you are stressed or exhausted. - A home without a cooker can still make what needs no cooking: a salad, a fruit bowl, cheese and fruit. Clicking a fridge works as it always did, and anything in it can be eaten as it is. - Click a coffee machine at home to make a coffee. - Exercise and what you eat move your fitness over days, and slowly your build. The Wellbeing contact on the phone says how you are doing, and starts tidying, floor exercises and a run of six checkpoints out of doors. # Sleep, and why you wake groggy - Every night of three hours or more gets a score when you wake, and the morning summary says how long you slept, from lying down to getting up, and how you feel: well rested lifts your mood for the day (Well rested), groggy lowers it for a few hours (Groggy), and in between is fair. A shorter sleep is a nap: it pays off some of what you owe and nothing more. - How long: seven hours or more helps; under six costs, and under five costs a lot. - The bed: the game's quality of the bed you lie in counts, a good bed for, a cheap one against. A night in a car is far worse, and can leave you with a bad back ({sleep_back_car} of the time). A hotel room counts as its own bed. - When: going to bed between {sleep_late_from} and {sleep_late_to} is far too late, and sleeping in the daytime, from 08:00 to 18:00, is broken by the day's noise. - What spoils it: a messy home (tidiness under {sleep_mess}), stress over {sleep_stress}, going to bed hungry, and being ill. Each costs on its own, so two or three of them make a groggy morning even after a long night. - You need about {sleep_need} hours a day. Every hour awake adds to the sleep you owe, up to {sleep_debt_most} hours, and a good night pays off more of it than a poor one. Over {sleep_short} hours owed you are Short of sleep: a lower mood, stress that keeps rising, and colds and flu come more easily. A roommate's noise or a baby waking you in the night adds to what you owe. - To wake well rested: a good bed in a tidy home, to bed before {sleep_late_from}, seven hours or more, fed, calm and well. A check-up at the doctor's desk says how much sleep you owe. # Being ill - A cold, flu, food poisoning, a bad back or burnout can follow from how you live (out in the rain, no sleep, junk food, work without a break). The Wellbeing contact says what you have and what helps. A good night of six hours or more shortens an illness. - At the doctor's desk in a hospital or clinic (just inside the door where there is no desk) a panel offers a consultation for {doctor_consult}, on the key it shows: a diagnosis, a prescription ({doctor_prescription}) that halves what is left, and a sick note ({doctor_note} more) that covers a missed job shift for two days. # Options - "Easy needs" halves what wears a need down, the sleep you owe and every chance of illness. Each part (needs, the bars, routines, sleep, illness, fitness, the changing body, the run, the morning summary and the night's news in it) has its own switch, listed below. With sleep switched off, nights are not scored and no sleep is owed.
reallife_meta_title_law: Police stations, custody and your record
reallife_guide_law_about: A police station in every district, a holding cell if you are arrested, and a record that follows you.
reallife_guide_law: # Police stations (option: 'Police stations in every district') - One building in each district is a police station with a name of its own: a sign, patrol cars at the kerb, officers at the door. With Police stations on the city map on it has a blue marker and its own row, Police stations, in the city map's list. The Police Records Desk contact on your phone points you to the nearest. - At the door the game's panel offers Go into the station on {key_interact}. With Police stations you can walk into off, or where a station cannot be entered, the front desk answers at the door. - The front desk is a list: report a crime, an accident or a fire near you, pay your outstanding fines, ask about your record, collect your car from the pound, apply for a licence or permit (with driving licences on), and ask for a police report ({law_report_fee}) on a break-in at one of your shops or your car broken into in the last {law_report_days} days. The insurer takes its number: after a break-in report the newest theft claim is paid in full, and after a car report the car's next repair is paid without the excess. - Inside, the station is furnished with the game's own furniture: waiting chairs and a queue at the front desk, desks where officers work, a briefing screen, a break table and the holding cell. The way to the front desk is always kept clear. Furnished police stations off leaves the station bare. # Arrest and custody (option: 'Arrests end in a holding cell') - You are arrested when you are caught after fleeing a traffic stop or a crash. With Arrests for serious offences on, you are also arrested after a death on the road, even if you stayed, and when your 911 calls about nothing reach {law_wasted_calls} in one day. - You are held in a holding cell at the nearest police station, shown as a list that cannot be closed. The time follows the charges and is longer if you were held lately, never more than {law_most_hours} hours. - In the cell you can sit it out, pay bail to walk at once (no bail after a death), or call a lawyer once for {law_lawyer_fee} (less if the public thinks well of you), which strikes a third off what is left. - After release your car is at the police pound: any front desk has it brought to the kerb for {law_impound_fee}. Where the station cannot be entered, the car is brought round at release for the same fee. - If you got away after hurting someone, you are wanted. For {law_turnin_days} days a front desk lets you hand yourself in for half the time and half the bail. - The fines are charged once, by whoever stopped you. With the courts on, the hours in the cell count as time served, bail paid here is the bail of your case, and custody ordered by a court is served in the same cell. # Record and reputation (option: 'Your record and reputation matter') - Every ticket, every stay in a cell and every escape goes on your record and lowers your standing with the police and with the public. With a long record lately the police watch you more closely and stop letting you off with a warning; a clean spell ends that. - Staying with someone hurt in an accident, reporting an accident and stopping a thief raise what the public thinks of you. From a good name on, passers-by say thanks, and with a very good one now and then give you a few dollars. - The Police Records Desk and the front desk read out both.
reallife_meta_title_transport: Buses, the subway and car ownership
reallife_guide_transport_about: Bus stops with buses to board, subway journeys that take time, and a car that needs looking after.
reallife_guide_transport: # Buses - Bus stops stand along up to {bus_routes} routes between the subway stations, {bus_station_lines} to a station where the roads allow; where lines share a street they share its stops. - Each line runs to a timetable. The main lines run most often, above all at the weekday rush hours, and they alone run from {bus_night_from} to {bus_night_until}. In the rain every line runs a little less often, and the city's transit policy (see City government and building sites) makes them run more or less often. - Point at a bus stop, its shelter or the bus standing at it and click, as with any object of the game: you walk over. Within {bus_reach} m of a stop the game's panel shows the stop and every line that calls there with its next bus (Delayed shows only when a bus is held up, with its new time), and each button on it shows its key. While a building's box is on screen in the same place, the panel stands beside it. - Choose a stop opens the city map, as a subway entrance does. Every stop the buses reach from there is marked on it, and the stop you are at is marked in red. Beside the map, the game's list of stations lists the stops with the line, the time and the fare; type in its search field to find one by name. Point at an entry and the map glides to the stop; point at a marker to see its name. Click either to pick it. - Each entry names the bus to take. A stop one of the lines here reaches is on that bus; any other takes one change of bus, at a stop both lines call at or a short walk away: you get off, walk to it if you must, and board the next bus of the second line there. A stop no single change reaches passes under a fade. One {bus_fare} fare covers the ride either way. - Pick a stop while the bus stands and you board at once; pick one while you wait and you board by yourself when the bus pulls in. You walk to the nearer of its two doors and tap your card on the validator. You sit by the middle door; on a full bus you stand and hold a strap. Until the doors close, move to get off again and the fare is given back. - When the doors close, the game's own activity panel shows the ride, its title naming your stop and its bar how far you have come. The bus drives its route through the city, calling at every stop on the way, until it reaches yours (from above, its roof is taken off so that you can see in). Use the panel's fast forward to ride at the game's fast speed, or its skip to pass the rest of the ride under a fade. - Move, or press Get off at the next stop, and you get off at the next stop instead, with nothing given back; the button then reads Stay on. On a journey with a change the panel's title names the change, and at the change the stop's panel offers Skip the rest of the journey. - A ride along a route the bus cannot drive passes under a fade, and so does a journey whose second line does not run at that hour, and the rest of a ride on a bus that has been stuck for a long while. - At your stop you step off by the middle door and the bus leaves. A save made during a ride puts you at the last stop the bus called at, or back at the stop you boarded at, with the fare, if it has not called at one yet. - A bus held up close to its stop, by a car, somebody in the road or you, opens its doors where it stands. Street furniture on the kerb by the doors and on the way to them is taken away while the buses run. - The first entry of the list sells the day pass: {day_pass} for every bus and subway journey until midnight. Sit down puts you on the bench where a shelter has a free seat; Get up or any key gets you up, and so does the bus. # The subway - At a subway entrance the game's panel shows how often trains run and any delays. Click the entrance and the game's own subway map opens: pick a station and pay the game's {subway_fare} fare (given back as the train leaves if you hold a day pass). When you come up at the other end, the clock moves on by the whole journey under a fade: the wait for a train, the stops and any delays. A note says how long it took. The City Transit contact tells you the state of the subway and sells the day pass. # Your car - A car you own wears: tyres and brakes lose grip and bite with distance, and a service falls due every so often. Once the service is overdue the car can break down. - What a car needs (a service, tyres, brakes, a breakdown) is written in the game's vehicle panel, after its condition. - Once a game year its registration and inspection fall due. You are reminded, it can be renewed from {car_reg_early} days before, and renewing late costs {car_reg_late} more. - Stop in a filling station's repair bay and the game's panel there says what is due and what it comes to. Its Garage button, on the key it shows, opens a list: Order has everything that is due done, the registration included. - Broken down or out of fuel and standing still, a panel over the car offers Call roadside assistance or Have fuel brought on the key it shows. - The Garage contact lists every car with its fuel, condition, tyres, brakes, service, insurance and registration. Roadside Assistance sends a mechanic ({car_roadside}, half that for an insured car) or {car_fuel_litres} litres of fuel ({car_fuel_callout}) to your car, or tows it to a repair bay ({tow_fee}). - Insurance runs {car_policy_days} days, renews itself and pays {car_cover} of a repair bill above the first {car_excess}; each claim makes the next premium dearer. A car modified at the custom shop wears faster and costs more to insure. - A mobile mechanic from Household staff can see to your cars at home. # Options - Easy car ownership switches fuel use, wear and breakdowns off.
reallife_guide_leisure_about: Chess, fishing, a night out, sights to see, clothes to buy, city sounds and photo mode.
reallife_guide_leisure: # Things to do - The game's panel appears where something can be done, naming it and its cost, with a button on {key_interact} or a click. One thing at a time, never during a job, a police stop or in a vehicle, and not with your energy nearly gone. Walk away and it ends. - Your best scores are kept: a new one says so on the result card, and My leisure records and landmarks on the options page lists them. Done with a friend on an outing, it counts as time together. - Street chess: from 09:00 to 20:00 in dry weather a chess player sits at a table on the pavement near you ('People working and out on the pavements' must be on); the city map's What's on marks it. The stake is {chess_stake}. Five positions, three moves to choose from, 22 seconds each (a move not chosen scores nothing): 7 points of 10 wins {chess_stake}, 5 or 6 gets the stake back. Walk off before the first move and the stake is returned; after it, it is lost. - Fishing: stand still at the water's edge near a waterside sight (the ferris wheel, a bridge, the casino pier, a harbour, the Hamptons), facing open water; the city map's Sights and fishing spots row shows them. Bait is {fish_bait} for five casts. Time the cast on the bar of the job panel, wait for the bite and strike in time, then keep the line in the green zone for three pulls; strike too early or miss too often and it gets away. A better cast brings a bite sooner and rarer fish. There are eight kinds to catch, one of them an old boot worth nothing; the catch is sold by weight, also if you pack up early or walk off. - A night out: in a nightclub, dance on the dance floor (press the button on the beat; the job panel shows where the beat is) with empty hands, and order at the bar: beer {drink_beer}, cocktail {drink_cocktail}, soft drink {drink_soft}. From {leisure_tipsy_from} drinks you are tipsy (a beer counts as 0.8, a cocktail as 1.2): your car wanders, and driving like that is an offence. From {leisure_served_up_to} the bartender pours only soft drinks. A drink's worth wears off every 90 minutes. - Sightseeing: at a landmark you have not seen, take a selfie with it behind you. The card counts the landmarks you have seen out of all of them. - Cinemas and theatres name the day's show as you go in. Watch it for 45 minutes or more and you get a verdict: a great show lifts your mood more than a good one, and a dud not at all. - At night, from 20:00 to 03:00 in dry weather, two people stand talking outside an open club, cinema or theatre near you. # Clothes - The mod's clothes and shoes are sold at the Real Life Overhaul rack in any clothing store: it opens the game's own clothes screen as a shop, with every garment in every colour and its price. A click tries it on; the Save button then reads Buy with the price of what you are trying, and buying keeps it on. What you do not buy comes off when you close the screen. It needs the mod's clothes files. - At home, the wardrobe's own Change clothes has what you own of the mod's after the game's pieces, in the colours you bought. Save keeps what you pick; closing without saving puts back what you wore. - "Clothes must be bought" is kept per save: on for a new game, off for a save that was already going. # Sound and photos - Out of doors: birds by day and crickets at night in dry weather, distant traffic, and a crowd murmur near people, each with its own volume, quieter in a car. In a car, the radio's station and song can be named on screen. - {key_photo_mode} opens and leaves photo mode: the game pauses (not in a Going Public session, where the clock is shared) and the camera flies free within 150 m of you. Pressed in a menu, it starts when you close the menu. A notification names the keys: the mouse to look, W A S D to fly, X and Z for up and down, Shift and Ctrl for speed, the wheel to zoom, J and L to roll, comma and full stop for exposure, K for a filter, G, Y and U for focus, "1" hides you, "2" the game's interface, "3" resets, and Enter saves a picture. - Selfies: in photo mode the "4" key holds the camera out at arm's length in front of you, with your back to what the free camera was looking at, so point it at what you want behind you first. The mouse moves the phone round your face, the wheel brings it nearer or farther, and "5" changes the pose: the phone held out, a wave, a fist in the air or talking to the camera. On foot only, indoors or out; not in a vehicle. A selfie with a friend beside you on an outing pleases them, once an outing.
reallife_meta_title_events: City events: fires, weather, street events
reallife_guide_events_about: Fires and the fire service, weather that matters, and markets, parades and fireworks in the street.
reallife_guide_events: # Fires (option: 'Fires and the fire service') - Now and then a car, a bin or a shopfront catches fire near you, more often in a heat wave and less often in the rain. The lane beside it is closed, a fire engine comes and the crew puts the fire out. Report it through 911 and the engine is sent at once. - At a burning shopfront, {key_interact} at the door warns the people inside. - A fire at a business of your own closes it for some hours and leaves a repair bill of up to {fire_repair_most}. Both are smaller the sooner water is on the fire, and if you rang 911, warned the people inside or the business has good security. With fire cover on the Company app's Cover tab, claim it there. A save's only business is spared in its first {fire_grace_days} days. # Weather (option: 'Weather affects driving, crime and energy') - Rain, mist, thunderstorms, snow on the roads and, on some summer and winter days, a heat wave, a cold snap or ice change your car's grip, the speed of traffic, how far the police see, and how often accidents and street crime happen. Fewer people are out in the rain, and nobody new comes out in a thunderstorm. - On foot out of doors, heat in the middle of the day and cold or ice at any hour cost a little energy, never the last of it. In a warm top (the game's own sweaters, hoodies, jackets, cardigans, blazers and coats, or the mod's bomber jacket) the cold costs none. - Heat, cold and ice are announced, not shown. The City Bulletin contact has the morning forecast. # Street events (option: 'Street events') - Street markets, a farmers' market on Saturday mornings, parades, protests, fun runs, film shoots and fireworks on New Year's Eve and Independence Day close a stretch of road near you for a few hours. Each is announced the evening before and the morning of the day, on screen and by the City Bulletin. With Notifications about protests off, protests still happen, without the notices. - With {key_interact} you can buy a snack at a stall for {snack_price}, sign the petition, cheer the runners or marchers, or watch a take. A thunderstorm calls the event off. # One thing at a time - One fire or street event runs at a time, and none starts while an accident, a crime, a police stop or a rally is going on. - For a guest in a Going Public session, fires and street events are off: the traffic is the host's.
reallife_guide_social_about: People you get to know, and things to do together.
reallife_guide_social: # People - {social_cast} people can be in your life: Mom and your old friend Alex from the start. Others come up to you now and then: in the street, after the gym, after a paid job shift, at the coffee cart once you are a regular, after a good turn, outside your home or shop, at an evening out, or through Flare. New faces keep coming, one a day at most, while 'New people come up to you' is on. The game's panel over them offers Talk on {key_interact} or a click, and Swap numbers. You can also stop anybody on the pavement yourself and swap numbers (see Street talk). Mom and Alex look the same in every game; somebody you meet in the street keeps the look you saw, and somebody met on Flare the face they have there. - The People contact lists everyone and how things stand: their age, stage, mood, how close you are (familiarity, affection and trust, each out of 100), the last thing said, what they would like to do and their birthday. More about them shows their traits, how long you have known them, money between you and memories. # Stages - Friend: familiarity {social_friend_fam}, affection {social_friend_aff}, trust {social_friend_trust} and {social_friend_shared} things done together. Close friend: {social_close_fam}, {social_close_aff} and {social_close_trust}, {social_close_shared} things done together and {social_close_days} days known. A stage is kept until the figures fall {social_slack} below what earned it; Mom stays at least a friend. - Calls, outings kept, favours, presents and selfies together raise them. Neglect cools them: a few days without a word and closeness slips, sooner for a partner, later for a close friend. Standing somebody up is remembered. - Romance is asked for, never earned. With no partner, Ask them out is offered to a friend or closer who could fall for you, not again within a few days: they say yes from affection {social_date_aff} and trust {social_date_trust}. Make it official needs affection {social_partner_aff}, trust {social_partner_trust}, {social_partner_days} days of dating and {social_partner_dates} dates. Below affection {social_breakup_aff} or trust {social_breakup_trust} they end it. - Living together: with Family on, it is part of family life (see Family). With Family off, Ask them to move in needs trust {social_movein_trust} and {social_movein_days} days as partners. # Calls and texts - Chat brings up something to talk about, once a day each; a call covers {social_topics} topics. With an RLO Texts pack installed and running, or Your own AI, Type a reply opens the game's text box: you say it in your own words, and they answer in theirs. It counts the same as the friendly answer. Without either, for Mom, or with 'Type your own words in calls' off, you pick one of two answers. - Something else offers, one at a time, only what applies: a favour of somebody with a position (see Networking), Make plans, a birthday greeting on the day (then Send a present), Pay back what you owe, Ask them out, Make it official, Family matters for a partner, Ask to borrow and Ask to meet their friends. - Borrowing needs some trust and costs a little each time; a third ask within {social_ask_window} days costs more. A close friend, Mom or a partner lends more, a generous person more still. Pay it back within {social_repay_days} days or lose trust, again every {social_repay_days} days. - A friend may ask to borrow a little of your cash (Of course or I can't, sorry) and pays it back within a week or so; a flaky one may ask for {social_loan_grace} days more, and may never pay. - Call somebody back the day they text you, or the next, and the call opens on what they wrote about: their news, a worry, a little moment of their day or yours. It is the call's chat, worth what any chat is, and each text is taken up once. - People text one at a time, at most once a day each and never between {social_quiet_from} and {social_quiet_to}; 'Most texts in a day' caps them all. With 'Text messages from people' off, only what must be said comes, as a notification. - Only the {social_circle} closest to you, family, your partner and anyone met in the last {social_circle_new} days get in touch on their own; call the others whenever you like. Friends also text when you get richer, after a crash or a break-in at your shop, and after an arrest, which costs some trust with everyone. # Outings - Plans are made by calling somebody: Make plans, then the outing and one of two times they are free (The first or The second), from {social_plan_lead} minutes ahead up to {social_plan_hours} hours. One plan at a time. Paid outings, a head, and the hours they can be agreed for: {social_outings_paid}. Free: {social_outings_free}. Drinks, a drive and a look round your business need a friend; a drive needs a car of yours near. - Somebody on a rough day may say no. If the place is shut at that hour they suggest a walk. - Friends also ask for a lift (On my way: your own car, near you) or help moving (I'll help), and invite you out (I'm in or Not this time). A favour well done can bring a thank-you gift. - An invitation in a Flare message books an outing too: when the answer is yes it names the place and the time, and it is a plan like any other. - From {social_early} minutes before, the place and time are on the game's job panel at the top right, with the game's marker for the place. Meet them outside and use the panel over them to say hello, on {key_interact} or a click. On time earns trust; over {social_late} minutes late costs affection and trust; after {social_stood_up} you have stood them up, which costs a lot. I have to cancel on a call costs a little, more within the last hour. Walking off after hello is rude. - At hello for a paid outing: My treat pays for both and pleases them, Let's split it halves it, and If you insist lets them pay when it was their idea or they are generous. If you cannot pay, they cover it and you lose a little trust. - At a business they go in at the door and the time inside passes as a fade: you do not see the inside and nobody sits down. If the place has shut by then, it becomes a walk. A walk, a drive (they ride in the back) and carrying boxes happen in the street. On a walk, stand by one of the city's benches and the game's panel offers Sit down: you sit, your companion sits beside you if the second place is free, and a rest counts as 40 m of the walk, once a walk. - A selfie together on an outing brings you a little closer, once an outing. The day after an outing or a date, they may text about how it went, good or bad. # Losing touch - On a person's page, More about them offers Lose touch: after the game's own question they leave your phone, and somebody new can take their place. Family, Alex, a partner or somebody you are dating, anyone who lives with you or is moving in, anyone you have plans or money with, and Flare's influencers stay, and the page says why. - Once your life is full, an acquaintance who has drifted and you have not spoken to for {social_lose_days} days may go by themselves to make room. With 'Relationships fade if neglected' off, nobody drifts or goes. # With the rest of the mod - The morning paper is a feature of its own: see The City Ledger. Its contact on the phone is the paper's subscriptions desk. - A close friend speaks for you in court and visits you in prison. Friends know of a record, and of a good name.
reallife_guide_travel_about: Hotels to stay in when you have no bed, and holidays booked at the travel agencies.
reallife_guide_travel: # Hotels (option: 'Hotels to stay in') - {travel_hotels} places to stay: city hotels from a hostel to luxury, named on the city map, and cottages in the Hamptons. At a hotel's door the game's panel offers Reception on {key_interact}: choose a room, then the nights, and pay now or leave a deposit. - With a room booked, the panel offers Go up to your room on its second key. The room is a list of choices, not a place you walk around: sleep, shower, food, laundry, rest, extend, check out. A night there counts as sleep. Checkout is at {room_checkout}; a late checkout, free in a luxury room, runs to {room_late_checkout}. - A night costs from {room_dorm} for a dorm bed to {room_suite} for a corner suite, before district, weekend and season. A long stay is cheaper a night, and every {room_free_stamps} nights earn a free one. - The Trips contact shows your booking and points you to the nearest hotel. # Holidays (option: 'Holidays, and burnout without a break') - At the door of an open travel agency the game's panel offers the agent on {key_interact}. After the first visit Getaways Travel also takes bookings by phone. - Trips run from a Hamptons weekend ({trip_hamptons}) to a Europe tour ({trip_europe}), dearer or cheaper by season. First class, insurance ({trip_insurance} of the price) and a companion cost extra. A ticket is good for {trip_ticket_days} days. Now and then a trip falls through at the gate: insurance pays it all back, without it you get {trip_refund_uninsured}. - The Hamptons weekend is a real stay at the cottages: you travel there yourself. Every other trip is told in a list, one page a day with a choice, while the days pass at home and your businesses run without you. - You come back rested, with souvenirs for friends. Your partner or a close friend can come along, which does the relationship good. - With Suitcase, insurance, a companion, trade fairs on, the agent sells a suitcase ({travel_suitcase}) so that more souvenirs get home whole, and a business owner is invited to a trade fair now and then. - You cannot leave town with a warrant out, a bail decision pending or a court date inside the trip. - After {travel_burnout_warn} days of work without a break a friend says so; after {travel_burnout_days} you are worn out, which lowers your happiness until you take a holiday or rest in a hotel room over a few afternoons. # Known limits - In a Going Public session holidays wait until you play alone, and a hotel room cannot sleep the night away for you.
reallife_guide_careers_about: A steady job with an employer: a rota, reviews, promotion and a CV.
reallife_guide_careers: # How it works - Six employers have their offices at the help-wanted boards: Brightline Promotions (flyers), Brightside Contract Cleaning, Uncle Lou's Street Eats (the drinks cart), Fairway Markets (shelves), Hudson Parcel Co. (parcels) and Five Borough Cabs. Walk up to a board and the game's own panel appears over it with a Speak to the office button (the button shows its key; the mod's own interact key is {key_interact}), or call the Work contact and choose Apply for a job: it asks the same questions and gives the same job. Where the city has no board for an employer, the phone is the only way. Three take anyone, Fairway Markets and Hudson Parcel Co. want one good reference, Five Borough Cabs wants two. A reference letter from gig work counts as one. - You pick a rota of fixed days: Monday, Wednesday and Friday mornings, Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday afternoons, or the weekend. A shift is {career_shift_hours} hours and is always shown with its start and its end, such as 13:00 to 17:00. On a rota day, clock on at the office or through the Work contact, from {career_early} hours before the start. Clocking on starts the employer's kind of gig work where you stand, paid as the gig without the Gig Line's day to day offers, the higher ranks taking a bigger share of what the work pays and of its tips, plus a basic hourly wage for up to {career_shift_hours} hours. The Jobs page says how each kind of work is done; at Uncle Lou's Street Eats the cart is set up beside you and you walk round behind it. - Clocking on {career_on_time} hour or more after the start is late: it costs a mark and an hour's basic pay. From {career_late} hours after the start the shift has gone and is a no-show, which is a mark too. {career_marks} marks and you are dismissed, your reference is marked down and that employer will not take you back for {career_ban_days} days. - If no client of the shift is open when you clock on, you are turned away without blame: neither a later start nor the day missed is held against you. - A doctor's sick note, or being ill, excuses the day: say "I'm not well today" to the boss or the Work contact. - After every {career_review_shifts} shifts a review is due at the office (by phone where the employer has no office in this city). A good score brings a raise or the next rank, a poor one a mark; at most {career_raises} raises at one rank. The top ranks work the dispatch desk or a shift in charge, both clocked on at the office. At the desk the panel has a button for each van; on a shift in charge the buttons are what you say or do. Neither has Let time pass: every call is a decision. - Two ranks have no basic wage and keep what they take: the cart owner with a licence at Uncle Lou's and the owner-operator at Five Borough Cabs. A raise there is a bigger share of what the work pays. - To leave, give notice and work {career_notice_shifts} more shifts, or {career_notice_days} days, whichever comes first. Walking out marks your reference down. - The Work contact shows your rota and your CV: where you have worked, your references, gig levels and any criminal record. - Each of these employers has one help-wanted board of its own, outside a shop in the city, so there is no Fairway shop to look for: Fairway Markets' office is its board. To find a board, open the Career app's Professions tab: it lists each employer with the address of its board and a Show on map button that puts the game's destination marker on it. The city map's Job offices row marks every board by its employer's name, and the map's search finds an employer by that name. You can also call the Work contact, choose Something else twice and then Show me the office. - These employers are the gig work's own. Work in a profession, with a CV of qualifications, is on the Professional jobs page.
reallife_guide_business_about: Things that happen to the businesses you run: rivals, inspections, staff, suppliers, an audit.
reallife_guide_business: # What happens - Each morning at 09:00 there is a chance that one of your businesses gets an issue: {biz_chance_least} a day at frequency 1, {biz_chance_most} at 10. Nothing comes up in the first {biz_save_days} days, or at a business you have had for less than {biz_shop_days}. - One issue per business and {biz_open_most} in all at a time. A business is left alone for {biz_rest_days} days after one ends, and each kind waits a while before it comes again. - An issue comes as a message from the Business desk contact, with a deadline and up to four answers. Call the desk to go through what is open: each answer is read out with its cost before you take it. An issue left alone is settled by its default at the deadline. The desk's messages are the record of what happened. - Costs follow what that business takes in a day, between a least and a most. A charge you did not choose, such as a fine, a repair or a tax adjustment, is never more than {biz_cash_share} of the cash you hold, and nothing is taken that you cannot pay: the issue ends the other way instead. - Effects are limited: customers down by {biz_dip_most} or up by {biz_boost_most} at most for a few days, a closure of {biz_closed_most} hours at most. A change in customers shows in the promotion figure on the business's page in BizMan. A closure ticks the business's own closed switch, and the mod unticks it when the closure ends. - If you are in the shop, the collector, an inspector or the police may walk in. # The kinds - Rival moves: a competitor undercuts you (push your marketing, match prices, raise cleanliness and satisfaction, or ride it out); a rival offers one of your staff {biz_poach_raise} more, answered in the employee's own messages as the game's offers are; a smear in the paper (reply, call a lawyer or ignore it). Undercutting and smears do not come where the game's own special rival is already after you. - Protection racket: only at a business that takes {biz_racket_least} a day or more. A collector asks for a weekly sum. Pay, and it grows each week. Refuse, and a brick may come through the window: a repair and a few hours shut, less likely the better your security. Go to the police, and if they make a case the collector is caught at the shop and the racket is over for good in that save. Or raise the game's security level to {biz_racket_security} within a few days, and he gives up for a while. After a refusal, or once he backs off, nothing for {biz_racket_rest} days. - Inspections: a health inspection for a business that sells food, a fire-safety inspection for any, the next day at {biz_inspection_hour}. Health reads the game's cleanliness figure: {biz_health_pass} passes, under {biz_health_fail} is a fine, and under {biz_health_shut} or an unpaid fine shuts the shop for some hours; in between is a warning and a second visit. Fire needs cleanliness of {biz_fire_clean} and the game's facility score of {biz_fire_facility}. A contract clean or a contractor's check booked beforehand helps, and a clean pass brings a few more customers. A licence renewal asks for a fee within a few days: paid late it costs more, unpaid it shuts the shop for some hours. With the Company app's licences on, this one does not come up, as that app already charges for your licences. - Staff trouble: a strike threat when wages are well under the going rate (agree to raises, pay a bonus, or refuse and risk a walkout); theft by an employee at a self-service shop with cameras (dismiss, warn or let it go); an argument between two employees. Satisfaction is never pushed below {biz_floor}, and a wage only ever goes up. - Supplier trouble: a wholesale delivery due soon is late (pay for express or take the delay), or comes with a surcharge (pay, haggle with your negotiation skill, or switch haulier). - Customer complaints and praise: a complaint that spreads when satisfaction or cleanliness is low, naming the weakest of the game's figures (apologise with a voucher or ignore it); praise that spreads when satisfaction is high (share it to make it last longer). - Tax audits: once a business has a week of books. With an accountant it is mostly clean; alone there is a fair chance of an adjustment and a small chance of a refund. - Opportunities: a bulk order, paid if the shop is open at noon the next day; a feature in the paper; an award for a clean shop with happy customers. # Options - Each kind of issue has its own switch. Good news only leaves only the opportunities and praise. - Switching Business events off closes every issue without its outcome and puts customer numbers and closures back. - The test buttons start the next kind of a group at the business you stand in, or your first, without the waits. A kind that cannot happen there says why.
reallife_guide_garage_about: Paint, parts and tuning for your cars in any repair bay, and bicycles and motorbikes.
reallife_guide_garage: # The custom shop - Drive a car you own into a repair bay and stop. The game's panel there has a Garage button on the key it shows; choose Custom shop in its list. Each choice shows on the car at once with its price. Drag to turn the car, and mix a colour of your own in the game's colour picker. - Pay, the first entry, keeps the build. Cancel puts the car back as it came in. - With Underglow lights up after dark on, an underglow kit from the lights page glows at night. - Performance parts cost something in use: faster wear of tyres and brakes and dearer insurance (both need car ownership switched on), less grip in the wet with some tyres, and a straight-through exhaust that the police can fine ({fine_exhaust}) while Fines for loud exhausts and no helmet is on. - My vehicles (in that list and on the options page) lists every build. With Custom shop work counts when a car is sold on, a build is valued at {garage_resale} of what was spent, and when you sell the car the buyer pays that on top of the game's price, less as much as the car's condition takes off. - The Figures page reads the car as standard, as it came in and with this visit's work: power, torque, 0 to 100 km/h, top speed, gear change, braking, weight, ride height and grip. The Gear change parts make every change of gear quicker. # Recorded car sounds - With Recorded car sounds on, the car you drive and the car on the shop's turntable play recorded engines, by kind: a small petrol engine, a V8, a sports engine or a diesel. Traffic keeps the game's sound. - A sports or straight-through exhaust and a turbo are heard. On the turntable, hold the throttle key to rev the engine and hear a build before you pay. # Bicycles and motorbikes - At a bike-share dock, a bicycle rack outside a supermarket or a motorbike stand outside a car dealership a panel offers hire, return or what is for sale, on the key it shows. All three are on the map. - Hiring a bicycle costs {bike_dock}. Return it to any dock by the end of the next day, or it is collected with a {bike_late} late fee. - Bicycles cost {bike_city} and {bike_road}, motorbikes {moto_standard} and {moto_sport}, a helmet {helmet_price}. A rack or stand buys yours back at {garage_resale} of its price. - Pedalling uses energy. Riding a motorbike without a helmet can be fined ({fine_helmet}). - A motorbike needs a motorcycle licence (see Driving licences). The dealer will sell you one without, and says so. Riding it unlicensed is for the police to find: a fine, and the bike is towed. - My vehicles shows where each two-wheeler stands. Show me puts the game's destination marker on it. Bring it here works on foot and out of doors; from further off than a short walk it costs {bike_bring}. - Bicycles and motorbikes are solid: they stop against walls, poles and cars, a hard crash at speed throws you off, and anyone you ride into is knocked off their feet. A bike left in a post or a pole is stood clear of it when you get on or off. The game's panels and messages call each one by its own name.
reallife_guide_justice_about: An arrest for something serious opens a case: bail, a lawyer, a hearing, a sentence.
reallife_guide_justice: # A case - Tickets stay tickets. An arrest for something serious, or a charge by post, opens a case with a court date {justice_court_least} to {justice_court_most} days ahead. Texts remind you; the Legal contact has your file. - Other features can take you to court too: an audit that finds tax kept back, shares sold after talking them up on Flare, a bribe or campaign money that came out, a data breach, an undeclared interest in a council vote. Lenders, former employers and rival tycoons can bring civil claims. - Bail: released on your promise, an amount returned when you appear, a bondsman's fee you do not get back, or custody until the court sits, in the holding cell of the nearest police station. A grave charge or a warrant can mean no bail. Bail already paid at a police station is the bail of your case. - Weak charges are dropped the day after. A case left with nothing is dismissed, with compensation for a wrongful arrest. - A lawyer tells you the odds, can move to dismiss weak charges and can bring a plea deal. The public defender and yourself are free. A law firm's fee depends on its rating and how serious the charge is: a quarter at once, the rest over {justice_fee_days} days. - On the day, between {justice_court_opens} and {justice_court_closes}, go to the courthouse: the game's panel at its door offers Attend the hearing on {key_interact} or a click. Without a courthouse, or with Hearings in person at the courthouse off, the hearing is by video link from the Legal file. - Miss it and a warrant is issued, your bail is lost and failure to appear is charged. The next police stop takes you in, or officers come to your door after {justice_warrant_days} days, unless you Hand yourself in at the courthouse first. # The hearing and the sentence - Plead guilty ({justice_guilty_off} off the sentence), take a deal ({justice_deal_off} off), or fight it: each round of a trial has a choice, and every term of the verdict is shown. - A sentence can be a fine (never more than a share of your cash, at most {justice_fine_cap}), community service (up to {justice_community_cap} hours of litter picking), custody (at most {justice_custody_cap} hours, served in the holding cell of the nearest police station; hours already spent in a cell count), prison (days, at most Longest prison term (days)), probation and a driving ban. - What you paid at the roadside is taken off the fine. A fine too large to pay at once is taken in daily instalments. - Community service is worked at the courthouse door (Report for service) or from the Legal file, {justice_community_shift} hours of litter a shift, within {justice_community_days} days or it becomes a fine. - Prison passes a day at a time, with choices each morning. Good behaviour takes days off. # Afterwards - One appeal within {justice_appeal_days} days. The record is sealed after {justice_seal_days} clean days. - Someone you crash into may sue: settle or contest the claim from the Legal file, as any other civil claim. - No prison, only fines and custody turns prison into custody and a larger fine. - In a Going Public session custody and prison are served at once.
reallife_guide_licences_about: A licence to drive: the school, the theory and driven tests, points and what a stop finds.
reallife_guide_licences: # Getting a licence - At a driving school desk (the learner plate outside a school building), between {lic_school_opens} and {lic_school_closes}, the game's panel offers Speak to the instructor on {key_interact}. The list has your licence card, the theory test ({lic_theory_fee}), a lesson ({lic_lesson_fee}) and the driven test ({lic_test_fee}) in the school's car. An entry you cannot have says why. The written test is a question card with three answers and a Give up the test entry; during a drive the game's job panel shows the instruction, the checkpoints, your faults and the time. A failed driven test costs {lic_retest_fee} to sit again. - A commercial licence (vans and trucks; driven test {lic_commercial_fee}) and a taxi endorsement ({lic_taxi_fee}, once you have held a car licence for {lic_taxi_days} days with no more than {lic_taxi_points} points) build on the car licence. A bicycle and an electric scooter need none. - A heavy goods licence is for the Freight Truck, the game's largest vehicle. It needs a valid commercial licence: pass its own theory test, take a lesson in the school's truck, then the driven test ({lic_heavy_test_fee}), which can be booked {lic_heavy_wait_days} days after the theory pass; a failed one can be sat again after {lic_heavy_wait_days} days. With it, the Gig Line's courier round offers heavy loads, paid {lic_heavy_load_pay} more, in your own heavy truck or one hired for the day. - A motorcycle licence is for motorbikes and stands on its own. Pass the theory test, then pay {lic_motorcycle_fee} at the desk for the ride assessment. The school has no motorbike to lend, so there is no driven test: the assessment is recorded as passed at the desk. - A licence runs {lic_valid_days} days. It can be renewed from {lic_renew_from} days before it runs out, for {lic_renewal_fee}; one that ran out more than {lic_lapsed_days} days ago needs the tests again. Renewals, the taxi endorsement and your licence card can also be had by phone from the Licensing Office contact. - If you already own a car or a motorbike when the rules first run, you are given that licence. With New saves start with a licence on, a save with no vehicle is given a car licence too. # Points - Offences booked at a stop put points on your licence: a red light, speeding, driving on the pavement or against the traffic, driving after drinking, fleeing, leaving a crash, hurting somebody, driving without a licence, driving on from a check. - Points count for {lic_points_days} days. {lic_points_limit} points suspend every licence for {lic_suspension_days} days. A court can suspend it too: it is the same suspension. # Driving without one - Nobody knows until police stop you: after an offence, after a pursuit, or at a routine roadside check. - A motorbike is checked the same way as a car. A licence for another class, such as a car licence on a motorbike, is the wrong class: a fine of {lic_wrong_class_fine}, and the vehicle is towed. - No licence: a fine of {lic_no_licence_fine}, and the car is towed to the pound for {law_impound_fee}. Run out: a fine of {lic_expired_fine}, and the car stays. Suspended: a fine of {lic_suspended_fine}, the car towed, and a court case. - Caught {lic_arrest_count} times within {lic_repeat_days} days, you are arrested. While suspended, being caught again within that time is enough. - A hired van, the job van or another player's car is never towed. # Options - Driving needs a licence off: everyone may drive anything, as in the base game. - Penalty points on your licence and Roadside licence checks can each be switched off. - Heavy trucks need a heavy goods licence off: the commercial licence covers the Freight Truck, as before, and there are no heavy loads.
reallife_guide_civic_about: A mayor and a council whose policies change the city, elections you can vote and stand in, and building sites that progress over days.
reallife_guide_civic: # The city government (option: 'City government and public works') - The city has a mayor, a council of {civic_seats} and {civic_levers} policy matters, from policing and traffic enforcement to business tax, rent, parking, transit, night life and wages. Each is as the city came, or one step either way. - A policy in force changes the game: how many police are about, street crime and accidents, police fines, parking prices and tickets, the subway fare, how often buses and street events come, and a weekly city account that charges or pays you by your sales, rents and wages. - An election is held every {civic_term_weeks} weeks (option: 'Elections and the mayor'; off, every policy effect is taken back). In the {civic_campaign_days} days before it there are posters, a canvasser with leaflets and rallies, and through the City Hall contact you can Donate, Endorse a candidate or Volunteer now to hand out leaflets. An endorsement from somebody with a criminal record is a scandal. If the candidate you gave to wins, every {civic_favour_per} you gave earns you a fast-track permit, which makes a building site work faster. - On election day, {civic_polls_open} to {civic_polls_close}, vote at your district's polling place: stand at the white sign by its door and the game's panel offers Go in and vote on {key_interact} or a click. The count is at {civic_result_hour}. The winner's policies come in one a day. - Anyone may start a petition through City Hall for a policy that is not in force. With the signatures of {civic_petition_share} of the voters, the council must vote on it. - Call the City Hall contact for the mayor and the policies in force and what they cost or pay you, the election and its count, building sites, petitions and standing for office. # Standing for office (option: 'Standing for office') - You can stand yourself: for the council seat of the district your home is in, or for mayor. Papers may be filed from {office_open} days before election day until the first {office_late_days} days of the campaign are over, through the last topic of the City Hall contact. - To stand you need a home in the city, no conviction that still counts and no case in court, a platform of policies, and either signatures ({office_signatures_council} for the council, {office_signatures_mayor} for mayor) or a deposit ({office_deposit_council} or {office_deposit_mayor}), returned if you take {office_deposit_back} of the vote. Your businesses sign once; knocking on doors brings more. A party gives your campaign money and wants a policy on its issue; an independent gets none. - The campaign has a fund: your own money, a party's grant and donors. A donor may give {office_limit_council} for the council or {office_limit_mayor} for mayor. More than that, cash from nobody named or money passed through other people's names is against the law, and it can come out, go to court and cost you the race. - Spend the fund on posters you put up yourself ({key_interact} facing a shop wall), adverts in the City Ledger and on social media, a rally you speak at, or canvassers. Between {office_doors_from} and {office_doors_to}, knock on the front doors of homes ({key_interact}) and talk about what the person is worried about. Ask the city's bodies for their endorsement, and answer your rivals' attacks. - The debate is on television {civic_debate_days} days before the vote, in the evening. As a candidate you take part once you are free that evening; miss it and it counts against you. Result night is at {civic_result_hour} on election day. The vote is counted district by district, from what each district cares about, what the city thinks of you, your campaign and the economy. - In office you are paid ({office_salary_council} or {office_salary_mayor} a week) and the council meets every week from {office_meeting_hour}: you vote on each motion, or as mayor speak for or against it and set the agenda. A mayor proposes the city's budget and may order how the city is kept. File your register of interests, and declare an interest in a vote that touches your own businesses or property: an undeclared one can come out as a scandal, and go to court if your vote decided it. Approval under {office_recall_below} for {office_recall_days} days brings a recall. # Building sites (option: 'Construction sites') - Roadworks, scaffolding, shop refits and utility works are in progress around the city, {civic_sites} at a time, and move through {civic_stages} stages over days. Crews work on weekdays and stop for rain. One at a time, a whole building is rebuilt: it is wrapped to its roof in the game's own scaffolding and fabric, which fades with the building when it would hide you. - A site near you is set out in the street, with a lane closed where it must be and a notice board you can read from the game's panel beside it ({key_interact} or a click). There, or through City Hall, you can complain about noise, report the site as unsafe, or call in a fast-track permit. - Refitting your own shopfront through City Hall ({refit_least} to {refit_most}) puts up a hoarding for some days and lifts your mood when it comes down; the shop's trade does not change. # Known limits - Posters, boards, scaffolding and the things on a site are plain shapes without artwork. - The night-life policy changes street crime only: bars and clubs keep the game's hours. The transit policy does not change bus fares. - In a Going Public session the city's government is the host's, and standing for office is not offered.
reallife_map_places_shown: The mod's places on the city map
reallife_fine_rest_court: That was all the police took at the roadside. The rest of the fine, {rest}, goes to court with the case.
reallife_fine_rest_waived: The roadside fine was held to what you could pay. The remaining {rest} is not collected.
reallife_transit_stop_coming: The bus is {metres} m away, about {minutes} min. It calls at:
reallife_transit_stop_delayed_none: DELAYED: no bus has been able to set out yet. It calls at:
reallife_transit_stop_delayed_light: DELAYED: the bus is held at a red light, {metres} m away.
reallife_transit_stop_delayed_traffic: DELAYED: the bus is held up in traffic, {metres} m away.
reallife_transit_stop_delayed_closure: DELAYED: the road is closed ahead of the bus, {metres} m away.
reallife_transit_stop_delayed_late: DELAYED: the bus is running late, {metres} m away.
reallife_transit_bus_skipped: The {route} bus you were waiting for is stuck and is not coming. The next one has been sent.
reallife_changes_001: First public release. In it: a camera behind your character and behind the car; cars that drive like their kind; traffic accidents with police, an ambulance and a cordon; street crime, police stops, police stations, custody, courts and prison; driving licences and a driving school; life events; jobs and careers; home life, health and a doctor; people to know, outings and a morning paper; a partner, a wedding and children; buses, the subway as a journey and car ownership; a custom shop, bicycles and motorbikes; hotels and holidays; fires, weather and street events; a city government and building sites; pressure on your businesses; leisure, clothes and photo mode; presets, this Guide, and tools for taking the mod out of a save.
reallife_guide_family_about: A partner who moves in, an engagement and a wedding, children and relatives, run from your fridge's Family button, your partner's call and face to face.
reallife_guide_family: # Where family life is run - Family life is run from the Family contact, which is made on every save while Family life is on (it needs the mod's phone contacts option). It opens the Family page and its Things to do, one at a time, and it is the way to ask for what happens out of doors: a walk with the pushchair, a proposal or a wedding in the open air. - At home there are two more ways in: the Family button in your fridge's panel, which opens the same page without what needs your partner in the room, and face to face, where your partner's panel offers Talk on {key_interact} (cooking or watching together, their work and wishes, chipping in, the car, the allowance). With Social life on, Family matters in your partner's call in People offers making another home of yours the family home, dinner at Mom's, the in-laws' favour, counselling, time apart, coming home and parting. - Standing in another home of yours, your partner's messages offer Make this our new home. # A partner - With Social life on, your partner is one of the people in the People contact: ask them out and make it official (see Social life). With it off, the Someone special contact has a friend introduce you to someone; after a parting, {family_meet_again} days pass before someone new. - An evening out: from Things to do, dinner for two at the nearest restaurant or coffee shop, {family_dinner}. Be at the door in time: the key prompt there pays, and {family_dinner_hours} hours pass. Missing it stands them up. - Moving in: Ask them to move in with you? once you are partners, or after {family_move_in_days} days dating with affection {family_move_in_affection}. You need a home of your own, rented or owned, of {family_sqm} square metres, plus {family_sqm_child} for each child. - At home they go about the place by the hour, with your own furniture: the cooker at dinner time, a mat or weights in the morning, a desk in the day, the plants, and the sofa and the television in the evening. Their sweeping and wiping down really tidy the home, a little each day. They sit only on a chair, an armchair or a sofa you have put there, beside you on a sofa too. At night they sleep in your bed: in a bed for two they leave you room, and from a bed for one they make way while you are in it. When they have something to ask, they come over and wait for you. - From 18:00 each day they pay a share of the rent and the bills: at most {family_rent_share} of them, and at most {family_income_share} of their day's pay. # Engagement and wedding - A jeweller sells {family_rings} rings, {family_ring_least} to {family_ring_most}, at its counter. Once you have been together {family_propose_days} days with affection {family_propose_affection}, Things to do shows you the way to one. - With the ring, ask them to come to you and propose. At home they come over while they live with you and are at home; out of doors you need the Family contact. The odds are better in the evening, at the weekend, on a dry day out of doors, on a day you went out together, dressed formally and with a dearer ring; worse late at night, in the rain and within two days of an argument. After a no, wait {family_propose_again} days. - Plan the wedding from Things to do, or at an event planning agency's counter for {family_planner_fee} more: the place (city hall, a restaurant, a theatre or cinema; {family_venue_least} to {family_venue_most}), the size (simple, classic or grand, which costs more), the guests and the day, one to three weeks ahead. Flowers, music and catering for each guest are added. {family_deposit} of the whole is paid at once and kept if it is called off; the rest is paid on the day, less the guests' gifts. Putting it off costs {family_postpone} and moves it a week. - Be there between {family_wedding_from}:00 and {family_wedding_to}:00 on the day. Miss it once and it moves three days; twice and it is off. Married, your partner moves in with you if you have a home. A honeymoon of {family_honeymoon_length} days is offered for {family_honeymoon}; put off, ask for it from Things to do within {family_honeymoon_days} days. # Children - Once you live together in a happy home with room for another child, Talk to them about having children?: a pregnancy, or an adoption ({family_adoption_fee} to file at a law firm or the tax office, then a home visit and a meeting day). Up to {family_children_most} children. Your partner may want a little time first. - A scan is {family_scan} and the birth {family_birth}, at a hospital or clinic. A cot and a pushchair are bought as errands. Care for a child under {family_school_from}: you, your partner, a nursery ({family_nursery} a month) or a nanny ({family_nanny}). School from {family_school_from}: public, or private for {family_school} a month. - Pocket money from {family_pocket_from}; a college fund paid {family_fund_step} at a time, full at {family_fund_full}. A child is grown up at {family_grown} and ages a year every {family_year_weeks} in-game weeks (an option). - Children are never seen as characters: a baby is a cot at home, an older child is messages and appointments. # Relatives - Mom is next of kin until you marry (change it from Things to do). Four holidays a year bring a family dinner: at home if you live together or have children, otherwise at Mom's. Mom drops in on some Sundays. - An engagement brings The in-laws contact: a chat, their advice, now and then a favour or a loan. # Hard times - Your partner asks for a chore only when it is needed: the fridge nearly empty, the home a mess, a filthy car, or you unwashed (that one face to face only). They ask face to face at home or by text, and it counts once it is really done, by the day after next (a shower the same day), with {family_chore_gap} days at least between chores. Done, the home grows warmer; a promise not kept cools it. {family_neglect_days} days without a word cools it too. - Difficult moments come from what is really going on: long nights at work, money trouble, not calling. - Counselling is {family_counselling} a session, booked for the next day at a hospital or clinic; the first sessions help most, and a missed one hurts. - When things are hard, ask for some time apart. Apart, you can call once a day, and they come home when things have mended. After {family_divorce_days} days apart either of you may end it; with no word at all for {family_files_days} days they file. A divorce settlement is {family_settlement} of your cash, at most {family_settlement_most}, if you were married. Children stay with you and the other parent pays {family_support} of their costs. - Your partner hears of every arrest and of a prison sentence. They take it hard; it does not end things by itself, but a home that stays very unhappy for days does. While you are locked up, family life waits. - Chores, arguments, time apart and divorce can be switched off. # Your partner and your fortune - As your cash grows they react by how they are: a supportive partner is proud of you, an envious one minds the gap more the richer you get (less once you are married). - Once you have earned {family_work_income} a day for a week and have {family_work_cash} in cash, they may ask to cut back to half days ({family_part_time} hours): they are home more and pay a smaller share. Ask them back to full days from Things to do. A no is asked again after {family_ask_again} days. - Once you have earned {family_wish_income} a day for a week and have {family_wish_cash}, they may ask to stop working or to retrain for the job they always wanted: retraining takes {family_retrain_days} days without pay. While they earn nothing you can ask them to chip in for the rent, for {family_chip_weeks} weeks. - As your income and cash grow they expect more: a bigger home, evenings out more often, a weekly allowance, a car of their own and later a second home. Meet it and the home grows warmer; leave it and it slowly cools.
reallife_guide_limits:
What is rough, partial or absent in version {version}.

# Little played
- Much of the mod was built by reading the game's code, and its newest parts have had little play so far. If something goes wrong, see 'Troubleshooting' for how to report it.

# Told, not shown
- The subway journey is a fade to black while time passes, and there is no train interior. On the bus you are seen getting on, riding and getting off; a journey no single change of bus reaches is a fade. Other passengers get on and off at the doors but are not seen inside.
- A hotel room is a list of choices, not a place you walk around. Holidays other than the Hamptons weekend are told in a list, one page a day.
- On an outing that goes indoors your companion goes in at the door and the screen fades while the time passes. Nobody sits at a table.
- A court hearing and prison are pages of text with choices. Custody, an arrest's or a court's, is served in a police station's holding cell only where the station can be walked into and its room has space for a cell; elsewhere it is a list over a dark screen. A police station can be walked into only where its district has an empty unit for it; elsewhere the front desk answers at the door.
- Life events are text. The people in them do not appear.
- A cooked dish is never an item of the game's: you eat a portion when it is done or pack it to take (up to {meals_takeout_most} at a time), and leftovers are a count on the cooking list, not something you can take out of the fridge.

# Family
- Children are never seen as characters: a baby is a cot at home and a pushchair on walks, an older child is messages and appointments.
- Your partner sits at home only on a chair, an armchair or a sofa you have put there, and never lies down. In a home with no clear floor they are not shown.
- A wedding is held on the pavement outside the venue, with five guests at most.

# The city
- One incident at a time: no crime starts while an accident, a fire or a street event is on.
- A bus can be held up in traffic, and a place the roads do not connect may have no line. A journey that needs two or more changes of bus still passes under the fade.
- Heat, cold, ice and mist change grip, traffic and energy but have no look of their own. Rain and snow are drawn.
- The transit policy changes the subway fare and how often buses run, but not bus fares, and the night-life policy does not change opening hours.
- Chess is five positions with a choice of moves, not a board you play on.
- Some actions use an animation of the game's own where the mod has none, and can look approximate.

# Vehicles
- Parts from the custom shop do not raise what the game pays when you sell the car.
- A car added by another mod gets the performance of the nearest kind of car.

# Work
- A job or a shift in progress does not carry on after a load: you are paid what you were owed when you saved, and the shift is over. A home routine or a leisure activity in progress is simply over, with nothing for the time spent: food that was cooking is used up, and fishing bait and a chess stake are not returned.

# The mod as a whole
- Its models and animations are built for Windows.
- English, Brazilian Portuguese, Simplified Chinese, German, French, Spanish, Russian, Dutch and Turkish. In any other language, and for a text not yet translated, the mod is in English.
- While another camera mod drives the camera, this mod's cameras stand aside: the two are never on together.

# Life and death
- There is no permanent death unless you switch Permadeath on. An older save of a character who has died is read as ended only on the computer the death happened on, and only if Permadeath was on in it. Preparing a save for the mod's removal takes everything of the mod out of it, a death too.

# Going Public
- In a session of Going Public, the multiplayer mod, this mod passes no time of its own: custody and prison are served at once, rides take none and photo mode does not pause. Holidays are not booked and a hotel room cannot pass the night for you. Selling a business, the sale of a building and hiring out cars wait until you play alone, the rivals rest, and Permadeath is off. A guest has nothing of this mod that takes cars from the traffic, and the people on the pavement are each player's own. The page 'Going Public' says it all.

reallife_guide_trouble_stutter:
# It stutters after a while
- Most long frames are the game's own. Walking into or out of a building takes the game a frame of a tenth of a second to more than half a second, behind its black screen, so it is not seen. The game's save takes a moment too; the mod's share of it is small. Right after midnight the game frees memory it no longer uses, which can take up to a second on a long session; the mod does not start it.
- The mod does its larger pieces of work, such as dressing people or changing a look, behind the game's black screen at a door. It prepares its code for the game's midnight about {perf_warm_after} seconds after a save loads, so the first midnight of a session no longer stutters. 'Prepare the code for the game's midnight now', a test under Performance, does it at once.
- To find a stutter, switch on 'Developer diagnostics' (options page, Diagnostics) and play until it stutters, for ten minutes at least. Once a minute of play the mod then writes a line to Player.log that begins 'Session': how long the frames took, how many took longer than 33 ms and 50 ms, how much memory is in use, how many things of the mod's are in the city, and the mod's own scripts' share. A frame longer than {session_long_ms} ms gets a line of its own ({session_long_most} a minute at most), which says what the mod was doing at the time, where you were (on foot, driving or indoors), and whether the game's black screen was up or it was saving. After each midnight a line names the mod's share of that frame, and after each save one says how long the mod took to write its part.
- Send Player.log from that session. Say how long you had played when it began, your processor, graphics card and memory, and which other mods were on.
- To see what the mod adds, play the same save for the same time with the mod switched off under Mods, and say whether it still stutters.
reallife_changes_001_1: Smoother over a long session. The mod's people are now made ready while the city loads, where 0.1.0 made each one in the middle of play, and a passer-by keeps the same look for three outings or ten minutes before it changes. A bus stop is only solid to people on foot while you are on foot within 60 m of it, so driving past stops no longer costs anything; until you walk up, pedestrians may pass through its pole and panels. The first time a kind of worker is wanted, their site can take a few seconds longer to appear. For reports of stutter: with 'Developer diagnostics' on, the mod writes a line a minute to Player.log, and the Guide's Troubleshooting page says what to send. With the Workshop item and a local copy both switched on, the second one now does nothing where it used to run everything twice.
