reallife_guide_planner_about: An app on the phone that lists what you have to do, with reminders and your own notes.
reallife_guide_planner: # What it is - Planner is an app on your phone. On the phone at the edge of the screen it stands in the dock at the foot of the home screen until you move it; with folders switched off it is on one of the further pages: turn the page with the mouse wheel or the More apps button. In the phone's full menu it is in the row of apps at the top. - It lists what you have to do and what falls due, from the mod's features and the game: rota shifts, working days, interviews, job offers to answer, freelance deliveries, classes, exams and graduations; court hearings, community service, probation, release from a cell, licence dates and theory test retries; family appointments, a wedding, plans with friends, a hotel checkout, a sick note running out, city events, election day and debates, and your own campaign and council duties if you stand for office; bills, loans, power, water and internet connections and cut-offs, paper subscriptions, dividends, bonds and the game's tax bill; deadlines at your businesses, brands, ventures and listed company; and your own entries. - A feature that is switched off adds nothing to it. The Calendar app shows the same dated entries over a whole month. # Reading it - Today shows today in time order. Upcoming shows the next {planner_days} days, each under its day. Week shows a column for each day of the week ahead, from today, with each entry's kind, its hour and its title. - The filter over the tabs shows Everything, or only Work and study, Money, Family and life or Business. Each tab keeps its own filter while the game runs. - The last column says where an entry stands: Next, Now, Done, Missed, Over, or Clash. Something you have to attend is missed once it can no longer be begun: a class, a shift, a working day and an interview each have their own last moment. - Two things you have to attend clash when their hours overlap, or when their places are too far apart to get from one to the other in time by car or taxi. - Click a day for the day at a glance: the first entry and when to leave for it, the free time between entries, the clashes, and the money due that day and in the next seven days. Click an entry for its details: when, where, what it costs or pays and what happens if you miss it. Set destination points the game's guide at the place, where the Planner knows it. - For an entry at a place the details give a time to leave by. It is worked out from the distance between you and the place along the streets, at {planner_drive} metres a game minute by car or taxi and {planner_walk} on foot, by car if you have one. It is a guess by the distance, not a route. - A number on the app's button counts what begins within {planner_badge_hours} hours, and your own all-day notes for today. It goes when you open the app and comes back only when something new is due. # Reminders - In an entry's details, choose a reminder: 15 minutes before, 30 minutes before, 1 hour before, At the time, The evening before ({planner_evening}), or When to leave for an entry at a place. It arrives as a notification at its minute; click it to open the entry. - A reminder is not sent for something that is done, over or gone. One that fell due while time was skipped arrives once, marked late. - With Planner reminders off in the options, no reminder is offered or sent; the entries stay. - With The morning line on, you wake to one notification of your day: how many entries, the first and when to leave for it. Nothing comes on an empty day. # Your own entries - Add an entry in a day's box, or New note over the tabs: pick a title or type one, a day, an hour or all day, once, every day or every week on that day, and a reminder. Inside a building, This building keeps its address with the entry. - An entry can be marked as done (each time, for one that repeats), edited and deleted. The Planner holds {planner_notes} of them. # Settings - Settings in the app chooses which kinds of entry are shown and the reminder a new entry starts with (at first 1 hour before). Times follow the game's own 12 or 24 hour option. - Your entries, reminders and these settings are kept with the save.

reallife_changes_001_3: Planner: a new app on the phone that lists what you have to do, with reminders and your own notes. Cooking works: click the cooker at home and choose from the dishes your fridge can make. Coffee, tidying and exercises at home now start when you press Start. Every employer can be applied to by phone. A motorbike needs its own licence. Your partner is someone you have met, and hears when you are arrested. A honeymoon you turned down stays on offer for a while.
reallife_changes_001_4: Buses: nobody waits more than about 20 minutes of the game clock for a bus, and a bus waits at the stop for you instead of leaving after a few seconds. Bus stops are there when you arrive: after loading a save, a taxi ride or the subway, a stop near you is put up at once, and when driving they are put up from further away. The driving school takes its car back: when a lesson or test ends you are asked to step out, and the car can no longer be kept and driven. An officer posted at a junction stands watch and no longer waves at traffic that is following the lights. Bicycles are faster: about 38 km/h for the city bicycle and 50 for the road bicycle.

reallife_guide_nav: # The minimap - A small map of the streets around you is on screen while you are out in the city, on foot or driving. It is hidden indoors, on the subway, while the city map or a menu is open, and during scenes that take the screen. - Under the roads it shows the buildings and the water, in the colours of the game's interface. The city is measured for this once for each version of the game, while it loads, and kept in the mod's folder beside your saves. - The arrow in the middle is you. The markers are the places the city map marks: your own buildings, the subway stations, the place of a job or a quest, and the places of this mod whose rows are ticked in the city map's list. - At 100% zoom it shows {nav_view} m of the city from side to side. It shows more while you drive fast. - It stands at the left of the screen, between the task list and the control hints. When a long task list leaves no room there, it stands beside them at the bottom. # The GPS - Set a destination the way the game does it: on a building's card, from a task, or with one of this mod's own destination buttons and map markers. The route appears by itself. A delivery job's destination gets a route as well. - On the city map, two quick clicks on a spot make that spot your destination. - The route is the blue line on the minimap and on the city map. Under the minimap is the next turn with its distance, then the distance left and the time on the game's clock at which you should arrive. - Driving, the route follows the lanes the way traffic may use them. On foot it follows the same streets in either direction. It does not know paths through parks or buildings. - A street's name comes from the addresses of the buildings along it. Where they do not agree, the turn is given without a name. - More than {nav_off_car} m from the route in a car, or {nav_off_foot} m on foot, a new route is found from where you are. - You have arrived within {nav_arrive_car} m of the place in a car, or {nav_arrive_foot} m on foot. The route clears. The destination's marker goes with it. # Names of special buildings - A building the mod gives a role carries that name wherever the game names a building: the utilities office is City Utilities, and the courthouse, each police station, each hotel and Hudson City University have their own names. You see it on the building's card in the street and on the city map, on the destination marker, in the GPS, at the top of the screen inside, and in the city map's search. The address is still shown beside it. - A building you rent or own keeps the name you gave it. Newspaper kiosks and street stalls keep theirs too. - While their features are on, these buildings are not to rent, buy or take over: BizMan says whose they are, and the real estate list and the map's rows of units to let and for sale leave them out. One you already rented or owned stays yours, and the office or company moves to another building. - Only what is shown changes: nothing in your save is renamed, and with the option 'Special buildings carry their own names' off the game's own names come back. # Options - The minimap and the GPS can each be switched off. Special buildings carry their own names is the switch for the names above. - The minimap turns with you or keeps north up. Its size and zoom are sliders. - Buildings and water on the minimap can be switched off. It then shows roads only. - If the mod Voogle Route is also switched on, the city map is left to it: this mod's route shows on its own minimap only, and the double click on the city map is not this mod's. With Use the other mod's route line on, the route is left to that mod altogether and only the minimap is shown.

reallife_guide_taxi: # Calling a taxi - Call City Cabs from your contacts. The dispatcher says how long a taxi will take and what the call-out is. Send one sends it. - The taxi is one of the city's own. It drives to the lane nearest where you stood when you called and stops there, at the kerb where the roadside is free. Click it as you would any taxi: the map opens, you pick where to go and pay the game's fare. - The call-out is {taxi_callout}, or {taxi_callout_night} from {taxi_night_from} to {taxi_night_until}. It is charged when the ride begins, on top of the fare. - In rain or a storm, with Weather affects driving, crime and energy on, the call-out is {taxi_wet_extra} more and the taxi sets out from further off: {taxi_wet_start_least} to {taxi_wet_start_most} m away, where it is {taxi_start_least} to {taxi_start_most} m in the dry. - The minimap marks the taxi while it comes. Call City Cabs again to hear how far it still has to drive. - The taxi waits {taxi_wait} seconds for you, and {taxi_grace} more if you are within {taxi_grace_within} m of it by then. If you are more than {taxi_far} m away when it stops, a notification says so and the game's marker shows where it stands. If you do not get in, it leaves and {taxi_noshow_share} of the call-out is charged. - Cancel it, on a second call, is free while the taxi has more than {taxi_cancel_free} m to drive. Nearer than that it costs {taxi_cancel_share} of the call-out. Getting into a vehicle or another taxi, boarding a bus or the subway, or going indoors while it comes cancels it on the same terms. - The call-out, a cancel and a taxi left standing never take more than the money you have. # Limits - A taxi comes to a street: call on foot, out of doors, within {taxi_road_within} m of a road that cars use. - No call goes through from inside a vehicle, while a bus, the subway or a taxi takes you somewhere, or while the police, a driving test or prison holds you. - One taxi at a time. If no taxi is free, or yours gets stuck and no other can be sent, nothing is charged. - The contact is added with The mod's phone contacts on. - A taxi on its way is not kept in a save: after loading, call again.

reallife_guide_economy: # Your credit rating - One score from {econ_min} to {econ_max}, shown with a grade. A save with no debts and no record starts at {econ_start}. {econ_bands}- It is worked out from what is on your credit file. Nothing in it is left to chance. - The game's loans, this mod's accounts and the student loan for a degree all count in it. # The threshold - Under {econ_threshold} no bank lends you anything, on every preset. Only the private lender still does. # What moves it - Payment history, {econ_w_payments}: each daily loan payment taken in full counts for you. One that could not be taken counts against you as much as {econ_miss_weight} paid ones. Both count less each day and stop after {econ_fade_days} days, but payments made on time keep a small weight for good. - What you owe, {econ_w_owed}: your loans against what the city's banks would lend on their own terms, and your daily payments against your daily income. - Length of credit history, {econ_w_length}: it counts in full after {econ_history_days} days. - Legal and public record, {econ_w_legal}: a conviction, a civil judgment, a fine or court debt still owed, each day one could not be taken, and recent entries on your police record. - Recent applications, {econ_w_applications}: each loan you take out and each account you open counts against you a little for {econ_application_days} days. # What lenders offer - At {econ_threshold} a bank lends {econ_cap_low} of its usual limit at its usual rate plus {econ_rate_low} points. From {econ_best_from} it lends {econ_cap_high} of its limit at its rate less {econ_rate_high} points. Between the two the terms move in a straight line. A rate is never under {econ_rate_floor}. - Each bank also keeps the game's own means test: no more than your wealth before loans or a share of your income, whichever is more, less what you owe on loans. - The terms are the same at the counter, on a call to the bank and in the Finance app. - With The city's economy on, its central bank rate is added to every rate here. - While the tutorial's first loan or the bankruptcy quest's emergency loan is open, the banks keep their own terms. # Finance - Finance is an app on your phone. With app folders on, it is in the Money folder. - Overview: every debt, your cash, what you owe, your rating, what leaves tomorrow and your net worth, with buttons to The city and Repay in EconoView. - Credit: the score, how each part stands, what would raise it most, and the last {econ_events_shown} entries on your file. - Borrow: each bank's offer today. Pick one, choose an amount from {econ_loan_least} up, read what it costs, and apply. A loan by phone costs an arrangement fee of {econ_fee} of the amount at the largest bank, at least {econ_fee_least}. The other banks take less. A bank in person charges none. - Cash flow: money in and out for yesterday, the last {econ_week} days or the last {econ_month}, with the {econ_top} largest items. - A loan from the phone is an ordinary bank loan. Repay it, or change its daily payment, in EconoView. The Banks app can pay it too. - A number on the app's button means a payment was missed or your grade changed. It goes when you open the app. - You are told when your grade falls, and with A notification when your credit rating rises (on) when it rises too. # More kinds of credit - They are in Finance, under Borrow, below the banks, and on the Apply tab of the Banks app. Under {econ_threshold}, or with Overdraft, cards, mortgage and other credit off, none is opened and nothing can be drawn. What you already owe stays owed. - Rates and limits below are the largest bank's. The other banks differ a little: see the Banks app page. - Overdraft: a limit from {econ_od_low} to {econ_od_high} of what the city's banks would lend you, but no more than {econ_od_income} days of your average income, and never under {econ_od_least}. If your cash is short of what leaves at midnight, it pays the difference. What is drawn costs the bank's rate for your rating plus {econ_od_points} points a year. Cash above {econ_od_float} pays it back each night. It is free to hold. - Credit card: a limit from {econ_card_low} to {econ_card_high}, but no more than {econ_card_income} days of your average income, and never under {econ_card_least}. Drawing cash costs {econ_card_fee}, at least {econ_card_fee_least}. A statement comes every {econ_card_days} days. {econ_card_grace} days later the minimum is taken: {econ_card_min} of the statement, at least {econ_card_min_least}. What you carry over costs the bank's rate plus {econ_card_points} points. A statement paid in full costs no interest. A minimum not paid on its day is taken as soon as the cash is there. It counts as one missed payment for that statement, and what is still unpaid of it is added to the next minimum. Draw cash under Accounts or on the Banks app's Card tab. - Business loan: an ordinary bank loan against one of your businesses that has {econ_biz_days} days of takings on record. Up to {econ_biz_multiple} times its average daily profit, at the bank's rate less {econ_biz_points} point. It does not use up what the bank lends you otherwise. EconoView lists it with your other loans. - Car finance: get approved in Finance, then buy a vehicle the usual way. It finances from {econ_car_least} up to what the bank would lend you otherwise. The approval lasts to the end of the day after ({econ_approval_days} day on). The game asks for the whole price in cash, so the approved amount is paid into your cash first. The lender finances the price less your deposit of {econ_car_dep_low} to {econ_car_dep_high}, over {econ_car_term_low} to {econ_car_term_high} days, at the bank's rate plus {econ_car_points} points. What is not used goes back, and all of it if you buy nothing. Holding the approved money costs interest at that rate: once you buy, only on the part the lender finances, for the days before; if you buy nothing, on all of it. - Mortgage: the same for a building you buy in BizMan, from {econ_home_least}. Deposit {econ_home_dep_low} to {econ_home_dep_high}, {econ_home_term_low} to {econ_home_term_high} days, the bank's rate less {econ_home_points} point, and up to {econ_home_multiple} times what the bank would lend you otherwise. - Consolidate: one new bank loan pays off every loan, your card and your overdraft. The fee is {econ_cons_fee} of what you owe, at least {econ_cons_fee_least}. Finance shows the daily cost, the interest and the days before and after. - Accounts in Finance lists every debt and how it stands. Pay any amount into an account there at any time. Paying early costs nothing. - At midnight the game takes its own loans first. Your other accounts follow. # If you do not pay - Each debt counts the payments missed in a row. A payment made in full puts the count back to nothing. The misses stay on your credit file. {econ_ladder}- The late fee is {econ_late_share} of the payment, at least {econ_late_least}. The penalty rate is {econ_penalty_points} points a year and ends after {econ_penalty_run} payments in a row. - The collections call: pay what is overdue, or spread it over {econ_plan_days} days on top of your payments. One plan per debt. A plan that is broken goes straight to the next step. - A vehicle on finance is taken when you are not in it or near it, and sold for {econ_repo_share} of its price. What is left is still owed, and goes to court if it stands for {econ_unsecured_days} days. A business loan takes {econ_divert} of that business's daily takings until the arrears are paid. A mortgage takes the building's rents. Your home, your businesses and your buildings are not taken. - A court claim is for the balance and the lender's costs: {econ_claim_costs}, at least {econ_claim_costs_least}. It is in your Legal file, where you settle or contest it. - The option How hard not paying hits sets how far this goes, and the presets set the option. With Consequences of not paying off, only your rating suffers. Being refused credit depends on neither. # The private lender - When a bank has refused you, or your rating is under {econ_threshold}, a private lender sends you a text. It becomes a contact on your phone. - It lends {econ_shark_least} to {econ_shark_most}, or up to {econ_shark_days} days of your average income if that is more. Each day adds {econ_shark_rate} of the sum. All of it is due in {econ_shark_due} days. One extension by the same time costs {econ_shark_extend} of what you owe. - What you owe never passes {econ_shark_cap} times the sum. - It is not on your credit file. Paying it does not raise your rating. - If you do not pay: a warning {econ_shark_warn} day late. {econ_shark_assault} days late you are set upon in the street, if you are on foot: you are hurt and lose energy, and the cash on you is taken against the debt. {econ_shark_damage} days late one of your businesses is damaged, a repair bill of {econ_shark_bill_share} of what you owe, from {econ_shark_bill_low} to {econ_shark_bill_high}. Then one or the other again every {econ_shark_repeat} days. On Relaxed there are only warnings. - Nothing happens while you are in custody, in hospital, away on a trip or in the middle of something else. - With The private lender off it lends nothing, and what you owe it stops growing and can still be paid. # Ways out of debt - Debt advice is a free contact, offered when something has been overdue for {econ_advice_days} days or a lender has filed a claim. The ways out are in Finance, under Accounts. - Sell and settle: Finance shows your cash, your investments and what your vehicles and property cost. Selling is up to you. - A debt arrangement: every loan and every unsecured account stands still, with no interest, no fees and no further steps. You pay {econ_arr_share} of your average daily income each day, at least {econ_arr_least}, until it is cleared. Your rating is held at {econ_arr_cap} or under while it runs and for {econ_arr_after} days after. Missing {econ_arr_misses} payments ends it. The private lender is not part of it. You can still pay any of them off sooner, in Finance, the Banks app or EconoView. The arrangement ends as soon as everything in it is paid. - Bankruptcy: every loan, the card, the overdraft, car finance and what you owe the private lender are written off. A vehicle on finance goes back. Cash above {econ_bank_keep} goes to the creditors. A mortgage, fines and court debts stay. Your rating goes to {econ_bank_score}, nobody lends for {econ_bank_days} days, and then it rebuilds from {econ_bank_from} by up to {econ_bank_per_day} points a day. Once in {econ_bank_every} days. - While the tutorial's first loan is open or the game's own bankruptcy quest is running, consolidation, a debt arrangement and this bankruptcy are not offered. # Options - Credit rating and phone loans runs all of this. Off, the banks keep their own terms and there is no Finance app. - Every switch here is on to begin with. How hard not paying hits starts at Standard. # Known limits - Nobody walks up to you for the private lender. You are told what happened. - The mod's own accounts do not exist without the mod. "Prepare this save for removing the mod" pays them from your cash as far as it goes and forgives the rest. The game's loans stay, on their own terms.

reallife_changes_002_0: Money and credit: you have a credit rating from 300 to 850, worked out from how you pay. Under 580 no bank lends. A Finance app on the phone shows your money, your rating and your cash flow, and lets you borrow without going to the bank. There is an overdraft, a credit card, a business loan, car finance and a mortgage, real consequences for not paying, a lender of last resort, and ways out of debt. Getting around: call City Cabs for a taxi to where you are. Every bus stop now stands all the time, and where a street has room a bus pulls into a marked bay so traffic passes it. The bus countdown shows how long the bus will really take. Work: gigs pay about 2.8 times what they did and no two shifts are alike. Cleaning uses the game's own mop and dirt, to 100%. A shift in progress is paid out when a save is loaded. Life: a court's custody is served in the station's cell. Your partner sits down at home, and you can sit on a bench on a walk. More goes on in the street. Family, courts, friends, leisure, the council and the dispatch desk now use the game's own interface. Fixed: hotel reception closed as soon as it opened.

reallife_guide_economy_city_about: A central bank, prices that rise and fall, good and bad times, districts with an income level and wholesale prices that move.
reallife_guide_economy_city: # What it is - The city has an economy of its own. A central bank sets a rate, prices rise or fall, the economy has good and bad times, each district has an income level and wholesale prices move. - It runs while Credit rating and phone loans is on. Switch The city's economy off in the options and every figure is the game's own again. - It is worked out by rule from a number drawn once for your save. - In a Going Public session a guest's city follows the host's economy. - A month is a twelfth of the game's year, {macro_month_least} days at least. # The bank rate - The central bank decides once a month. The paper prints the decision the day before it takes effect. - The evening before a decision takes effect, from {macro_eve_hour}, a notification says what the market expects. It is on to begin with. Switch off The rate decision ahead to go without it. - Its rate is counted in points on top of the banks' own rates, from {macro_base_low} points under them to {macro_base_high} points over. One decision moves it by {macro_move_most} point at most. - It raises the rate when prices rise faster than {macro_target} a year and cuts it when they rise more slowly. A slowdown or a recession makes it cut. With nothing pressing it goes back towards the banks' own rates. - Every bank's offer carries the rate, at the counter and in Finance. A loan or a purchase on finance you already have keeps its rate. An overdraft and a card follow the rate from day to day. # Prices - A price index starts at 100. Each month it moves by a twelfth of the year's inflation, which stays between minus {macro_inflation_low} and {macro_inflation_high} a year. - Rents and wages follow the index, and so do the game's own shops and services at prices of its own: tickets and rides, the hospital and the doctor, gyms, shopping, fit-outs, training and hiring. Each night, after the game has taken rent and paid wages, a line adjusts each by how far the index is from 100, booked to the business or home it belongs to, so that it is in that business's statement in EconoView and the game's taxes and its bank count it. Every price of the mod's (fares, fines, fees, pay, family costs, trips) is at the same index. Nothing moves while the index is within {macro_adjust_band}% of 100. - Takings follow the index too, and what customers spend in good and bad times. One line a night adjusts the day's takings. - An adjustment never takes more than the cash you have. What cannot be taken is carried to the next day at no cost. - The lines are in Finance under Cash flow and in EconoView, each under its own name. # Good and bad times - The economy is in a boom, steady, in a slowdown or in a recession. A state lasts {macro_state_least} to {macro_state_most} months. The first {macro_opening} months of the economy in a save are steady. - Against a steady economy, at Standard: {macro_states}- With Business events on, rivals undercut more often in a slowdown or a recession, and business troubles come up more often. In a boom they come up less often. # Districts - Each district has an income level from {macro_income_low} to {macro_income_high}, started from the game's own shares of working, middle and upper class there. It drifts a little each month and never moves more than {macro_income_band} points from where it started. - A business gains or loses a tenth of a per cent of its customers for each point its district is over or under 100. - A district bears prices by its income and by the state of the economy. The measure is the game's own price for a product in that district. Up to {macro_over_band}% over what the district bears costs nothing. Past that a business loses {macro_over_loss}% of its customers for each per cent over, {macro_over_most}% at most. At or under what the district bears it gains {macro_under_gain}%. - District, economy and prices together never change a business's customers by more than {macro_footfall_low}% down or {macro_footfall_high}% up. They are worked out each morning. - A business's interior can let its district bear a little more of its price: see Interiors and decor. # Wholesale prices - Goods are of six kinds: fresh produce and flowers, groceries and drink, clothing and gifts, electronics and appliances, home and office goods, and general goods. Each kind's wholesale and import price moves with the season, the weather, what is on in the city and the price index. - Now and then a kind is short or in glut for {macro_shock_days_low} to {macro_shock_days_high} days, {macro_shocks_most} kinds at most at once. The paper says so the day before. Supply alone never takes a kind's price more than {macro_factor_high}% over or {macro_factor_low}% under the usual. - A raw material that the stock market's exchange prices costs the exchange's price instead: see Futures and options. # Rivals - A business that has made a profit every day for {macro_copycat_days} days may draw a rival who opens nearby and undercuts it. It is the Business desk's own competitor story with the same answers. It needs Business events switched on and comes at most once in {macro_copycat_rest} days. # What you can do - Read The city in Finance, opened from Overview. It lists the rate, prices, each district, each kind of goods, each of your businesses and what your buildings are worth today. - Borrow before a rise and after a cut. Pay down an overdraft or a card when the rate climbs. - Stock up before a shortage and wait out a glut. - Price for the district. The page marks a business whose prices are over what its district bears. # Strength - How far the economy swings follows the presets. Relaxed swings {macro_swing_relaxed} as far as Standard and never has a recession. Realistic swings {macro_swing_realistic} as far and Hardcore {macro_swing_hardcore}.

reallife_guide_ventures: # An offer comes to you - Once every {ven_offer_every} days a tycoon may make an offer for a business that made a profit on {ven_profit_days} of its last {ven_window} days and at least {ven_profit_floor} a day over its last {ven_average_days} days. The chance is {ven_offer_chance}, or {ven_offer_liked} if they like its sector. In a slowdown or a recession it is {ven_offer_slow} of that, in a boom {ven_offer_boom}. - They value the business at {ven_value_days} days of that profit and offer money for a share of each day's profit. The offer waits {ven_lapse_days} days in the Ventures app, in the Business folder. Up to {ven_offers_most} offers wait at once. - You can Accept, Refuse or Counter once: More money ({ven_counter_money} more) or Smaller share (a share {ven_counter_share} smaller). They agree, meet you half way or hold to their terms. # The investors - The city has a few angels, tycoons and venture firms. Each shows their kind, their temperament (patient, even-handed or demanding), the sectors they like, how closely they check figures, the sums they put in and the share they take. - A demanding investor asks for the most growth in the least time, a patient one for the least. - Your name with investors starts at {ven_name_start} of 100. Targets met and buy-outs raise it. Above where it started it adds to a meeting's score. Below, it takes from the score and every investor checks your figures more closely. - Somebody you know may arrange an investor meeting as a favour. One of the investors then sees you that day, whatever a recent approach said. # Going to an investor - In Ventures, press Raise money: pick a business you run, or the kind of business you mean to open and what it will cost, then Choose an investor and Ask for a meeting. Angels back young businesses with small sums. Tycoons and venture firms put in large ones. - The meeting has {ven_questions_least} to {ven_questions_most} questions from a list of {ven_bank}: figures they can check, your plan, and you. Each answer scores up to {ven_points} points. - A true figure always scores at least {ven_truth_base}. A figure made to sound better scores as if it were true, unless it is caught. The chance of that is the investor's care with figures times {ven_catch_little} for a figure a little better and {ven_catch_much} for one much better. - A caught figure ends the meeting. That investor will not see you for {ven_caught_days} days and your name with every investor falls by {ven_caught_name} of 100. - Answers about the plan have no single right list: each investor wants something different. Answers about you are checked against your businesses, your jobs, your credit file and your record. - An angel invests from a score of {ven_need_angel} of 100, a tycoon from {ven_need_tycoon}, a venture firm from {ven_need_firm}, at Standard. A sector they like adds a little to your score. The better the score, the more they pay ({ven_pitch_days_least} to {ven_pitch_days_most} days of profit) and the smaller their share. - For a business not yet open an angel or a venture firm puts in {ven_budget_least} to {ven_budget_most} of its budget, paid when you open one within {ven_pledge_days} days. If you do not, nothing is owed. Up to {ven_pledges_most} such promises wait at once, and Give it up drops one. A tycoon only backs a business that is open. - An angel backs a business under {ven_young_days} days old with their smallest sum even if it shows no profit. - One approach to an investor every {ven_cooldown} days. # What a deal costs you - Each night the investor takes their share of that day's profit of the business. On a day of loss they take nothing. A share your cash could not cover is owed and taken later. - Investors together never take more than {ven_share_cap} of one business's profit. You can hold {ven_deals_most} deals in all, {ven_deals_business} on one business. - They set a target for the recent daily profit. Meet it and they are pleased and may offer a second round, valued at {ven_follow_days} days of profit. Miss it and you are warned. Miss it again and they make a demand, to be answered within {ven_demand_days} days: Give a seat on the board ({ven_board_extra} more of the profit for {ven_board_days} days), or Promise to cut costs: daily costs down by {ven_cut} within {ven_cut_days} days. - After a third miss a demanding investor calls their money back: what they put in less {ven_call_kept} of what you have paid them, {ven_call_least} of what they put in at least, paid by the day. Pay it off clears it at once. After {ven_call_misses} payments missed running the debt goes to court as a civil claim, and your name with every investor falls by {ven_name_claim} of 100. - Other investors lose interest after a third miss: they keep taking their share and set no more targets. One who has not had their money back by then will not back you again, and your name with every investor falls by {ven_cold_name} of 100. - An investor who has had their money back and sees a target met sets no more targets. {ven_levels}- The level also sets how closely every investor checks figures and the score they want: less on Relaxed, more on Realistic and Hardcore. - Buy them out at any time: their share of {ven_buy_out_days} days of recent profit, never less than {ven_buy_out_floor} of what they put in, with any share still owed. - If the business is sold or closed another way, each investor is owed what they put in less what they have been paid, called back by the day. Sold in the Services app, they are bought out from the price instead. - With Investors off, no new offer, meeting or promise comes. Deals, promises and offers you already have carry on. # Shares - Shares of the city's companies are bought and sold in the Stocks app: see the stock market's page. Shares you held in the market that used to be here went over to it as they were. # Property - The game already lets the buildings you own. The Property tab shows what they cost, what they are worth now, how much is let, the rent of the last week and month, the yield and any mortgage. Rents are set in BizMan: Open BizMan takes you there. - To let buildings to tenants yourself, see the Property page.

reallife_guide_economy_company: # What it is - Running a business adds what the game leaves out: staff who know the going rate, insurance, campaigns you can measure, a return to file, an accountant, and licences. - It runs while Credit rating and phone loans is on. Each part has its own switch in the options. Off, a part charges nothing and does nothing. - How strict running a business is sets Relaxed, Standard (the start), Realistic or Hardcore. The presets set it. - Everything is in the Company app on the phone: Overview, Staff, Cover, Marketing and Tax and licences. Rota and Managers have pages of their own. A business's page has Open in BizMan. - The Planner lists what is due, and a business that lost money {co_loss_days} days running. - Every charge is a line of its own in EconoView and in Finance. The game's own wages, tax and marketing are not changed. - Premiums, campaign costs, licence fees and the accountant's fee are given here at a price index of 100 and, with the city's economy on, follow prices. Late penalties and the back-tax that goes to court are at today's prices. Excesses and the most a claim counts are fixed sums. # Staff - The going rate for a job is the game's own wage for that skill, moved by the economy and by the district's income (between {co_market_low}% and {co_market_high}% of it), at today's prices. What staff are paid is counted the same way: the game's wage at today's prices, as the city's cost of living pays it, and any raise you agreed on top. Rising prices make nobody underpaid by themselves. - Only staff at a business that takes money are counted. - Standing is this mod's own figure from 0 to 100. It stands beside the game's satisfaction, which is not changed. It starts at {co_stand_start}. Each day underpaid costs a point. Paid fairly it climbs back to {co_stand_calm}, and a comfortable workplace (Interiors and decor) raises that level. With Standing and reputation on, your name moves a newcomer's start by up to {co_esteem} points either way, and a good name keeps rivals away more. - At Standard, somebody paid {co_raise_gap}% or more under the going rate for {co_raise_days} days asks for a raise. You have {co_answer_days} days to answer on the Staff tab. No answer counts as a refusal. They do not ask again for {co_raise_rest} days. - Agree and they are paid the going rate and gain {co_stand_agree} standing. Offer less and they get half of what they asked and lose {co_stand_less}. Refuse and they get nothing and lose {co_stand_refuse}. Agree to all and Refuse all answer every request at once. - Somebody underpaid can be given Raise to the going rate on their page without asking, at the soonest {co_raise_rest} days after their last answer. - A raise is paid as a line of its own, Wages, agreed raise, for the hours the game counted. The wage in the game's own staff app does not change. - To give several people a raise at once, tick them in the game's MyEmployees app (its filter picks a business) and choose Give a raise among its actions: up to the going rate, a share of their pay or an amount an hour. The question shows their pay in all before and after. Each counts as one raise: standing moves as above and they wait {co_raise_rest} days for the next. Anybody raised in the last {co_raise_rest} days or with a rival's offer to answer is left out. - A rival may make an offer to somebody with a skill of {co_poach_skill} or more who is {co_poach_gap}% or more under the going rate. The offer is the going rate and {co_poach_premium}% more. Match it within {co_poach_answer} days, which adds {co_stand_match} standing, or they leave {co_poach_notice} days later, by the game's own resignation. Nobody has a second offer within {co_poach_rest} days. - Rival tycoons may make offers too, never on Relaxed. A person has one offer at a time: when one of the game's own rivals approaches somebody, an offer from here gives way to theirs. - When {co_strike_share}% of a business's staff ({co_strike_staff_least} or more) stand at {co_strike_standing} or lower they call a strike for the next day. {co_strike_footfall}% of customers stay away while it lasts, and with Business events on the doors are shut for {co_strike_hours} hours each morning. The morning paper reports it. No new strike comes for {co_strike_rest} days afterwards. - End a strike on the Staff tab: Raise for all brings everybody to the going rate and nobody's standing under {co_strike_raise_standing}, Pay once pays {co_strike_pay_hours} hours' pay each and adds {co_strike_pay_standing} standing, and Sit it out waits for its end and leaves nobody under {co_strike_after_standing}. - When trade is brisk (a campaign running or a boom) the staff may offer overtime: {co_ot_hours} extra hours a day each at time and a half for {co_ot_days} days, for {co_ot_footfall}% more customers. Answer within {co_ot_answer} days. Agreeing adds {co_ot_standing} standing. The next offer comes {co_ot_rest} days later at the soonest. None is offered or worked while a strike is called or on. - The game decides who is off sick and pays them nothing. Your Sick pay policy on the Staff tab pays nothing, half a day's pay or all of it (half to begin with), and changes their standing by {co_sick_none}, {co_sick_statutory} or {co_sick_generous} a sick day. - By strictness: {co_levels} # Insurance - A policy covers one business against one thing: a fire's repair bill, the stock and repair of a break-in, or a fine from a health or fire safety inspection. - On the Cover tab pick a row, step through the insurers for a quote and press Take this policy. It starts the next morning. - The loss still happens in full, as before. A notice says when a policy would pay. Press Put the claim in within {co_claim_window} days and the insurer pays it back less the excess. - The premium leaves each night and is fixed for a term of one game year ({co_term_least} days at least), then renews by itself. It is worked out from the kind of cover: {co_covers}- And from the insurer: {co_insurers}- Theft cover is dearer in a poor district. Fire and liability cover are dearer in a rich one. - A claim adds {co_claim_loading}% to the next term's premium. An insurer that declines to renew will not write that cover there again. A term's claims stay with the business when a policy ends, and the next policy there is priced on them. - A policy lapses when its premium cannot be paid {co_premium_missed} days running. A business may stay uninsured. # Marketing {co_campaigns}- Pick a business on the Marketing tab, choose a campaign and press Book it. It is paid at once and runs from the next day, one at a time for each business. - With Flare, social media on, a sponsored post and influencers hired on Flare's Business tab join the list, priced by Flare. None can be booked where the game keeps no customer figure, or at an Empire Motors dealership. - It is stronger where the district suits the business and in a boom, and weaker in a recession. The same kind again within {co_repeat_days} days is weaker. No campaign adds more than {co_campaign_most}%. - The customers come through the same figure the game's own marketing uses, on top of it. Together with the city's economy it stays inside what Business events allows, so a campaign in a boom may add less than its figure. - The morning after it ends you get a report: customers, takings and profit on its days against the same number of days before, the cost, the extra profit and the return. The last {co_reports} reports are kept. - The game's own marketing through an agency is a daily budget with no end and no report. It is unchanged, and the two add up. # Tax - The game's own tax is unchanged: once a year, on what your businesses sold, less deductible expenses, if the year's income passes its threshold. - Premiums, campaigns, agreed raises, sick pay, overtime, licence fees and the accountant's fee are marked deductible when they are paid, so the game's tax deducts them itself. - A quarter is three months. When it closes you have {co_return_days} days to file its return on the Tax and licences tab. It is one button, File the return, once the game's own tax bill is not overdue. The quarter's takings include the gain on a business you sold. - A late return costs {co_penalty_share}% of the quarter's takings, between {co_penalty_least} and {co_penalty_most}, and the same again after each further {co_penalty_repeat} days, {co_penalties_most} times at most. {co_late_audit} late returns running bring a tax audit from Business events. - An accountant, hired on the same tab, files the return on the day the quarter closes: {co_accountants}- About {co_error_chance}% of the cheapest one's returns carry an error that costs half a late penalty. The fee is taken each month, and an accountant who cannot be paid stops working for you. # Cash off the books - For each business you may keep {co_hide_steps}% of takings off the books. The tax that share would bear is paid to you each morning. While the year's income is under the game's tax threshold no tax is due and nothing is paid. - Each per cent hidden adds {co_risk_per} points a day to the chance of an audit, up to {co_risk_most}% a day. With nothing hidden it falls by {co_risk_decay} a day. - An audit takes back everything kept back since the last one, with a fine on top: {co_fines}. It sets every share back to nothing, and what your cash cannot cover is taken each day as far as it goes. From {co_court} of back-tax you are also summoned to court for tax evasion, which the credit rating counts as any conviction. - On Relaxed the most is {co_hide_relaxed}% and it never goes to court. - With cash off the books the dearest accountant resigns, the middle one will not file, and the cheapest charges {co_hide_fee}% more. # Licences {co_licences}- Every business needs signage. Food hygiene is for a business that sells food, alcohol for one that sells drink, and late opening for one open past {co_late_hour}:00 or before {co_early_hour}:00 on any day. - Pick a licence on the Tax and licences tab and press Buy a term, or Add a term to renew early: the new term starts where the old one ends. - A business that already ran when this first appeared in your save holds every licence it needs for a first term, free. A business you open later may trade {co_lic_grace} days before it needs them, and so may a business that comes to need a new one. - A reminder comes {co_lic_remind} days before one runs out. Renew by itself takes the fee the day after it runs out, and tries again each day until it is paid. - While one is missing, an inspection is asked for on about {co_lic_check}% of days. Trading without one costs {co_lic_fine} times its fee when an inspector next calls, and for food hygiene or alcohol the doors are shut for {co_lic_hours} hours. Inspectors come from Business events.
reallife_co_staff_asks: Raises asked for: {count}. Agreeing to all adds {amount} an hour.

reallife_changes_002_1: The city now has an economy of its own. A central bank sets a rate each month, and bank offers, overdrafts and cards follow it. Prices rise or fall, and rents, wages, wholesale prices and takings follow them. There are booms, slowdowns and recessions that change how many customers come and what they spend. Each district has an income level that sets what its customers will pay. Wholesale prices move with the season, the weather and what is on in the city, and the paper announces a shortage or a glut the day before. Finance has a page for all of it, The city. Investors: a tycoon may offer money for a business that does well, and you can pitch to angel investors, tycoons and venture firms yourself. They ask questions, check your figures and take a share of the profit each day. There is a stock market of the city's companies, moved by the day's news. Both are in a new Ventures app, with what your buildings earn. Running a business has an app of its own, Company. Staff have a going rate by job and district: they ask for raises, get offers from rivals and may strike. Each business can be insured against fire, theft and an inspector's fine. Campaigns have a cost, an end and a report of what they brought. A return is filed each quarter, an accountant can file it and find savings, and cash kept off the books saves tax until an audit finds it. Businesses need licences that cost money and run out. The Planner lists what is due.

reallife_perf_textures_whole: Textures kept whole in graphics memory, picture unchanged
reallife_rota_test_open: Open the rota of my busiest business

reallife_guide_economy_rota: # What it is - The Rota tab of the Company app plans the staff of every business you run. It runs while Staff rota planner and Running a business are on. - The customers are the game's own forecast for each hour of the week, with the business's promotion, satisfaction and marketing in it. A campaign, overtime or a strike of this mod counts on the days it runs. - Nothing is written until you press a button. Only your choice between staff first and lean is kept in the save. - A manager given the Weekly rota uses this planner on Sunday evenings. The Managers page says when they write it. # Forecast and opening hours - What a customer brings is taken from the business's books of the last {rota_books_days} days: the takings and the cost of the goods. With fewer than {rota_books_customers} customers on the books it is worked out from what is on sale and its prices, and the page says so. - An hour is worth opening when its customers bring more than the wages of the staff it takes. At a cinema or a theatre the day's licensing fee has to be earned as well. - Opening hours are advised as at most {rota_blocks} blocks a day of at least {rota_block_hours} hours each. - The game sells only at a till with somebody at it. An hour open with nobody there sells nothing, and the game's thieves still come. - While licences are on and the business holds no late opening permit, the hours from {rota_late_hour}:00 on and before {rota_early_hour}:00 are left out of the advice. The page says what the permit would add. - A campaign, a strike or a trouble of business pressure that ends or begins within the week is counted on its own days only. - A headquarters keeps the game's office hours. Where no customers come, the rota covers the hours you keep. A tech firm is one of these: the game sends it no customers, so the rota puts somebody at every workstation for all the hours it opens. A warehouse has no rota: the game gives its drivers their vehicles. # The plans - Each business has a ladder of plans. As it is is the week you have. Best with the people you have is the best of a new rota for your hours, your hours without those nobody can keep, and the hours that pay as far as your people can keep them. It keeps everybody's hours a week, which the week you have may not, so it can be worth less. The page then says so. - Each further plan hires one more person, at the going wage, for the group of stations where that adds most. It is shown only if it adds at least {rota_share_least} per cent and at least {rota_gain_least} a week. The plans stop at the first hire that does not, and never go past {rota_hires_most} hires. - Every plan is valued the same way: what customers served leave, less wages, licensing fees, the game's hourly theft, the risk of a break-in on a night shut, and what unmet demands cost. A station that serves nobody itself, such as a guard's, is paid in every hour the plan opens, and theft counts the guards at work. - An unmet demand takes satisfaction away every hour. At nothing the employee resigns. The planner counts the sales lost while the post stands empty for {rota_replace_days} days, and the worse work on the way. - The hours a week somebody asks for are compulsory at both ends, part-time and full-time alike: in every rota the planner writes they work no fewer than the least and no more than the most. The figures are the game's own for each demand. - Shifts follow the customers. The busiest hours are staffed first, a second till where one cannot serve everybody, and extra hours go to the next busiest. Cleaning is one shift a day around the busy hours. - The more skilled are given their hours first. Somebody the stations have no hours for is named as not needed, and the page suggests a way, such as another of your businesses with hours nobody works. - Where the hours you keep cannot hold everybody's least hours, the plan with the people you have opens the best paying hours beside them until they do, and says which and for whom. Where no hours within the rules can, the person is named with the figures and given no hours rather than too few. - Staff first lets nothing your people ask for give way. Lean lets their other demands of low and medium priority give way to an hour that pays. Left alone, the planner takes whichever comes to more. The choice shows only where it makes a difference, and is kept for each business. - A plan for the people you have can be written with Use this plan. A plan that takes a hire cannot be written until you have hired: its button reads Use these hours once you have hired, and its page says who to look for and what they cost. Hire in the game's MyEmployees app or from a job board in the building. The game charges nothing to take somebody on unless you offer a signing bonus, which the page sets against the gain. - Goods are counted where a Delivery Contract or a Logistics Manager brings them. Customers buy a product only while some is on site. The shelves fill again from storage the moment they run empty, a contract delivers at {rota_delivery_hour}:00 on a Monday, a Logistics Manager tops up at {rota_round_hour}:00 every morning, and a delivery that finds no room goes back. When the wholesaler is short of a product or has it on backorder this week, the plans count the smaller delivery. - From the hour a product runs out, a plan counts no sales of it. The page names the goods that run out, when, and what would keep them on the shelves. An Urgent Order is a delivery once, so the plans count a week without it. Goods nothing brings are taken to be restocked by you, and the page says how long they last. # Staff and stations - A till or a service station serves as many customers an hour as the game gives it. A further one is advised only when the customers it adds pay its wage. - A till serves the same number of customers an hour whatever the skill of whoever stands at it. Skill and satisfaction change how well each customer is served. - Cleaning is counted from the dirt each customer brings and from what a cleaner clears in an hour. The week is run hour by hour, and cleaning hours are put where they bring most: cleanliness is a quarter of the satisfaction that decides how much customers buy. - Where the cleaning service of this mod cleans a business, no cleaning shift is planned there. - People to hire are counted at the hours a week each employee's own demand allows, {rota_week} with none. - Where the customers outnumber what the stations can serve, the page says what one more station would serve. # The rota - Fill the rota writes shifts for the hours the business keeps. Use this plan sets that plan's hours first, after telling you the hours open now and after. The game asks before a rota is written over. - No shift is longer than {rota_shift} hours and nobody works more than {rota_day} hours in a day. Nobody is put at a station they have no skill for. - Demands about hours a week, days a week, free days, times of day, cleaning shifts and stations are kept. If hours stay uncovered, demands of low and medium priority give way where that covers them. Demands of high priority never do. The page lists what could not be met and why. - Delivery drivers are left as they are. So is whoever has a desk at a headquarters: only empty desks are filled, so nobody loses the plan the game ties to a desk. - A business with more than {rota_stations_most} stations or {rota_staff_most} staff is not planned, and nothing of its rota is touched. - Put the old rota back restores the opening hours and every shift as they were. It is there until you close the Company app. - A large business is worked out over a few moments. The page says so while it lasts. If the business changes meanwhile, nothing is written and you press the button again. - The Planner lists a business that is open with nobody at work. - The sums shown are estimates after wages. Rent and other costs are not in them.

reallife_guide_economy_online_about: A business or a warehouse sells what it stocks to the whole city: orders by the hour, picked by your staff, delivered by your vans or a courier, with a rating to keep up.
reallife_guide_economy_online: # What it is - The Web shop app on the phone opens an online shop for any business you run that takes money, and for a warehouse. It runs while the credit rating does and Online shops is on in the options. - Orders come from every district of the city, not from the street outside. The goods are the real stock of the place: every unit sold leaves its storage or its shelves, and you restock as you always do. - You can have {online_shops} online shops, each with up to {online_lines} products. # Setting up - Pick a business in the Shops tab, choose a site, the delivery and the promise, and press Open an online shop. The set-up is paid once and has the first month of hosting in it. Hosting is then taken every month. {online_sites}- If you run a web development agency, your own people build the site: the set-up is {online_agency} cheaper and the shop takes {online_agency_orders} more orders. - Everything the place has in stock goes on the online shop at the shop's own prices. The Catalogue tab takes products off, puts them on and prices them. - If the hosting cannot be paid the site goes offline and takes no orders. It is asked for again each day, or press Pay the hosting on the shop's Settings page. - The Settings page also changes the delivery and the promise, and has Build a better site (you pay the difference in set-up), Advertise online, Rename and Close the online shop. Closing drops the open orders, and the set-up is not paid back. # Orders - How many come follows the game's own demand for your products across all districts, the width of the catalogue, your prices, the promise, the rating, marketing, the economy and the season. Most come in the evening, and more in winter. - A catalogue of one product brings {online_breadth_least} of the orders that {online_breadth_lines} products or more bring. - A price under the going price sells more and one over it sells less, by the square of the going price over yours. Under it by {online_price_floor} or more it sells no more. At {online_price_ceiling} over the going price nobody orders. A product's page says what share it sells at its price. - A same-day promise brings {online_same_day} more orders. An order before {online_cutoff}:00 is then due {online_same_hours} hours later, never after {online_same_latest}:00, and a later one by {online_next_morning}:00 the next day. A next-day promise is due by {online_next_hour}:00 the next day. - Each further online shop of yours shares the city's orders with the others: with two, each takes {online_crowd_two} of what it would alone. - The building's internet connection sets the most orders a day, as a share of what the site could take: {net_speed_shop}. With no connection, or during an outage, no orders come; a shop you had when speed first counted in your save was given {net_grace_days} days. The shop's page shows the connection, the orders a day it allows and the plan that would allow more. With Internet speed matters or the utilities off, the connection does not count. - A site holds {online_open_most} open orders at most. Past that, new ones are turned away. - An order is one to three products for one district. # Picking - Orders are picked by staff with the customer service skill during their shifts, {online_pick} orders an hour each. At a warehouse the delivery drivers pick, between {online_warehouse_from}:00 and {online_warehouse_until}:00. - What is not in stock is left out of the order. An order with nothing in stock is cancelled. - With nobody on shift orders wait. A customer gives up {online_wait} hours after the promise. The Planner says so after {online_idle} opening hours of orders waiting, with a notification that A notification for orders nobody can pick switches off; orders that come after closing wait for the opening, with no notice. # Delivery - Your own vans: every van at one of your warehouses with a driver takes rounds between {online_drive_from}:00 and {online_drive_until}:00, one district at a time, as many parcels as it holds. A driver works {online_driver_hours} hours a day, as the game pays them. A round costs {online_van_km} a kilometre. - A courier: collects within the hour and delivers {online_courier_hours} hours later or more by distance, for {online_courier_base} a parcel and {online_courier_km} a kilometre. - A late order has {online_late_refund} of its value refunded. An order packed for a van that none took is refunded in full {online_missing_hours} hours after its promise, and its goods go back to stock. # Rating and returns - A new shop starts at {online_stars_start} stars. Every order moves the rating: up for on time and complete, down for short, late, cancelled or lost. Dear prices pull it down and cheap ones lift it. One order moves it {online_rating_move} of a star at most. - At one star a shop takes {online_stars_low} of its orders, at five stars {online_stars_high}. The Planner says so when the rating falls {online_falling} of a star in a week, or is under {online_poor} stars. - Some delivered orders come back after {online_return_days} days and are refunded. How many depends on the goods: {online_returns} # Money - A day's takings, refunds and delivery costs are booked when the day ends, each as its own entry in EconoView. Costs are tax deductible. Day by day shows the past week a day at a time. - Online sales are added to the business's daily statement, so the game's tax and your quarterly return count them as the business's takings. - Advertising online costs {online_ad_cost} for {online_ad_days} days and adds about {online_ad_percent}% to the orders: more in a boom, less in a slowdown or a recession or soon after the last one, and {online_ad_most}% at most. A campaign you run at the business itself helps by half its effect. # Tests - The options page has test buttons for online shops under Troubleshooting, in Test tools. A test order is picked from your real stock and its money really moves. # Known limits - You cannot deliver the orders yourself. - A van's round starts at the business even when the van belongs to a warehouse elsewhere.

reallife_guide_streets_about: People answer your horn, accidents come from drivers you can watch go wrong, and traffic brakes for people and leaves you room.
reallife_guide_streets: # The horn - Sound the horn while driving and the people within about {horn_reach} m ahead of the car, or close beside it, react. At most {horn_most} do. - Somebody in your way who should not be there breaks into a jog and clears the road, or steps back to the kerb. Some lift a hand in apology. - If your light is red, or they are on a crossing with the light in their favour, they stop, turn to you and glare, then cross at their own pace. Further blasts make it longer, and people on the pavement join in. - People on the pavement may look round. - {horn_warn_blasts} such blasts within {horn_warn_seconds} seconds with a police officer or a parked patrol car within {horn_officer} m earn a warning. After a warning the next one within {horn_warned_minutes} minutes costs {horn_fine}. # Reckless drivers - Now and then an ordinary car near you is driven badly for {reckless_least} to {reckless_most} seconds: a speeder, a driver who runs a red light, one who brakes late, or at night a drunk who wanders in the lane. - Most get away with it. Some have a near miss, with horns and people jumping clear. - If the car meets another, the accident is where it happened. How bad it is follows from the speed they met at: under {crash_minor} km/h a bump, from {crash_severe} km/h a serious crash. - If it runs somebody down, the driver stops and waits for the police, or drives off and is chased. - A patrol car that sees a speeder or a red-light runner pulls the driver over, or chases one who will not stop. - Sometimes a pedestrian steps into the road in front of a car. Usually the driver brakes in time. - If a reckless driver runs into your car, it is their fault and you pay nothing for it. - How often accidents happen (1 to 10) sets how often all of this happens. With Reckless drivers cause the accidents off, accidents are set up out of view as before. # People in the road - With Traffic brakes for people in the road on, a traffic car brakes for anybody in its way, waits while they are there and drives on when they have gone. The cars behind it queue. - A driver sounds the horn at somebody who steps out close, and again every {solid_horn} seconds at somebody who stands in front of the stopped car. People answer it as they answer your horn. - Somebody about to step out in front of a car that could not stop waits at the kerb. - No car is held for long. After {solid_hold} seconds the person is moved on. - A car touches somebody only at walking pace: they shout at it and nobody falls. The one exception is an accident that is due. Then a driver who cannot stop hits them at the speed that is left, and stops or drives off as a reckless driver does. - People do not fade out beside a car that is braking for them. - With the option off, traffic drives through people as it does in the game. # The city's drivers - With 'Traffic brakes in good time and leaves you room' on, a traffic car near you reads the lane ahead and slows in good time for what is there: a car or a queue, a red light, a place where it must give way, a closed lane or a sharp corner. It no longer brakes hard at the last moment. - While you drive, it stays about {drivers_gap} seconds behind your car. Slow down in the lane by the kerb and it keeps at least {drivers_room} m back, so that you have room to park, and waits there while you park or reverse into a space. - Pull out of a space and the next car up the lane that can stop gently stops at least {drivers_letout} m behind you and lets you out. One too close to stop gently goes by first. None waits more than {drivers_hold} seconds. - With the option off, traffic drives as it does in the game. # Known limits - As a guest in a Going Public session all of this stands aside: the traffic is the host's.

reallife_guide_roommates_about: Somebody to share your flat and the rent, found by a notice or among your friends, with the frictions and comforts of living together.
reallife_guide_roommates: # Finding one - You need a home and somewhere for them to sleep: a second bed, or at least a sofa. Somebody on a sofa pays {rm_sofa} of the share they would pay for a bed. With your partner living in, it has to be a second bed. - Ring the Roommate contact on your phone. Put up a notice costs {rm_fee} and stays up for {rm_ad_days} days. Between {rm_least} and {rm_most} people answer by text over the next day or two. - Ring the contact again to read about each of them: their job and hours, the share of the rent they offer (between {rm_share_least} and {rm_share_most}) and the one thing you can tell about them. Offer the room and they move in that day. You can also take the notice down and choose nobody. - Ask a friend offers the room to a friend from your social life who trusts you enough. You know what a friend is like before they move in. # What they are like - Everybody has two or three of these: tidy or messy, quiet or noisy, an early bird or a night owl, generous or tight with money, reliable or late with rent, cooks or raids the fridge, sociable or keeps to themselves. - You learn the rest by living together: one more every {rm_reveal} days, or sooner when it shows. # Living together - Every {rm_rent_days} days they pay their share of the rent and the bills. It appears in your statement as Roommate's share of the rent. If you own your home they are a lodger and pay you the same share of what the home would let for and of its bills. - Somebody who is late with rent sometimes pays nothing on the day, or part of it, and promises the rest. You can wait, ask for it now, let it go, or give notice. - When their hours say they are in and you are at home, they are in the flat. Walk up to them and the game's panel over them offers Talk on {key_interact}. Asleep, or in their room, they are in the flat but you do not see them. - A messy roommate leaves the flat dirtier and a tidy one cleans it. One who cooks leaves a portion in your fridge some evenings: eat it together, or reheat it at a cooker later. One who raids the fridge takes one item at a time, at most {rm_raids} a week, and never when {rm_raid_leaves} or fewer are left. You can ask them to stop. - A noisy night costs you some mood and some sleep. Company at dinner and a meal together lift your mood. - The Planner shows the next rent day, money they owe you and the day they move out. # Getting on - Talking, shared meals, lending them money and letting a late week go bring you closer. Short answers, rows and unpaid rent do the opposite. - At {rm_friend} out of 100 they become one of the people in your social life, if you have not met your neighbour there yet, and may introduce you to somebody. # Ending it - Either of you can give notice. They move out {rm_notice_days} days later, pay for the days since the last rent day, and their share stops. Nobody leaves of their own accord in the first {rm_stay} days unless things are very bad. - When your partner moves in, a roommate with a bed of their own asks whether to stay. One on the sofa moves out. - When you move home they come along if the new home has room and you get on ({rm_good} out of 100 or more). Otherwise it ends. # Known limits - They never lie down: asleep, they are not shown. - Food is only taken from the fridge while you are at home, or from portions you have put by. - Cooking, the fridge, dirt and sleep need Home life and health to be on.
