reallife_roommate_page_no_home: You have no home to share. Rent a flat first.
reallife_roommate_page_empty_none: A roommate needs somewhere to sleep: a second bed, or at least a sofa. With your partner living in, it has to be a second bed. Buy one at a furniture shop and put it in your home.
reallife_roommate_page_empty_bed: Your home has a spare bed. A roommate would pay about {amount} a week towards the rent. Put up a notice, or ask a friend.
reallife_roommate_page_empty_lodger: You own your home and it has a spare bed. A lodger would pay you about {amount} a week. Put up a notice, or ask a friend.
reallife_roommate_page_empty_sofa: You have no spare bed, only a sofa. Somebody would take the sofa for {n}% of the usual share: about {amount} a week. With a second bed they pay the full share.
reallife_roommate_ad_up: The notice is up for {n} days and cost {amount}. People who are interested will text you over the next day or two.
reallife_roommate_no_already: Somebody lives with you already. Give notice first.
reallife_roommate_no_money: You cannot pay for the notice just now.
reallife_roommate_no_still_in: Your roommate has not moved out yet. Ask again when the room is free.
reallife_roommate_friend_none: None of your friends is close enough to ask yet.
reallife_roommate_friend_page: {name} is {other}. What you know of them: {text}. They would pay {amount} a week.
reallife_roommate_friend_yes: {name} says yes and moves in today. Their share is {amount} a week.
reallife_roommate_friend_no: They would rather not, for now.
reallife_roommate_page_ad: Your notice is up until {day}. Answers so far: {n}.
reallife_roommate_page_ad_quiet: Your notice is up until {day}. Nobody has answered yet.
reallife_roommate_applicant: {name}, {age}, is {job}. {hours} Offers {amount} a week, {share}% of the rent. What you can tell so far: {traits}.
reallife_roommate_hours_days: Out at work in the daytime, home in the evenings.
reallife_roommate_hours_early: Starts work early and is home by the afternoon.
reallife_roommate_hours_evenings: Works evenings and comes home late.
reallife_roommate_hours_shifts: Works shifts, early one day and late the next.
reallife_roommate_moved_in: {name} moves in today and pays {amount} a week. The first rent day: {day}.
reallife_roommate_page_living: {name} is {job} and has lived with you for {days} days. {hours} Just now: {where}. Pays {amount} a week, next rent day: {day}. You get on: {level}. What you know of them: {traits}. {status}
reallife_roommate_page_lodger: {name} is {job} and has lodged with you for {days} days. {hours} Just now: {where}. Pays you {amount} a week, next rent day: {day}. You get on: {level}. What you know of them: {traits}. {status}
reallife_roommate_status_notice: {name} is moving out, and will be gone by {day}: {text}.
reallife_roommate_why_partner: they are moving in with somebody
reallife_roommate_why_row: the two of you no longer get on
reallife_roommate_why_no_room: there is no bed for them
reallife_roommate_why_not_close: they did not want to move with you
reallife_roommate_why_together: the two of you are together now
reallife_roommate_phone_off: Roommates are switched off on the mod's options page.
reallife_roommate_notice_ask: Give {name} notice? They move out in {n} days and their share of the rent stops.
reallife_roommate_notice_given: {name} takes it quietly. They will be gone by {day}.
reallife_roommate_notice_back_no: It is too late for that. {name} is leaving.
reallife_roommate_greet_late: {name}: "You are back late. Everything all right?"
reallife_roommate_home_room: {name} is in their room with the door shut.
reallife_roommate_rent_paid: {name} paid their share of the rent: {amount}.
reallife_roommate_loan_back: {name} paid back the {amount} you lent them.
reallife_roommate_noise: {name} had music on and people round until late. You slept badly.
reallife_roommate_company: {name} is in. You eat together and talk about the day.
reallife_roommate_gone: {name} has moved out: {text}. They left you {amount} for the last days and what they owed.
reallife_roommate_food_leftovers: the portion you had put by
reallife_roommate_talk_nothing: Nothing to talk about just now.
reallife_roommate_talk_later: {name}: "We've had our chat for today. I'm about to put the kettle on, if you want one."
reallife_roommate_day_1: Long day. Being {text} sounds easier than it is. How was yours?
reallife_roommate_day_2: Work was quiet for once. I got home, sat down and didn't move for an hour. You?
reallife_roommate_day_3: Somebody at work asked who I live with now. I said somebody decent, so don't make a liar of me. How are things?
reallife_roommate_day_4: I've been meaning to ask how it's going with you. You look tired.
reallife_roommate_day_5: I walked home today. This city is something when you're not in a hurry. Good day?
reallife_roommate_talk_day_warm: You talk for a while. It is good to have somebody to tell.
reallife_roommate_talk_day_short: "Fair enough." {name} goes back to what they were doing.
reallife_roommate_talk_rent: About the rent. I'm {amount} short this week. Can you give me until {day}?
reallife_roommate_talk_rent_again: I know, I said I'd have it. I still owe you {amount}. Give me until {day}, I promise.
reallife_roommate_talk_rent_paid: {name} sighs, finds the money and counts out {amount}.
reallife_roommate_talk_rent_cannot: "I haven't got it. Asking twice won't change that." It is not a comfortable evening.
reallife_roommate_talk_noise: Sorry about last night. A few people came back with me. Were we loud?
reallife_roommate_talk_noise_agreed: "Fair. After eleven it's headphones, I promise."
reallife_roommate_talk_noise_row: It turns into a row. {name} says it will not happen again, and shuts their door.
reallife_roommate_talk_raid: I ate something of yours: {other}. I was starving and the shops were shut. Sorry.
reallife_roommate_talk_raid_fine: "You're a good sort. I'll cook for us one night."
reallife_roommate_talk_raid_replace: {name} puts {amount} on the table for it.
reallife_roommate_talk_raid_grumble: {name} grumbles that it was hardly anything, and pays nothing.
reallife_roommate_talk_borrow: This is awkward. Could you lend me {amount} until {day}? I get paid then.
reallife_roommate_talk_borrow_yes: "You're a lifesaver. You'll have it back, I promise."
reallife_roommate_talk_borrow_short: You have not got {amount} to lend.
reallife_roommate_talk_cooked: I made too much. There's a portion in the fridge with your name on it.
reallife_roommate_talk_cooked_eat: You heat it up and eat at the table together. It is good.
reallife_roommate_talk_cooked_gone: The portion has gone already. You talk while {name} eats.
reallife_roommate_talk_cooked_later: "It keeps. Reheat it at the cooker when you want it."
reallife_roommate_talk_partner: So {other} is moving in. I'm glad for you both. Do you want me to look for somewhere else?
reallife_roommate_talk_partner_stays: "Then I'll stay. I'll keep out of your way."
reallife_roommate_talk_partner_goes: "No hard feelings. I'll be gone by {day}."
reallife_roommate_talk_leaving: I've got news. I'm moving out, and I'll be gone by {day}. It's nothing you did.
reallife_roommate_talk_leaving_luck: "Thanks. You've been good to live with."
reallife_roommate_talk_leaving_stays: {name} thinks about it. "All right. I'll stay."
reallife_roommate_talk_leaving_row: This isn't working, is it? I've found somewhere else. I'll be gone by {day}.
reallife_roommate_reply_sorry: Say sorry, ask them to stay
reallife_roommate_talk_leaving_row_fair: {name} nods. There is not much more to say.
reallife_text_roommate_answer: {name} has answered your notice. {name} is {text}. Ring this contact to read about everyone who answered.
reallife_text_roommate_ad_over: Your notice has come down. Put up a new one when you want to.
reallife_text_roommate_moved_in: {name} has moved in. Their share is {amount} a week and the first rent day is {day}.
reallife_text_roommate_rent_late: {name}: Sorry, I haven't got the rent today. I owe you {amount}. Give me until {day}.
reallife_text_roommate_rent_short: {name}: I've paid what I could. I'm {amount} short. Give me until {day} for the rest.
reallife_text_roommate_rent_slips: {name}: I still haven't got the {amount}. Give me until {day}.
reallife_text_roommate_cooked: {name}: I cooked. There's a portion in the fridge for you.
reallife_text_roommate_borrow: {name}: Are you in later? There's something I want to ask you.
reallife_text_roommate_notice: {name}: I need to tell you something when you're in. I'm moving out, and I'll be gone by {day}.
reallife_text_roommate_notice_row: {name}: I've found somewhere else. I'll be gone by {day}.
reallife_text_roommate_partner_talk: {name}: I hear {other} is moving in. We should talk about what that means for me.
reallife_text_roommate_partner_go: {name}: With the two of you here there's no room for me. I'll be gone by {day}. No hard feelings.
reallife_text_roommate_no_bed: {name}: There's nowhere for me to sleep now. I'll be gone by {day}.
reallife_text_roommate_moved_along: {name}: The new place is good. Thanks for bringing me along.
reallife_text_roommate_introduce: {name}: I know somebody you should meet: {other}. I'll bring them over when you're next out and about.
reallife_roommate_plan_rent_what: Your roommate pays their share for the week.
reallife_roommate_plan_rent_lodger: Your lodger pays the week's rent.
reallife_roommate_plan_owed_what: The day {name} promised the rest of the rent for.
reallife_roommate_plan_owed_missed: You can wait, ask for it now or give notice.
reallife_roommate_plan_loan_what: The day {name} promised your money back for.
reallife_roommate_plan_leaves_missed: Their share of the rent stops. You can put up a notice for somebody new.
reallife_roommate_plan_ad_what: The last day your notice for a roommate is up.

reallife_roommate_test_noise_done: Test: {name} kept you up last night. Talk to them.

reallife_guide_economy_cleaning: # What it is - A crew of cleaners who go round several businesses, in place of a cleaner standing in each shop all day. - It runs while Credit rating and phone loans is on, and has its own switch, Cleaning service (on). Off, there is no round and no contract, and nothing is cleaned or charged by it. - Everything is in the Services app, in the phone's Business folder. The Company app's Overview has a Cleaning service button to it. # The crew - Hire cleaners through the game's recruitment. Assign each to a building of yours and give them cleaning shifts there in BizMan. - Those shifts are their working hours. The game pays them for those hours as it always does. - On the Crew tab, pick a cleaner and press Put on the crew. It takes up to {svc_crew_most} cleaners. Without a building and a cleaning shift there, a cleaner goes on no round. - While a cleaner is at their own building they clean it as the game has it. While they are out, it does not get their work. - A cleaner who is off sick makes no visit that day. # The round - On the Cleaning tab, pick a business and press Add to the round, up to {svc_clients_most}. Take off the round drops it. Each is served when needed, or at up to {svc_visits} hours a day that you set. - When needed means: a visit is due once cleanliness falls under the threshold you choose. It is {svc_threshold} to begin with. - A business on the round needs none of its own cleaning shifts. The page shows how many its own rota has. - The round is planned again every hour for the rest of the day. Of all the visits that are due, the one a cleaner can start soonest is given to that cleaner, then the next, until nothing more fits. A visit a cleaner has already set out for stays as it is. - A cleaner must reach the place, clean for {svc_visit_least} minutes at least and be back at their own building before their shift ends. No visit is longer than {svc_visit_most} minutes. - The plan looks for the earliest start of each visit, not for the shortest way round. - A shop is visited only on a day it is open and not shut for a time, as the game cleans it only then. # What a visit does - For every minute a cleaner is there, the floor is cleaned as a cleaning shift of theirs would clean it: their skill by their satisfaction, divided by the cleaners the floor needs for its size. - It is written to the game's own floor, so customers, satisfaction and BizMan all see it. - If you are in the shop during a visit and it has a free cleaning station, the cleaner is there with a mop. Without a station the visit still cleans, and the page says when the cleaner was in. # Travel - The way between two doors is the straight line and {svc_street}% more for the streets. - On foot the crew makes {svc_walk} m in a game minute, by van {svc_van} m. Take a van and Give up the van switch between the two. A door more than {svc_travel_most} minutes away is on nobody's round. - The van costs {svc_van_cost} a kilometre at a price index of 100. It is charged each morning for the day before. # What the page shows - For each business: the minutes of cleaning a day it needs, what it got today, its cleanliness with the change since the morning, and its next visit. - What a business needs is measured: how much dirtier its worst floor tile gets in a day, averaged over {svc_need_days} days. - For the service: its cost a week, the crew's wages and the van, against one cleaner at each of your shops for the whole hours each needs. # Contracts - With somebody on the crew, other businesses ask for cleaning on the Contracts tab: about one every {svc_offer_every} days, {svc_offers} open at most, each for {svc_offer_open} days. Take the contract or Refuse. Up to {svc_contracts} contracts run at once. - A contract pays a weekly fee, {svc_fee_least} at least, and names a cleanliness to keep. Its visits are set on the Cleaning tab like your own shops'. - The floor is measured each morning. With more than {svc_days_under} mornings of a week under the standard, the week pays nothing and costs {svc_penalty}% of the fee. After {svc_misses} such weeks running the contract ends. - End the contract takes the business off the round that day. The running week is not paid. - A client's floor is kept by this mod, since the game keeps none for a business that is not yours. It gets dirtier each morning, more so where there is room for more customers. A visit cleans it by the same sum as your own shops. # Known limits - At their own building a cleaner is still seen at work while they are out on the round.
reallife_guide_economy_sale: # What it is - A business that takes money can be sold for what it is worth, instead of being shut. - It runs while Credit rating and phone loans is on, and has its own switch, Selling a business (on). Off, nothing is offered, paid or charged by it. - It is on the Sell tab of the Services app, in the Business folder. A business's page in the Company app has a Sell this business button that opens it. # What a business is worth - The start is {sale_days} days of its recent daily profit: the figure investors value a business by. - That is taken by its kind, by its district's income ({sale_district_least}% to {sale_district_most}%) and by the economy ({sale_boom}% in a boom, {sale_slow}% in a slowdown or a recession). - A business with fewer than {sale_history} days of books counts in proportion. One with no books, or with a loss, has no such value. - Its stock and furniture are added at the price the game itself pays when a lease ends. - Investors with a share of the business are bought out at their buy-out price, and business loans secured on it are paid off, out of the price first. The page shows what is left. # The market - Choose an asking price from {sale_asking_least}% to {sale_asking_most}% of the value and press Put on the market. Set this price changes it and Take off the market ends the listing. - Offers come from the next day on. At the value there are {sale_gap_value} days between offers and {sale_offers_value} offers in all. A lower price brings more, sooner. A higher price brings fewer, later, and the highest may bring none. - An offer follows the asking price part of the way and is never above it. It stands for {sale_offer_least} to {sale_offer_most} days. - A listing ends by itself after {sale_listing_days} days. # The buyers - A rival owner offers about {sale_rival}% of the value, pays at once, takes on none of the staff and asks you to stay out of that trade in the district for {sale_rival_clause} days. - An investor offers about {sale_investor}%, pays at once and keeps the staff. - Your staff offer about {sale_staff}%, pay in {sale_staff_parts} weekly parts and keep their jobs. - A chain offers about {sale_chain}%, pays at once or in {sale_chain_parts} parts, takes on none of the staff and asks for {sale_chain_clause} days. - You may Accept, Refuse, or Ask for more once: {sale_counter}% more, never above your asking price. An offer at your asking price cannot be countered. The buyer pays it, meets you half way or refuses. Of the buyers who refuse, {sale_walk}% walk away. - Quick sale pays {sale_quick}% of the value at once. # The sale - The game asks before anything is done. A sale cannot be undone. - You cannot sell while you stand in the building, while a vehicle of yours is kept there, or while a special gift is inside. A car dealership or a car showroom must sell its cars first. - If investors and loans come to more than the day's payment and your cash together, the sale cannot complete. - Staff the buyer keeps are paid for the day and leave your payroll. Staff the buyer does not keep stay with you, unassigned. - The business is shut as the game shuts one, its stock and furniture go with it, the lease ends and your deposit comes back. - Where the game has a business of that kind for a building of that size, one opens there. Otherwise the building is free to rent. A building you own stays yours. - A price in parts comes every {sale_part_days} days. - The price above what the stock and furniture are worth is a gain. With tax on in Running a business, it goes into that quarter's tax return. - If you promised to stay out of the trade and take on a business of that kind in that district in time, you pay {sale_clause_penalty}% of the price, once.
reallife_svc_empty_cleaning: Nothing of the kind chosen. Businesses on the round and your other shops are listed here.
reallife_svc_empty_crew: Nobody of the kind chosen. The cleaners you employ are listed here.
reallife_svc_empty_contracts: Nothing of the kind chosen. Contract offers and the contracts that run are listed here.
reallife_svc_empty_sale: Nothing of the kind chosen. Offers and your businesses are listed here.
reallife_brand_test_make: Make my best shop a brand with high recognition
reallife_brand_test_sign: Sign a franchise in the next district
reallife_brand_test_scandal: A scandal at a member shop
reallife_brand_test_year: A year passes for the brand
reallife_brand_test_done: Brands test done. The Brands app shows it and the log has the details.
reallife_brand_test_no_brand: Brands test: not started. You have no brand yet. Run the test that makes one, or make a brand in the Brands app.
reallife_brand_test_no_business: Brands test: not started. You run no business that takes money.
reallife_brand_test_no_franchise: Brands test: not started. No franchised shop is trading. Run the test that signs one first.
reallife_brand_test_no_site: Brands test: not started. No district has a building to let for this kind of business, and none has a shop of the kind to take on.
reallife_brand_test_nothing_back: Brands test: there are no test changes to put back.
reallife_guide_economy_brands_about: Turn shops of one type into a brand with recognition and standards, franchise it to others for a fee and a royalty, or put a shop of yours under a city chain.
reallife_guide_economy_brands_chain: {name}: {fee} to join and {royalty}% of takings. {percent}% more customers. Standards of {standards} or more, prices from {least}% to {most}% of the market price.
reallife_guide_economy_brands_scandals: {inspection} points for a failed inspection, {strike} for a strike, {fire} for a fire
reallife_guide_economy_brands: # What it is - A brand is a name that several of your shops of one type trade under. It runs while Credit rating and phone loans and Brands and franchises are both on in the options. Off, nothing is paid, no applicant comes and every shop's customers are without it. - Everything is in the Brands app on the phone. The Planner lists an applicant who waits, what a franchisee asks, a renewal, an inspection that is due and a shop in breach of a city chain. - Sums given here are at a price index of 100. With the city's economy on they follow prices. - You can keep {br_brands_most} brands, with {br_members_most} of your shops in them, {br_franchises_most} franchised shops and {br_chain_shops} of your shops under a city chain. # Making a brand - Pick a shop on the Shops tab and press Make it a brand. It takes the shop's name, which Rename changes. Other shops of the same type join with Join the brand. A shop under a brand or a chain cannot join another. - That first shop is the flagship. If it leaves, the oldest member left takes its place. On the brand's Settings page, Share prices and Share hours copy its prices and its opening hours to every other member shop. Prices are only changed for products a shop already sells. Shifts are not changed: fill the rotas afterwards. - Instead of copying once, Keep member shops on the flagship's prices. A change at the flagship is followed within the hour, and a change made at a member shop is put back. With Adjust for each shop's district, each shop may be up to {br_local}% higher or lower, by what its district bears against the flagship's. - Give up the brand ends it: its shops trade on under their own names and its recognition is lost. End its franchise agreements first. # Standards - A shop's standards run from 0 to 100: {br_w_sat}% the game's customer satisfaction, {br_w_clean}% its cleanliness, {br_w_stock}% the share of its main goods on the shelves, {br_w_skill}% its staff's skill. Its interior adds or takes up to {in_brand_most} points. - The brand's standards are {br_mean}% the mean of all its shops, franchised ones included, and {br_worst}% its worst shop. One bad shop drags the brand. - On the Settings page you set the required minimum: {br_minimums}. A new brand starts at {br_offer_standards}. A franchisee found under it can be warned. # Recognition - Each district has a figure from 0 to 100, and there is one for the whole city. - A district's figure grows each day with the shops there ({br_presence_shops} count at most), the customers they serve, the brand's standards and campaigns. Standards over 50 add to it and standards under 50 take away. A gain counts for less the nearer the figure is to 100. - A district with a shop of the brand also gains from its shops in other districts: {br_pull_first} points a day for the first, {br_pull_less} less for each one after, {br_pull_shops} counted at most. - It fades by {br_decay}% of itself a day, and by {br_decay_empty}% where the brand has no shop left. - On the Campaigns page, a campaign in one district adds {br_push_local} points a day there for {br_push_local_days} days, at {br_push_local_cost} for each shop of the brand there. A city-wide one adds {br_push_city} a day in every district with a shop for {br_push_city_days} days, at {br_push_city_cost}. One runs at a time; the franchisees' levy pays first. - Something the city hears about at a member shop costs recognition in its district: {br_scandals}, and {br_scandal_influencer} when an influencer it hired has a scandal. The city-wide figure loses a quarter of that. How far the talk spreads on Flare scales it from {br_scandal_least}% to {br_scandal_most}%; an honest answer there within {flare_draft_days} days wins part back. - In a brand with no shops elsewhere, shops with standards of 75 and 100 customers a day each settle near {br_settle_one} with one shop, {br_settle_two} with two and {br_settle_four} with four. - {br_three_gain} points a day is what three shops with standards of 75 and 100 customers a day gain at first: a new brand of them is near {br_three_after} after {br_three_days} days. - The city-wide figure moves {br_city_step}% of the way each day towards the districts' figures added up and divided by {br_city_districts}, times the districts with a shop, never above their average. A brand in one district stays at {br_city_one} or under city-wide; from three districts on it heads for their average. - Three shops in three districts, each with standards of 75 and 100 customers a day, are near {br_spread_after} in each district after {br_spread_days} days, and near {br_spread_city} city-wide. - A member shop is never counted under {br_floor}% of the city-wide figure in its district, so a known brand helps a shop in a new district from its first day. - The brand's Figures page shows each figure to a tenth and says on how many mornings recognition moved. It stands still while brands are off, and several days passing at once count as one morning. # What a member shop gets - Up to {br_rec_most}% more customers at recognition of 100. With standards under {br_low} the name is worth half. - Of the customers its prices cost it by the city's economy, up to {br_tolerance} points are given back at standards of 100, and nothing at 50 or under. - A brand never adds more than {br_cap}% at a shop. The city's economy, your campaigns and the brand are added up, and the sum is kept to {br_sum_cap}% more customers. - Where the game keeps no customer figure for the building, and at an Empire Motors dealership, the brand brings no customers. The shop's standards still count in the brand's. # Franchising - A brand can be offered once it has {br_offer_shops} member shops with standards of {br_offer_standards} or more, and recognition of {br_offer_city} city-wide, {br_offer_district} in one district, or {br_offer_mean} on average over the districts where it has a member shop (from {br_offer_mean_districts} districts). - Press Offer as a franchise on the Settings page. A brand that falls short later is taken off offer. - Each day a brand on offer has a {br_app_base}% chance of an applicant, and {br_app_per}% more for each point of city-wide recognition. Each waits {br_app_days} days and up to {br_app_most} wait at a time over all brands. You see their capital, their years in the trade, their record and their temperament: careful, ambitious, or one who cuts corners. - Press Offer terms and pick a building to let in the district they want, and the terms: an entry fee of {br_fees}, a royalty of {br_royalties} of takings, a marketing levy of {br_levies}, the district to themselves or not, and {br_lengths} years. - Their capital must cover the entry fee and {br_fitout} for the fit-out. An applicant refuses terms that ask too much for how well the brand is known there; the app shows what the terms weigh and what they bear. A district to themselves makes harder terms acceptable, and no other franchisee can then open there. - The shop opens as a business of the city's where the game has one of the type that fits the building. It keeps the game's own name and sign. The Brands app and the city map show it under your brand. - Where the game has none that fits, the franchisee takes on a shop of the type that already trades in the district. Failing that, the shop is kept in the Brands app's books only, and takes up to {br_cannibal}% of the customers of each member shop within {br_radius} m, {br_cannibal_most}% in all. - Each day you are paid the royalty and the levy, and you pay support of {br_support_base} and {br_support_share}% of takings for each shop. Franchisees expect the levy spent on brand campaigns: past {br_fund_idle} unspent it is a grievance. - A franchised shop's takings follow the franchisee's ability, the brand's recognition there, the district's income, the economy, its own standards and the brand's other shops in the district. - A franchise brings about 15% of what a shop you run yourself does. It takes none of your capital and little of your time. # Keeping a franchisee to the standards - A franchisee's standards count in the brand's from the first day. You only see them when the shop is inspected. - Stand in the shop and press Inspect to do it yourself, free, or Send an inspector for {br_inspector}. The Planner asks for an inspection after {br_inspect_due} days. - A shop found under the minimum in the last {br_fresh} days can be warned with Warn. A warning lifts its standards for {br_warn_days} days. Retrain costs {br_retrain} and lifts them at once. - After {br_cause} warnings, a fresh inspection that still finds it under the minimum is cause to end the agreement at no cost. - Ending an agreement without cause costs compensation, at least {br_comp_share}% of the entry fee, and {br_unfair} points of recognition in the district. # What a franchisee may do - Close, once its debts reach {br_fail_days} ordinary days' takings. That costs {br_failure} points of recognition in the district. While a franchisee is short of cash its standards head {br_trouble_drop} points lower. - Ask for help when short of cash: a grant of {br_help_days} ordinary days' takings, or the royalty and levy waived for {br_waive} days. - Ask to open a second shop, at {br_second_share}% of the entry fee. Agree and they join the applicants. - Ask to renew {br_renewal_notice} days before the agreement runs out, for {br_renewal_share}% of the entry fee. You can answer up to its last day. Decline, or leave it, and the shop leaves the brand that day. - Dispute the terms. With the courts on, the claim is filed there and answered in your Legal file. You can also give way: the royalty goes down a step. Decline, or leave it, and their standards suffer. - Bid for the brand. If you sell, your member shops trade on under their own names and every agreement passes to the buyer. - What is asked waits {br_ask_days} days for an answer. # A franchise of a city chain - A shop of yours that is under no brand can take a franchise of one of three city chains with Take the franchise on its page. The agreement runs a year and renews itself: {br_chains}- The chain's customers come from the first day, for as long as the shop keeps the chain's standards and prices. - Keep the chain's prices on the shop's page keeps its prices for you. Each morning every product is priced inside the chain's range, {br_keep_margin} points in from each end, as high as the district bears, never over what the game's own pricing manager would ask and not under the wholesale price and a tenth where the range allows. A price changed by anything else, a pricing manager or another mod included, is put back within the hour, so kept prices are never in breach. Set the chain's prices puts them once at the middle of the range. - After {br_chain_warn} days outside them the chain writes and its name brings nothing. After {br_chain_fine} days it fines {br_chain_fine_days} ordinary days of royalty, at least {br_chain_fine_least}. After {br_chain_end} it ends the agreement and charges the fee for leaving. - Leaving costs {br_chain_exit} ordinary days of royalty, and never less than half the fee. # Known limits - Royalties are paid to you and not to one of your businesses, so the game's yearly tax on business sales does not count them. - A franchised shop that is a business of the city's can be closed by the city's own market, like any other. The agreement then ends with nobody at fault. - A franchised shop that is a business of the city's stays in the city while the option is off. Nothing is paid then. - A shop whose prices are kept cannot be priced by hand: switch the keeping off first. At most {br_keep_round} shops are put back in one hour.
reallife_brand_headline: Brands: {brands}. Shops under them: {shops}. Waiting for an answer: {waiting}.
reallife_brand_off_body: Brands and franchises is switched off in the options, or the credit rating it depends on is not running.
reallife_brand_row_no_brand: No brand yet. Pick one of your shops on the Shops tab to make one.
reallife_brand_row_no_shop: You run no business that takes money.
reallife_brand_row_no_applicant: Nobody is waiting. Applicants come to a brand that is on offer as a franchise.
reallife_brand_intro_what: A brand is a name that several of your shops of one type trade under. It has recognition in each district, and standards that all its shops share.
reallife_brand_intro_effect: A member shop gets up to {most}% more customers from the name. Everything added to a shop's customers together is kept to {cap}%.
reallife_brand_intro_franchise: A brand that is known and well kept can be offered as a franchise. Others then open shops under it and pay you a fee and a share of their takings.
reallife_brand_intro_start: To start, pick one of your shops on the Shops tab.
reallife_brand_bid: {name} bids {amount} for the brand, until day {day}. Sell, and your member shops trade on under their own names and every agreement passes to the buyer.
reallife_brand_fig_shops: {type}. Shops of yours: {members}. Franchised shops: {franchised}. Founded on day {day}.
reallife_brand_fig_rec: Recognition: {city} city-wide, {best} in its best district, of 100. Shops, customers, good standards and campaigns raise it; it fades {fade} a day, {empty} where the brand has no shop left.
reallife_brand_fig_standards: Standards are {standards} out of 100. The required minimum is {minimum}.
reallife_brand_fig_worst: They are {mean} the mean of all its shops and {worst} its worst shop. The lowest of yours is {business}, at {standards}.
reallife_brand_fig_no_members: None of your shops is a member at present. The standards are those of the franchised shops alone.
reallife_brand_fig_effect: The name brings a member shop up to {most}% more customers at recognition 100, and gives back up to {tolerance} points of the customers its prices cost. A brand adds {cap}% at most.
reallife_brand_fig_effect_low: Standards are under {low}, so the name is worth half of the {most}% it could bring. Nothing of what prices cost is given back.
reallife_brand_fig_money: Franchises: {net} a day after support, on the week's average. Royalties so far {earned}. Levy not yet spent on campaigns {fund}. Franchisees closed {failed}
reallife_brand_set_minimum: The minimum for standards that every shop of the brand is held to. A franchisee found under it can be warned.
reallife_brand_set_offered: The brand is on offer as a franchise. Applicants will come.
reallife_brand_set_can_offer: The brand can be offered as a franchise. Member shops with standards of {standards} or more: {good}.
reallife_brand_set_cannot_offer: Not ready to offer: it needs {shops} member shops with standards of {standards} or more (it has {good}), and recognition of {city} city-wide (it has {has}), or {district} in one district (its best is {best}), or {mean} on average over its districts when it has shops in two or more (its average is {average}).
reallife_brand_set_shared: Shared settings are copied from the flagship, {business}, to every other member shop.
reallife_brand_push_about: A campaign in one district adds {local} points of recognition there each day it runs. A city-wide one adds {city} in every district where the brand has a shop.
reallife_brand_push_fund: Levy collected from franchisees: {fund}. It pays for campaigns first. Past {most} unspent, franchisees take it as a grievance.
reallife_brand_push_quote: Cost: {cost}, of which the levy covers {fund}. It runs for {days} days from tomorrow.
reallife_brand_dist_rec: Recognition here is {points} out of 100. Tomorrow it will be about {next}.
reallife_brand_dist_parts: A day it gains {presence} for the shops here ({shops}, four at most), {footfall} for yesterday's customers ({customers}), {good} for standards of {standards}, {pull} for its shops in other districts ({others}), and {campaign} from a campaign.
reallife_brand_dist_no_shop: The brand has no shop here at present, so nothing is gained and the figure fades by {fade} of itself a day.
reallife_brand_dist_slow: {gain} in all before it slows: a gain counts for less the nearer the figure is to 100. Then {fade} fades.
reallife_brand_dist_floor: A shop here counts {points}: a brand is never counted under half its city-wide figure of {city}.
reallife_brand_dist_worth: To a member shop here the name is worth {percent} customers today. At recognition of 100 it would be {most}%.
reallife_brand_shops_intro: Every shop you run, and every franchised shop. Pick one of yours to make a brand of it, join a brand, or take a city chain's franchise.
reallife_brand_shops_standards: A shop's standards: {satisfaction}% the game's customer satisfaction, {clean}% cleanliness, {stock}% main goods on the shelves, {skill}% staff skill.
reallife_brand_shops_franchised: A franchised shop shows the standards its last inspection found. What they are today, only an inspection shows.
reallife_brand_member_of: A member of {brand} since day {day}, in {district}.
reallife_brand_member_standards: Standards: {standards}. Customer satisfaction {satisfaction}, cleanliness {clean}, main goods on the shelves {stock}%, staff skill {skill}.
reallife_brand_member_weights: They count {satisfaction}%, {clean}%, {stock}% and {skill}%, in that order.
reallife_brand_member_no_figure: The game keeps no customer figure for this kind of building, so the brand cannot bring it customers. Its standards still count in the brand's.
reallife_brand_member_name: The name brings {percent} customers: recognition counts {points} here, and {most}% is given at 100.
reallife_brand_member_prices: Its prices cost it {loss} customers by the city's economy. The brand gives {back} of that back, {most} points at most at these standards.
reallife_brand_member_prices_none: Its prices cost it no customers, so there is nothing to give back. At these standards up to {most} points would be.
reallife_brand_member_all: In all the brand asks for {percent} customers here. With the city's economy and your campaigns the sum is kept to +{cap}%.
reallife_brand_chain_of: Under {chain} since day {day}. The name brings {percent} customers and takes {royalty} of the takings each day.
reallife_brand_chain_standards: Standards: {standards}. The chain asks for {minimum} or more.
reallife_brand_chain_prices: Prices stand at {prices} of the market price. The chain asks for {least} to {most}.
reallife_brand_chain_no_prices: The shop has no priced goods to judge by.
reallife_brand_chain_breach: Days running outside what the chain asks: {days}. Day {warn}: it writes and the name stops bringing customers. Day {fine}: a fine of {amount}. Day {end}: it ends the agreement and charges the fee for leaving.
reallife_brand_chain_good: In good standing with the chain.
reallife_brand_chain_money: An ordinary day's royalty is {average}. Paid so far: {paid}. Leaving would cost {exit}.
reallife_brand_plain: {type} in {district}. It trades under no brand.
reallife_brand_plain_join: A brand of yours covers this type of business:
reallife_brand_plain_chain: Or take a franchise of a city chain:
reallife_brand_plain_chain_quote: {fee} to join, {royalty} of takings a day, {percent} customers from the first day. Keep standards of {standards} or more and prices from {least} to {most} of the market price. Leaving costs a fee.
reallife_brand_app_intro: Applicants come to a brand that is on offer. Each waits {days} days. Up to {most} wait at a time.
reallife_brand_app_chance: The chance of one a day is {base}%, and {per}% more for each point of city-wide recognition.
reallife_brand_app_tempers: Look at their capital, record and temperament before you sign. A franchisee who loses money closes, and that costs the brand recognition.
reallife_brand_app_wants: Wants to open a shop under {brand} in {district}. Waits until day {day}.
reallife_brand_app_second: Your franchisee asks to open a second shop under {brand} in {district}. The entry fee is half. Waits until day {day}.
reallife_brand_app_capital: Capital: {capital}. Opening costs them the entry fee and {fitout} for the fit-out. What is left is their cash.
reallife_brand_app_record: Years in the trade: {years}. Shops run before: {run}. Of those, closed: {closed}.
reallife_brand_app_record_none: Years in the trade: {years}. No shop of their own before.
reallife_brand_app_temper_about_0: Keeps standards high, grows slowly and does not dispute.

reallife_estate_enabled: Property to buy, let and sell
reallife_guide_economy_estate_about: Buy run-down buildings, let them to tenants, improve them and sell them on. Run an estate agency, own a hotel, and hire out your cars.
reallife_guide_economy_estate: # What it is - Property is three businesses in one app, Property, in the Business folder of the phone. Each has its own switch under Your businesses in the options (Property to buy, let and sell, Owning a hotel and Car hire business), and all three run while Credit rating and phone loans is on. - The game already lets you buy a building and takes rent for it. This adds a market that moves, tenants you choose, repairs and works, a sale with offers, an estate agency, a hotel and car hire. - Nothing new is built and no building changes its look: this is rules and money over the city as it stands. # The market - A building's price is the game's own value of it, by the property market, prices, its district's income and its condition. The game's own screens show the same price. - About {est_run_down} of the city's buildings are run down. They cost less, let for less and cost money to put right. - The property market moves once a month of the city's economy, by {est_step} at most. A boom takes it towards {est_boom} of its usual level and a recession towards {est_recession}. A high bank rate holds it down. - Rents follow prices, not the property market. A building bought in a boom earns less on its price. - The Market tab lists what is for sale. Its Make an offer button opens the game's own purchase screen. For a mortgage, arrange it in Finance first. # Letting - A building you own is let by the game, as before, until you press Let it yourself on the Mine tab. Each of its units then has a tenant of its own on a lease of its own. Hand back to the game gives it back while no unit is let and no works are under way. - The game counts a building's units: its floor over the size of its street unit, {est_units} at most. The Tenants tab shows how they stand and opens each one's lease. - The market's rent is between {est_yield_low} and {est_yield_high} of the game's value a year, by use and district: dear districts yield less. A unit's share is the building's rent over its units. You set its Asking rent between {est_ask_low} and {est_ask_high} of it, unit by unit, and switch Look for a tenant on or off. - The Rental income option, now {est_rent_scale}, sets the market's rent at a share of the above, from {est_rent_least} to {est_rent_most}. What you ask and what applicants offer move with it, and so does whether a tenant renews, and applicants come as often as before, so a higher setting does not empty your buildings. A lease keeps the rent it was agreed at. A building the game lets for you is paid the game's own rent at the same setting: the difference comes as a second rent line each night, or is taken back under 100%. The yields and returns on this page are at 100%. - Up to {est_applicants} applicants wait for a unit, for {est_applicant_days} days each, and a building takes one more for each unit after the first, {est_applicants_building} at most. Each offers a rent and has a record of paying. A poorer record offers more, misses more days and wears the place faster. - A lease runs {est_lease_least} to {est_lease_most} days. At its end the tenant renews or leaves. One in a building in poor condition, or paying well over the market's rent, is likelier to leave. - The building's condition, refurbishment, cover and works count for every unit. A refurbishment or a change of use needs every unit empty. - The game pays each unit's agreed rent every night. On a day a tenant misses, nothing comes in from that unit. A deposit of {est_deposit_days} days' rent is held against what is owed. - With {est_arrears_days} days owed at a unit, or once its lease has run out, you can Serve notice: {est_notice_days} days, more under rent controls. If the tenant stays, Apply to the court: it gives possession {est_court_days} days after you apply, for {est_court_fee}. A tenant with a poor record who is put out can damage the place. - In a steady economy a let shop building returns about {est_return_let} a year after empty days, arrears, cover and wear: about {est_return_let_poor} in the poorest district and {est_return_let_rich} in the richest. A shop of your own is taken to return about {est_return_shop}. # Condition and works - Condition falls a little every day. Under {est_poor} far fewer applicants come, and under {est_unfit} a building cannot be let. - Repairs, a refurbishment and a change of use are on the Works tab. A repair from nothing to new costs {est_repair} of the game's value. Landlord's cover, switched on a building's page, costs {est_cover} of it a year and pays for a fire or a flood, less {est_cover_excess} of the bill. - A refurbishment has {est_levels} levels. All three add {est_level_value} to the value and {est_level_rent} to the rent. In a boom the value added is more than the cost, in a slump less. - A change of use needs the council first: Apply for permission takes {est_planning_days} days and a fee, with about a {est_planning_chance} chance of permission, more when the council has eased permits. Then Convert. The game's own building type stays as it is. # Selling - Choose an asking price as a share of a building's worth on the Mine tab and press Put up for sale. Offers come by price and by the economy and stand for {est_offer_days} days. - An accepted sale completes {est_completion_days} days later, unless the buyer's own sale fails. The selling fee is {est_agent_fee} of the price, and a gain is taxed at {est_gains} of the game's tax rate. # The agency - Open it on the Agency tab at an office you hold. Staff on that office's rota with the customer service skill are its negotiators. - Owners ask it to sell or let, by district and by its reputation there. You have {est_answer_days} days to take an instruction on, and it holds {est_instructions} at a time. - Taking one on costs its marketing at once. It then needs hours of a negotiator's time, and a deal within {est_lapse_days} days. - A completed sale pays {est_commission_sale} of the price and a letting {est_commission_let} of the first year's rent. A completion raises the reputation in that district. A lost instruction lowers it. # A hotel - The city's hotels are on the Market tab. A hotel costs {est_hotel_years} years of its takings at {est_hotel_occupancy} of rooms sold. Or lease it for a deposit of {est_lease_days} days' lease and a lease every day. Its rates, staff, campaigns and groups are on the Hotel tab. - Set each room type's rate between {est_rate_low} and {est_rate_high} of the going rate. A dearer room sells less. - Rooms sold follow the season, the weekend, events in the city, the economy, the district, your rate, your rating and a campaign of {est_campaign_days} days. - Staff come on a contract at three levels. A better one costs more and keeps the place cleaner. The rating is made of cleanliness, staff and price. - An inspector calls every {est_inspection} days and fines a hotel under {est_inspection_pass} clean. A pipe can burst. A group can ask for rooms at {est_group_discount} off. - At a hotel you hold, your own room is free, and the reception has The books. - End the lease gives a leased hotel back with its deposit. Sell the hotel sells one you bought for {est_hotel_sell} of its price now. # Car hire - Open a lot on the Car hire tab at a building you hold. It has the building's own vehicle spaces, or {est_hire_spaces} at the kerb, and {est_hire_cars} at most. - Park a car of yours within {est_hire_metres} m of the lot's door, legally and empty, then pick it in the list and press Put on hire. It goes out only while it stands there, and never while you stand by it. A showroom's stock car cannot go on hire. - Set each car's rate between {est_rate_low} and {est_rate_high} of the going rate for its class. The customers' opinion of the business counts too: a car in good order adds to it, and worn tyres or brakes, or a breakdown, take more away. - A hire lasts up to {est_hire_days} days. The customer pays a deposit of {est_hire_deposit} days' hire, which goes back with the car. A hired car is gone from the city until then. - It comes back to the same spot with the distance on its record, less fuel, and worn tyres and brakes. It is cleaned that day and goes out again the next. About {est_hire_damage} of hires end with damage and {est_hire_late} a day late. About {est_hire_stolen} of cars do not come back at all. - Fleet cover costs {est_hire_cover} of a car's list price a year and pays {est_hire_pays} of what the deposit does not meet. A hire car returns about {est_return_hire} of its list price a year. # Tax - The agency's commissions are its office's takings, so the game's tax counts them with your businesses' sales. - Your hotels and car hire are taxed by themselves when the game's tax year turns: the game's own rate on the year's takings less their running costs, nothing on a loss, and nothing while your businesses' takings in all are under the game's threshold of {est_tax_threshold}. Their running costs are counted there, not among the game's deductions. # Known limits - No new building, hotel room or showroom can be made. A hotel's rooms are counted, not furnished. - A hotel is held in this mod's books. The game cannot put your employees in a hotel building, so its staff are a contract. - A tenant, a guest and a hirer are not seen in the city. Whoever the game shows in a building's unit stays there. - A building's units are all of one size, its floor shared out. Taking a unit for yourself in the game's own app ends every lease there, and the game lets the rest. - The business looks after up to {est_holdings} of your buildings. A building past that is the game's alone.

reallife_changes_002_2: The Company app has a Rota tab. It shows the game's customer forecast for each hour, the opening hours that pay for their staff, and how many people a business needs. One button fills the week's rota by each employee's skills and demands, and another puts the old rota back. A business or a warehouse can now sell online: the new Web shop app opens an online shop, orders come in from the whole city by the hour, and your staff pick them from the real stock. Orders go out with your own vans or a courier. Late and missing deliveries cost refunds and a star rating, and some orders come back. The day's online takings, refunds and delivery costs are booked each night and count as the business's takings for tax. Cleaners can be shared. Put them on a crew in the new Services app and they go round the businesses on its list, when a floor needs it or at hours you set, on foot or by van. Other businesses in the city offer cleaning contracts with a weekly fee and a standard to keep. A business can be sold. The Services app shows what it is worth line by line. Put it on the market and a rival owner, an investor, your staff or a chain make offers with their own terms, or take a quick sale at a discount. Shops of one type can now trade as a brand, with recognition in each district and standards all its shops share: a known, well-kept brand brings its shops up to 12% more customers. A brand can be franchised: applicants open shops under it, pay an entry fee and a share of their takings every day, and need inspecting, warning and sometimes help. One of your own shops can instead take a franchise of a city chain. Hair keeps its own colour against a lamp. With a car's lights behind or beside your head, dark hair stays dark; before, it could glow as bright as skin and look bald. The Tests section has three entries for hair: one says what your hair is made of, one stands a strong lamp beyond your head for 20 seconds, one switches the hair finish off and on. Traffic now sees people in the road: cars brake for anyone in their way, sound the horn at somebody who steps out close or dawdles, wait, and drive on. People no longer fade out beside a braking car. A driver who cannot stop when an accident is due really hits the person, at the speed that is left, and stops or drives off. Cars that collide on the road slide to rest before the scene is set up, a car that loses a bend ends against what stands there, and a reckless driver who calms down drives on without pulling up. Property is a new app on the phone. Buy run-down buildings at prices that move with the economy, let them to tenants you choose, repair and refurbish them, and sell them for offers; or run an estate agency from an office with your own staff. You can also buy or lease one of the city's hotels and set its rates and staff, and put your own cars out on hire from a lot. The rota planner now shows a ladder of plans for each business: the week as it is, the best week your people can keep, and one plan for each further person worth hiring, with what each adds. Plans count what the game counts: nothing sells at an unstaffed till, a till serves a fixed number an hour, cleanliness, theft, and what an unmet demand costs. You can choose staff first or lean for each business; the choice is saved. Every hour a plan opens or closes is listed with its reason. A plan that needs a hire cannot be written until you have hired. A business cleaned by the cleaning service gets no cleaning shift. The options page is in ten groups, from "Start here" to "Troubleshooting". A group opens to short sections, one at a time, and each button says how many of its switches are on. Every option has a short name and one sentence, shown when the pointer rests on its row. A greyed row says which option it needs. Test tools are under Troubleshooting and only on the page while "Show test tools" is on. Fixed: the game froze for seconds when an ambulance crew stepped out. Fixed: a car in the custom shop shot backwards when the shop closed. reallife_opt_ask_preset:
{about}

This changes {count} of your options, {switches} of them switches. Camera, picture, clothes, keys and performance stay as they are. Your choices are saved to a file first, so 'Load my choices from the file' brings them back.
reallife_opt_test_layout: Write the options page's layout to Player.log
reallife_opt_test_layout_done: The layout of the options page is in Player.log.
reallife_opt_tip_camera_enabled: The camera follows behind your character. Off, the game's own camera is used.
reallife_opt_tip_camera_mouselook: Move the mouse to look around. The 'Free the cursor' key under Controls gives the pointer back.
reallife_opt_tip_camera_sensitivity: How far the view turns for the same movement of the mouse.
reallife_opt_tip_enter_with_key: The interact keys take you into buildings and into your vehicles without a click.
reallife_opt_tip_camera_indoors: The third-person camera is used inside buildings as well.
reallife_opt_tip_camera_pitch: How steeply the camera looks down. With mouse look on, this is the tilt it starts at.
reallife_opt_tip_camera_distance: How far behind your character the camera stands.
reallife_opt_tip_camera_fov: How wide the view is. A higher number shows more and makes things smaller.
reallife_opt_tip_camera_height: The height on your character that the camera looks at.
reallife_opt_tip_car_camera: A camera that follows behind your car. Hold the look-behind key to look back.
reallife_opt_tip_car_camera_distance: How far behind your car the chase camera stands.
reallife_opt_tip_car_tuning: Every car accelerates and tops out like its kind. Off, the game's own cars.
reallife_opt_tip_car_top_speed: The top speed of every car, as a share of what its kind really reaches.
reallife_opt_tip_car_acceleration: How quickly every car gains speed, as a share of what its kind really does.
reallife_opt_tip_smooth_throttle: The key eases the pedal down, so a tap pulls away gently.
reallife_opt_tip_speedometer: Your speed is shown on screen while you drive.
reallife_opt_tip_camera_follow: With mouse look off, how quickly the camera comes round behind you.
reallife_opt_tip_map_places_shown: Bus stops, hotels, the courthouse, driving schools, custom shops and the mod's other places are marked on the city map, each with its own filter.
reallife_opt_tip_visuals_enabled: The colour, contrast, bloom and detail settings below are applied. Off, the picture is the game's own.
reallife_opt_tip_visuals_contrast: How far light and dark are apart.
reallife_opt_tip_visuals_bloom: The glow round bright lights. At 0 it is the game's own.
reallife_opt_tip_visuals_detail: How far away the game still draws things in full detail.
reallife_opt_tip_character_high_detail: Your character uses the game's detailed model in the city. This changes the picture.
reallife_opt_tip_character_hair: Hair and beards on detailed characters are thicker. This changes the picture.
reallife_opt_tip_character_lighting: Faces are lit more softly in character creation and in shop previews.
reallife_opt_tip_character_skin: A fine grain and a calmer shine on your character's skin when the camera is close.
reallife_opt_tip_character_new_looks: The mod's clothes and shoes can be worn, and hair no longer looks thin from a distance.
reallife_opt_tip_look2_top_m: The top a male character wears.
reallife_opt_tip_look2_top_m_colour: Its colour. A print the top cannot carry shows as a plain colour.
reallife_opt_tip_look2_legs_m: The trousers a male character wears.
reallife_opt_tip_look2_legs_m_colour: Their colour. A print the trousers cannot carry shows as a plain colour.
reallife_opt_tip_look_feet_m: The shoes a male character wears.
reallife_opt_tip_look2_dress_f: A dress for a female character. It replaces the top and the trousers.
reallife_opt_tip_look2_dress_f_colour: Its colour. A print the dress cannot carry shows as a plain colour.
reallife_opt_tip_look2_top_f: The top a female character wears.
reallife_opt_tip_look2_top_f_colour: Its colour. A print the top cannot carry shows as a plain colour.
reallife_opt_tip_look2_legs_f: The trousers or skirt a female character wears.
reallife_opt_tip_look2_legs_f_colour: Their colour. A print the garment cannot carry shows as a plain colour.
reallife_opt_tip_look_feet_f: The shoes a female character wears.
reallife_opt_tip_life_events: Now and then something happens to you: a windfall, a cold, a call from Mom.
reallife_opt_tip_life_frequency: About how many life events come in a week.
reallife_opt_tip_crash_consequences: Crashing your car costs damages and can hurt you.
reallife_opt_tip_traffic_accidents: Other cars crash now and then, and police and ambulances come.
reallife_opt_tip_accident_frequency: 1 is rare, 10 is often. At 2, the default, about one accident near you every 32 game hours in the street, fewer at night, more in bad weather.
reallife_opt_tip_police: Patrol cars come to accidents and crimes, officers walk the streets, and drivers are pulled over.
reallife_opt_tip_police_presence: How many parked patrol cars and officers you see about. 0 is none.
reallife_opt_tip_police_pursuit: If you hit a car or a person and drive off, the police come after you.
reallife_opt_tip_siren: Police cars, ambulances and fire engines sound their sirens on the way.
reallife_opt_tip_people: Drivers get out after a crash, paramedics work, and officers stand at scenes.
reallife_opt_tip_patrol_officers: Police officers on foot pass near you from time to time.
reallife_opt_tip_ragdolls: A person your car hits is thrown down and can be hurt or killed. Off, cars pass through people.
reallife_opt_tip_player_knockdown: A car that hits you on foot throws you down.
reallife_opt_tip_ped_incidents: Now and then a pedestrian near you is hit by a car, and help comes.
reallife_opt_tip_horn_reactions: People in your way hurry or stop and glare when you sound the horn, and others look round.
reallife_opt_tip_natural_accidents: Accidents come from speeders, red-light runners and drunk drivers you can watch go wrong. Off, they are set up out of view.
reallife_opt_tip_solid_streets: Cars brake for people in the road, sound the horn and wait. Off, cars drive through people.
reallife_opt_tip_phone_contacts: The phone gets the mod's contacts: 911, the doctor, a friend, Mom and the rest. This applies the next time a save is loaded.
reallife_opt_tip_phone_skin: The phone gets a modern body, wallpaper and status bar.
reallife_opt_tip_street_crime: Street crime, thieves in shops and drivers pulled over happen near you.
reallife_opt_tip_crime_against_player: Pickpockets, muggers, break-ins and scam calls can target you. What they take is limited.
reallife_opt_tip_player_offences: Red lights, speeding and reckless driving get you stopped, and jaywalking gets a warning or a fine.
reallife_opt_tip_city_life: People work and go about their day on the pavements. There are never more than 8 at once.
reallife_opt_tip_city_density: 1 is now and then, 10 is always something.
reallife_opt_tip_city_workers: Sweepers, road crews, window cleaners, couriers, painters and gardeners are at work.
reallife_opt_tip_city_everyday: Friends talk, people smoke, phone, jog, queue and put up umbrellas in the rain.
reallife_opt_tip_city_interactions: You can buy a coffee at the coffee cart with the interact key.
reallife_opt_tip_jobs: You can take jobs yourself by calling the Gig Line on your phone.
reallife_opt_tip_job_pay: What the jobs pay, as a share of normal.
reallife_opt_tip_careers: The help-wanted boards lead to employers with a rota, reviews and promotions.
reallife_opt_tip_business_pressure: Things happen to your businesses, good and bad. They are listed on the Business desk contact.
reallife_opt_tip_business_frequency: 1 is about one day in twelve, 10 is about one day in three. Never more than two are open at once.
reallife_opt_tip_business_easy: Only bulk orders, press coverage, praise and awards come up.
reallife_opt_tip_business_rivals: A competitor undercuts you, makes an offer to one of your staff or smears you in the paper.
reallife_opt_tip_business_racket: Someone demands protection money. You can pay, refuse, go to the police or rely on your security.
reallife_opt_tip_business_inspections: Health, fire safety and licence inspectors call.
reallife_opt_tip_business_staff: A strike threat over low wages, a theft caught on camera or an argument to settle.
reallife_opt_tip_business_suppliers: A delivery comes late or a supplier adds a surcharge.
reallife_opt_tip_business_customers: A complaint or a word of praise spreads.
reallife_opt_tip_business_audit: The tax office audits a business of yours now and then.
reallife_opt_tip_business_opportunities: A bulk order, a piece in the paper or an award comes your way.
reallife_opt_tip_home_life: Needs, routines at home, sleep, illness and fitness. Off, none of it runs.
reallife_opt_tip_home_needs: Hygiene, stress and the state of your home wear down and have to be looked after.
reallife_opt_tip_home_strip: Three more bars appear under the game's own, at home or when a need runs low.
reallife_opt_tip_home_easy: Needs wear down half as fast and illness is half as likely.
reallife_opt_tip_home_routines: At home you can cook, make coffee, tidy up and exercise on the floor.
reallife_opt_tip_home_sleep: How well you slept counts, and sleep you miss has to be caught up.
reallife_opt_tip_home_morning: After a night's sleep a short summary says how you are.
reallife_opt_tip_home_illness: You can catch a cold or the flu, get food poisoning, back pain or burnout, and see the doctor at the hospital.
reallife_opt_tip_home_fitness: Exercise and what you eat make you fitter or less fit.
reallife_opt_tip_home_body: Your character's build changes slowly with exercise and food, when you wake up.
reallife_opt_tip_home_jog: You can go for a run from home.
reallife_opt_tip_law_precincts: Each district has a police station with its sign, patrol cars and officers at the door.
reallife_opt_tip_law_custody: After an arrest you sit in a holding cell at the nearest police station. Off, time passes where you were caught.
reallife_opt_tip_law_arrests: A death on the road, repeated 911 calls about nothing, or being wanted after getting away end in an arrest.
reallife_opt_tip_law_reputation: A long record brings more police attention, and a good name brings thanks from passers-by.
reallife_opt_tip_law_station: You can go in to the front desk, the waiting area and the holding cell. Off, the front desk answers at the door.
reallife_opt_tip_law_map_markers: Police stations have markers, names and their own filter on the city map.
reallife_opt_tip_transit_buses: Buses run between bus stops, and you can ride for a flat fare.
reallife_opt_tip_transit_people: People wait at bus stops and get on and off.
reallife_opt_tip_transit_subway: A ride on the game's subway takes the time of a real journey: the wait for a train, the stops and any delays.
reallife_opt_tip_transit_taxi_call: You can call a taxi to where you stand from the phone.
reallife_opt_tip_car_ownership: Your cars need servicing and insurance, wear out and can break down.
reallife_opt_tip_car_easy: Your cars use no fuel, never break down and do not wear.
reallife_opt_tip_leisure: Chess, fishing, nights out, sightseeing and photo mode. Off, none of them can be started.
reallife_opt_tip_leisure_chess: A chess player sits on the pavement by day, and you can play.
reallife_opt_tip_leisure_fishing: You can fish at the water's edge.
reallife_opt_tip_leisure_night_out: Nightclubs have a dance floor and a bar. Driving after drinks is an offence.
reallife_opt_tip_leisure_sights: Landmarks can be taken in and ticked off.
reallife_opt_tip_leisure_cinema: Cinemas and theatres name the film or play that is on.
reallife_opt_tip_clothes_shops: Clothing stores have a rack to buy from, and your wardrobe holds the mod's clothes.
reallife_opt_tip_clothes_must_be_bought: You can only wear the mod's clothes you have bought. This is kept for each save.
reallife_opt_tip_night_life: Two people stand outside an open club, cinema or theatre at night.
reallife_opt_tip_ambient_sound: Birds, crickets, distant traffic and the murmur of crowds are heard in the city.
reallife_opt_tip_ambient_city: How loud the far-off traffic is.
reallife_opt_tip_ambient_crowd: How loud the murmur near people is.
reallife_opt_tip_radio_hud: The radio station and the song are named on screen while you drive.
reallife_opt_tip_photo_mode: The photo mode key stops the game for a picture.
reallife_opt_tip_city_fires: Cars, bins and shopfronts catch fire now and then, and the fire service comes.
reallife_opt_tip_fire_frequency: 1 is rare, 10 is one every eight minutes or so.
reallife_opt_tip_weather_matters: Wet roads, mist, storms, heat waves and cold snaps change driving, traffic, accidents, crime and your energy.
reallife_opt_tip_weather_frequency: 1 is hardly ever, 10 is nearly half the days of summer and winter.
reallife_opt_tip_street_events: Markets, parades, protests, fun runs, film shoots and fireworks close a street, announced the day before.
reallife_opt_tip_street_event_frequency: 1 is one day in twelve, 10 is four days in five. The Saturday market and fireworks nights are fixed.
reallife_opt_tip_social: You have family, friends and perhaps a partner, each with a contact on the phone.
reallife_opt_tip_social_meetings: Somebody new comes up to you after the gym, a shift, a coffee or a good turn.
reallife_opt_tip_social_relationships: People drift away if you neglect them, and a relationship can be damaged. Off, nothing is ever lost.
reallife_opt_tip_social_outings: You can make plans with people and keep them: coffee, a meal, the cinema, a walk, a drive.
reallife_opt_tip_social_contact: People invite you, ask favours, bring news and visit your shop.
reallife_opt_tip_social_texts_max: The most texts you get in one day, from everybody together.
reallife_opt_tip_social_newspaper: The city's morning paper as a newspaper: delivered to your door, bought at a kiosk near your home, or read on your phone. Off: no paper, and nothing is charged.
reallife_opt_tip_travel_hotels: Eight hotels take guests, booked at the door.
reallife_opt_tip_travel_holidays: Travel agencies sell holidays, and going too long without a break wears you out.
reallife_opt_tip_travel_extras: A suitcase, travel insurance, a companion and trade fairs can be added to a trip.
reallife_opt_tip_garage: Drive a car of yours into a repair bay to paint it and fit parts.
reallife_opt_tip_garage_cosmetics: Paint, lamp tints, underglow and fitted parts are seen on your cars.
reallife_opt_tip_garage_tuning: Fitted performance parts change how the car drives.
reallife_opt_tip_garage_underglow: Underglow kits light the road under the car after dark.
reallife_opt_tip_garage_police: A straight-through exhaust, or riding without a helmet, can be fined.
reallife_opt_tip_two_wheelers: Bicycles and motorbikes can be hired, bought and ridden.
reallife_opt_tip_justice: An arrest or a serious charge opens a case with bail, a court date, a verdict and a sentence.
reallife_opt_tip_justice_lawyers: You can hire one of the city's law firms. Off, there is the public defender or yourself.
reallife_opt_tip_justice_courthouse: You go to the courthouse for a hearing. Off, hearings are held by video link from the Legal file.
reallife_opt_tip_justice_no_prison: No sentence sends you to prison.
reallife_opt_tip_justice_prison_cap: No prison sentence is longer than this many in-game days.
reallife_opt_tip_justice_community: You work a community service sentence yourself. Off, it becomes a fine.
reallife_opt_tip_justice_civil: Someone you crash into may take you to court for damages, one claim at a time.
reallife_opt_tip_justice_aftermath: You can appeal, have an old record sealed and be paid for a wrongful arrest.
reallife_opt_tip_justice_phone: A Legal contact on the phone opens your Legal file.
reallife_opt_tip_driving_licence: You need a licence for what you drive. Off, anyone may drive anything, as in the game itself.
reallife_opt_tip_licence_start_with: A new save that owns no vehicle starts with a driving licence.
reallife_opt_tip_driving_school: Driving schools have desks for the theory test, lessons and the driven test.
reallife_opt_tip_licence_points: Booked offences put points on your licence, and twelve suspend it.
reallife_opt_tip_roadside_checks: Now and then a patrol car pulls you over to see your licence.
reallife_opt_tip_planner: An app on the phone lists everything you have to do.
reallife_opt_tip_planner_reminders: The Planner reminds you of what is coming up.
reallife_opt_tip_economy: You have a credit rating, banks lend by it, and loans can be taken from the phone. Off, the banks' own terms and no Finance app.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_products: Adds an overdraft, a credit card, a business loan, car finance, a mortgage and consolidation. Off, nothing new is opened and what you owe stays owed.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_shark: A private lender lends when no bank will. Off, it lends nothing, and a debt to it can still be paid.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_consequences: Missed payments bring fees, a penalty rate, collections, repossession and a court claim. Off, only your rating suffers.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_level: Relaxed is forgiving, Hardcore is strict. The presets set this.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_city: The city has a bank rate, prices and good and bad years that reach your customers. Off, the game's own rates, prices and customers.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_city_level: Relaxed keeps the economy calm, Hardcore lets it swing wide. The presets set this.
reallife_opt_tip_ventures_investors: Investors make offers for a share of your businesses and meet you. Off, no new offers, and deals you have carry on.
reallife_opt_tip_ventures_market: The city's stock market and the Stocks app. Off, the market stands still and nothing is traded; the shares you hold are kept.
reallife_opt_tip_ventures_level: Relaxed investors are patient, Hardcore ones want growth quickly. The presets set this.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_company: Staff, insurance, marketing, tax and licences for your businesses, with the Company app. Off, none of it runs and nothing is charged.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_company_staff: Staff expect the going rate, ask for raises, get offers from rivals, strike, and are paid overtime and sick pay.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_company_cover: You can take out policies, pay premiums and make claims.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_company_marketi: Campaigns cost money, run for a time and end with a report.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_company_tax: A tax return is due every quarter, and an accountant can file it.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_company_hide: You may keep some cash sales out of the return, at the risk of an audit. Off, nothing can be hidden.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_company_licence: Food hygiene, alcohol, late opening and signage need a licence or a permit.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_rota: The Company app forecasts customers, advises opening hours and writes a staff rota at a press.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_cleaning: Cleaners go round your businesses every day, and can clean for other businesses under contract.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_sale: The Services app says what a business is worth, brings offers from buyers and can sell it quickly.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_company_level: Relaxed is forgiving, Hardcore is strict. The presets set this.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_estate: Building values and rents move, and you can let buildings to tenants, do works and sell. Off, every value and rent is the game's own.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_estate_hotel: A hotel you own takes guests and pays you. Off, it stands still.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_estate_hire: You can hire your cars out. Off, no car goes out, and a car that is out is called back.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_online: A business or a warehouse sells its stock to the whole city through the Web shop app. Off, no orders come.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_brands: Your shops can become a brand and be franchised. Off, a brand has no effect and no franchise money is paid.
reallife_opt_tip_nav_minimap: A small map of the streets round you is shown on screen.
reallife_opt_tip_nav_gps: A route along the roads is drawn to your destination. Off, the game's marker only.
reallife_opt_tip_nav_other_route: The route line of the other mod is used. Off, this mod's route, on the minimap only.
reallife_opt_tip_nav_rotate: The minimap turns with the camera, so that what is ahead on the screen is up. Off, north is up.
reallife_opt_tip_nav_size: How large the minimap is on screen.
reallife_opt_tip_nav_zoom: How close the minimap looks. A higher number is closer.
reallife_opt_tip_nav_base: The minimap shows buildings and water. Off, roads only.
reallife_opt_tip_civic: The city has a government and a programme of public works, with City Hall on the phone.
reallife_opt_tip_civic_elections: Campaigns run in the street, you can vote, and policies change the city. Off, every policy effect is taken back.

reallife_guide_economy_banks: # What it is - The city's three largest banks share one Banks app, in the Money folder of the phone. Each bank has the game's own name for it. Pick the bank under the page's title. A city with fewer banks has fewer in the app. - A bank's page shows only what you hold with that bank. The Finance app still shows every lender at once. Both read the same records, so a payment made in one shows in the other at once. - The app's badge counts what is behind or has a call waiting, at every bank in the app. - It runs while Credit rating and phone loans is on. It has its own switch, Banks app, under Money in the options. # The tabs - Accounts: your current account and an overdraft held there, with a statement of the money that moved with that bank over a day, a week or a month. Your cash is held with the largest bank. - Loans: every loan you owe that bank, the game's own and this mod's. Pick one to see how it stands and to pay some of it or all of it. A game loan is paid as EconoView pays it. A call from collections that waits shows its answers here too. To change a game loan's daily payment, use EconoView: a button opens it. - Card: a card held there, with its limit, balance, statement, minimum and due day. Pay the minimum, an amount or all of it, or draw cash on it. Close it when nothing is owed. - Apply: what that bank offers you today: a loan, an overdraft, a card, a business loan, car finance, a mortgage and consolidation. Each has a page with the same questions as the Finance app. With Overdraft, cards, mortgage and other credit off, only the loan is offered. - Rating: what that bank lends at a row of ratings from just under {bank_threshold} to the best terms, and at yours, before your income and wealth count. It also shows what your next step up in rating would bring there, and what would raise your rating. # How the banks differ - The largest bank keeps the usual rates, limits and fees. - The second charges a point more, gives a quarter more on a card, an overdraft and finance, and takes half the usual fee on a loan by phone. - The third charges a point less, gives a fifth less, and takes three quarters of the usual fee. - A new overdraft is still held to {econ_od_income} days of your average daily income, and a new card to {econ_card_income} days, at every bank. A bank that gives a quarter more stops there too. - Consolidation at any bank pays off every loan, the card and the overdraft, whichever bank holds them. - The game's own loan at the bank counter keeps the bank's own terms. # Limits - You hold one overdraft and one card in all, with the bank that opened them. A car or home approval is held with the bank that gave it. - Under a rating of {bank_threshold} no bank lends at all, in any app or at the counter. - The app keeps nothing of its own in your save.
