reallife_opt_tip_tech_sector: Run a software studio, game studio, IT consultancy or cybersecurity firm with products, customers and client contracts in the Tech app.
reallife_guide_tech_sector_about: Software studios, game studios, IT consultancies, cybersecurity firms and AI labs as businesses of your own, with products, customers, contracts, outages and breaches.
reallife_guide_tech_sector: # Setting up a firm, step by step - 1. An office. Rent or buy an office building and start a business there in BizMan. The game's own list of types has a Software Studio, a Game Studio, an IT Consultancy, a Cybersecurity Firm and an AI Lab; they need the game's office businesses course. Your web development agencies and graphic designers join the same economy: they take contracts with the hours their staff did not sell to the game's customers. - 2. Staff. Hire at the game's recruitment agency, or on the jobs board in Open Roles, and assign each person to the firm. Programmers build products and do the contracts' work (at a cybersecurity firm they are its security analysts), graphic designers do the design and branding, and customer service people support customers and sell. - 3. Workstations. Buy and place the workstations the business needs (BizMan lists its requirements). Every shift is at a workstation. - 4. Opening hours and shifts. A new business opens 8:00 to 16:00, Monday to Saturday, but nobody works until they have a shift. Give shifts in BizMan, Schedule (its auto fill works too), or plan the week in the Company app, Rota tab, which puts somebody at every workstation of a tech firm for all the hours it opens. Only hours on a shift, with the business open, count. - 5. Open it. A new business starts temporarily closed. Switch it open on its page in BizMan. - 6. Internet and utilities. A tech firm cannot open without an internet plan: buy one in the Utilities app, Internet tab; it connects {tech_net_days} days later and the firm opens by itself then. A building you own needs power too: apply for an account in person at the utilities office. While the business is closed, nobody works. The speed of the office's plan sets the pace of the work: {net_speed_work} at most firms, more for a game studio or an AI lab and less for a consultancy or a design studio (the Utilities page of the Guide has the figures). The firm's page shows its connection, its pace and the plan that would lift it. - 7. A contract. Offers come on the Tech app's Contracts tab. Take one and its work starts the next day, from the hours worked the day before. The firm's page and the contract's page say who worked yesterday and for how long and, if nobody did, why and what to do; a notification says so as well. - 8. A product. On the Products tab, or on a firm's page, press Start a product, pick the kind and start building. The page says what each kind needs. When it has enough features (a game: when it is whole), press Launch on its page. - 9. The money. Each professional's points a day are their output: a mid-level in good heart does {tech_points} in an eight hour shift. A firm earns from its products and contracts, booked each morning among the business's takings in the game's statement, so its tax, its bank and its sale value see them. It pays its staff's wages (the game's own), tools at {tech_seat} a day for each professional, hosting and marketing. A project pays {tech_upfront} when it is taken and the rest when it is done. - The game sends a tech firm no customers of its own. The Tech app lists every firm with its people and what they can do. # Products - A software studio makes subscription services, apps and licensed software; a game studio makes games; a consultancy and a security firm make services of their own. Start one from a firm's page. - A feature costs {tech_feature_base} points and {tech_feature_step} more for each one built. A product can launch with {tech_launch_features}. - A firm can have {tech_products_firm} products being built or on sale at once, and your firms {tech_products_most} between them. A product holds {tech_features_most} features at most; past that its engineers' time for features is not used, so start another product. Withdrawn products stay in the list, the {tech_products_kept} newest of them, and the older ones go. - The firm's focus shares its engineers between features, fixing bugs and paying down technical debt. Testers fix bugs twice as fast; product managers make features go further; seniors build with less debt. Debt slows the work and brings outages. - Each product competes with a listed company of the city's stock market. Customers come by its features against the rival's, its quality, its price, the firm's reputation, marketing, sales people and the economy; they leave by churn, more for a buggy product, one short of support, a dear tier or a rival ahead. {tech_segments} - Of a consumer service's users, {tech_paying} pay. The price tiers are {tech_tiers} of the list price; marketing costs up to {tech_marketing_most} a day. One support person answers {tech_tickets} tickets a day. Tools cost {tech_seat} a day for each professional. - A licence sells for {tech_licence} to a company, with {tech_upkeep} of it a year for upkeep. - Games are built whole, then launched. Hype builds with marketing before launch; sales halve every {tech_half_life} days. The stores take {tech_store_cut}. {tech_game_sizes} # Contracts - Clients offer work to firms that take it: builds and integrations at {tech_point_rate} a point, security work at {tech_security_rate}, managed services at {tech_managed} a month. Some clients are your own businesses, which pay from their own books. - A project pays {tech_upfront} when it is taken and the rest when it is done, less {tech_late} a day late. One not done in twice its time fails. - Every {tech_tender_every} days the council puts a job out to tender, {tech_council} bigger than a client's, with {tech_tender_days} days to bid. Bid a price; rivals bid too, and reputation weighs each bid. # Risks - An outage loses {tech_outage_churn} of a product's customers, and companies get {tech_sla} of a month back. - A breach costs {tech_fine_customer} a customer affected, at least {tech_fine_least} and at most {tech_fine_year} of a year's revenue, half again off the data protection register (a year on it costs {tech_register_fee}). A firm off the register, or breached before, also faces a case in court. The insurer's liability cover may pay, and your standing for integrity falls. # Tax and growth - Every quarter {tech_relief} of the pay of the people who built products is given back as research and development relief, an extra deduction for the game's tax. - A scale-up has {tech_scale_monthly} of recurring revenue a month and {tech_scale_people} professionals. The Firms tab shows the way up and what each step still needs. # Data centres and the cloud - A warehouse of yours can be fitted out as a data centre on the Infra tab, for {infra_fit} a square metre by its tier of redundancy; a higher tier has fewer outages. A rack takes {infra_sqm} square metres. - When you rent or buy a warehouse, a question asks whether to set it up as a data centre. Yes opens the same fit-out on the Infra tab: the tier, the racks it has room for and the cost. It can be fitted out before the power, the water or the connection come, and it goes down until they do. The question has its own switch in the options. - A rack of servers costs {infra_rack} and draws {infra_kw} kW; a rack of AI accelerators costs {infra_gpu}, draws {infra_gpu_kw} kW and takes two racks' room. Every megawatt hour takes {infra_water} cubic metres of cooling water. Power and water are paid at the city's utilities' tariff, and with either cut the data centre is down. Racks are written down over {infra_years} years for tax. - It needs a business connection of {infra_net} Mbps and a technician, network engineer or other infrastructure professional for every {infra_technician} racks; hire them on the jobs board for the warehouse. Short of them, it goes down more often. - Racks are let to the city's companies at {infra_colo} a month. - A cloud of your own needs {infra_cloud_racks} racks at tier II or better, {infra_cloud_engineers} site reliability or DevOps people, {infra_cloud_cash} in cash, every data centre connected and a licence of {infra_licence} a year. It sells compute at {infra_unit} a unit a day and AI compute at {infra_gpu_unit} at the list price, and your own firms host on it at {infra_own} of the list. Each district with a data centre is a region. - Take more than {infra_war} of the city's compute and the rival clouds cut their prices by {infra_cut} a month, down to {infra_floor} of their list. - With data centres in {infra_regions} districts, {infra_hyper_racks} racks, a chief technology officer, two staff-level infrastructure people and {infra_hyper_cash} in cash, the cloud is a hyperscaler, and the city's large companies buy from it too. # AI labs - An AI lab makes AI models. Each generation needs engineering and training: {infra_train} AI compute unit-days for the first, twice as much for each one after. Training and running a model use your cloud's accelerators, or compute rented from a rival cloud at {infra_rented} of its list price. # Competitors - A firm's page has a Competitors button. Its page lists everyone the firm is up against: the city's listed tech companies that make the same kind of product or take on the same kind of work, the city's startups by what they do, and the firms you or other players run that do the same. - Pick one to see where you meet, each of your products that has it as its rival with your features against theirs and your share of the market, the council's tenders you both bid for (with both bids once decided), and where it is: a company's floor of its tower, with Set destination. - A council tender's page names the companies bidding against you. - On BizMan's start screen the cards of the Software Studio, the Game Studio, the IT Consultancy, the Cybersecurity Firm, the AI Lab and the Training Academy say how many competitors each has in the whole city, counted the same way. A Training Academy competes with Manhattan Business School, Hudson City University while it is open, and other academies. The game's own kinds of business keep the game's count of the neighbourhood.

reallife_guide_tech_startups: # The city's startups - Up to {vc_most} startups run at once. They are founded over time, more in a good market and more AI companies when the AI wave is high. Each grows its revenue by its founders' quality and the mood, and burns money. - With under {vc_raise_when} months of money left a startup raises {vc_raised_months} months of the next stage's burn. A round needs the revenue of its stage and a venture firm to lead it; it is valued at {vc_multiple_least} to {vc_multiple_most} times its revenue a year, by its growth and the mood, never under the stage's floor. {vc_rounds} - At the seed round {vc_pool} is set aside for staff options. A raise that finds no lead may become a down round, {vc_down} under the last value; after {vc_failed} failed raises with no money left, a startup fails or is taken on for its team at {vc_acquihire} of what was put in. From series B a buyer may come, at {vc_acquire_least} to {vc_acquire_most} times its revenue a year. - Every investor's money comes back first on a sale, once over, unless their share of the price is more. Then everyone shares the rest by their shares. # The venture firms {vc_firms} # Backing a startup - A raising startup may come to you for {vc_ask_share} of its round, at least {vc_ticket}. The Startups tab of the Tech app shows what it claims; a star marks a figure from its deck. Meet the founders to ask three questions: about its revenue, the team, the market, its burn or the terms. - A due diligence report costs {vc_diligence} and shows its true revenue, the founders' quality and how far its deck stretched the truth. - Back it as an angel with your own money, or from your fund. You may ask for a value {vc_haggle} lower; founders with a weaker hand agree. With pro rata rights you are offered your share of each later round for {vc_pro_rata_days} days. - Your fund is money you set aside for startups: its returns go back into it, and you can take its cash back out. # Raising for your own firm - On the Funding tab start a raise: for {vc_raise_days} days venture firms ask to meet, {vc_meetings} at most. In each meeting you answer three questions with the truth, a stretch or a bold claim. A firm's diligence may catch an untrue answer, which ends the meeting and closes its door for a while. - A good meeting earns a term sheet for {vc_sheet_days} days: an amount for a share of the firm, a board seat for the lead, pro rata rights and a preference. Take the one you like; the money comes into the firm. - The board expects recurring revenue {vc_target} higher every {vc_target_days} days. Missed twice in a row with the investors holding most of the board's seats, the board replaces the chief executive: a professional you named is laid off, and the board's choice joins the payroll. - Between rounds the last lead lends a bridge of {vc_bridge_months} months of your burn at {vc_bridge_interest} a year; it turns into shares at the next round at {vc_bridge_discount} off. - Share options grant {vc_grant} of the firm to its people at a time. They vest over {vc_vest} years after a {vc_cliff} year cliff, lift morale and cut a rival's approaches by {vc_option_poach}. - You can sell a tenth of your shares to the lead investor. A firm of yours comes to the stock market as part of your company: asking for a listing opens Your company in the Stocks app, where advisers, an audit and a prospectus take it there. - A growth startup with {vc_listing_arr} of recurring revenue a year may list: it is valued at {vc_listing_multiple} times that, never under its last round, and every investor sells at the offer.

reallife_guide_economy_dealer_about: A car showroom of your own: buy cars new, used and at the trade auction, and sell them to customers with your own finance and warranties.
reallife_guide_economy_dealer: # What it is - Car Showroom is a business type of its own. Found it in a shop unit with BizMan, as any shop. You hire its staff in the game's own way: salespeople with customer service as their main skill, and cleaners. Give each salesperson a shift at a cash register, which is their desk. Opening hours, rent, wages, utilities, licences, insurance and the rota are the game's and this mod's as for any business. - The first time you walk in, the floor is laid out as a lot: {dealer_places_least} to {dealer_places_most} places, by its size. Leave the middle of the room clear. The cars are real cars of the game's, parked on the lot. They are the showroom's stock, not yours: no Garage page, insurance or registration, and they cannot go on hire or into the custom shop. - The Car Showroom app, in the Business folder of the phone, runs it. Its tabs are Stock, Market, Offers, Finance, Showrooms, Growth and Reports. - While you stand in a showroom, Lay out the lot again on the Showrooms tab lays its places out afresh. - Up to {dealer_showrooms} showrooms trade. One past that does not. # Buying cars - Buy on the Market tab. - New: {dealer_wholesale_count} cars a day from the wholesaler, at {dealer_wholesale_least} to {dealer_wholesale_most} of their price new. - Used: {dealer_used_count} private owners a day. They say the car is better than it is if it has faults. An inspection costs {dealer_inspection} of its worth ({dealer_inspection_least} to {dealer_inspection_most}). It shows the truth, and each fault found brings the owner's least down. You may make {dealer_haggles} offers before they sell elsewhere. - The trade auction: {dealer_lots} lots at a time between {dealer_auction_from} and {dealer_auction_to}, opening at {dealer_opening} of their worth. The other dealers in the room bid each hour. A lot won costs the hammer price and a fee of {dealer_fee}. A look over a lot costs {dealer_lot_inspection}. A lot won is paid at once if you have the cash, a free place on a lot and fewer than {dealer_deliveries_most} cars on their way. A lot won and not paid for means no bids for {dealer_no_pay} days. - A car is worth its price new at the city's prices, less its kilometres and its condition. It goes on the lot asked at {dealer_markup} of its worth. You can set its price, from {dealer_ask_least} to {dealer_ask_most} of its worth, prepare it (a valet, a check and the faults you know of put right) or sell it to the trade at once for {dealer_trade} of its worth. # Selling - Customers come by the hour. Their number is a share ({dealer_visitors}) of the customers the game itself would send a shop of that size, at the building's promotion. So campaigns, brands, Standing, Flare, the city and business pressure all count, and nobody comes while it is closed. - Each salesperson on shift looks after {dealer_serve} visitors an hour. With nobody on shift, visitors leave. A more skilled salesperson draws more offers and better ones. A dear car, or one that has stood long, draws fewer. - An offer stands {dealer_deal_hours} hours. The staff close any offer of at least {dealer_floor} of the asking price on their own. You can set this share for each showroom on the Showrooms tab, from {dealer_floor_least} to {dealer_floor_most}. Anything else waits in the Offers tab: take it, counter it ({dealer_counters} counters at most), or turn it down. A showroom holds {dealer_offers_most} offers at most, and a notice says when offers wait for you. - Some buyers ask for a test drive first. The staff take them out, or press Test drive on the offer. A drive puts kilometres on the car and now and then a mark, and a buyer who has driven takes a counter more often. - Some buyers bring a car of their own in part exchange. It is taken at its allowance and goes on the lot in place of the car sold. # Finance and warranties - On a car over {dealer_finance_least}, some buyers ask to pay over time. The showroom lends from a credit rating of {dealer_threshold}, at the banks' rate for the rating and {dealer_rate_points} points more, with a deposit of {dealer_deposit_least} to {dealer_deposit_most}. Instalments come in each week. {dealer_misses} weeks missed running and the car is taken back and sold at the auction for {dealer_recover} of its worth. - Warranties sold with a car: {dealer_tiers}- A warranty pays at most {dealer_claims} claims, with {dealer_claim_rest} days between them. - Switch finance and warranties on or off for each showroom on the Showrooms tab. The Finance tab lists the cars being paid for. - Up to {dealer_plans_most} finance plans and {dealer_covers_most} warranties are kept. Past that, a buyer's finance is sold on at once and the car is paid for in full, and no more warranties are sold. # Events - From the Growth tab, book an event at a showroom. It is paid at once and runs from that day: {dealer_events}- One event at a time at a showroom, and the same one again there {dealer_event_rest} days after it ends. Its extra visitors are points on the building's promotion, never past its top of {dealer_promotion_top}, so a Company app campaign that has the promotion high already leaves an event less to add. # Reputation and missions - Each showroom has its own reputation with car buyers. A car sold to a customer adds {dealer_rep_sale}, and {dealer_rep_good} more for one in fine condition. Each fault the buyer finds takes {dealer_rep_fault}. An offer left to lapse, a buyer who walks away after your counters and a car taken back on finance cost it too, and a warranty claim paid adds a little. - Its steps and their perks: {dealer_steps}- It never brings visitors: those come with the building's promotion, which your Standing with customers already moves. So nothing is counted twice. - Missions, each done once at a showroom, said with a notice and paid in reputation: {dealer_missions} # Extras - Some buyers take extras on top of the car, each booked on a line of its own. You can stop them for a showroom on the Showrooms tab: {dealer_extras} # The workshop - Pick a car on the Stock tab to send it to the workshop. It is off show for {dealer_workshop_least} to {dealer_workshop_most} hours and comes back with every fault put right, the hidden ones too, and {dealer_workshop_restore} of its missing condition back. Preparing puts back {dealer_prepare_restore}, and only the faults you know of. A showroom's workshop takes {dealer_workshop_bays} cars at a time. - A better condition lifts a car's worth, and a tired car draws fewer buyers. # Deliveries - A lot won at the trade auction is paid at once and arrives {dealer_delivery_least} to {dealer_delivery_most} days later at {dealer_delivery_hour}. Its place on the lot is held until then. The Stock tab lists the cars on their way. # Reports - The Reports tab charts a figure's days for one showroom or all of them: cars sold, takings, gross profit, stock age, visitors, the share who bought, and finance arrears. {dealer_report_days} days are kept, with the average of {dealer_average_days} days drawn over the bars. # The books - A car sold and a car bought are booked as the game books a vehicle sold and bought, at the showroom's address. Instalments and premiums are its takings, and inspections, fees, preparation and claims are its costs. So the game's statement and tax, the Company app, brands, loans, investors and a sale's value all see what it really makes. The tax counts the margin, as the costs are deducted. A showroom is not sold while cars stand on its lot. - It runs while the credit rating does. Switched off, the showrooms do not trade, and their cars stay on the lots. # On the floor - While you stand in one of your showrooms, its customers walk round it: up to {showroom_shown} of an hour's visitors, {showroom_at_once} at a time. They come in at the door, stop at cars to look them over, and leave. A salesperson on shift goes to as many of them as were served. A customer who made an offer looks first at that car. One nobody saw to shows it as they go. What you see is the hour as the showroom worked it, and it changes nothing. The option Visitors on the floor switches them off. - Choose its bay, on a car's page of the Stock tab while you stand in its showroom: the game pauses, the car follows the pointer from bay to bay, and a click puts it down. The car on that bay takes its old one. The game's key for turning an item, or a short right click, turns it round, and the cancel key puts everything back. Your choice is kept, and a new car takes the first free bay. - Look round it, on the same page, takes the showroom's camera close round the car. Hold the right button and drag, or use the game's rotate keys, to go round it, and scroll to come closer. The interact key chooses its bay from there, and the cancel key leaves. - A car's page shows a picture of it: the game's own picture of its kind where it has one, or a photo taken in its showroom.

reallife_guide_economy_ownbank_about: In the middle of a game, found a bank of your own and grow it from a community bank to a national one: take the city's savings, lend them to its people and businesses, put a share into the Stocks app, and keep the regulator satisfied.
reallife_guide_economy_ownbank: # What it is - A bank of your own, run from your headquarters, in the Your bank app in the Money folder of the phone. The Company app's first page has a button to it. Its tabs are Bank, Savers, Lending, Fund and Branches. - It runs while Credit rating and phone loans is on, and has its own switch, Your own bank, under Your businesses in the options. Off, a bank you have stands still and nothing is run or charged. - The city's own banks are its rivals. The game's banks lend to you; this one is yours. # Founding it - Found it on the Bank tab and give it a name. You need a headquarters of your own: rent one first. With careers on, the regulator also wants a qualified person: your own BSc Finance, BA Accounting, MBA or chartered accountant exams, or a senior accountant or financial analyst on your staff. - The banking licence costs {ob_licence}, paid once and not given back. The regulator wants {ob_capital} of capital paid in before the bank takes a single saver. - The capital is the bank's, not yours: what the bank makes stays in it, and what it loses comes out of it. Take a dividend from it, or put more in, in steps of {ob_step}. A dividend never takes the bank under its reserves, its least capital or its lending line. - Each day the bank's takings, what its savers are paid, its losses and its staff are in your headquarters' statement, so the game's tax counts them. The staff cost {ob_hall_community} a day as a Community Bank, {ob_hall_regional} as a Regional Bank and {ob_staff} as a National Bank, and a share of what it holds. The day's profit then goes into the bank's capital, so your own cash is where it was. # Savers - The city's people and its businesses keep their savings with the rival banks, which pay the bank rate less {ob_rival_margin} points. Set your rate against theirs on the Savers tab. - Savers move over months, by your rate and by how far the city trusts the bank: your integrity as an owner (Standing), the bank's capital, what the City Ledger has printed about it and the economy. A new bank earns its name over {ob_trust_months} months. - The rival banks answer: as you take their savers they pay up to {ob_answer} points more, and as you take their borrowers they charge as much less. - When the city's confidence falls far enough, savers run on the bank: {ob_run_people} of people's savings and {ob_run_firms} of businesses' leave each day, and nothing new is lent, until confidence comes back. If the reserves cannot pay them the fund is sold under the market's price, and a bank that still cannot pay is closed. # Loans - On the Lending tab, five kinds of borrower, each with your rate against the rival banks' and a switch: people with a poor, a fair or a good rating, shops and small businesses, and established companies. No bank of the city lends to the poorly rated; their yardstick is the fair rate and {ob_poor_premium} points. - A cheaper rate wins more borrowers; each point dearer than the rivals brings borrowers {ob_adverse} likelier to default. - Defaults a year in a steady city: {ob_default_poor} of the poorly rated, {ob_default_fair} fair, {ob_default_good} good, {ob_default_shops} of shops and {ob_default_firms} of companies. People default more in a slowdown or a recession, when inflation runs away from its target and when landlords set their own rents, and less under a city wage floor or rent control; businesses default more with business pressure in the economy, a higher business tax or a licence fee, and less with grants. Each month has its own luck. - A loan that defaults pays nothing. Over a month a part of it is put right and the rest written off; a part of what is written off comes back over {ob_recover_months} months. With the justice system on, written off loans go to the courts: {ob_court_extra} more comes back, later, for {ob_court_cost} in costs. # The regulator - The capital must stay at least {ob_min} of the loans and the fund, weighted by their risk (a poorly rated person's loan at {ob_weight_poor}, a good one's at {ob_weight_good}, a share at {ob_weight_fund}). The bank lends and buys no further than {ob_lend}, keeps {ob_reserve} of its deposits in reserve, and is watched under {ob_watch}. - Under {ob_min} the bank is in breach: it lends nothing and has {ob_cure_months} month to put it right. A deadline missed is fined ({ob_fine_share} of the capital it is short of, at least {ob_fine_least}) with another month; the second closes the bank. A bank with no capital left, or under {ob_half}, is closed at once. - A bank that is closed is wound up: its savers are paid first, the regulator takes {ob_wind_fee} of what is left, and the rest is yours. A new licence may be applied for a year after the closure, on stricter terms: the next bank pays in {ob_again_capital} of capital in place of {ob_capital}, and more again after a second closure, and with Standing on your integrity as an owner must be back to {ob_again_integrity}. The Your bank app shows the date and what is still missing. # The fund - On the Fund tab, choose a strategy and a limit of up to {ob_fund_most} of the deposits. A cautious fund holds the {ob_fund_cautious} largest companies of the Stocks app, a balanced one {ob_fund_balanced} with no small ones, a bold one {ob_fund_bold} of any kind not near failing; never one under a bid. - Each week it is traded back to an even part of each, with a small commission. Its dividends come in a day at a time, and a company that fails is a loss. The fund's trades do not move the market's prices. # Selling it - A buyer pays the bank's capital and {ob_sale_years} years of its last year's profit. Its savers, loans and fund go with it. No buyer takes a bank the regulator is after or one its savers are running from. # Levels - Every bank starts as a Community Bank: the licence and capital above are a Community Bank's. It may run {ob_branches_community} branches, lend {ob_loans_community} and hold {ob_deposits_community} of savings. - A Regional Bank may run {ob_branches_regional} branches, lend {ob_loans_regional} and hold {ob_deposits_regional} of savings. A National Bank may run {ob_branches_national} branches, and its loans and savings have no limit but the regulator's ratio. - At its level's limit the bank makes no new loans and takes no new savings, at its counters too, and a branch past its count takes no customers. What it already holds stays. A notice tells you when its savings or its loans are full. - To move up, the bank needs {ob_record_regional} months at its level without a breach ({ob_record_national} to become a National Bank), the regulator satisfied and no run, and the capital of the level above: {ob_capital_regional} for a Regional Bank, {ob_capital_national} for a National Bank. Moving up costs the licence of the level above less the one it holds: {ob_up_regional}, then {ob_up_national}. - The Level row on the Bank tab shows what is met and has the Move up a level button. A notice tells you when all but the licence is met. - A bank founded before there were levels is a National Bank while its capital meets the least it was founded with, and otherwise the highest level its capital meets. It keeps every saver, loan and branch it has, even past that level's limits. # Your pay - The Your pay this month row on the Bank tab sets what the bank pays you: a share of each day's profit, in steps of {ob_pay_step} on the slider, or a fixed sum a day, never more than the day's profit. - What is not paid to you stays in the bank's capital, where it lends and counts towards the level above. Nothing is paid on a day without profit, during a breach or a run, or past what the bank must keep. - Your pay comes into your cash with each day's books, as a dividend does.

reallife_guide_districtview_about: The city map tints each district by one of {dv_layers} layers, with a key and a card of every figure for the district under the pointer.
reallife_guide_districtview: # Opening it - Open the city map. In its filter list, just above the game's own Neighbourhoods, is a line called District view with {dv_layers} rows: Wealth, Rents, Property prices, Footfall and demand, Crime, Your standing, Power and water, Internet, Competition and Council. It needs District view on the city map on. - Tick one and every district on the map is tinted by it. Ticking another shows that one instead; unticking it, or the yellow button at the foot of its window, puts the map back as it was, with the game's own neighbourhood filters as you had them. The map remembers the last one you ticked, on this computer. - A row's arrow button flies the map to the district at the top of that layer (on Crime, the one with fewest crimes). - The view is off while you choose a subway station or anything else on the map, and while the phone's full menu is over it. # The window - Beside the filter list is the view's own window. Under its headline it says what the layer shows. - Key: the {dv_bands} colours of the layer and what each covers. Grey is a district with no figure, such as one with none of your places on Power and water. - The card: every figure the mod keeps for one district, the layer shown first. It is the district under the pointer, or the one you last clicked on the map or in the list, or else the one you are in. - Districts: every district in order, highest first, with its colour and figure. Pointing at one shows its card; its arrow flies the map there. # The colours - Where more is better (footfall, your standing, power and water, the internet) the colours run from red at the bottom to green at the top; on Crime the other way round. Where more is neither better nor worse (wealth, rents, property prices, competition, the council's parking) they run from light blue to deep blue. - Wealth uses the city's economy's income level, where 100 is the city's middle: under {dv_wealth_low} is low, {dv_wealth_high} or more is wealthy. With the city's economy off it is worked out from the game's class shares, and the card says so. - Your standing is what the district thinks of you as an owner, 0 to 100, from Standing: under {dv_standing_low} is poor, {dv_standing_high} or more is excellent. Every district starts at {standing_start}. - Power and water goes by the share of your accounts there that are supplied, and Internet by how many providers reach the district. - Rents, property prices, footfall, competition and parking are split over the city's own range: the cheapest or quietest district is at one end and the dearest or busiest at the other, in {dv_bands} equal steps. # What each card says - Wealth: the income level and the class shares. Rents: what shops, offices and warehouses are let for, and homes, for their floor space a day. Property: what buildings are worth for their floor space. - Footfall and demand: the game's street traffic figure for its buildings, its customers' demand against the districts' average, and, with the city's economy on, the customers it brings or costs and the prices customers bear. - Crime: crimes reported in the district in the last {dv_crime_days} days: street crimes near you, cars broken into, hit and runs and break-ins at your shops. They are counted from the day you start using this version, and the crimes the mod stages happen near you, so a district you are often in has more reported. {dv_crime_many} or more is many. - Your standing: what people there think of you, and how well you are known there. - Power and water: how many of your places' accounts there are supplied, and any cut off. Internet: the providers that reach the district, any with an outage today, and your own fibre network there, open or still being laid with the day it is ready. - Competition: the businesses open, how many are yours and your rivals', and the three most common kinds. The game's own filter rows light the businesses of each kind. - Council: street parking an hour, building sites at work, the district's voters, and who won there at the last election once it is counted. # Cost - Nothing runs while the map is shut or no layer is ticked. The figures are read once a day: when you open the map on a new day, or when a day passes with it open. The crimes are the view's only line in your save.
reallife_changes_004_6: District view on the city map: ten new rows in its filter list tint each district by wealth, rents, property prices, footfall and demand, crime, your standing, power and water, the internet, competition or the council. Beside the filters a window gives the colours' key, a card with every figure for the district under the pointer, and the districts in order. The Guide has a page on it.
reallife_transit_fare_back: The bus fare of {fare} is given back: you did not ride.
reallife_changes_004_7: Buses: you are seen getting on and off. Board and you walk to the front door, pay, step in, tap your card on the validator and sit down by the middle door, or stand and hold a strap when the bus is full. You ride as it pulls away, and from above its roof is taken off so that you can see in. At your stop the doors open, you get up and step off by the middle door, and the bus leaves. A full bus now takes you, standing.
reallife_changes_004_8: Your own bank, late in a game: a banking licence at your headquarters and the capital the regulator wants paid in; the city's savers won from the rival banks by your rate and how far the city trusts you; loans to its people and businesses priced by risk, with defaults that follow the economy, business pressure and the council; arrears written off and partly recovered, through the courts with the justice system on; a fund in the Stocks app's companies; and a regulator that watches the capital ratio, fines a breach and closes a bank that cannot be saved. A run comes when the city's confidence falls, and the City Ledger reports it. The bank's books are in your headquarters' statement and the game's tax, in its own app.
reallife_changes_004_9: With Empire Motors switched on, the chase camera works again. V in a car is this mod's camera key once more; Empire Motors' view from the driver's seat, which on most cars only switched to the game's camera for driving inside a building and let the chase camera go, is kept off while the key is V. To use that view, give this mod's camera key another key in the options. New: a car dealership of your own. Found a Car Dealership in a shop unit with BizMan, hire salespeople and run it from the Dealership app. Buy cars new from the wholesaler, used from their owners after an inspection and a haggle, or at the trade auction against other dealers. Customers come by the hour by the building's promotion, your staff close what reaches your floor and take them on test drives, and you answer the rest. Sell on your own finance and with warranties; the takings and the costs are in the game's statement and tax.

reallife_guide_markets_listing_about: Your businesses as a company on the city's stock market: advisers, an audit, a prospectus and a book that prices it from your real books, then shareholders, their meetings and votes, investors who press the board and bids for it.
reallife_guide_markets_listing: # Coming to the market - Your businesses together are your company, and it can come to the city's market. In the Stocks app, Going public on the Market or Portfolio tab (Your company once it is listed) opens its page; in the Company app, Your company in Stocks opens it too. The page lists what it takes against your own figures (Show what it takes) and your books by quarter (Show the books). - What it takes: {lst_years} years since you took on your first business, {lst_quarters} complete quarters of books, takings of {lst_turnover} and a profit of {lst_profit} over the last four quarters, a profit in {lst_profitable} of them, and a clean audit. - Engage advisers once all but the audit is met: they take the company on for a retainer of {lst_retainer} of what it looks worth ({lst_retainer_least} to {lst_retainer_most}). Then Order the audit: the auditors charge {lst_audit} of a year's takings ({lst_audit_least} to {lst_audit_most}) and sign after {lst_audit_days} days. Tax owed past its day, tax returns filed late, takings kept off the books, or a bankruptcy or a debt arrangement stop the listing until a clean audit. A bribe that came out is disclosed, and cools the book. An audit is good for a quarter of a year. Withdraw stops the way until the offer is priced: nothing paid comes back, and an audit still good stands. - The prospectus offers {lst_float_least} to {lst_float_most} of the company in new shares. Its price is what your books say a share is worth: the market's own reckoning on the last year's takings and profit (with two years on record, never more than the two years' mean), the last quarter as a patch that passes, half of your growth, and your debt. The advisers take {lst_discount} off it, and the range runs {lst_range} either side. Choose how much to offer, the least price you take (the range's bottom, its middle, or whatever the book gives), Name the company, then Publish the prospectus. - The book is open for {lst_book_days} market days and priced at the next open: keener after a month in which the market rose and with your Standing, cooler for a bribe disclosed and for a larger offer, never more than {lst_beyond} outside the range. Under the least price you take, the offer is called off and nothing is sold. On the first day the money comes to you, less {lst_underwriting} to the underwriters ({lst_underwriting_large} of an offer over {lst_large}) and {lst_exchange} of the company's worth to the exchange, {lst_exchange_least} at least. # Your company on the market - It trades in the Stocks app as any company does, and its price is reckoned the same way, from its real takings and profit day by day as the game's statements have them: what it makes over the last quarter and what it usually makes over the year. A day far from its usual counts as a one-off. The council's policies, the bank rate, the market's mood, your Standing and what the papers say of you move it, and a scandal of yours cuts what the market expects of it for good. - Each day the other holders' part of the profit, after tax and your pay, is taken from your cash and kept for them: the reserve. Dividends are paid out of it and it is in the price; out of a loss, their part comes back to you from it. Your own part is yours already. - Each quarter its results come out as its books have them, with the dividend you proposed (Propose a dividend), never more than the reserve. Your pay is a share of the profit: {lst_pay_fair} is fair, {lst_pay_most} the most. Its page shows the holders (Show the shareholders) and its results (Show the results). - Each year you pay the exchange {lst_yearly} of the company's worth ({lst_yearly_least} at least) and the auditors their fee. The market hears what the audit finds. # Dealing in your own shares - Your shares on its page buys and sells your company's shares at the market, by the rules every founder deals by: nothing from the last third of a quarter until its results are out, no sale for {lst_lockup} days after the listing, never more than {lst_founder_most} of the company, no more than {lst_deal_year} of it bought, and as much sold, in a game year, every deal announced to the market, and any gain on shares bought and sold within {lst_swing} days paid back to the company. Your trading bots' deals in it count with yours. - The company can Buy back shares, up to {lst_buyback_most} of them in a game year, Sell new shares, up to {lst_issue_most} in a year at {lst_placing} under the bid, or be taken private (Take it private) while you hold at least {lst_private_least}: every other holder is then paid {lst_private_premium} over the price, and never less than its highest close of the last year. None of the three while a bid is open. - A business sold while the company is listed was the company's: the other holders' part of its price goes into their reserve. # Shareholders - {lst_agm_days} market days after the year's last results the shareholders meet and vote on your pay, on a payout of the reserve when too much of it is held back, and on your place as chair. You vote all your shares. The others vote by how their year went against the city index, your pay, the reserve, your scandals and any investor's campaign, and not all of them turn up. With half the shares or more you carry every vote. - Pay voted down goes back to the fair rate. A board you no longer chair pays out {lst_board_payout} of the reserve at each results, pays you the fair rate and decides no buy-back, new shares or taking private until the next yearly meeting. - When the company is cheap, its reserve held back, your pay high or its year poor, an investor may buy in after results, ask for a sale, a payout of {lst_payout} of the reserve, your pay cut or you off the board, and call a meeting {lst_egm_days} market days later. Give them what they ask before it and they drop it. A sale voted through brings a bid {lst_sale_days} market days later. # A bid for your company - While its price is well under what it is worth, a larger company of its sector, a private buyer or a rival tycoon's holding may bid {lst_bid_least} to {lst_bid_most} over it, and the bid is decided {lst_bid_days_least} to {lst_bid_days_most} market days later. It can win only while you hold under {lst_threshold} of the company, and then only if its holders take it. If it wins, your shares are bought at the bid and the company's businesses pass to the buyer within {lst_handover_days} days, as the game lets each one go; any it cannot have by then you pay for at the company's price. # Tax and the books - {lst_dividend_tax} of every dividend you are paid from the market is withheld as tax, {lst_dividend_tax_step} more or less for each step of the council's business tax. The audits and the exchange's fees are business costs the game's tax deducts; the costs of coming to the market are not. - The Planner shows the audit signed, the offer priced, the first day of trading, the end of the lock-up, your company's results, its yearly meeting, an investor's meeting, a bid's end and a hand-over due. - With 'Listing your own company' off (options page, under 'The stock market'), no advisers, audit or prospectus can be started; a book already open and a listed company carry on. The save tools take the company private at its last price before the mod is removed. # In a Going Public session - The host's company is on the city's market for every player. As a guest your own company is set aside and nothing of it moves; it is back as it was when you play alone, and the profit of the days away is counted then. Another player's company leaves your market when you play alone again, your shares in it paid at its last price.

reallife_changes_005_0: The mod can now be read in Simplified Chinese: it follows the language the game is set to. Running for office: stand for your district's council seat or for mayor yourself. File papers with signatures or a deposit, stand for a party or as an independent, and choose a platform. Run a campaign with a fund and donors (and the law on them), posters you put up, doors you knock on, rallies you speak at, adverts, endorsements, rivals who attack you and a televised debate. The vote is counted district by district, with a result night. In office the council meets every week: you vote and table motions, a mayor sets the agenda, the city's budget and some policies by order, and conflicts of interest, scandals, approval and recall follow you. City Hall, the Planner, the City Ledger and Flare follow your run. Your own company on the stock market. Once your businesses have two years and a year of books behind them, advisers, an audit and a prospectus take them to the city's market, where a book prices the shares from your real results and the money raised is yours. Its price then follows your real takings and profit, your Standing and the press; the other holders' part of each day's profit is kept for them, and dividends, a yearly shareholders' meeting with votes on your pay and the board, investors who press the board and bids for a cheap company follow, with rules that stop you dealing on what you know. The welcome panel's list of what changed since you last played shows the versions again; it had stayed empty since 0.1.1. Version numbers now follow major, minor and patch: a new feature raises the middle number and a fix alone the last one.

reallife_changes_006_0: Professionals: your programmers, designers, lawyers and HR staff now have a role (36 of them, from back end engineer to accountant), a level from junior to principal, two skills of their own beside the game's, experience, a school and certificates. They learn on the job and from seniors, are reviewed twice a year, ask for rises, can be promoted, sent on courses and exams, and have notice periods, probation, severance and restraint clauses. Rivals come for your seniors. See the new Open Roles app. A jobs board in Open Roles: post ads for any professional role, screen applicants from one labour market the whole city shares (rivals post and hire from it too), check references and records, interview, make offers and match counter-offers, or brief a search firm for senior people. The recruitment office now brings more candidates than you ask for, matched to the role your business needs. The tech sector: start a Software Studio, Game Studio, IT Consultancy, Cybersecurity Firm or AI Lab from the game's own list in an office building, build subscription services, apps, licensed software and games feature by feature against a rival listed on the stock market, win customers, take on client contracts and bid for the council's tenders, and deal with outages, data breaches, fines and technical debt, all in the new Tech app. Your web agencies and graphic designers take contracts with their spare hours, and research and development relief comes back each quarter. Startups and venture capital: the city's startups grow, raise rounds led by fictional venture firms, take down rounds, fail or are bought, and come to you for money. Meet the founders, buy due diligence, back them as an angel or from a fund of your own, haggle and follow on. Your own tech firms can raise too: pitch to the venture firms, take a term sheet, answer to a board with growth targets that can replace a chief executive, take a bridge loan and grant share options. Data centres, the cloud and AI: fit out a warehouse as a data centre, buy racks of servers and AI accelerators, pay their power and cooling water at the utilities' tariff, staff them and keep them up; let racks to companies, then launch a cloud of your own that sells compute to the city and to your own firms, fights the rival clouds' price war and grows into a hyperscaler with regions across the city. AI labs train models on that compute, or on compute rented from a rival.

reallife_guide_careers_study_about: Short courses and diplomas at the school, with a timetable, homework and exams, and skills of your own that grow and fade.
reallife_guide_careers_study: # The courses - The Campus app lists every course on offer, with where and when its classes are, its fee and what it teaches. The game's own business courses are still studied at their desks in the school, as before. - At the school: {study_school_courses}. - Up to {study_at_once} courses can be followed at once. A course is full time, or part time where it allows (Saturday mornings at the school), and a few are online from home. - Persona's Education box lists the game's five courses, then every course of the mod's, grouped by where it is taught, each with where you stand on it: the classes done and the next one, an exam to sit, or the grade. # Classes - Each class is on set days at a set hour, at Manhattan Business School (inside the building) or online from a home of yours with working internet. - A class can be joined from {study_early} minutes before it starts until {study_late} minutes after. At the school, use one of its study desks as for the game's courses: the game's panel has a button for your class or exam. At the university it is the classroom door of your course. An online class is joined at your computer at home, with working internet: it has a button for the class beside Pass Time. On a ward, it is the game's panel over the place, on the interact key. Attend in the Studying tab of the Campus app takes you to the desk or the computer and sits you down. When a class's hour comes, a notification says how to join it. The time is then passed as the game's own study is, with fast forward and skip, and spends energy the same way. - Leave before {study_counted} of it and it does not count. A class gone by without you is missed. An online class you could not join because your internet provider had an outage is excused: it is left out of your attendance and of the exam's mark, neither for nor against you. No internet plan, one not yet connected or one cut off for an unpaid bill is no excuse. - Each class sets a piece of homework, done at your computer at home or where the classes are: {study_homework_hours} hours each. More pieces after the classes are revision, which helps in the exam. # Exams - A short course is assessed at its last class. A diploma's exam is sat on a weekday within {study_exam_window} days of the last class, between {study_exam_open} and {study_exam_close}, and takes {study_exam_hours} hours. - With fewer than {study_barred} of the classes attended you may not sit it. - The mark is out of 100: attendance counts most, then homework, then how far the skill has come, then revision; the day itself adds or takes up to ten. {study_pass} passes, {study_merit} is a merit and {study_distinction} a distinction. - A fail can be retaken {study_retakes} times, from {study_retake_days} days later, for {study_retake_fee} of the fee. - A driving refresher takes up to {study_refresher} recent penalty points off your licence. # Your skills - You have {study_skills} skills of 0 to 100 points: the professions' own skills and the trades and care. The Skills tab of the Campus app shows them; employers read the two a post asks for. - Each course teaches two skills, and its box in the Campus app says which and how many points the whole course adds to each. Every class attended adds its share, and each piece of homework {study_homework_share} of a class. The nearer a skill is to 100, the less is learnt: at 100 only {study_gain_top} of it. - How well you learn follows the best schooling you have passed: with none yet {study_learn_none} less, with a degree {study_learn_degree} more, with a master's degree {study_learn_master} more. - Work raises the two skills of your post too, and keeps them in use; so do classes, homework and tutoring. - A skill not used for {study_fade_days} days fades a little each day, never below {study_fade_floor} of the best it reached. - More than {study_stressed} hours of study in a week leaves you stressed. Below {study_tired} energy no class or homework can be started.

reallife_guide_careers_jobs: # Your first offer, step by step - A new player has no skills and no qualifications, so no employer can make an offer on the first day. The first page of the Career app, Professions, says for each profession what you still need, and what you can apply for now. - Step 1: open the Career app. Its first page names your first step: a course to take and where it is taught, more points of a skill, or a vacancy to wait for. The first time nothing is open to you, a notification says the same. - Step 2: enrol on that course in the Campus app. The quickest start is a short course at Manhattan Business School, such as the security licence, the forklift ticket, bartending or customer service: two or three classes in a week or so. A degree at Hudson City University is {work_degree_weeks} weeks of classes full time and opens the professions. - Step 3: go to each class at its hour, then sit the exam in the {study_exam_window} days after the last class. The classes give the skill points and the pass is the qualification. - Step 4: on the Jobs tab, pick a vacancy marked Open to you. Its box shows your Chance of an offer and, under For a good chance, how many more skill points would make it even or better. Press Apply. - Step 5: the employer answers in {work_answer_least} to {work_answer_most} days. An invitation names the day and hour of the interview: see "The interview" below. - Step 6: a good interview brings an offer that stands for {work_offer_days} days. Accept it on the Applications tab and the job starts {work_start_days} days later. From a new game that is about two or three weeks. # The game's own jobs - The game's cashier job at El Gato Food Market, the delivery van and food deliveries are as they were, and so are the mod's gigs and their employers. # Professions - The Career app lists the city's vacancies. Each profession is a ladder, judged on two of your skills (the first counting three fifths) and on the qualifications from the Campus app. Each rung's own rate is in brackets, the first and the top: {work_professions} - A vacancy, an application and your job each have a Show on map button that puts the game's destination marker on the employer's building. The city map's Employers hiring row marks every building with a post open today, and the map's search finds an employer by its name. - A post asks for a number of points of its skills. In the tech professions, design, marketing, sales and management a first post can be had without its qualification for {work_self_taught} points more. - Higher rungs need a professional certificate in accountancy, law, architecture, engineering and security. # How an employer scores you - When you apply, the employer scores you out of 100. The score is kept with the application, as Their rating of you in its box on the Applications tab, and later changes on your side do not move it. Without the qualification the post needs it is 0; with it, and exactly the points the post asks, it starts at {work_score_base}. - Skills: each point of the post's two skills above what it asks adds one, up to {work_score_fit_most}; each point below takes {work_score_short}. Courses and homework in the Campus app raise the two skills a course teaches, and the work itself raises the post's two. - Experience: one point for every {work_score_exp_days} days you have worked in that profession, in this job or earlier ones, up to {work_score_exp_most}. - References from the jobs on your CV: {work_score_good} for each good one, {work_score_good_most} at most; a poor one takes {work_score_poor}. Two weeks or more in a job, turning up and rated well, gives a good one; walking out or a dismissal gives a poor one. - Your name: up to {work_score_name} either way, from your recognition and your integrity (see Standing and reputation). - A friend's word or a job lead: {work_score_referral}. Registered with a recruitment office: {work_score_agency}. A degree passed with a first or an upper second, or a diploma or certificate with a distinction: {work_score_honours}. A master's degree: {work_score_master}. - A criminal record (a conviction, or a night in a cell; a ticket is not one) takes {work_score_record}. - The city's economy: {work_score_boom} more in a boom, {work_score_slowdown} less in a slowdown, {work_score_recession} less in a recession. In summer the graduates are looking too, and a first rung post takes {work_score_summer} off. # From the score to an offer - Two steps, each with the day's luck. The screening: your score, give or take up to {work_screen_luck}, must reach {work_screen} for an invitation. The interview: your score, give or take up to {work_interview_luck}, must reach {work_offer} for an offer. - Chance of an offer is the share of all that luck which passes both steps. A vacancy is marked open to you only where some luck would do; otherwise its box says how many more skill points you need first, and Apply says so too. - The luck of each step is fixed when you apply: loading a save does not change the answer. After a no, the same post at that employer takes an application from you again {work_reapply_days} days later. - With The reason for a rejection on, the no says how many points short you were, or that your score was enough and the luck went the other way. - To raise your chance: more points of the post's skills (a course, homework, the work), a course passed well, time in the profession, good references, a better name, a friend's word, the recruitment office, or a better time in the economy. A post a rung lower asks fewer points. # What a post pays - Each rung has its own rate, the figure in the list above. A post pays it by the kind of employer: a rival's business {work_rival_pay} more, a tech company {work_tech_pay} more, the public sector {work_public_pay} less. - Then by how short the city is of people in that field, from the jobs on offer against the people looking for one (the labour market of the Jobs board): {work_shortage_least} to {work_shortage_most} of it. A rival's ad on the Jobs board may add a little more. - The offer is {work_offer_pay_least} to {work_offer_pay_most} of the post's rate: the higher they scored you, the more. You can then ask for more (see "An offer" below). - Every rate is written at the start's prices and moves with the city's prices. Once in the job, reviews, rises and promotions raise it (see Working life). # The interview - The invitation sets it {work_interview_after} days later on a weekday, at an hour from {work_interview_from} to {work_interview_to}. The application's box on the Applications tab names the day, the hour and the place, and a notification comes an hour before. - The place: at the employer, inside its building or by its door; or by video from a home of yours, for a post worked from home. - It can be begun from {work_interview_early} minutes before its hour until {work_interview_late} minutes after. Open the application on the Applications tab and press Attend the interview; if it is the wrong hour or place, the box says so. - At the employer you walk in at the door, the {work_interview_minutes} minutes pass behind a black screen with the game's skip, and you come back out at the same door. By video you sit down at your computer at home, with working internet; with no computer at home it is held where you stand. - Leave it part way and it can still be attended within its window. Miss it and the invitation lapses. If your internet provider has an outage over a video interview, the employer moves it to the next weekday at the same hour. # Where the vacancies come from - About {work_openings} vacancies are open at a time, more in a boom and fewer in a slowdown or a recession, each for {work_opening_least} to {work_opening_most} days. Most are first rungs; the top seats come only through search firms. - They are at the city's own businesses of the right kind, your rivals', the city's tech companies, and the hospitals, the school and the council. - Your rivals' ads on the Jobs board of the Open Roles app are vacancies too: one you take is filled. - While you have no job, the city keeps {work_reach} first posts open in the professions you could be offered one in now, so a course passed is soon a vacancy to apply to. - With {work_friends} friends or more, about {work_referral_share} of new vacancies come with a friend's word. A contact who holds a position can also give you a job lead (see Networking). # The recruitment office - The game's recruitment agencies, such as Anderson Recruitment Corp., are the recruitment offices. Go inside one, open the Jobs tab of the Career app and press Register with the recruitment office. It costs nothing. - For {work_agency_days} days you see {work_agency_more} more vacancies, and each application has {work_score_agency} on its score. The Jobs tab says until when; register again inside one to carry on. With Recruitment office reminder on, a notification says so on the last day. # Applying, and an offer - Up to {work_live} applications at once. Withdraw takes one back. - An offer stands for {work_offer_days} days. Ask for 5% more or Ask for 10% more up to {work_asks} times: the higher they scored you, the likelier a yes, and a large ask, or a second one, can lose the offer. Taking it while in a job means working your notice first. # Working - A working day is worked at your own desk, as the game's own job at El Gato Food Market is: go to the employer, click your desk and press Start working on the game's work panel, with its fast forward and skip. It is the same desk every working day: a desk with a computer for office work, the till, counter or station a business works at, a desk at the nurses' station, the teacher's desk or a service desk. Where the building has none, one is set up for you. The My job page says where it is and can set it as your destination. - A working day starts from {work_early} minutes before its hour until {work_late} minutes after. On a day worked from home (every day remote, Mondays and Fridays hybrid), click your computer, with the internet on, and press Start the working day beside Pass Time to sit down at it and work. After {work_late_after} minutes it is late. - The day is passed as the game's own job is and pays by the minute. Under {work_counted} of it worked is a missed day: a warning, and {work_warnings} warnings are the sack. A day off sick is excused. So is a day from home you could not start because your internet provider had an outage: no pay, no missed day, no warning, and your boss texts to say so. No internet plan, one not yet connected or one cut off for an unpaid bill is no excuse. An hour into a day you have not started, your boss texts you, as the game's own employer does, and the warnings come in the boss's texts. - The game takes no tax from wages. The student loan takes {work_loan_share} of pay over {work_loan_threshold} an hour. - Work raises the post's two skills. Hand in notice to leave with a reference, or walk out with a poor one. - While you work, your own businesses carry on as they do whenever you are away: give one a manager of the game's and it is run for you.

reallife_guide_careers_life: # Your first promotion, step by step - Step 1: work every working day of the job. Attendance is half of each review, lateness costs a little, and {work_warnings} missed days are the sack. A day off sick, or a day from home lost to your internet provider's outage, is excused. - Step 2: your first review comes {life_review_days} days after you start, and another every {life_review_days} days after it. A 4 or a 5 can bring a promotion. - Step 3: you also need the time at your rank and the points and qualifications of the rung above. Pick your profession on the Professions tab of the Career app to see its ladder. Work raises the post's two skills; a course or a certificate in the Campus app gives the rest. - Step 4: with all of it at a review you are promoted, with at least {life_promote} more pay. You can also apply for a vacancy a rung up: experience counts in the employer's score. # Reviews - Every {life_review_days} days your employer reviews you and rates you 1 to 5: half of it is turning up (lateness costs a little), then your skills against the post, overtime, how you stand with colleagues, the boss's manner and burnout. - A 3 brings a rise of {life_rise_half}, a 4 {life_rise} and a bonus of {life_bonus_4} days' pay, a 5 {life_rise_top} and {life_bonus_5} days' pay, at most {life_rises} rises at one rank. {life_low_runs} ratings of 1 in a row and you are let go; a 3 or better clears the warnings and the run. - With a 4 or a 5, time at the rank and the skills and qualifications of the rung above, you are promoted: at least {life_promote} more. Promotions are posted about on Flare. - Between reviews you can ask for a rise of {life_ask} once every {life_ask_days} days: the better the last rating, the likelier a yes. # The working week - After a full day you can work {life_overtime} hours late: click your desk again, or your computer on a day worked from home, and press Work late. More than {life_long_week} hours in a week builds burnout; days off ease it. Too much and the doctor signs you off for a day or two. - Your boss is a mentor (the work teaches more), a driver of results (overtime counts twice), a micromanager (lateness counts twice) or hands-off. - Now and then an office matter comes up. Answer it within {life_matter_days} days, or the second answer is taken for you. # Moving on - From the third rung, with a good review, search firms come with an offer {life_poach_premium} over your pay, a rung up where there is one. - In a slowdown or a recession posts are cut, never in the public sector: notice, severance of {life_severance} week's pay a year of service ({life_severance_least} at least), then unemployment benefit of {life_benefit_share} of your last week's pay ({life_benefit_most} at most) for {life_benefit_weeks} weeks. If the business you work for closes or is bought, you are laid off that hour with redundancy pay and a good reference, and nothing is held against you. # Pay beyond the wage - At a tech company, {life_options} share options for each rung above the first, a quarter of them yours every {life_vest_days} days, sold at a price that follows the city's economy. - The pension takes {life_pension_own} of pay and the employer adds {life_pension_employer} ({life_pension_public} in the public sector); the pot grows {life_pension_growth} a year. Retire from {life_retire} (or {life_retire_early} with {life_retire_cut} less) and it pays a day over {life_pension_years} years. # The top of a rival's company - Rise to the top seats of a rival's business and you take a share of its week's takings: {life_share_chief} as its chief executive, {life_share_exec} on its other top seats. - A business of your own in the same trade is a conflict of interest. Declare it and the top seats of that employer are closed to you; leave it undeclared and it may come out, which is dismissal for misconduct, a mark against your integrity and a story in the City Ledger.

reallife_guide_careers_own: # Freelance contracts - Clients of the city offer contracts in your profession now and then, up to {own_contracts} at once: hours of work for a fee of {own_freelance} of the profession's rate an hour. An offer stands for {own_offer_days} days. - Work on a contract in stints at home, or inside an office business of yours; a trade's work is done at the client's building. Late work is paid {own_late} less, and a client who waits a week past the day gives up. - A contract of yours that does not allow side work means each stint may be noticed ({own_side}): a warning, as a missed day is. # A practice of your own - With the qualification (the bar for law, chartered status for accountancy, architecture and engineering), open a practice from the Own work tab of the Career app: registration from {own_register_least} ({own_register_law} for law). - A practice's contracts pay {own_practice} of the rate, {own_office} more from an office of yours, and come more often the better its name, which rises with each delivery on time and falls with a late one. # Leaving to found a company - From the second rung of a tech profession, hand in your notice to found a company, alone or with up to {own_colleagues} colleagues. Start a tech firm from the game's own list within {own_colleagues_days} days and they join its payroll. - At a pitch the venture firms count your record: the rungs you reached, the years and your name, up to {own_founder_most} more. # A restraint clause - From the third rung a contract has a restraint clause that binds for {own_restraint_days} days after leaving. Take your colleagues ({own_claim_colleagues} chance) or work for yourself in the same field ({own_claim_field}) and the old employer may file a claim of {own_claim_weeks} weeks of your pay, {own_claim_colleague} more for each colleague, heard by the courts.

reallife_guide_careers_degrees: # The university - Hudson City University has a permanent building of its own at {degrees_address} in Midtown, the same in every game: an office building kept off the market for it, its name lit on the front. In an older game where a player or a business has that building, the university is meanwhile in the largest free office building, or, with none free, its classes are joined at the door of Manhattan Business School; it moves to its own building for good once that is free. Inside it are the classrooms of Manhattan Business School on several floors, five courses to a floor. Choose the floor at its door; a sign over each classroom door names its course. The door opens the game's study panel for that course: to attend its class or sit its exam when one is on, or to say when the next class is, Not enrolled, Completed or Free classroom. The mark over a door shows a class within the hour, a course you are on, or one you have passed. Nursing is taught on the wards of the city's hospitals and clinics. - Degrees: {degrees_list}. - After a degree: {degrees_after}. - Part time, a degree's classes are {degrees_part_time}; several can be followed online from home with working internet, and their exams are sat at the school. # Professional certificates - {degrees_certs}. - Each is studied at home in pieces, then examined at the school within {degrees_window} days. They are the same certificates the professions' staff sit, and the posts that ask for them read yours. # Exams and classes - A degree's mark gives its class: {degrees_pass} a third, {degrees_lower} a lower second, {degrees_upper} an upper second, {degrees_first} a first. A first or an upper second is with honours, and employers notice. # Fees, grants and the loan - A degree's fee is paid in {degrees_parts} instalments: at the start, a third of the way and two thirds of the way. One that cannot be paid stops the classes until it is. - Grants: {degrees_merit} off after a distinction or a first, {degrees_need} off with less than {degrees_need_cash} in hand, and the council's grants policy adds a subsidy of {degrees_council} or a surcharge of the same. {degrees_grant_most} off at most. - A diploma or a degree can be paid by the student loan instead, up to {degrees_loan_most} owed. It costs {degrees_loan_rate} a year and is taken from a professional's pay: {degrees_loan_share} of what an hour pays over {degrees_loan_threshold}. It is an account on your credit file. # Graduation day - A degree passed is celebrated on the Saturday after, at {degrees_ceremony} at the university. Attend and the day lifts you, Flare has a post for you to make and the City Ledger prints it; miss it and the degree is yours all the same.

The college fund pays what it can and you pay the rest; they graduate a degree later with a class that follows how close you are and their school. # Tutoring - With {family_tutor_least} points or more in a subject you can tutor it from home online, {family_tutor_hours} hours a session, {family_tutor_per_day} a day between {family_tutor_from} and {family_tutor_to}: from {family_tutor_rate} an hour to {family_tutor_top} for a subject at 100.
