reallife_changes_006_1: Fixed: getting out of the driving school's car after a lesson or a test could fail with the game's warning that there was no room to get out, and leave you held against the side of the car until the game was restarted. The school now names a place beside the car that you can walk away from, and finishes the exit itself if anything stops it half way. Fixed: accidents came one after another. At the default setting there is now about one near you for every 32 game hours you spend in the street, where there were nearly three a game day, and fewer in the small hours, when the road is quiet. Rain, storms, mist and ice still bring more, and each step of 'How often accidents happen' now brings half as many again. The Guide gives the figures for your setting. Fixed: at an accident the driver who caused it was handcuffed even after staying and calling an ambulance. A driver who stays is now questioned by an officer and given a ticket, and only a driver who runs for it is chased and, if caught, arrested. Permadeath and hunger: with Permadeath on, going without food is now a danger. After a day with your hunger bar empty you feel weak, after two you tire faster, after three you are starving, and from four days it can be fatal, rarely and never while you sleep or are in hospital. Eating anything ends it. Rental income: a new option in the Property settings sets the rent your buildings earn, the units you let yourself and the buildings the game lets for you, from 50% to 300% (150% on the Relaxed preset, 80% on Hardcore). Asking rents, offers and renewals move with it, so your buildings stay let.
reallife_changes_006_2: Fixed: after a night in hospital, or any time the game skipped ahead, the game's card over something that had been removed meanwhile kept looking for it, filling the game's log with errors every frame and slowing the game. The card is now put away when what it points at is gone.
reallife_changes_007_0: Courses and skills: the city's courses beyond the game's own. Short courses at Manhattan Business School (first aid, barista, bartending, a forklift ticket, a security licence, a driving refresher that takes penalty points off, bookkeeping, customer service) and online ones (a coding bootcamp, digital marketing), and diplomas for electricians, plumbers, carpenters, chefs, hairdressers, beauticians, care workers and IT support. Each has a timetable of classes on set days and hours, homework at home and an exam with a grade, failing and retakes, in the new Campus app and the Planner. They teach skills of your own, 0 to 100, that grow with study and fade a little without use. Professional jobs: work as anything you are qualified for. Twenty-five professions, from developer, data scientist, accountant, lawyer, architect, civil engineer, nurse and teacher to marketing, banking, management up to chief executive, the council, the trades, kitchens, salons, bars, door security and warehouses, each a ladder judged on your own skills and qualifications. The city's businesses, your rivals' among them, its tech companies and the public sector advertise posts, and your rivals' ads on the jobs board are posts too. Apply, attend the interview at the employer or by video, haggle over the offer, then work your days at the office or from home, paid by the minute, in the new Career app with your CV. Working life: reviews twice a year with a rating, rises, bonuses and promotions up to the top seats, a boss with a manner of their own, office matters to answer, overtime and burnout, search firms that come for good people, redundancy in a downturn with severance and unemployment benefit, share options at tech companies, a pension and retirement. Rise to the top of a rival's company for a share of its takings, and declare a business of your own in the same trade or risk being dismissed for it. Working for yourself: freelance contracts from the city's clients, worked at home or at the client's; a practice of your own once qualified, whose name brings more work; side work that an exclusive contract may catch. Leave a tech profession to found a company, bring colleagues to your new firm and pitch with a founder's record the venture firms count, and mind a restraint clause: break it and your old employer takes you to court. University and degrees: Hudson City University in one of the city's large office buildings, with fourteen degrees from computer science, law, nursing (on the hospital wards) and architecture to teaching, then an MBA, an MSc, the Legal Practice Course and a teaching certificate, and twelve professional certificates studied at home (cloud, security, project management, chartered accountant, the bar exam and more). Degrees are classed from a third to a first, fees come in instalments with merit and need grants and the council's subsidy, a student loan on your credit file is repaid from your pay, and graduation day has its ceremony, a Flare post and a story in the City Ledger. Family and the rest: a grown child is offered a place at the university, paid from the college fund and by you, and graduates with a class of their own; tutoring from home in your best subject; a Training Academy of your own as a business type whose staff teach the city's students, and courses at half the fee for your staff while you have one; degrees for your professionals sponsored by the business. The banking licence now asks for a qualified person, and Permadeath's obituary names your best qualification and your career.

reallife_changes_007_1: Bus rides now use the game's own activity panel once you are seated and the doors close. Let it run and the bus drives its route through the city in real time, calling at every stop on the way, where people get on and off, until it reaches yours. Use the panel's fast forward to ride at the game's fast speed, or skip to pass the rest of the ride under a fade as before. Move, or press the panel's button, to get off at the next stop; nothing is given back. A save during the ride puts you at the last stop the bus called at. A ride with a change of bus still passes under a fade. Fixed: a pole, a bin or a bench by a bus stop could stop you reaching the bus's door. Street furniture on the kerb by the doors and on the way to them from the stop is now cleared, you are walked to a place by the door that can be reached, and as a last resort you get on by the middle door and walk up to the validator to pay.
reallife_changes_007_2: Police stations are furnished inside. The walls, the floors and much of the furniture come from the game's own office designs for that very unit, with waiting chairs and a queue at the front desk, desks with computers, lockers, a briefing screen with a row of chairs, a break table by the coffee machine, and the holding cell. Officers sit at the desks typing, take a break, walk between the rooms and come on and off shift through the door, and now and then a member of the public waits on the chairs. The way to the front desk and to the cell is always kept clear. The option 'Furnished police stations' switches it off.

reallife_guide_trouble_update:
# After a game update
- When Big Ambitions is updated, the pieces of the game this mod relies on can change. The mod checks every one of them each time the game starts, before any of its features runs. A part whose piece has changed switches itself off, and everything else keeps working.
- If your game is older than the build this version of the mod is made for, Build {game_build}, the notice says so in the main menu too, and names the parts that are off or work without what it lacks. The section above says how to update the game in Steam.
- If anything is switched off, a notice names the parts when you load a city, and the options page says so after the names of the features concerned. Under Troubleshooting, Diagnostics, the button 'What a game update switched off' lists them, with the game's build and the build this version of the mod is made for.
- Your saves are safe. What the mod has saved for a part that is off is kept as it is, and comes back when the mod is updated. A saved record the mod cannot read is kept in the save untouched, never written over.
- A part that meets a missing piece of the game only later stops at once and says so once, instead of failing every frame. If one feature runs into the same error again and again, it switches itself off until you load a game again, says so, and clears away what it had in the street. The rest of the mod and the game carry on.
- Player.log names exactly what changed, in its lines that begin 'Game build' and 'Game contract'. An update of the mod reaches you through the Steam Workshop, or as a new setup on the mod's GitHub page; if there is none yet, tell us what the notice said on the mod's Discord or Steam page.

reallife_changes_007_6: More bus lines: up to 16 routes between the subway stations, laid so that every station has three lines where the roads allow, gathered on the avenues, where the lines share their stops. A stop's panel lists every line that calls there with its next bus, and the city map offers each stop with the line to take and, where one is needed, the change of bus. More buses: every line runs to a timetable, every 36 minutes on the main lines at the rush hours, less often in the evening, and between 01:00 and 05:00 only the main lines run; the bus of the next line can follow close behind. A journey with a change of bus is driven on both buses with the ride panel, with a walk to the second stop where it is not the same one, on one fare. You board by the nearer of the bus's two doors, tapping in at a validator by each. In a Going Public session the ride is driven in real time too, on the host's machine, with no fast forward. Fixed: a bus could stand still in the road and vanish, at the end of its line or when it was let go where you could see it. A bus now drives on out of sight before it is taken away, and never appears where you can see it or near you. Fixed: Delayed showed for buses that were on time. The time shown is now the timetable's, and the bus is sent so as to keep it; Delayed shows only when a bus is held up, with its new time.

reallife_guide_interiors_about: How your business looks counts: walls and floors, decor, wear and cleanliness change customers, prices, staff and your name. BizMan has an Interior tab.
reallife_guide_interiors: # What counts - Interior design: the game's own score for your walls and floors, 0 to 100, set in the interior designer. - Decor: what you place, sorted by the game's own kinds of item: art and ornaments, plants, lighting, music and speakers, rugs and floor decor, then furniture and fittings, which count for a little only. The first of each item counts in full, each further copy of the same item {in_repeat}% of the one before, {in_repeat_most} copies at most. - Each kind fills only its share: art {in_cap_art}%, plants {in_cap_greenery}%, lighting {in_cap_lighting}%, rugs {in_cap_floor}%, music {in_cap_audio}%, furniture {in_cap_furniture}%, fittings {in_cap_equipment}%. A full score needs several kinds, and each different item over {in_variety_from} adds a point, {in_variety_most} at most. - A bigger place needs more: {in_target_least} points up to {in_target_from} square metres, one more for each {in_target_sqm} square metres over that, {in_target_most} at most. - Overall: {in_interior_share}% the interior design, the rest the decor. # Wear and dirt - Finishes and decor wear {in_wear_day}% a day, up to {in_wear_dirt}% more on a dirty floor, and half as fast while the cleaning service looks after the place. - At full wear both scores lose {in_wear_penalty}%. Under cleanliness {in_dirt_from} they lose up to {in_dirt_penalty}% more. - Refresh the finishes from the Interior tab: {in_refresh_sqm} a square metre, {in_refresh_least} to {in_refresh_most}. If a refresh cannot be done, the tab says why. Redecorating in the interior designer so that its score rises by {in_redecorate} or more halves the wear. - A health inspector takes {in_worn_points} off the cleanliness of a place worn {in_worn}% or more. # What it does - Prices: over the district's standard the district bears up to {in_bears_over}% more of your price before customers find it dear. Under it the price is never judged more harshly. - Brands: a shop counts up to {in_brand_most} points more or less in its brand's standards, one for each {in_brand_per} over or under 50. - Standing: a shop moves its customers' figure up to {in_standing_most} points, one for each {in_standing_per} over or under 50. - Staff: plants (two points with {in_plants_two} or more), good light and a rest corner give up to {in_comfort_most} points of comfort. Staff paid fairly settle that many points higher, and a professional's morale heads {in_morale}% higher for each point. - Offices: your best office at {in_office_one} or over adds a point to what candidates on the jobs board think of you, two at {in_office_two}. A firm whose office scores over {in_bid_from} weighs its bids up to {in_bid_most}% better. An office that takes clients is booked more of them an hour ahead: {in_decor_most}% more at an overall score of 100 by default, up to {in_decor_top}% with the decor's slider at double, never more than its staffed workstations left free. - News: a business at {in_striking} or over may be in the City Ledger and gives you a Flare draft; one worn {in_shabby_wear}% or {in_shabby_short} points short of its standard may be in the paper too. Once in {in_story_days} days at most. # The Interior tab - In BizMan, beside Marketing. On the left the scores, each kind of decor's share, wear and cleanliness. On the right four pages, turned with the arrows at the top: what each figure is doing and what to add next, with the button that refreshes the finishes; every placed item that counts, by kind, with its points; today's customers by where they came from, as the game counts them (the street's traffic, your marketing, interiors and decor, the rest of the mod, and Meaningful Ambience if it is on); and the game's own rules for the business, what its customers want and what it needs to open, each met or missing with the items that meet it. - The figures are worked out each morning, for your own businesses and offices only. # How strong each part is - In the options four sliders set the parts, each from 0% (off) to {in_strength_top}% (double); the figures on these pages are at 100%, the default. - District standards: what falling short costs and what being over it brings. - Customers drawn by decor: customers drawn by decor, and an office's extra clients. - What a nicer place lets you charge: the price the district bears and the bigger baskets. - Wear and refreshing: how fast the finishes wear. - Two switches beside them: Brands, Standing and the news turns the brand, Standing and news effects on or off, and Staff, hiring and bids the staff's comfort, the candidates and the bids. - The presets set the sliders: Relaxed is gentler and more generous, Realistic keeps the defaults, Hardcore is stricter and slower to reward. Bigger baskets is on in all of them. # Never a sharp drop - At the defaults the interior costs an established business {in_bound}% of its customers at most, and nothing of its prices or its baskets. A complaint it brings counts inside the same {in_bound}%. - Every effect on customers and takings comes in over {in_ramp} days: from a new business's first day, and for a business already trading from the day this version first reads the save. - The Interior tab shows what its interior does to each business today, in figures and with the reason.
reallife_guide_interiors_standard_about: Each district expects its own standard; falling short costs customers and brings complaints.
reallife_guide_interiors_standard: # The standard - Each district expects a standard, from {in_standard_least} in the poorest (income {in_income_least}) to {in_standard_most} in the richest ({in_income_most}), rising with its income in the city's economy. It is never under the game's own minimum for the district, as in Midtown. - Your overall figure is held against it. A new business gets {in_grace} days to fit out: falling short costs it nothing until then, and being over counts at once. Every effect comes in over {in_ramp} days. # Short of it - 1% fewer customers for each whole {in_short_points} points short, {in_short_most}% at most at the default strength and {in_bound_top}% at double. Never no customers. - From {in_complaint_from} points short a customer's complaint may start: {in_complaint_per}% a day for each point, {in_complaint_most}% at most. A complaint costs {in_complaint_dip}% of customers for a few days and counts inside the {in_bound}%: while it lasts the shortfall gives way. Under the default strength there are no complaints. # Over it - 1% more customers for each {in_over_points} points over, {in_over_most}% at most. With decor's part the interior adds or takes {in_footfall_most}% at most. - Bigger baskets: each customer takes more of what you sell and have on the shelves, by the size of their order. Nothing at the standard, rising to its most at an overall figure of {in_basket_full}: {in_basket_poor}% more products where the standard is lowest, {in_basket_rich}% where it is highest, {in_basket_middle}% in a district of middle income. The whole products are certain, and what is left over is a chance of one more. Never an entrance fee or a ticket, a service only once a customer, and nothing while the business sells nothing. What a nicer place lets you charge sizes it as Meaningful Interiors' strength sizes its own. On at first. # With Meaningful Interiors - While that mod is switched on it sets each district's minimum and adds to baskets itself, so this part stays off. The Interior tab shows its minimum.
reallife_guide_interiors_decor_about: Good decor brings a few more customers each day.
reallife_guide_interiors_decor: # Decor and customers - Decor brings up to {in_decor_most}% more customers each day by default, {in_decor_top}% with Customers drawn by decor at double, in step with the decor score after wear and dirt. With the district's standard the interior adds or takes {in_footfall_most}% at most, beside what the mod's other parts add. - While a business sells nothing (closed, nothing on its shelves, nobody on shift, or its last {in_recent} customers all turning its prices down) its interior brings it nobody extra and adds nothing to a basket. It starts again once something can sell. Falling short of the standard still costs. # With Meaningful Ambience - While that mod is switched on it adds customers for decor itself, so this part stays off. The scores, prices, wear, staff and the tab carry on, and when the day's customers are drawn again the hour under way is kept, so the customers that mod adds for it stay.

reallife_changes_008_0: Interiors and decor matter. How your business looks now counts. The game's interior design score for walls and floors and a decor score from what you place, sorted by the game's own kinds of item, are worked out each morning. Each district expects its own standard, rising with its wealth: short of it you get fewer customers and complaints, never none; over it a few more, and the district bears a little more of your price. Decor brings a few more customers. Finishes wear and get dirty; refresh them from the new Interior tab in BizMan, which shows every figure and what to add next. A well kept place lifts its brand, your standing and your staff, helps an office's hiring and a firm's bids, and can make the City Ledger. An extra product in customers' baskets can be switched on in the options. With Meaningful Interiors or Meaningful Ambience switched on, the parts they already do stay off. Fixed: a Flare post about a graduation was dropped when the save was read. Fixed: with Meaningful Ambience on, the customers it had added for the hour were lost whenever this mod redrew a business's day. They now stay.

reallife_opt_tip_tech_site_rooms: Your data centres get rows of racks, cooling, power and status lights by their racks and redundancy, technicians at work, and stores and a workbench round the hall.
reallife_opt_tip_tech_site_hq: The city's tech companies each have an office building, named on the map, with their jobs there. Inside, the whole floor is their offices, with staff at work.
reallife_opt_tip_tech_site_cloud: Your data centres carry your cloud's name on a sign outside, with a security booth and a barrier where there is room, and are on the map.
reallife_opt_tip_tech_site_offices: An office your tech firm runs in gets a server closet, a developer's desk and a whiteboard where a wall has room, never in your furniture's way.
reallife_guide_tech_sites_about: Server rooms inside your data centres, the city's tech companies in a few shared towers, a whole floor fitted out for each, your data centres' signs outside, and fittings in your tech offices.
reallife_guide_tech_sites:
# Server rooms
- A data centre in one of your warehouses is fitted out inside: rows of server racks, a row of AI accelerator racks once you have them, the network core, cooling units, battery cabinets, cable trays over the rows and a raised floor.
- The rows grow with the racks you buy. A higher tier packs the hall tighter and adds cooling and power to spare. Up to {sites_most} racks are shown; a larger data centre shows a full hall.
- The racks face onto cold aisles and back onto hot aisles, and every aisle stays clear to walk. Nothing goes on or in front of your own furniture.
- The status lights blink while you are inside. In an outage they turn amber and red and the room dims; without power or a connection they turn red.
- With technicians on the staff, one or two of them walk the aisles.
- The rest of the warehouse's floor has stores with shelving, deliveries on pallets waiting to be racked, a workbench, a staff desk and a break corner. They keep clear of your own furniture and of the vehicle door.
# Tech companies
- The city's {sites_companies} tech companies share {sites_towers} of the city's largest empty office buildings, {sites_floors} to a tower, a floor each. A tower's name is on the building's card, the map and the GPS, and the search finds it by its name or by any of its companies'.
- At a tower's door, choose a floor: each names its company, and the floor of the company you work for says so. The game's own door takes you to your employer's floor, or the first. Inside, the panel by the entrance is the lift to the other floors.
- Each floor is its company's: the lobby with a reception desk, a wall in the company's colours with its name, seating, plants and screens; then open-plan desks with computers, meeting rooms with a table and a screen, a kitchen, a lounge, printers, a server closet and plants. The game's own office designs for the building furnish most of it.
- Staff work at the desks and a few walk about, a receptionist is at the desk and now and then a visitor waits. Every way from the door stays clear.
- A job at one of these companies is on its floor, and your desk is there.
- A tower is not to rent, buy or take over: BizMan says whose it is. A building you or another player already rented or owned stays so, and the tower moves to another. Every other office building is to let as the game has it.
# Your data centres from outside
- A sign with your cloud's name stands by the door, with a security booth, and a barrier and fence by the vehicle door where there is room.
- Your cloud is on the city map. A hyperscaler shows every region.
# Tech offices
- An office your tech firm runs in gets a server closet, a developer's desk and a whiteboard where a wall has room. They never stand in your furniture's way.
# Good to know
- All of this is only to be seen. None of it is saved, none of it is your furniture, and it does not count towards what your furniture is worth.
- In a Going Public session everybody sees the same towers and floors, and nobody else's buildings change.

reallife_changes_009_0: The tech sector has buildings of its own. A data centre is fitted out inside with rows of racks, cooling, power and blinking status lights by its tier and its racks, with technicians walking the aisles, and outside it carries your cloud's name. The city's tech companies each have a headquarters on the map with a lobby to walk into, and their jobs are there. An office your tech firm runs in gets a few fittings where there is room.
reallife_changes_009_1: Fixed: a nicer interior now sells more to each customer, as Meaningful Interiors does. At Standard, with an overall figure of 85, each order takes up to 10% more products in the poorest districts, 8.1% in a district of middle income and 6% in the richest, and it is on by default. Decor brings up to 10% more customers by default, as Meaningful Ambience does. If you had the old defaults (no extra products, decor 5%), they move to the new ones once; any other choice stays.

They are now off the market: BizMan says whose they are, and they are left out of the real estate list and the map's rows of units to let. reallife_changes_009_7: Fixed: the city bus could stop short of its stop and stand there for good, the stop's panel saying DELAYED and nobody able to get on. Held up near the stop, by a car, somebody in the road or you, it now opens its doors where it stands, and a car of the traffic that waits for the bus while the bus waits for it is let go. Fixed: at a narrow stop the bus braked for people waiting at the kerb. Fixed: an old file left in the mod's folder by an earlier version could dress the city bus in the wrong textures, fuel price boards and fire engine lettering. The mod now ignores such files, and the steps for installing from the zip say to delete the old folder first.
reallife_changes_009_8: Fixed: stutters every few seconds in the street, and short freezes the first time traffic met a crossing, the first time you went into a building and the first time a bus stop was cleared. The mod searched the whole city for other characters' hair every five seconds, and for the crossings, the building's panel and the street furniture the first time it needed them; it now does this only behind a loading screen or the dark screen at a door.

reallife_guide_markets_bots: # Orders that wait - On a company's page in the Stocks app the order ticket has four kinds: At the market, Limit, Stop loss and Take profit. Each lasts For the day or Until cancelled, {mkt_good_till} market days at most, and the Orders tab lists them with Cancel the order for each. - A limit buys at its price or under, or sells at its price or over, once the market reaches it, taking at most {bot_participation} of a step's volume at a time. - A stop loss is on shares you hold: it sells them once the bid falls to its price, or buys back shares sold short once the offer rises to it. From then it is an order at the market and goes at the market's next price, the price the step ends on, less what its size moves it. After a fast fall, or a night that opens under it, that is under the stop: a stop limits a loss, it does not promise a price. - A take profit sells what you hold at its price or better once the bid rises to it, or buys back a short at its price or under. - A stop loss and a take profit only ever close what you still hold, and hold nothing back from your other orders. When nothing is left to close, the other one is cancelled. - An order at the market for more than one order's most is worked: with 'Worked orders and larger bond purchases' on, the ticket says so, and Work it places it. From the market's next step it takes a slice of each step's own trading, {mkt_order_share} of it at most, at the market's price with the move its size makes, so about one order's most a day, until it is done, your cash or the shares run out, the most you may hold is reached, or you cancel it. Its slices move the price together as one order of their size would, the least commission is paid once, and it never expires. The Orders tab shows what is done and what is left, and a notification tells each day's part. A worked sale only sells shares you hold. On a cash account its money is settled once a market day: a purchase holds what a day of it costs, with a tenth more, at its first slice of the day, and what is not spent comes back at the close; a sale's takings, after the commission, are paid at each close. Your other purchases and charges in the Stocks app still use that money first, taking back only what they need; anywhere else it is yours again at the close, or at once when you cancel the order. A margin account holds nothing. # Trading bots - Four firms run bots you can hire on the Bots tab, one each. {bot_trend} follows trends: it buys while the close is over its {bot_trend_fast}-day average and that is over the {bot_trend_slow}-day one, and sells under the {bot_trend_slow}-day average. {bot_reversion} buys falls: an RSI over {bot_rsi_days} days under {bot_rsi_in} while the close is over its {bot_reversion_filter}-day average; it sells when the RSI passes {bot_rsi_out} or after {bot_reversion_days} market days. {bot_momentum} holds for a month the companies, small ones too, that gained most over {bot_momentum_days} market days up to {bot_momentum_skip} market days ago. {bot_income} holds the highest dividends of companies whose last {bot_income_quarters} quarters made a profit that covered them. - Pick a firm to see its terms, set its bot, type the capital and Hire it. A bot trades with your own cash, up to the capital you give it, {bot_capital_least} at least, out of the cash your other bots do not already have to trade. Every purchase and sale is yours: in your transactions and the Finance app as your own trades are, at the same prices, spread and commission, and its trades move prices as yours do. Keep the cash in your account: a purchase your cash cannot pay for is not made. - While a bot runs, its capital can be changed on the first page of its settings, {bot_change_least} or more at a time. Add capital gives it more of your cash to trade, and Take out takes some of its money not in shares off it. Nothing is sold either way and it keeps what it holds. Money added goes into its holdings, up to its size each, and into new ones as its rules buy them, from the next session's first step; if your cash is short of a purchase then, it tries once more the next market day. The most it may lose is then reckoned on the new capital, the money is never counted as profit, and its fee is a share of its worth for the days the money was there. Money added to a bot that has lost moves the point where it stops further away, as its loss is measured on all the capital given. No more can be taken out than leaves it {bot_capital_least} and keeps it over the point where it stops by its limit's share of what it holds in shares, so the next ordinary move cannot stop it. - Settings: how it trades, which can be changed at any time: how much of its worth goes into each holding ({bot_sizes}), a stop on each holding ({bot_stops} under what it cost, or none), and the most it may lose ({bot_losses} of its capital). Under that it sells everything at the market and stops; a gap can take it further under. - It decides at each close on what anyone could see by then, and trades at the next session's first step at the market's price of that moment. It buys nothing worth less than {bot_trade_least}, nothing listed for fewer than {bot_listed_days} days, no company under a bid and, on its strategy's whole market, no player's own company and no rival tycoon's holding. - Settings: the shares it trades: its strategy's whole market, only the companies you pick for it ({bot_picks_most} at most, chosen from your own listed company and those you hold or watch), or only the shares you hold. A holding outside them is sold at the next session. A company you chose is bought whatever its size. - Your own company is traded by the rules its founder deals by: nothing from the last third of a quarter until its results are out, no sale within {bot_own_swing} days of a purchase nor a purchase within them of a sale, your bots' trades and your own together no more than {bot_deal_year} of the company in a game year, your shares and theirs no more than {bot_founder_most} of it, and every bot of yours together no more than {bot_own_volume} of its ordinary day's volume in a day, so that no bot moves its price on its own. A bot holding its shares sells them up before it can be let go. - Settings: its payouts to you: a share of its new profit, from none to all of it a tenth at a time, paid each day, each week or each month. A bot trades your own cash, so what it makes is in your account already: a payout takes that part off what the bot trades with, and the rest stays in the bot. Its profit is what it gained on what it sold and its dividends, less its fees. A loss is carried forward, and nothing is paid until it is made good. What its money not in shares cannot cover waits for the next payout. A weekly payout has a notification, and the month's statement says what it paid. - Each month it takes its fee for the days it traded, a share of its worth ({bot_trend_fee}, {bot_reversion_fee}, {bot_momentum_fee} and {bot_income_fee} for the four in that order, {bot_fee_least} at least), and a share of its profit over its best month's end so far ({bot_trend_share}, {bot_reversion_share}, {bot_momentum_share} and {bot_income_share}). A notification gives its statement. - The Bots tab shows each bot's worth, profit, deepest fall and trades, the Portfolio tab what it holds and History its trades. Sell up sells everything at the next step and stops it. A stopped bot that holds nothing can be started again with Start again, with {bot_capital_least} or more left. Let go takes its fee and its share to date and hands you what it holds as your own. # What to expect - No bot sees tomorrow. The market is a fair bet at every moment, so a bot wins or loses by luck and pays its costs and its fees either way. Over a run of bad days, with large holdings and a wide limit, it can lose most of what it was given. In the mod's own tests no bot beat holding the market. - Nothing about a bot can be changed while the market is catching up with the clock or replaying after a load. - With 'Trading bots' off (options page, under 'The stock market'), none can be hired and every bot is let go, what it held now your own; one holding your own company's shares sells them first, by its founder's rules. - In a Going Public session your bots are your own and trade in the city's market as you do. - The save tools sell what your bots hold at today's price before the mod is removed.

reallife_changes_011_1: Fixed: the mod's companies and institutions no longer have the game's For rent sign outside. Each tech company's headquarters has its own sign and logo in the company's colours, lit after dark like the game's signs. reallife_guide_office_space_about: Some empty shops in the districts with offices are offices to rent while the mod runs, so there is always an office for you.
reallife_guide_office_space: # Why - The two largest office buildings, {offices_kept_1} and {offices_kept_2}, are never taken by the mod: they stay for you to rent or buy, though the game's own businesses and rivals can still open in them. City Utilities takes no office: its desk is at the door of {util_address}, a residential building kept for it. - The mod's own places (the tech companies' headquarters, the police stations, and at times the courthouse or the university) take some of the city's other empty offices, and the game's businesses hold the rest. So while Empty shops as offices is on, some empty shops in the districts with offices are offices. # How many - In every district with offices you can choose between at least {offices_district} offices to let, and between at least {offices_city} across the city. - The game's own empty offices count first. Only as many shops as are short become offices, and never more than half of a district's shops of that kind. - Only shops the game builds the same as its offices are used, so inside it is the game's own office floor. Warehouses stay warehouses. # What you can do there - It is an office everywhere in the game: on the map under offices to let, in BizMan, and at an office's rent and deposit. - Any office business can start there, the tech firms included, with the game's office layouts and the interior designer's office designs. - Once you or anyone else has it, it stays an office. An empty one is a shop again when the game's own offices are enough. # Good to know - The same shops are offices on every computer, so in a Going Public session every player with the mod sees the same offices. Nobody else's building changes. - Your save keeps which of these offices you hold, so one with no business in it yet is still an office after a load. Without the mod each of these is a shop again, and an office business in a shop does not get an office's clients. Prepare this save for removing the mod names any business of yours in one: start it again in one of the game's own offices first. - Switching the option off makes them shops again at once.

Without the mod the game counts each of these buildings as a shop again, and an office business in a shop does not get an office's clients. Before you remove the mod, start each of them again in one of the game's own offices, or close it.
reallife_changes_011_2: Fixed: the mod's buildings took every empty office in the city, so there was none left to rent. The 12 tech companies now share 3 office towers, a floor each, so the mod holds 3 office buildings for them where it held 12, and the rest are to let. Choose a floor at a tower's door, or take the lift inside; a job at one of them is on its company's floor. A building the mod holds is on the market again as soon as its feature is switched off, on a page already open too. Fixed: where a district with offices has fewer than two to let, some of its empty shops are offices while the mod runs, so there are always at least two to choose from.
reallife_changes_011_3: Developer diagnostics: a stutter's line in Player.log now says how long the game waited for the graphics card, how long its own thread ran and how busy the processor was, so a pause caused by another program shows as one.
reallife_changes_011_4: Fixed: the pause the first time you get into a car, and most of the pause just after a save loads, both caused by the mod. The work behind them is now done while the loading screen is still up, or read from lists the game keeps itself, and the logos of the phone's contacts are drawn faster.
reallife_changes_012_0: Ready for game updates: as the game starts, Real Life Overhaul checks every piece of Big Ambitions it relies on, switches off only the parts that stand on a piece the game lacks, and says which in one notice, with how to update the game in Steam when it is the older one. Everything else keeps working, a part that meets a missing piece later stops once instead of failing every frame, and a saved record the mod cannot read is kept in the save untouched.
reallife_changes_012_1: Fixed: a short freeze just as the loading screen goes, when the parts of the mod that read the save all started at the same moment; they now start one after another. reallife_changes_019_1: Developer diagnostics: a stutter's line in Player.log now counts every part of the mod, its work done step by step and what it does when the game announces something (a new hour, a door), so it always names the part of the mod that took the time. Fixed: a short pause the first time an ambulance, a patrol car or a fire engine was sent out in a city, while the sound of its siren was being made; the sounds are now made while the loading screen is still up. Fixed: short hitches when the game was paused, while the mod looked through the whole scene for characters with detailed hair or finished work left over from the loading screen; both now wait for the black screen at a door or a loading screen. Fixed: a hitch the first time one of the mod's own panels opened, while it looked for the game's font. Fixed: short hitches near police stations and at accidents, arrests, road closures and street events, when the mod looked for the nearest lane of a road by going through every one of the city's 19,000 lane points, sometimes dozens of times in one frame; it now looks only near the place, and finds exactly the same lane. Fixed: hitches in the first minute after a save loaded. The roads for the GPS and the buses, the minimap's pictures, the bus routes and the performance options are now prepared while the loading screen is still up, the city's road data is looked for once instead of twice, and the phone's contact pictures are drawn a little at a time. Fixed: a stutter at the stock market's close at 16:00 and its open at 09:30; both are now worked out over a few frames, with exactly the same prices, and after a sleep or a skip the market catches up smoothly. Fixed: heavier frames at midnight and when saving: the tech sector's people, the city's job vacancies, Utilities' accounts and Flare's shops are now looked up directly instead of one by one, the stock market and the tech sector write their save data without piles of throwaway text, and the workers on your job shifts change their looks only when it causes no stutter. Fixed: a heavy frame at the start of each game day, and a smaller one each hour, with many businesses: several parts of the mod each had the game draw a shop's customers again, three or four times over in one frame. Now each shop is drawn again once, only where its footfall really changed, a little each frame within the hour, and the economy reads the day's books once.

reallife_guide_trouble_report:
# Reporting a bug
- Press 'Report a bug', under Start here on the options page or in the Mod settings app on your phone. Say in a sentence or two what went wrong, or leave it empty.
- The mod writes a report to your computer, in the game's data folder under RealLifeOverhaul, Reports: the versions of the mod and the game, your settings, the day and time, the mod's last warnings, the game's log of this session and of the one before, and, while a city is loaded, a picture of the screen. Your Windows user name, Steam ids and the Steam names on the lines known to carry one are taken out. Other names may still be in the log: look through the zip before you post it where everyone can read it. The mod sends nothing. Older reports there are deleted, so it keeps only the last few.
- Its folder then opens with the report as a zip file, and the mod's Discord opens in your browser. Post the zip in #bug-reports and paste the summary the mod copied for you.

reallife_guide_endscale_about: Late in a game, data centres, the cloud, a broadband network and a bank cost hundreds of millions, need crews and upkeep, and earn in proportion.
reallife_guide_endscale: # What it is - Late in a game, the ventures that make billions cost what the real ones do: data centres, the cloud and the hyperscaler, your broadband company and your bank. They need crews and upkeep, and they earn in proportion to what you build. - It has its own switch in the options, The end game at scale, on at first. Off, every figure is as before. The Relaxed preset switches it off. - A data centre or cloud well run pays back what you put in after {es_tech_days_least} to {es_tech_days_most} game days; a broadband network or a bank after {es_years_least} to {es_years_most} of your game's years. The largest builds take the longer end. # Coming to scale - What you buy while the switch is on (racks, a fit-out, a network, a licence, a bank's capital) is at the full scale's price at once. Only the running costs and income come in over the weeks. - A venture you held before the switch comes to scale a step a day over {es_days} days, with a notice on the first day. One started later is at scale at once. Switching it off and on again does not start the weeks again. - What the scale adds to a day's costs is paid after the day's takings and never past your cash, so it never takes you below nothing in one step. What your cash cannot meet is owed to the next day, and the crews it could not pay leave in that share, so the venture does less until it is paid. - Racks bought and networks dug before the scale stay the old kind. Replace old racks, or extend an old district's network, when you are ready. # Crews - Each venture hires its own crews, {es_pace} of what it needs a day. Short of a crew it does as little as {es_working} of its work and fails up to {es_outages} times as often, so a fast build is weak for a few weeks. - These crews are hired and paid by the venture itself. A data centre still needs the technicians or network engineers you hire, one for every {infra_technician} racks, as its own page in the Guide says. # Data centres, the cloud and the hyperscaler - Fitting out costs {es_fit} a square metre by tier. A rack of dense servers costs {es_rack} and sells {es_units} units of compute (the old kind {es_units_old}); an AI rack costs {es_gpu} and sells {es_gpu_units} (the old kind {es_gpu_units_old}). - Upkeep a day: {es_upkeep_rack} a rack and {es_upkeep_gpu} an AI rack for support, spares, transit and licences, and {es_facility} of the fit-out a year for the building and its insurance. Cooling adds {es_cooling} to the racks' power, less at a better tier. - Crews: an operator for every {es_operators} racks or {es_operators_gpu} AI racks, an electrical and cooling engineer for every {es_engineer_kw} kW, {es_guards} security staff and one more for every {es_guard_sqm} square metres, and for the cloud an operations person for every {es_ops_units} units. Their wages are {es_dc_wages} a day. - A rack of the new kind let to the city's companies rents for {es_colo} a month as managed servers; the old kind keeps the old rent and is let first. - The cloud's licence is {es_cloud_licence} a game year. A cloud needs {es_cloud_racks} racks and {es_cloud_cash} in cash; a hyperscaler {es_hyper_racks} racks and {es_hyper_cash}. - The city buys {es_market} times as much compute. A hyperscaler sells to {es_hyper_market} times that, and each region past three adds {es_region_market} times more. # Your broadband company - The city's homes and businesses are {es_bb_market} times as many. The operator's licence with its core network costs {es_bb_licence}; a district's network costs {es_bb_home} a home or business passed ({es_bb_far} in the Hamptons), {es_bb_build} a district. - Upkeep is {es_bb_upkeep} of the network a month, and an installation costs {es_bb_install}. - Crews: a field engineer for every {es_bb_field} connections, a call centre agent for every {es_bb_calls}, and {es_bb_ops} network operations engineers for each district open. They take the place of the old cost per connection. # Your bank - The licence with its systems and branches costs {es_ob_licence}, and the regulator wants {es_ob_capital} of capital. The city's savings and borrowing are {es_ob_pool} times as large. - Crews: a teller for every {es_ob_tellers} of people's savings, a relationship manager for every {es_ob_managers} of businesses' savings, a loan officer for every {es_ob_officers} of loans, and {es_ob_compliance} compliance officers and one more for every {es_ob_compliance_per} the bank holds. Short of them it lends and takes savings more slowly. - Its systems cost {es_ob_systems} a day, and deposit insurance {es_ob_insurance} of the savings a year. - A bank keeps the least capital it was founded under, even if the switch is turned off or on later. - These are a National Bank's figures. reallife_guide_rivals: # What it is - Three tycoons, Space Karen, Bald Luthor and The Zucc, each with a holding company on the stock market. They grow with the city and with you, and once you are rich they move against you. - Nobody moves against you while you are worth less than {rival_tens}. The first rival comes forward then, the second at {rival_hundreds} and the third at {rival_billions}. From {rival_ten_billions} they hit harder still. A player already rich meets them one a day. - Their page is in the Finance app: Rivals and the rich list on the Overview. # How often - One move at a time for all the rivals together. At the Normal strength the next can come {rival_gap_tens} days after the last while you are worth tens of millions, {rival_gap_hundreds} at hundreds of millions, {rival_gap_billions} at billions and {rival_gap_top} at ten billion, up to {rival_jitter} days more. On Ruthless it can be {rival_gap_ruthless}. - Every move is in the City Ledger and on your phone {rival_telegraph} days before it comes, so you can answer first. A move that finds nothing of yours to touch on its day comes to nothing. # Their moves - Buying up a district: the district of your best business. For {rival_property_days} days buildings for sale there cost {rival_property_premium} more (never more than {rival_property_most}), and if you rent there your rent rises by {rival_rent_rise} (never more than {rival_rent_most}, and one buying up at a business at a time). - A business near yours: of the same kind in the same district, for {rival_outlet_days} days: {rival_outlet_dip}% fewer customers at yours of that kind there, {rival_outlet_most}% at most from all of them together, and {rival_outlets_most} open at once at most. - An offer to your staff: your most skilled employee is offered {rival_poach_premium} over the going rate (never more than {rival_poach_most}). Match it on the Company app's Staff tab within {rival_poach_answer} days, or they work their notice and leave. It needs the option Staff pay, raises, strikes and sick pay on, and comes no sooner than {rival_poach_gap} days after any other offer to your staff. - A stake in your company, from hundreds of millions, once it has traded a quarter of a year: a block of your listed company and a vote at its board. - A bid for your company, from billions, once it has traded a quarter of a year, within {rival_bid_after} days of the same rival's stake and never twice in {rival_bid_rest} days. It wins only while you hold less than {rival_threshold} and the holders take it. - Lobbying the council: for {rival_lobby_days} days inspections, licence checks and audits come {rival_lobby_weight} more often ({rival_lobby_most} at most), and one is called in at once. - A claim in court: {rival_suit_share} of what you are worth ({rival_suit_most_share} at most, never under {rival_suit_least} or over {rival_suit_most}), answered in your Legal file. - A piece in the paper: your customers think a little less of you, and your best business may have a smear to answer. - The moves are smaller while you are small and on the Gentle strength, larger on Hard and Ruthless, and never past the most above. # Your answers - Pick a rival on the page. Each answer is asked with the game's own question, costs a share of what you are worth and is used once against one move. - Outbid them ({rival_outbid_share} of your worth): ends their buying up or their business near yours. Once every {rival_outbid_rest} days against the same rival. - Hire away their people ({rival_poach_share}): their next move waits {rival_poach_quiet} days and their fortune grows at half the pace for {rival_poach_slow} days. Once every {rival_poach_rest} days. - A piece in the paper ({rival_press_share}): a move they have announced never comes, unless it is a bid: a bid is answered by what you hold of your company. With none announced, their next waits {rival_press_delay} days and they lose {rival_press_cut} of their worth. Once every {rival_press_rest} days. - Lobby the council ({rival_lobby_share}): their lobbying ends, and they may not lobby or buy up buildings for {rival_lobby_bar} days. Once every {rival_lobby_rest} days. - Take their holding over: buy its shares in the Stocks app up to the most one holder may have ({rival_held_most}), then buy the rest at {rival_takeover_premium} over its price, or over their fortune a share if that is more: their holding comes to the market worth their fortune. Your own shares are paid out at its price. They are out for good, and {rival_breakup_days} days later its parts bring you {rival_breakup} of what the shares you bought were worth. # The rich list - The rivals, you and six old fortunes (The Oracle of Omaha among them), richest first, with each one's week. The City Ledger prints it once a week, and the page opens it as a front page of its own. # Options - Rival tycoons who grow with you and fight you switches them on or off. Off, they stand still: nothing grows and nothing moves, and the save keeps them. - How hard the rivals push: Gentle, Normal, Hard or Ruthless. The presets set it: Relaxed is Gentle, Realistic is Hard, Hardcore is Ruthless. - When the first rival comes forward: at 5 million as before, or at 10, 20, 30 or 50 million, at the start's prices. Only the first moves; a rival who has come forward stays. - In a Going Public session the rivals rest: they act in single player only.

reallife_guide_photos: # Taking photos - Open the Camera app on the phone. The phone is put away and the camera opens at once, as a phone's does. Flare's camera and selfie buttons open it too, and the first photo goes straight into a new post. - The rear camera looks from where you hold the phone. Drag with the mouse to aim, and you turn with it; the wheel zooms up to {photos_zoom}x. Sitting down, you stay seated and the camera turns to either side. - The selfie turns the lens to you, and you hold the phone out. Drag to move the phone round your face, and use the wheel to bring it nearer or farther. Pose goes through photo mode's poses. - Grid shows the rule of thirds; with The camera opens with its grid on, as it is at first, the grid shows each time the camera opens. The chips over the shutter are the filters (Natural, Warm, Cool, Black and white, Vivid) and the frames (No frame, Border, Film). A frame is part of the photo; the grid and the buttons are not. - The confirm key or the shutter takes a photo. The cancel key or Close puts the phone away, and everything is as it was: the view, your character, the HUD. - The game's HUD is hidden while the camera is open. Time goes on as usual. # Where it works - On foot, outdoors and indoors. - Not in a car, on a bicycle or a motorbike, on a boat, on the bus, in the subway or in a taxi; not while you are busy (working, sleeping, an activity, a scene of the game's), while a window or a question is open, while the police hold you, while time is skipped, or in photo mode. A notice says why. - The camera closes by itself when any of those comes about, and when you open the phone, the map or the menu. # The Gallery - Every photo of this save as square tiles, under the game day it was taken: Today, Yesterday, then the day's number. The latest day comes first, and the newest photo first within it. A wide screen fits more tiles across. - The albums at the top: All photos, Selfies and Favourites. The album's count is under its name, and the foot of the grid says how many of the {photos_cap} photos a save keeps this one has. - Click a photo to see it whole. The round arrows, the arrow keys or the mouse wheel go to the photo before or after, and the strip under it jumps to a neighbour. Back, or the cancel key, returns to the grid where you left it. - Under the photo: To Flare opens a post with it attached, while Flare runs. Wallpaper puts it on the phone's home screen, which needs Modern phone look on; press it again for the phone's own. The heart adds it to Favourites. Delete removes it for good, after asking. - The small photo in the camera's corner opens the newest photo whole. - The Gallery is light by day and dark in the evening and at night of the game's clock, as the phone and Flare are. # Where the photos are kept - On your computer, not in the save: in the game's own data folder, under RealLifeOverhaul, Photos, one folder for each save. Each photo is a JPG of about {photos_lines} lines, with a small copy {photos_small} pixels wide beside it in Thumbs. Your favourites are a list beside them, in favourites.txt. - All the saves of one game share their photos: your own saves, the autosaves and a copy saved under another name. - A save keeps up to {photos_cap} photos. When it is full, opening the camera asks whether the oldest {photos_offer} may go, never the one that is your wallpaper. Nothing is deleted without your yes. - When every save of a game has been deleted in the game's own Load screen, its photos are kept {photos_grace} more days by your computer's clock and then deleted. If the save comes back meanwhile, from a backup or the cloud, they stay. # Going Public - Nothing of the Camera or the Gallery is sent to the other players. A photo shared to Flare goes as Flare sends any picture: its small copy only.

reallife_guide_faults_about: Street lights, roads, litter and unsafe places really break, at random, and Flare reports are checked against them.
reallife_guide_faults: # What breaks - With Real faults in the city on, things in the city really break as you play, at random: a street light goes dark, a pothole opens in a road, litter piles up on a pavement, a manhole is left open or a sign falls over. No two games break the same way, even from the same save. - Street lights fail more where the council spends less on upkeep, after a storm and as they age. Potholes open after rain or frost and on busy roads. Litter piles up where street cleaning was cut, by busy shops and where people go out at night. - Places where crimes really happened lately become hot spots. You cannot see them, but the police know of them. - How many faults at once sets the most the city has at one time: A few ({faults_few}), Some ({faults_some}, the default) or Many ({faults_many}). The city sweeps litter away after {faults_litter_days} days, or {faults_litter_days_cut} where street cleaning was cut, and a hot spot ends after {faults_hotspot_days} days without a crime. # What they do - A dark street makes crime there {faults_dark_crime}% likelier after dark. - A pothole jolts your car and wears its tyres, more the faster you go. Traffic slows by {faults_slow_kmh} km/h there. - Litter costs a business {faults_litter_percent}% of its customers for each heap near its door, {faults_litter_most}% at most, and dampens your mood in its district. - Now and then somebody trips at an unsafe place and gets back up. # Reporting them - Report a fault on Flare where you stand, or name the district. The City Office checks it: a real fault within {faults_match} metres of you, or in the district you named, gets a crew. The works show at the place, and the fault is gone when they are done. - Reporting a fault that a crew already has in hand is true, costs you nothing and stays with the first report. - The city's people report faults too, more often the longer one is left. Each time they report the same fault its answer comes sooner, and complaints left alone reach the City Ledger and pull on the mayor's approval. - A report of nothing is answered with "we looked and found nothing" and costs {faults_reputation} points of your Flare reputation. Make {faults_warn_at} within {faults_strike_days} days and you are warned; at {faults_bar_at} the City Office sends no crews for your reports for {faults_bar_days} days. Reports of nothing cost something switches this off. - A business you report is still inspected, but a clean one comes out of it with nothing against it. # Going Public - In a session the host's game makes the city's faults, and every player sees the same ones.

reallife_guide_texts_about: With a pack installed, a small model on your own PC writes the words of Flare posts, replies, messages and street talk. Offline, unless you choose Your own AI.
reallife_guide_texts: # What it does - RLO Texts writes the words of the city's messages with a small text model that runs on your own PC: replies and comments on Flare, the city's posts, messages from friends, family, your roommate, your boss and the lender, the City Office's answers, the rival tycoons and the City Ledger's briefs. With any pack, people answer what you write to them on Flare: a message, a post, or a reply under one of theirs, and the author of a post may answer your reply under it. - In the street, when you talk to somebody (see Street talk), it words the whole conversation, every line they say to you, while the game decides how it goes and names the places, streets and distances. - On a call, with Type your own words in calls on, Type a reply lets you say it in your own words, and they answer in theirs (see Social life). It works with a pack or with Your own AI. - The game still decides everything: who writes, when, what happened and what it does. The model only chooses the words, from what the game knows: the person, the place, the time, the news. None of it changes anything in the game, and each message has its written line for when the model is not ready. - With a pack it works offline, and nothing is sent anywhere. Your own AI, off unless you choose a service, can word the lines through an AI service instead, with a pack or without one. # How to start - Subscribe to a pack on the Workshop and switch on Messages written by a small model on your PC (on at first). The model starts once a save is loaded, never in the main menu; until it is ready, the written lines are used. RLO Texts status on the options page says what it found and how it runs, and Write a sample message shows one. - The packs: RLO Texts has the best words of these three (a model fine-tuned from Qwen 3.5 2B). RLO Texts Medium sits between the two (from Qwen 3.5 0.8B). RLO Texts Lite is the smallest and fastest, for weaker PCs (from LFM2.5 by Liquid AI). With several, the best one your PC can run is used. A pack can also sit in the "RLO Texts" folder in the game's data folder. - RLO Texts Large, the largest, with the best words of all, runs only on a graphics card (not graphics built into the processor) with about {texts_large_mb} MB of its memory free, and only while it writes a reply in {texts_large_slow} s or less there; slower than that, it is not tried on that card again. Otherwise the next pack you have is used. A notification tells you once if your card is fast enough for it. - Runs on: Auto uses a graphics card when it has the memory free, else the processor; Processor never runs Large. On the processor the model runs at low priority and always leaves the game {texts_game_cores} cores, so the game comes first. On a graphics card it runs at normal priority with {texts_gpu_threads} threads at most, so it keeps up while you play. - If the model stops answering, it is started again by itself, up to {texts_restarts} times a session. After that the status says to switch RLO Texts off and on. # Languages - A newer pack says which languages it was trained in, and writes in the game's language when it is one of these {texts_languages}: English, Portuguese, Chinese, German, French, Spanish or Russian. In Dutch and Turkish the written lines are used, since a reply cannot be checked in them. In a language the mod has no texts of its own in, its lines are in English, and so are the model's. - An older pack writes only in English, and only while the game is in English; in any other language it leaves the written lines. # People remember you - With a newer pack, the people you deal with remember you: how and when you met, when you last talked and what about, how it went, favours such as directions, a number or a loan, what they know of you (your name, your job, your business, how well known you are) and your news they heard. The game records all of it, and the model only uses it in its words, at most {texts_memory_lines} things at a time. - A text also remembers what that person last texted you about, and a call back what they just wrote, whichever part of your life the text came from. - A stranger in the street remembers you for that day and the next; swap numbers and they keep it. At most {texts_memory_people} people are remembered, {texts_memory_facts} things each, and old talk is forgotten after a while. Lose touch with somebody and what they remembered goes with them. # More of the city - The people in your life text after your own news, with a pack or without one: a crash, being knocked down by a car, a court case, a graduation, a new business, your company on the stock market, a wedding, a baby, or a day your net worth moves by {texts_big_share}% or more. Who texts depends on the news: your partner or Mom after a crash, Mom or your closest friend after a graduation. It comes the same day or the next. - With a newer pack, {texts_gossip_from} to {texts_gossip_to} days later, somebody who knows the one who texted may text that they heard. An arrest is passed on too. - These texts are the social life's own: they need Texts from your staff, about your news, and gossip, the social life and its Text messages from people on, and keep to its Most texts in a day and its quiet hours at night. - With a newer pack, your staff text you in their own thread, between {texts_staff_from} and {texts_staff_to}, when they ask for a raise, are off sick, thank you for a raise, or are down for more hours than they agreed to. - With a newer pack, reviews of your own businesses on Flare speak of their real figures: the service, the prices, how clean they are, the interior and how busy they were. # How it keeps up - Messages are written ahead: a reply due later is written as soon as the game knows it is coming. A text that is not ready in time, or whose words fail the checks, is sent with its written line. You never wait for it. When the game saves, messages still waiting go out with their written line. - A reply may take at most {texts_timeout} s on the processor and {texts_timeout_gpu} s on a graphics card, and at most {texts_per_minute} replies are written a minute, fewer when the game is busy, fast forwarding or loading, or when replies keep coming late. - On a slow PC: if RLO Texts or RLO Texts Medium takes more than {texts_slow} s a reply, you are told once to try the Lite pack. Past {texts_ahead} s, any pack writes only what is asked {texts_ahead_notice} s or more ahead, never a spoken line. # The checks - Every reply is checked before you see it: one line, not too long for its language, the facts it must name, no numbers or money that are not true, no dashes, no swearing, the right language, a capital at the start of each sentence, no exclamation mark from somebody who never uses one, nobody calling themselves an AI or a bot, no stranger using a name you did not tell them, and not the same as one of that person's last lines. With a newer pack the reply is held to these rules while it is written, too, and a reply cut off short is refused. - Words for Flare and the paper are kept in your save for as long as the post, message or paper is, and never change once you have seen them. - The comments under the city's Flare posts, and the answers under your replies, are written only by the model: a comment shows once its words are written and never changes after. Without the model the thread shows how many replied. # Going Public - Your own messages are written on your PC alone, and what people remember of you is kept in your own save. The shared feed and the shared paper are written by the host and sent to everyone as text, with their language; a player whose game is in another language sees the written lines. Without the host's words every player sees the written lines. # Options and tests - Each kind of message has its own switch, listed below. Under Test tools: RLO Texts: what was shown counts the model's words and the written lines this session, and why each written line was used; three more send a message from your staff, a text about your news, or gossip now.
reallife_opt_tip_texts: A small text model on your PC writes the city's messages. Needs RLO Texts, Medium, Lite, or Large on a strong graphics card. Off, or without a pack: the written lines.
reallife_opt_tip_texts_device: Auto runs on the processor unless your graphics card has plenty of free memory. Changing it restarts the model.
reallife_opt_tip_texts_threads: How many processor threads the model may use. Auto takes 2 to 4 by your cores and always leaves the game two cores. On a graphics card it uses two at most.

reallife_changes_028_2: Fixed: the office for your job's reviews and shifts was hard to find. Messages now name its address, the Work contact can show it on the map, and the city map has a Job offices row.
reallife_dayroll_note_goods: The game's night could stop halfway because the city's market held goods of a mod that is not loaded. They are taken out, so wages, staff hours and each day's work run as they should.
reallife_dayroll_note_hours: The game's night stopped halfway (an error, written in Player.log), so your staff's hours were not cleared. They are put right, so wages are paid for the hours worked.
reallife_changes_028_3: Fixed: when the city's market held goods of a mod that is no longer loaded, the game stopped every night halfway, so staff wages grew day by day, staff's hours and days a week were counted wrong against what they ask for, and brand recognition never moved. Those goods are now taken out at night and the counts put right before the wages. Fixed: you can like your friends' replies under your posts on Flare.

reallife_guide_street: # Talking to people - With Talk to people in the street on, walk up to anybody on the pavement and face them: the game's panel over them offers Talk on your interact key. They stop, turn to you and answer in the game's own dialogue panel. People standing about or sitting on a bench can be talked to as well: a seated person stays seated. - The blue button is what fits the moment and what they just said: how their day is going, the weather or the hour, the street event of the day, what they do and then whether they like it or how old they are, thanks after they show you the way, their name and number after a compliment that landed. Two people do not open the same way. Something else goes through the rest: their name, what's good around here, the way somewhere, a compliment, a joke, a flirt, their number, a coffee, the election, prices, your own business, and goodbye. Nothing you have already said to them today comes round again. - Say something of your own opens the game's text box for your own words. The game's cancel key (Esc) says goodbye at any time. - Everybody is somebody: a name, a job, a home district, a mood today and a way of talking. The same face is the same person all day, and they remember how it went. - Anybody who stops gives you at least {street_turns} turns, more when they warm to you, and each good exchange wins you another, up to {street_turns_most}. Then they have to go. # Who stops - Some have no time: on their way to work at the rush hours, late at night, in the rain, on a bad day or on the phone. How often is set by How often people have no time to talk: Rarely, Sometimes (the default) or Often. - How the city sees you counts. Well liked, they are warmer; disliked, cooler. Somebody who knows your face may have read about you, and about your record. If you have not washed, some will not stop and the rest are a little cooler. - A stranger is never more than a little cool with you, however their day is going, unless you were rude to them, they know your bad name or your record, or it is night. - Be rude and they answer coldly or walk off, and nobody you were rude to talks to you again that day. A threat sends them away, and an officer within {street_police} metres hears it: the police watch you more closely for the rest of the day. # What comes of it - Ask the way to a cafe, somewhere to eat, a bar, a supermarket, a clothes shop, a gym, a cinema or a bank, or to a business by its name: they name the nearest within {street_find} metres and its street, which way it is and how far, and the game sets it as your destination. - After a good talk they give you their number: they join People, met in the street, with the look you saw, and the social life goes on from there. Nobody new can be met once all of its people have been. - Invite them for a coffee (or dinner after a flirt that went well) and the game decides as it does for an invitation on Flare: a yes books the outing at a place near you, as a call would. - Tell them about your business: somebody who takes to it brings it {street_mouth}% more customers for {street_mouth_days} days, {street_mouth_most}% at most for one business, and {street_mouth_day} people a day count. - Your own words are read with fixed rules: an invitation, the way somewhere, a number, your business, how their day is going, thanks, a threat or an insult count as they would as a choice. Anything else is just talk. - Nobody says the same written line to you twice in a day. # RLO Texts - With an RLO Texts pack, the model words the conversation: their greeting or why they have no time, small talk, what they do and their name, the area, the way, compliments, jokes, flirting, their number, an invitation, the election, prices, your business, your own words, rudeness and threats, and goodbye. It writes from who they are, their mood, the hour, the weather and the last few lines of the conversation. The game still decides everything that happens, and gives the model the names, places, streets and distances to say. With a newer pack, it also words how their day is going, the street event, their work, their answer to thanks and hello again, and their small talk knows the rain, the hour and the day's event. A stranger says your name only if you told them, or if they know your face as somebody famous or infamous. A line waits at most {street_hold} seconds for its words; otherwise, without a pack, or with the game in a language the pack does not write, the written lines are used. # Going Public - Your conversations are your own: nothing is sent to the session, and other players are never passers-by.

reallife_changes_029_0: RLO Texts: with the RLO Texts or RLO Texts Lite pack from the Workshop, a small model on your own PC writes the words of Flare replies and posts, messages from people, the city's answers, the rival tycoons and the City Ledger's briefs, offline. Without it, or when it is slow, the written lines stay. People answer what you write to them on Flare, in a message, a post or a reply, and the author of a post may answer your reply under it. The posts of the city's people, its accounts, its businesses and its influencers have comments under them, written by RLO Texts for each kind of post, and the thread says how many more replied. On a graphics card the model runs at normal priority, so it keeps up while you play; on the processor it stays at low priority, so the game comes first. Invite somebody out in a Flare message, for a coffee, a meal, drinks, the cinema, a walk or a workout, and the game decides yes, maybe or no. A yes names a place and a time and books the outing as a call would, and somebody you had not met joins People as met online, with the face they have on Flare. Flare: every account has a picture beside its name (faces drawn by the game's own portrait camera, the game's logos for businesses, emblems for the city's offices), and some of the city's posts carry a photo of the place, taken where you are. Both are options. While a save loads, Flare draws the faces you are likely to see first behind the loading screen, for two seconds at most, and keeps every face it has read for the session. Street talk: walk up to anybody on the pavement and talk to them in the game's own dialogue panel. Everybody has a name, a job, a mood and a memory of the day, and some have no time. Ask the way and the game sets your destination, swap numbers and they join People with the look you saw, invite them for a coffee and the game decides, and tell them about your business. With RLO Texts the model words the whole conversation, while the game decides how it goes and names the places. Fixed: you can like the comments under other people's posts on Flare. Street talk: the blue button now follows the moment and what they just said: how their day is going, the weather or the hour, the street event, what they do and whether they like it, thanks after the way somewhere, their name and number after a compliment that landed, and two people no longer open the same way. Say something of your own is always one press away, and Esc says goodbye. People who stop give you at least four turns and more when the talk goes well, not having washed cools them a little instead of freezing everyone, and nobody says the same written line to you twice in a day.
reallife_changes_029_1: RLO Texts: both packs have new models with better words. RLO Texts Lite now runs LFM2.5 by Liquid AI, smaller and faster for weaker PCs, and the mod also finds RLO Texts Medium, a pack between the two, once it is on the Workshop. In the street the model now words five more things people say: how their day is going, the street event, their work, their answer to thanks and hello again, and small talk knows the rain, the hour and the day's event. Report a bug now lists your staff with each wage next to the game's usual wage for the skill and their hours, and yesterday's and today's money in and out by kind, so a report on wages or a sudden loss shows where the money went. Fixed: in street talk a stranger no longer calls you by a name you never told them, unless they know your face as somebody famous or infamous.
