reallife_guide_textsai: # What it is - Your own AI lets the people who answer through RLO Texts answer through an AI service you choose: ChatGPT with your own plan, Player2 through its App, a service with your own API key, or an app on this PC. - It is off unless you choose a service. The game still decides everything; the service only words the line, from the same card the newest pack is given. It works with no pack installed, but people remember you, and your staff text and gossip comes, only with a newer pack. - It needs Messages written by a small model on your PC on, and keeps to RLO Texts' switches for each kind of message. - It writes in the game's language when that is English, Portuguese, Chinese, German, French, Spanish or Russian, as native speakers write it, and its replies are checked in that language as the pack's are. In a language the mod has no texts of its own in, it writes in English. In Dutch and Turkish it is not asked: the mod cannot check a reply in them, so every message keeps its written line. # How to set it up - On the options page, under Your own AI, choose a service in AI service. A notification says once a session that the cards now go to it. - ChatGPT: press Continue with ChatGPT and sign in in your browser. Replies count towards your ChatGPT plan's usage, and Manage ChatGPT usage opens its page. - With an API key: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenRouter (its free models too), Groq, Mistral, Cerebras and OpenCode Zen. Get a key from the service, press API key and paste it in. OpenCode Zen's free models answer only inside OpenCode itself, so one of Zen's paid models is asked. - On this PC: Ollama and LM Studio, with no key. Address on this PC changes where the app listens, an address on this PC only. Player2 needs no key either: install the Player2 App from player2.game, sign in to it and leave it running, then choose Player2 in "AI service". The App hands the mod your sign-in while the game runs, and the mod keeps nothing of it. Player2 is free to start: replies use your Player2 joules, its measure of AI power, and a Player2 plan gives more. "Your own AI status" says whether the App is found and you are signed in, and "Player2: test the App and a reply" in the tests checks a whole reply. - Each service has a model of its own; Model names another of the service's models, and an empty line goes back to its own. ChatGPT, Ollama and LM Studio use the first model they list unless you name another. Player2 chooses its model itself. - API key, Model and Address on this PC open the game's text box, so they need a game loaded. Test the service sends it a sample message, and Your own AI status says whether it is ready, resting after a fault or stopped. - Forget the key or sign out forgets the chosen service's key, or signs you out of ChatGPT. Player2 keeps nothing to forget. - GitHub Copilot is not offered: GitHub gives other apps no way to use it. A Claude subscription is not offered either, as Anthropic does not allow its sign-in in other apps; an Anthropic API key works. # What is sent - With a service chosen, each message's card goes to that service over the internet: who is speaking and how they are, the place, the time, what happened, the last lines of the thread and what you typed to them. Nothing else of your save is sent. - Ollama and LM Studio run on this PC, so their cards stay on it. - Your key, or your ChatGPT sign-in, is kept on this PC only, protected for your Windows user. It is never shown again after you enter it, and never goes in a save, the options or the log. Player2's key is asked of the Player2 App when it is needed and stays in the game's memory only. # How it keeps up - A reply may take at most {textsai_timeout} s, at most {textsai_in_flight} are asked at once, and at most {textsai_per_minute} a minute. A line somebody says to you in the street waits at most {textsai_spoken} s for it, a short pause before they answer. - Every reply goes through the same checks as the pack's. When it fails them, comes too late, or the service fails, the pack writes it if one is installed and there is time; otherwise the written line is used. You never wait for it. - After a fault (no connection, too many requests, your ChatGPT allowance used up) the service rests a while, and the pack or the written lines are used meanwhile. It stops until you mend it when the service refuses your key or sign-in, has no such model, or a ChatGPT plan cannot be used in apps, or when no key is kept or the address is not on this PC. With Player2 it also rests while the Player2 App is not running or nobody is signed in to it, and when your joules are used up; the App is asked again after each rest, so starting it later is enough. # Going Public - Only your own messages go to your service. The shared feed and the shared paper, which every player must see the same, are never sent: the host's pack writes them as before.

reallife_guide_walking: # Walking on a key - On foot, press {key_walk} to walk at the game's own walking pace, the one the city's people walk at. Press it again for your usual pace. It works indoors and out of doors. - Hold the game's Toggle Running key (Left Shift unless you changed it) to hurry for a moment: the game's own pace comes back while you hold it, and you walk again when you let go. - The key does nothing while you type, while a menu, the phone or the map is open, in a vehicle or on a bicycle, or while you sit, work or study. Walking carries on afterwards. - Out of energy, the game's own slow walk stays as it is, and a pace a job or another mod sets is left alone. - Walking ends when a save is loaded. Every save starts at your usual pace, as it does in the game. - In a Going Public session only your own pace changes, and the other players see you walk. # The key and the switch - Change the key on the options page, under Controls, Keys. The switch, Walk on foot with the walk key, is under Controls, On foot. Off, the key does nothing.
reallife_changes_041_0: Once you are well off, a partner who lives with you may ask to cut back to half days at work. Say yes and they are home more and pay a smaller share of the rent; they can go back to full days from a family conversation. It has its own switch, in a new section of the options page: Your partner and your fortune. With the social life on, the Family contact is gone and family life is face to face: talk to your partner at home, use the new Family button in your fridge's panel for the overview and the rest, and Family matters in your partner's People call for time apart and the in-laws. Standing in another home of yours, text your partner to make it your new home. Your partner now reacts as your cash grows, by how they are: a supportive partner is proud and the home grows warmer, an envious one minds the gap more as you get richer, a little less once you are married. It has its own switch in the same section. Once you are rich, a partner who lives with you may ask either to stop working or to retrain for the job they always wanted. Stopping means no pay from them until they go back to work; retraining takes about three weeks without pay, then they start the new job. While your partner earns nothing, you can ask them to chip in for the rent from their savings. As your cash grows, a partner who lives with you expects a bigger home, evenings out more often, a weekly allowance, a car of their own and in time a second home. Meet it and the home grows warmer; leave it and the home slowly cools. Set the allowance when you talk to your partner at home. It has its own switch in the same section. Meeting your partner's wishes now also brings you closer. The allowance they expect follows how they are with money, whether they earn, marriage and children. A car is really handed over, or bought for them at the game's price, and can be asked back. Your own AI: the people who answer through RLO Texts can answer through an AI service you choose, off unless you choose one. Sign in with ChatGPT to use your own plan, paste your own key for one of eight services, or run a model on this PC. Every reply goes through the same checks as the pack's, and the pack or the written line is used when it fails or is late. The card, with what you typed, goes to the service you chose; your key stays on this PC. Careers from a course or a degree now pay fairly against the gigs: a barista starts on about 70 an hour instead of 18, a junior developer on 120 instead of 38, and the top of a ladder pays three to seven times its first rung. Degrees take three to four weeks instead of eight or more, diplomas two to three, reviews come every two weeks in the game's own year of 60 days (every four at most in a longer year), a good review's bonus is days of pay, and a working day teaches enough to climb the ladder. A walk key: on foot, press F3 to walk at the game's own walking pace, and press it again for your usual pace. Hold the game's Toggle Running key to hurry for a moment. The key can be changed under Controls, and walking has its own switch there. Fixed: an outing is no longer arranged at a place that is shut when you meet. The hour and the place are now chosen so that it is open for the whole outing, another place nearby is tried when the nearest is shut, and when everywhere is shut a walk is suggested instead. Fixed: with the social life on, your partner's texts about family life (being stood up, a missed appointment, an arrest) only showed as a notice; they now arrive as texts from them in People. Fixed: with the social life on, your partner's job at home and in family talks is the one People gives them, not a different one; a retired partner stays at home. Fixed: a car your partner has from you is no longer billed for parking while it is theirs, and with their expectations switched off it is yours again, back in the city or left at the nearest repair shop. Fixed: with the social life on, a Family contact you already have stays in your phone with all its messages. Fixed: after your partner retrains for a new job, People shows the new job. Fixed: a good review at Uncle Lou's Street Eats or Five Borough Cabs no longer reads as a wage of 0 an hour. Your own cart and the owner-operator's cab have no basic wage, so the boss now says what you keep, both pay more than the rank below, and a good review there raises your share of what you take. Fixed: the mod's apps on the phone and in the full menu's top row stand in the same order every time, whichever loaded first. Fixed: notifications in the top right no longer cover the panel of a shift, a gig, a lesson or a driving test: while it shows, they start under it. Fixed: a class and a shift on the same day no longer look like a clash when they fit. A class's panel says how much of it counts, a course's page in Campus says when to leave class for work or where it clashes, and a vacancy's page in Career says the same for your classes.

reallife_changes_041_1: Fixed: with your own AI chosen, people you stop in the street answered from the pack almost every time: their line waited only about a second, and ChatGPT takes longer to reply. Their line now waits for your AI a moment more, a short pause before they answer; they start to talk with their hands as its first words come, and the line shows as soon as its last word is in. If it is still late, the pack or the written line answers as before. Fixed: bike racks, bike-share docks and motorbike stands are put only on level pavement, never on a crossing, over the kerb or in the air. Fixed: a product launched with three features sells. Software sold by licence closes deals at a steady pace, sooner with sales people, and its page says about when the next comes; a consumer service that wins only a few users a day still gets some who pay. Fixed: online orders placed after closing wait for the opening hours without a notification, and the Planner counts from the opening. Orders left with nobody on shift while you are open still notify you, with a switch of their own in the options. Fixed: a bus held up for good gets going again. It goes round a closed lane or a car standing in its lane by the lane beside it, a red light in view no longer holds it for ever, and a bus driving off keeps going instead of standing in the road.

reallife_changes_043_0: At night your partner sleeps in your bed, where you can see them, and gets up in the morning; in a bed for two they leave you room, and from a bed for one they make way while you sleep. Household chores are real now: your partner asks only when it is so (the fridge nearly empty, the flat a mess, you unwashed, a filthy car), face to face at home or by text, and it counts once it is really done (groceries in the fridge, the flat tidied, a shower, a car wash) in a day or two; a promise not kept is a text and a cooler home. In Dutch and Turkish messages keep their written lines, since a reply in them cannot be checked. Fixed: credit card and overdraft limits now follow your income as well as your rating. Fixed: texts your partner writes at night no longer slip by while you sleep; they come in the morning, with a notice. Fixed: Cook together now opens your cooking list and uses what is in the fridge or the leftovers; you cook it at the stove and a portion is theirs. Fixed: your partner no longer stands at one spot doing the same thing for days; they move between more places and do different things. Fixed: your partner now comes in when they get home while you are in, and only comforts you after a bad day when you are both at home. Fixed: your partner comes in and leaves by the flat's real door; their sweeping and wiping really clean the flat; and next of kin stays Mom until you marry. Fixed: texts from your partner and family that wait for the morning are now kept in your save, so a save and quit at night no longer loses them; they arrive in the morning after you load. Fixed: a building you sold, such as a car park another mod sells, could come back as yours when the save loaded, still on the market, and be sold again for the same price. reallife_guide_markets_derivatives: # The raw materials exchange - The game's factories make goods from raw materials bought from the importers, {drv_materials} of them, from seeds and barley to circuits and uncut gems. On the city's exchange each has a price that moves at every market close: about {drv_farm_day} a day for farm goods down to {drv_paper_day} for paper, cloth and plastic, half of it shared with its group, and pulled back towards its own price at the price level (a farm good's move away from it halves in {drv_farm_half} market days, a metal's in {drv_metals_half}). Over a week farm goods move about {drv_farm_week} either way, paper and cloth about {drv_paper_week}. - The price set at a close is what the importers charge until the next close, for regular imports and urgent orders alike. The city's economy writes it as the importers' price, so it needs 'The city's economy' on; without it the prices are the game's own and only options on shares trade. # The Futures tab - On the Stocks app's Futures tab, show Raw materials, Companies or My contracts, or Everything, and narrow the materials by group. A material your factories use is marked so. Pick one for its price, the week's prices on offer and the ticket. - Each contract ends with a notification: settled, paid, lapsed or delivered. A margin call and the broker closing a future have one too. # Futures - Buy a future or Sell a future on a material. A future fixes its price for a week: it settles at the close of a Friday, {drv_weeks} Fridays are on offer (the nearest at least {drv_closes_least} closes away), and the price that close sets is the importers' for the week after. - Its price is the price the exchange expects at that close, worked out exactly from how its prices move, with {drv_spread} either side for buying or selling and {drv_commission} commission. Bought and held to its day, a future costs that spread on average: there is no money in timing it. Close it ends one before its day at the price then, with the same spread and commission. - A future holds a margin with the broker: {drv_margin_times} times the spread of a week's move of its price, {drv_margin_farm} of its worth for farm goods down to {drv_margin_paper} for paper and cloth, never under {drv_margin_least} nor over {drv_margin_most}. Each close settles the day's move in the margin account, and what is over the margins goes back to your cash. - Under {drv_maintenance} of the margins at a close, the broker calls for what brings the account back, due by the close {drv_call_days} market day later: Pay the call on the Futures tab. Unpaid at that close, or under {drv_forced} of that at any close, the broker closes your futures, the largest first, and what the account owes after is taken from your cash. - A future bought can name one of your warehouses or factories. At its day the goods go onto its pallets at that day's price and are charged to it as an import is, so with what the future made they cost what you agreed. What does not fit, or what your cash cannot pay for, is settled in cash. A future sold, or bought without a place, is settled in cash, and in a Going Public session every future is. # Options - Buy a call or Buy a put. A call pays at its day what the price is over its strike, a put what it is under, times its units or shares; out of the money it lapses. You buy them and the market writes them. The strikes run from {drv_strikes} under the price now to {drv_strikes} over it, in even steps. - On a material an option's premium is its exact price on the exchange's own moves, {drv_markup} over it and {drv_option_spread} of the price either side; Sell it back before its day and it fetches that much under. - On shares, options are written on the city's own large and middling companies that have been on the market {drv_listed_days} market days or more, not under a bid nor near failing, with at most {drv_share_adv} of a day's usual trading, and half the most you may hold, under option on one. None is written on a property trust, a rival's holding or a player's company. The premium comes from the market's own moves to its day, its results day, and the chance of a crisis, a windfall, a bid or a crash. It settles at the mean price of the last {drv_settle_steps} minutes of its day. A company that leaves the market settles its options at what it paid out a share, and a split changes them so they are worth the same. # Limits - {drv_contracts} contracts at once, and {drv_units} units under contract on one material. Units come in {drv_quantities}; shares in {drv_shares}. Contracts trade while the market is open, never while it catches up, nor after a load until it is back where it was. Ended contracts stay on the tab {drv_kept_days} market days. - With 'Futures and options' off (options page, under 'The stock market'), nothing new can be bought and what you hold runs to its day; the importers' prices go back to the city's own.
reallife_opt_tip_economy_managers: Managers chosen from a place's own staff make the small decisions you give them, inside your limits, on the Company app's Managers tab, and every one can be undone.
reallife_guide_economy_managers_about: A manager for each business, warehouse and factory, chosen from its own staff, and a regional manager for a district: they make the small decisions you hand them, within your limits, and report each month.
reallife_guide_economy_managers: # What it is - The Managers tab of the Company app gives each business, warehouse and factory you run a manager, chosen from the staff who work there, and each district a regional manager from your headquarters. It runs while Managers for your businesses and Running a business are on. - You choose what each manager decides and set their limits. Everything a manager decides goes in their log with what it changed, and can be undone. - Pick a place with no manager, then one of its staff, and press Appoint. The higher their main skill, the fewer mistakes they make. Replace puts somebody else in with the same limits. You can have at most {mgr_most} managers, regional managers included. - A regional manager is somebody at your headquarters who is on none of the game's plans there. With Company hierarchy on, a regional manager can look over a region you make instead of a district. - A manager keeps their own wage and shifts and is paid an allowance on top each day, as a business cost: {mgr_allowance_place} and {mgr_allowance_place_skill} more for each point of skill. A regional manager's is {mgr_allowance_region} and {mgr_allowance_region_skill}. These are given at a price index of 100 and follow prices. - To find somebody new, hire them the game's own way first: through a job board, the recruitment agency or a headhunter. Then appoint them. - A manager who stops working where they managed leaves the post empty, and the decisions there are yours again. # What the game already does - The game's own roles at a headquarters stay the game's. A Pricing Manager sets the prices of a district, a Logistics Manager tops up shops and factories from a warehouse, imports come through the game's own import partnerships, a Headhunter replaces staff who resign or retire and an HR Manager trains staff. - A manager never does their work: products a Logistics Manager tops up are left alone, and so are prices in a district a Pricing Manager covers or that a brand keeps. # What a manager decides - A business's manager can take every kind below. A factory's or an office's takes stock orders, the weekly rota and replacing staff, and a warehouse's stock orders and replacing staff. - Each kind has its own switch in the manager's panel, all on when they are appointed. Switched off, the manager never does it: with Weekly rota off they never touch a schedule, so yours or another mod's stays as it is. - A kind waits while what it needs is off: raises, offers and overtime need the staff part of Running a business, claims need insurance, and the rota needs the Staff rota planner. - Raises, at {mgr_staff_hour}:00: a request is agreed in full if the pay asked for is inside the wage band, by half if only that fits, and refused otherwise. A manager's own request stays yours. - Rivals' offers, at {mgr_staff_hour}:00: matched if the offer is inside the wage band, otherwise the employee goes. - Overtime, at {mgr_staff_hour}:00: agreed if all of its days fit what is left of the month's budget. - Insurance claims, at {mgr_staff_hour}:00: put in when what it pays is more than it adds to the next term. One left stays open for you. - Stock orders, on Sundays at {mgr_stock_hour}:00: the amounts of each repeating Delivery Contract for Monday are set to last the week and the stock floor, from what was used since the last look. It takes at least {mgr_learn_hours} hours of use, so a new manager learns first. A product on two contracts to the same place is left to you, and an amount moves only by {mgr_stock_step} or more. - Prices, at {mgr_price_hour}:00: worked out as the game's own Pricing Manager would at the manager's skill and kept inside the price band, at most {mgr_items} products a day. A price moves only by {mgr_price_step} or more. - Weekly rota, on Sundays at {mgr_rota_hour}:00, only when the week has a gap: an hour that wants somebody has nobody, or somebody who can work has no shift. The staff rota planner works out a new week for the same opening hours, and the manager writes it only if everybody on the rota now stays on it and no hour that has somebody is left with nobody. Otherwise the rota stays as it is, and the log says why. - Replacing staff, at {mgr_hire_hour}:00: when the staff fall below the number to keep, one candidate a day from the place's own job board is hired the game's way, inside the wage band, and {mgr_hire_hours} hours of their wage come off the month's budget. - With Company hierarchy on, the company policy binds these too: the largest raise, the days between raises, the least skill of a hire and the boards a gap is filled from. A request past the band can go to whoever approves exceptions. - The day's decisions are told in one notice at {mgr_digest_hour}:00, and the month's in a report. With Company hierarchy on, its Reports rule can make that weekly or only what needs you. # Their limits - Pick a kind in a manager's panel to set its limit. - Wage band: the most anybody is paid after a raise, a matched offer or a hire, from {mgr_band_least} to {mgr_band_most} of the going rate, {mgr_band_default} to begin with. - Budget a month for overtime and hires: up to {mgr_budget_most}, {mgr_budget_default} to begin with, at a price index of 100. - Staff to keep: the number replacing staff keeps up, up to {mgr_keep_most}. It starts at the staff the place has. - Stock floor: days of use kept on top of the week, {mgr_stock_default} to begin with. - Lowest price and Highest price: the price band as a share of the market price, {mgr_price_low_default} to {mgr_price_high_default} to begin with. - With Company hierarchy on, a band or a budget set here is that store's rule in the company policy, and a stricter rule above it binds. # Skill and mistakes - A manager's skill is the game's value of their main skill. At nothing a decision goes wrong {mgr_mistake_most} of the time, and at 100 never. A regional manager at 100 takes {mgr_review_cut} of that away. - A mistake never goes past a limit. It is a meaner answer to a request, a match let go, a claim left for you, an order up to {mgr_slip_most} off, a lower price inside the band, a week's rota missed or the second best candidate. The log marks every one. - A manager off sick decides nothing that day. The district's regional manager stands in, {mgr_far} points less skilled. # Undoing and taking back - Pick a decision in a place's list and press Undo. A raise, a match or a price can be undone for {mgr_undo_days} days, a hire for {mgr_hire_undo_days}, an order until the game locks it on Sunday evening, overtime while it runs and a claim until it is paid. Money that has moved stays moved, and an undone hire leaves the game's way. - A product whose order or price you undo, or change yourself in the game, is yours from then on. The manager leaves it alone until you press Hand them back. - A rota as it was before is kept until the game is closed or another save is loaded. - Stand down empties a post at once. With the option off nothing is decided, and the Company app's notices ask you again as before. - The last {mgr_kept} decisions are kept. # Finding your managers - The tab opens on a directory, one row a group: Needs you, Regional managers, the managers of businesses, of factories and offices and of warehouses, and Places with no manager. Each row counts its group, what it costs a month and its open decisions. - A group's list can be sorted by any column, such as name, cost, skill, district or open decisions, and filtered by district or by how each manager stands. The order and the filters are kept until the game is closed. - Regional managers lists each district with its regional manager, the places they look over and how many they stand in for today. A district's page lists its places with their managers, and the decisions the regional manager made standing in. - Needs you lists a mistake you can still undo, a manager off sick with nobody standing in, and a budget with {mgr_budget_near} or more of it used. Each line takes you to its page. - A manager's panel shows their pay, their allowance and the chance of a mistake today, and has a row to the district's regional manager. A regional manager off sick looks over nothing that day. - With more places than the company follows, the tab says how many are not listed.

reallife_guide_designs: # Ready-made designs - Call an interior installation firm from your contacts and choose the address of one of the mod's businesses: its Design list now has ready-made designs, as the game's own businesses have. Choose the day and the design as for any other, and the firm puts it in on that day. - The price is the game's own: the layout price is what the design's furniture costs at market prices, the installation fee goes by the floor area, and what is in the building already is sold and taken off the bill. - Every design is made from the game's own designs and furniture, for every building size the game has designs for. # What each business gets - Car Showroom: up to {designs_showroom_most} designs for each size, which keep the middle of the floor clear for the cars on the lot. The sales counter with its till, seats for visitors, plants, lamps and the washrooms stand round the walls where the room allows. In the two largest shop sizes one of them is the room of one of the game's own car dealerships. In the narrowest shops nearly all the floor is the lot, so little more than the washrooms fits. - Bank Branch: up to {designs_branch_most} designs for each size, from the game's shop designs cut down to a bank's furniture: a counter with a till for the teller, queue barriers, glass counters, seats to wait on, plants, lamps and the washrooms. Designs with seats come first. - Ice Cream Parlour, Tea Bar and Tobacconist: up to {designs_shop_most} designs for each size, from the game's designs of the shop each works as (coffee shops and fast food restaurants, coffee shops, liquor stores), without the shelves for goods it does not sell. Each keeps a till and somewhere to show its goods. - Software Studio, Cybersecurity Firm and AI Lab: the game's web development offices, with desks and computers for everyone, washrooms and a break corner. - Game Studio: the game's graphic design studios as well, with drawing tablets. - IT Consultancy: the game's law firm offices as well, with meeting rooms. - Training Academy: the game's travel agency, event planning agency and law firm offices, with desks and computers for the classes and seats for the students. # Good to know - The designs are files in the game's own design folder (StreamingAssets, InteriorDesigns), in folders that only the mod's kinds of business read. Switch Ready-made designs for the mod's businesses off and they are taken out again, and preparing a save for removing the mod takes them out too. - An order for a design that has been taken out is cancelled by the firm on its day, as the game does for any design that is gone.
reallife_changes_044_0: Futures and options on the Stocks app's new Futures tab. The raw materials your factories buy now have prices that move at each market close, set by the city's exchange as the importers' prices. Buy a future to fix next week's price, with its goods delivered to your warehouse or factory or settled in cash, or buy calls and puts on materials and on the city's larger companies. Managers for your empire: on the Company app's new Managers tab, appoint a manager for any business, warehouse or factory from its own staff, and a regional manager for a district from your headquarters. They answer raises and rivals' offers, agree overtime, put in claims, set the week's orders and prices, write the rota and replace staff from the job board, inside the limits you set, with mistakes in line with their skill, a monthly report, and every decision can be undone. Ready-made designs for the mod's own businesses: the interior installation firms now offer designs for a Car Showroom, the tech firms and a Training Academy, as they do for the game's businesses, at every building size the game has designs for. reallife_guide_phonefolders: # Folders - The mod's apps stand in five folders on the phone's home screen, after the game's own apps: Money, Work and study, Social and life, Business and Settings. A folder's tile shows small pictures of the apps in it. - Click a folder to open it. Its apps fill the screen, after a Back tile with the folder's name. Click Back, or press the game's cancel key (Esc), to go back to the home screen. - The row of apps at the top of the phone's full menu has the same folders. An app opened from a folder shows that folder in the row. - A folder with no app in it, because its features are switched off, is not shown. # The dock - The dock is the last row of the phone at the edge of the screen. It holds {phone_dock} apps and stays on every page of the home screen. It starts with the Planner and Flare. - In the row of the full menu, the dock's apps stand first after the game's own. - Move both apps out of the dock and its row goes back to the home screen. # Moving an app - Right click an app of the mod's on the phone at the edge of the screen. A list opens: pick a folder, the home screen or the dock, and the app moves there at once, on both phones. - The dock holds {phone_dock} apps: move one out before you put another in. - Put every app back in its folder on the options page puts every app back where it started. - Your layout is kept on this computer, for every save. In a Going Public session each player keeps their own. - The game's own apps and other mods' apps stay where they always were. # Numbers on the tiles - A folder's tile shows the numbers of its apps added up, as a real phone does. - On a folder's page the Back tile shows how many apps outside it have a number. - The More apps button counts the tiles with a number on the other pages. # One Banks app - The city's three largest banks share one Banks app, in the Money folder. Pick the bank at the top of its page: each bank has the same five tabs. # Switching it off - With App folders on the phone off, every app has its own tile again, on pages you turn with the mouse wheel or the More apps button. - A screen with room for only two apps in the full menu's row keeps that row without folders.

reallife_guide_economy_bank_branch: # What it is - A Bank Branch is a business type of its own for your bank. Open it in a shop unit with BizMan, as any shop, while your bank is running. You pay its rent, its fit-out and its staff's wages the game's way. - Hire tellers in the game's own way, with customer service as their main skill, and give each a shift at a till: the till is their counter. Opening hours, the rota and cleaners are the game's, as for any shop. - The interior installation firms offer it up to {branch_designs_most} ready-made designs a size: counters with a till, seats to wait on, desks and plants, made from the game's own shop designs. # How many branches - How many branches your bank may run depends on its level: {ob_branches_community} as a Community Bank, {ob_branches_regional} as a Regional Bank and {ob_branches_national} as a National Bank. A branch opened past that count takes no customers and has no counter to work until the bank moves up a level. The branches it already runs carry on. # Customers - While it is open, people come in as they would to a shop of its size: by its promotion, its customers' satisfaction and the hour. Lunchtime and the end of the working day are the busiest. - Each teller sees to about {branch_serve} customers an hour, from {branch_skill_least} to {branch_skill_most} of that by their skill. Those nobody sees to leave. - A customer opens an account, pays in, takes money out, asks for a loan or only asks a question. All of it is booked in your bank: what is paid in goes into its people's savings and its reserves, a loan comes out of its reserves. There is one set of books. - A loan at the counter (about {branch_loan}) is made only to people your bank lends to, and only while its reserves and its capital ratio allow it, and never during a run or a breach. During a run those who came to pay in take money out. A bank at its level's limit for savings takes no more money in at the counter either. # Fees - An account opened costs the customer {branch_open_fee}, cash paid in or taken out {branch_counter_fee}, and a loan {branch_loan_fee} of it, at least {branch_loan_fee_least}. The fees are the bank's takings with the next day. - In the game's own statement a branch shows only its costs, so it looks like a loss every day. Its fees and the business it brings are your bank's income, booked at your headquarters. The Branches tab sets what your branches bring against what they cost. # Reach - The customers your branches saw to in the last week bring your bank more of the city: its hold of the city's people grows towards {branch_reach_most} more, half of that at {branch_reach_half} customers a week across all your branches. Businesses get {branch_firms} of it. - Each branch more adds less than the one before, so a few busy branches pay and many quiet ones do not. - The Branches tab of Your bank shows each branch's month, its rent and wages a day, the reach, and what it brings the bank in deposits, loans and margin a day. # On the floor - While you are inside one of your branches, up to {branch_shown} of the hour's customers come in at the door, {branch_at_once} at a time. They queue at a till with a teller, are seen to and leave, or wait and leave unseen. What you see is the hour as the branch worked it, and it changes nothing. # Working the counter - Inside one of your branches, click a free till to work the counter yourself in the game's own work panel. While you work you count as a teller of middling skill, up to four hours at a time. Stop when you like. # Options - Bank branches, under Your businesses in the options, needs Your own bank. Off, branches do nothing, the counter cannot be clicked, and the bank holds what it would without them.

reallife_guide_calendar: # What it is - Calendar is an app on your phone. It starts in the Social and life folder. It shows the month you are in as the year you chose divides it, the days money moves and your own time. - The game has no months of its own. A month here is a twelfth of your year: 5 days in a 60-day year, 10 in a 120-day year, 30 or 31 in a 365-day year. The year begins with January, in midwinter, as the weather has it. - The line over the month says the day it ends on: "This month ends on day 90." Days are the game's own numbers, as the top bar shows them. # Reading a month - Month shows the weeks from Monday to Sunday. Each day shows its date, money coming in in green, money going out in red, and how many other things are on it. Today is marked in yellow. - Previous month and Next month turn the page, back to your first month and up to {calendar_ahead} months ahead. - Click a day for its page on the left: its money, your time and the city's events, the money still to come this month, and what moves every night. - Day lists everything on the chosen day. Click a row for its page, with a button that opens the app that deals with it. # What it shows - Money: power, water and internet bills, card statements and minimum payments, the private lender, car insurance and registration, web hosting, the paper delivered, your businesses' tax quarter and returns, the accountant, business cover, licences and claims, your tech firms' monthly invoices, dividends and bonds, the trading bots' statements, profit shares, benefit, the children's week and the game's tax year. - Your time: shifts and working days, reviews at work, interviews, classes and exams, court dates, licence dates, family appointments, plans with friends, deliveries, birthdays and your own Planner entries. - In the city: events, elections, the central bank's rate decisions, the first day of each season with what sells more in it, and snow on the days the forecast reaches. # Every night - What moves every night at midnight is not marked on the days: the game's rent, wages, loans and accounts, fines and court debts, and with the mod business cover, the rent from buildings you let, your tech products' subscriptions and your pension. A day's page says what they come to under Every night. - Subscriptions to your tech firms' products are paid in a thirtieth of the month's each day. A managed service is invoiced once every 30 days, on the day the calendar shows. - Something paid by the month counts its month from its own first day: a bill, a policy or a fee comes a month after the last one, whatever the calendar's month. # Good to know - The calendar only reads. It sends no reminders: those are the Planner's. - A feature that is switched off adds nothing to it. - In Going Public each player sees their own calendar. - 'Calendar on the phone' on the options page switches it off.
reallife_changes_046_0: Faster frames: the mod's bus stops, police station fronts, signs, help-wanted boards and newspaper kiosks are no longer drawn beyond 200 m, the distance the game uses for its own street furniture. Performance in the mod's settings has three new choices for the picture: how far the sun's shadows reach, how many cascades they are drawn in, and how far away things keep their detailed models. Each stays as the game has it until you change it, and the performance test (Shift+F7) measures each of them. A bank branch of your own: open a Bank Branch in a shop unit, hire tellers for its tills, and customers come in during opening hours to open accounts, pay in, take out and borrow, all booked in your bank. Busy branches bring your bank more of the city, each one less than the last. Click a free till to work the counter yourself. The Branches tab of Your bank shows what each branch brings and costs. A Calendar app on the phone, in the Social and life folder. It shows the month as the year you chose divides it, from 5 days in a 60-day year to 30 or 31 in a 365-day one, and the day the month ends on. Each day shows the money that moves on it, from bills, card statements and your firms' monthly invoices to taxes and insurance, and your shifts, classes, appointments, deliveries and birthdays. Click a day for its page, and an entry to open its app. Rent, wages and loans are paid every night, and the calendar says so. Fixed: the street chess player faces the board again. Their stool is close to the table, and the way people walk round the table turned them away from it; they now keep facing the board's centre at every table, while they wait and while you play. Fixed: a bus held back at its start to keep the timetable stood still in its lane when you could see it, and looked stuck. It now waits only out of sight: as soon as you can see it, it drives on, and the stop's panel shows it coming sooner. Fixed: a stutter on the hour from Flare's work for the hour, which is now spread over a few frames. Fixed: a stutter the first time you were back on the street, from the parking beside the bus stops being laid out all at once. Fixed: the watch for bouncing cars and the interact key now cost less in every frame. Fixed: the Planner's day box said the new year began on the year's last day, day 60 in a 60-day year. It now counts the year as the calendar, the weather, the stock market and the game's tax year do: the new year begins the day after.

reallife_changes_047_1: Fixed: on Flare, a message from somebody in the city no longer says they saw your post when you have posted nothing. It mentions a post only after one of yours from the last three days. Fixed: the city's people no longer review your business on Flare while it is temporarily closed or outside its opening hours. A review comes of a visit while it is open, and shows at the time of that visit. Fixed: a startup's follow-on could be pressed again and again, each press buying more, until you held nearly all of it. It is now taken once a round, only with pro rata rights, and brings you back to the share you held before that round, never more. Shares you already hold stay yours. reallife_changes_048_0: Managers: each manager's panel on the Company app's Managers tab has a switch for every task they do, so you can keep the rota, prices or anything else for yourself or for another mod. The Company app has an Open in BizMan button on each business's page. It takes you straight to that business in BizMan. Levels for your own bank: it is now founded as a Community Bank for a small part of the old cost, with limits on its branches, loans and savings, and moves up to a Regional Bank and then a National Bank as it grows and you pay for a larger licence. A bank you already have keeps everything it holds. You can also pay yourself from the bank, a share of each day's profit on a slider or a fixed sum a day, and leave the rest in it to grow. Calling somebody back after a text opens on what they wrote about, from Mom's news to a friend's worry or one of life's little moments. Each text is taken up once, on its day or the next. People text the day after an outing or a date about how it went, and the people in your life text after your big news without an RLO Texts pack too. With a newer pack, a text remembers what that person last texted you about. Fixed: a manager no longer rewrites the rota out of nowhere and leaves staff off it. They look at it only on Sunday evening, only when an hour has nobody or somebody has no shift, and write a new one only if it keeps all the staff on it. Fixed: ending a call by putting the phone away or pressing Esc, instead of with its own button, no longer leaves its typing box open, which stopped doors, keys and the mod's buttons from working. The same goes for a talk in the street, a phone app's box, a door gone through and a load. A talk in person that a call interrupted can be ended again.

reallife_guide_meals:
# Eating seated
- When you eat anything, from your hands, a bag or the fridge, and a free seat is within {meals_reach} metres in the same room, you walk to it and sit down with the food in front of you, as customers do at the tables of a fast food place.
- At a table with a tray for its customers you get the tray. Elsewhere a plate goes on the table in front of the seat. On a sofa or a bench with no table the plate goes in your lap.
- You eat for {meals_least} to {meals_most} seconds, longer for a bigger meal, then get up. Move, or click somewhere to walk, to get up sooner.
- The food fills you, gives energy and costs what it costs just as in the game, once, when you eat it. Only what you see changes.
- With no free seat near, or while you are busy, in a vehicle or carrying a box, you eat where you stand.

# Home cooking
- Cook at home by clicking your cooker, or Cook a meal in the fridge's panel. When the dish is ready it is carried from the cooker to the nearest free seat or table and eaten there.
- What a dish fills, its leftovers and the time it takes are home cooking's own, set out on the Home life and health page.

# Takeaway and plates
- Food you buy comes in the game's own bag. Carry it to a chair or a bench, click it and rest: once you sit, the panel offers Eat with the name of the meal.
- Press Eat and the bag becomes a plate: the place's own tray at a table that has one, a plate on the table in front of you, or a plate in your lap on a bench or a sofa. You eat as at a seated meal, then go on resting.
- At home the cooking list has a Serve row. Choose take it with me and one portion of the dish is packed instead of eaten. You carry up to {meals_takeout_most} packed portions; one you cannot carry is put by with the leftovers.
- The food fills you just as eating it from the bag does, once, when you press Eat. Eating from the bag where you stand works as before.
- With the option off, nothing is offered at a seat, and packed portions go back with the leftovers the next time you cook.

# Dancing to the music
- While a speaker plays music in your home or your own business, click it: its radio panel offers Dance, and you dance one of the game's own dances.
- The dance ends when you move, press the button again (it reads Stop dancing), the music stops or you leave.
- After {meals_dance_minutes} game minutes of dancing your mood lifts a little, at most once every {meals_dance_hours} game hours. Dancing costs no energy and changes nothing else.

# Going Public
- All of this is what your own machine shows. Nothing is sent to the other players, none of it stops or speeds the clock, and a seat in a public place is yours to use for a meal.
reallife_changes_049_0: More people to meet: the gym, your job, the coffee cart, your street, your shop, Flare and evenings out keep bringing new faces, one a day at most, up to 400 people in your life. With that many, only those closest to you, family, your partner and anyone you met lately get in touch on their own. Call the others whenever you like. Interviews at a place: at an employer's you walk in at the door, the screen goes black while the interview lasts and you come back out at the same door. A video interview from home sits you down at your computer, if your home has one. Managers have a directory of their own on the Company app's Managers tab: regional managers by district, with the places they look over and who they stand in for, the managers of businesses, of factories and offices and of warehouses in lists of their own, the places with no manager, and a Needs you list of what to look at. Each list sorts by any column and filters by district, a manager's panel shows their pay and leads to their regional manager, and the first page counts every group, what it costs a month and who is off sick. Meals and music: when you eat and a free seat is near, you sit down with your food in front of you, as customers do in a fast food place. A dish cooked at home is carried to the table and eaten there, and a speaker playing music at home offers Dance in its panel. Dancing to the music lifts your mood and costs no energy. reallife_guide_hustles: # What it is - Marketplace is an app on your phone, in the Work and study folder, with four tabs: Listings, Yours, Offers and Freelance. Each morning the city's people put up about {hustle_goods} used things for sale (electronics, furniture, clothes and shoes) and {hustle_cars} used cars, each at their own door. What nobody bought is gone the next morning. - Clients ask for freelance visits on the Freelance tab: detailing a car, odd jobs, a junk run or a move. - All the work here needs {hustle_energy} energy an hour and never takes you below 12; with little energy left you are too tired to start. None of it can be done during one of the mod's jobs. # Buying - Each listing shows what the seller says of it and what that would be worth. Now and then ({hustle_overstate} of the time) an electronics seller says it is better than it is, and a car with faults is listed as better than it is: you see the true condition once it is yours. - Make the offer from {hustle_haggle_least} of the asking price up to all of it, or Buy at the price. A seller takes an offer at or above the least they want, or counters; after {hustle_haggles} refused offers they sell to someone else. Your negotiation skill brings their least down, by up to {hustle_negotiation} of the asking price at 100. - You pay at once. You can keep up to {hustle_owned_most} things at a time. - Goods are collected at the seller's door (Collect, with Show the way to find it), or brought home from {hustle_delivery_hour} the next morning for {hustle_delivery} plus {hustle_delivery_share} of the price. A car is always collected: press Take the keys at the door, standing by the road, and it waits at the kerb. # Fixing it up - On the Yours tab choose Fix it at home, Clean it at home or Take it to a repair shop. Then, inside your home or any building of yours, the game's panel over you offers Fix it or Clean it and its work panel and clock. Stop early and nothing is changed or paid. - A repair by hand takes half an hour to two and a half hours by the thing, and parts cost {hustle_parts} of its price new, paid only if you finish. It works {hustle_fix_base} of the time at first, {hustle_fix_xp} more for each point of repair experience ({hustle_fix_least} to {hustle_fix_most}), and {hustle_fix_wreck} less for a thing under {hustle_wreck_below}%. A repair that works brings it near the best that kind can reach; one that fails takes a little off. Each try gives experience: {hustle_xp_worked} points when it works, {hustle_xp_failed} when it does not. - A clean, for furniture, clothes and shoes, takes {hustle_clean_minutes} minutes and {hustle_clean_cost} of supplies, once a thing, and never past {hustle_clean_most}%. - Electronics can go to a repair shop: the nearest electronics store open now, or an appliance store if none is. Hand it in at the door while it is open, wait {hustle_shop_minutes} minutes and it comes back at {hustle_shop}%. It costs up to {hustle_shop_share} of the price new, less the better it is already, at least {hustle_shop_least}. - A car is the game's own vehicle: repair it and wash it at a petrol station, as any car of yours. Its condition and dirt are read from the car, and dirt takes a little off its worth. # Selling - List it for sale at {hustle_ask_least} to {hustle_ask_most} of its worth. Buyers write in between {hustle_buyers_from} and {hustle_buyers_until}, more often for a fair price and a good condition, one offer a thing at a time and {hustle_offers_most} in all. An offer stands for {hustle_offer_hours} hours. - Take the offer, Counter or Turn it down. A counter at their offer is always taken; the nearer it is to the most they would pay, the less likely, and above it never. After a refused counter they come up a little; after {hustle_counters} they go. - A car sold leaves your cars as soon as you take the offer. You cannot sell a car you are sitting in. # Freelance visits - {hustle_gigs} requests come each morning, one more with a rating of {hustle_good_rating} or better and one fewer under {hustle_poor_rating}. Each client wants you from an hour between {hustle_gig_from} and {hustle_gig_to}. Book it, then be at their door: the visit can begin an hour early and they wait {hustle_window} hours. Starting after the first hour is late. - The pay at today's prices: detailing {hustle_pay_detailing} for {hustle_minutes_detailing} minutes, odd jobs {hustle_pay_handyman} for {hustle_minutes_handyman}, a junk run {hustle_pay_junk} for {hustle_minutes_junk}, a move {hustle_pay_moving} for {hustle_minutes_moving} at each of its two addresses. Each client pays {hustle_client_least} to {hustle_client_most} of it, and {hustle_good_pay} more with a rating of {hustle_good_rating} or better. - At the door, Start the job opens the game's work panel. Junk runs and moves need a van or a pickup of yours within {hustle_van_reach} m of the door: if you have none there, Hire a van for {job_van_fee} for the day. A move is loaded at one address and unloaded at the other, within {hustle_window} hours after the client's hours end. The client pays at the end. - The client rates you one to five stars by your skill (cleaning for detailing, delivery driving for junk runs and moves, your repair experience for odd jobs), with a little luck: a star off for coming late and two for leaving before the end, which pays only for the time worked. Five stars bring a tip of {hustle_tip}. Call it off and they give {hustle_cancel_rating} stars; never come and {hustle_missed_rating}. Your rating is the average of your last {hustle_ratings_kept}. - Or Send a helper: they take {hustle_helper}% of the pay, do the visit in your place at the client's time and are rated three to five stars for you.

reallife_opt_tip_economy_estate_duties: Tenants have a satisfaction, report repairs and complain, and the city inspects let buildings. Lettings agencies, managers and payment plans come with it. Off, letting works as before.
reallife_guide_economy_estate_duties_abo: Your tenants have a say. They report repairs, complain and leave when unhappy, the city inspects the buildings you let, and a lettings agency or a property manager can run them for you.
reallife_guide_economy_estate_duties: # What it is - When you let a building yourself (Let it yourself on the Mine tab of Property), each tenant has a satisfaction, reports repairs and may complain or leave. The city inspects the buildings you let. It has its own switch, A landlord's duties, under Your businesses in the options, and needs Property to buy, let and sell. Off, letting works as before, with none of this page. - A building's page on the Mine tab shows its rent roll, what is owed, how its tenants feel, open repairs, the next inspection, the year's repairs, fees and fines, and who runs it. # Satisfaction - A tenant is pleased by a building in good condition, by refurbishment and by a rent under the market's. A repair left waiting, notice served on them and the city's order on the building annoy them. - Satisfaction moves a little each day towards what the building deserves. The lease page says where it is heading and what the tenant minds most. - A happy tenant renews a lease about {duty_renew_high} of the time, an unhappy one about {duty_renew_low}. An unhappy tenant also misses rent more often. - Under {duty_complain} a tenant complains now and then. Under {duty_quit} they may say they are leaving in {duty_quit_days} days. Lift it over {duty_stay} before then and they stay. # Repairs - A let unit reports a fault in about {duty_call_least} of months in a building in new condition, and {duty_call_poor} in one in poor condition. The Works tab lists every open repair. - Send a contractor: it costs about {duty_call_share} of the unit's share of the building's value and puts it right the next morning. Doing it yourself costs {duty_diy} of that in materials: press Do it yourself, follow the marker to the building's door within {duty_diy_days} days and do the job there in the game's own work panel. - A tenant expects a repair within {duty_grace} days. Left for {duty_lapse} days it damages the building and the tenant complains. Repair works to new on the Works tab put every open repair right as well. - After {duty_to_city} complaints in a lease, with a repair waiting {duty_city_days} days, the tenant goes to the city and the inspector comes within {duty_city_come} days. # The city's inspections - The city inspects each building you let about every {duty_inspect} days. It takes the condition, less a share for every repair waiting more than {duty_old} days, and passes it at {duty_pass}. - A failed inspection costs {duty_fine} and brings an order to put it right in {duty_order} days. Failing again costs {duty_fine_again}, and no new tenant can move in until it passes. The inspector then comes back every {duty_reinspect} days. # Rent owed - On a lease in arrears you can Send a reminder: the tenant is likelier to pay it all, and a little put out. - Or Offer a payment plan: the arrears over {duty_plan_low} to {duty_plan_high} days, paid with the rent, which comes in again at once. A tenant with a poor record takes one about {duty_plan_poor} of the time, one with a good record about {duty_plan_good}. A missed day ends the plan. - Notice and the court are on the lease page, as on the Property page of the Guide. # Agencies and managers - On a building's page choose who runs it. You can do everything yourself, for nothing. - A lettings agency brings {duty_more} more applicants and takes the best of them for each empty unit, none with a record under {duty_record}. Its fee is {duty_agent_days} days of the agreed rent at each letting. - A property manager does that too, sends a contractor to every repair, chases arrears with a reminder, a plan, notice and the court, and has the builders in before the city's order runs out. Its cut is {duty_manager} of the rent that comes in. The bills are paid from your cash. # Buying to sell - A building's page on the Mine tab adds up what it cost you, bought and improved, against what a sale at its worth today would leave after the selling fee and tax. Buy run down, repair and refurbish on the Works tab, and sell from the same page. # Known limits - A tenant is still not seen in the city, and a repair you do yourself is done at the building's door. - The court is the possession order on the lease page: there is no hearing to attend. - A building the game lets for you has none of this.

reallife_guide_seasons_about: The year has four seasons: what your customers buy follows them, some winter days it snows, and the other seasons bring their own rain.
reallife_guide_seasons: # What it is - The year has four seasons, as the Calendar has them. Each season is a quarter of the year you chose for the save, and a new game begins part way through winter, so its first winter is short. - In each season your customers buy more of some goods and less of others. Over a whole year it evens out. - On the first morning of each season a notification names the goods that sell most more and most less from now. The Calendar's day page says the season and what sells more and less in it, and marks the first day of each season. - Under the date on the top bar: the season, its day and how many days it has, with a picture of the season. # What sells when - Winter: more hot drinks (coffee {season_coffee_winter}, tea {season_tea_winter}), whisky {season_whisky_winter} and wine, gifts {season_gifts_winter}, jewellery, flowers {season_flowers_winter}, phones and headphones as presents, books and warm clothes ({season_clothes_winter}). Less ice cream ({season_icecream_winter}), slushies ({season_slushie_winter}), salads ({season_salad_winter}), soda and margaritas. - Spring: more flowers ({season_flowers_spring}), umbrellas ({season_umbrella_spring}) and salads. - Summer: more ice cream {season_icecream_summer}, slushies, soda, beer {season_beer_summer}, margaritas, salads ({season_salad_summer}) and fruit, hot dogs and kebabs ({season_kebab_summer}). Fewer umbrellas ({season_umbrella_summer}), clothes ({season_clothes_summer}), whisky ({season_whisky_summer}), tea and coffee. - Autumn: more umbrellas {season_umbrella_autumn}, apples and pears ({season_apple_autumn}), coats and tea. Fewer flowers ({season_flowers_autumn}) and ice cream. - It changes how many of each good your customers buy, from the night the season begins. Your prices and the demand Market Insider shows stay as they are. # Snow - On {season_snow_chance} of winter days it snows. A fall begins by {season_snow_latest} at the latest, lasts {season_snow_least} to {season_snow_most} hours and is over by midnight; {season_heavy_chance} of falls are heavy. A light fall leaves the ground patchy, a heavy one covers it. - Snow lies until midnight, then melts away over {season_melt_hours} hours the next day. - With Weather affects driving, crime and energy on, snow is forecast: in the morning for a fall later that day, and at 18:00 for one the next day, with a word when the first flakes fall. The Calendar then shows the snow of the next {season_forecast_days} days. With that option off, snow still falls and lies, but with no forecast and no word. - With the same option on, snowy roads take grip from your car and cause more accidents, traffic drives more slowly, the police see a little less far on covered roads, and people in the street set off walking more slowly. A covered road is worse than a patchy one, and snow adds to rain or ice. - While snow falls or lies on the roads, the game's own rain is neither seen nor heard; its weather carries on. # Rain, storms and the look of the year - Some spring days have a shower ({season_shower_chance} of days, up to {season_shower_hours} hours), some autumn days rain ({season_autumn_rain_chance}, up to {season_autumn_rain_hours} hours), and some summer days a thunderstorm with lightning ({season_storm_chance}, up to {season_storm_hours} hours). Each begins between {season_rain_from} and {season_rain_to}, never while the game's own rain is falling, and is over by midnight. It is the game's own rain, so with the weather option on a storm counts as a storm: people run for cover and the roads are slippery. - Snow lies only on streets, pavements and roofs, never on people or cars. Where the game's graphics settings cannot keep it there, only the flakes fall. - The trees' leaves turn with the year: fresh green in spring, the game's own green in summer, amber, red and brown in autumn, dull in winter. In autumn leaves drift down round you in the street, most in the middle of it, never indoors or in the rain. - On snow days the sky is greyer and the light softer; in summer the sun is a little warmer, except in a storm. - With people dressing warmer (off at first), the people in the street wear the game's own warm clothes: a warm top in autumn, long trousers too in winter. They change behind the black screen of a door as you go out, so you see it after you have been through one. - In a Going Public session everyone has the same seasons, the same snow and the same rain. # Other mods - If Alcware Seasons is switched on, these seasons stand down for it and a notification says so, unless Keep these seasons with Alcware Seasons is on. - Show the snow falling and on the ground off, for slower machines: the snow is not drawn, but it is still forecast and still felt on the roads.
reallife_opt_tip_social_networking: Some people you meet hold a position, such as a recruiter or an investor, and do you a favour or two as you grow closer. Off: nobody does.
reallife_guide_networking_about: Some of the people you meet hold a position, and help you as you grow closer.
reallife_guide_networking: # Who you meet - Some of the people you meet hold a position: a buyer at an importer, a manager at a wholesaler, a partner at a law firm, a recruiter, an investor, a city official or a landlord. A buyer's or a manager's firm is one of the city's real importers or wholesale stores where there is one. - About {net_street} of the people you meet by chance hold one, {net_work} of those met after a job shift, {net_evening} of those met at an evening out, {net_friend} of those a friend introduces and {net_family} of those Mom brings along. Mom and Alex hold none. - They say what they do when you meet, text you about it afterwards, and their page in People shows their position and what they could help with, or that they have done what they can. # What they do for you - Each position has two favours: the first once they are a friend and you have known them {net_known} days, the second once they are a close friend or your partner. Each favour happens once, and one comes at most every {net_gap} days from anybody; a refusal can be asked again another day. - A buyer: the importer, then the wholesaler. A wholesaler's manager: the wholesaler, then the delivery fee. A partner at a law firm: freelance work, then a job lead. A recruiter: a job lead, then freelance work. An investor: a meeting, then a property tip. A city official: a property tip, then a job lead. A landlord: a property tip, then a meeting with an investor. - When one is ready, call them: it is the first thing under Something else. Ask about the opening, Ask about the freelance work, Ask for the importer's contact, Ask for the wholesaler's contact, Ask about the delivery fee, Ask to meet the investor, Ask about the building. They also text to say so, when people may text you. # What each favour needs - A job lead puts a vacancy in your Career app, open for {net_lead_days} days, with your name put forward, which counts at the screening and at the interview. It needs a profession you are qualified for now, a better post than the one you have, and room for another application. - Freelance work is a contract offer on the Career app's Own work tab. It needs 'Working for yourself' on and room for another contract. - An introduction gives you an importer's or a wholesaler's own contact, so you can call them to set up deliveries, and makes the place your destination. An importer's goods need your headquarters to sign the contract and a warehouse or factory to receive them; a wholesaler delivers on Mondays to the orders placed by Sunday evening. - The delivery fee: a wholesaler's manager waives it on the delivery contracts you already have with them. Set your deliveries up first; a contract made later pays it. - An investor meeting opens an investor's door to your pitch today. It needs Investors on. - A property tip names a building for sale and makes it your destination; its seller takes an offer of {net_tip} of the asking price, through the game's real estate. In a Going Public session the tip only names the building.

reallife_guide_household: # Taking someone on - Ring the Household staff contact on your phone. You need a home of your own. With more than one, you choose the home each person works at, a house in the Hamptons as much as a flat in town. - The agency puts forward one person at a time, with their age, what they do, their hours and what they ask. Take them on, or ask for someone else. One of each kind can work at each home, at up to four homes. - Wages follow the city's going rate for a cleaner, as your businesses' staff are priced, and rise and fall with the economy. A more skilled person asks a little more. # Who does what - A cleaner comes on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays from {hh_cleaner_from} to {hh_cleaner_to} and leaves the home close to spotless. - A cook comes every evening from {hh_cook_from} to {hh_cook_to}, buys the food (about {hh_shopping} a portion) and cooks a dinner for two or three. The portions go in your fridge, up to {hh_portions}: reheat one at a cooker. With the fridge full the cook takes the evening off, unpaid. - A butler lives in and works every day from {hh_butler_from} to {hh_butler_to}: cleans the home, cooks into the fridge and washes the cars at home. A butler asks {hh_butler_share} more an hour than a cleaner, a cook {hh_cook_share} more. - A mobile mechanic comes on Saturdays at {hh_mechanic_at} and sees to every car of yours at home, in its garage, parked within {hh_reach} m of its door, or on its plot in the Hamptons: washed for {hh_wash} a car, repaired at the repair bay's price, and given what the bay's workshop would give it (the service, tyres, brakes, the inspection) at its prices. The call-out is about {hh_callout}. With no car at home nothing is charged. # Paying them - Each visit is paid from your account as it begins, and shows in your statement. If you cannot pay, they do not work that day, and after {hh_quit} unpaid visits in a row they leave. - At {hh_note} the Household staff contact texts you what was done that day and what it cost. - Ring the contact to see who works where, to move someone to another of your homes, or to let someone go at once. Nothing more is owed when they go. # At home - While you are at home during a visit you see them at work: the cook at the cooker, the cleaner mopping and sweeping, the butler at either. The mechanic works at the cars outside and is not shown. - When you give up a home, its staff move to another home of yours that has nobody of their kind. With no such home, they leave. # Known limits - Cleaning, cooking and the fridge need Home life and health and its cooking to be on. The service, tyres, brakes and inspection need car servicing to be on. - The car you are sitting in is left for the repair bay.
reallife_shops_enabled: Ice cream parlours, tea bars and tobacconists

reallife_guide_shops_about: An ice cream parlour, a tea bar and a tobacconist to start in BizMan, run as the game's own shops are, and where each gets its goods.
reallife_guide_shops: # New kinds of shop - Three more kinds of shop can be started in BizMan in any shop unit: an Ice Cream Parlour, a Tea Bar and a Tobacconist. Each sells goods the game already has, from furniture the game already has, and runs as the game's own shops do: staff, stock, opening hours, customers, prices and BizMan. - Each has its own page in the game's help, opened from the link of a requirement in BizMan: what it sells, where its goods come from and the furniture it needs. # What each sells - Ice Cream Parlour: ice cream from an Ice Cream Counter and slushies from a Slushie Machine, with cotton candy, cupcakes, donuts, soda, popcorn and coffee on the side. Its customers come most in the afternoon and at weekends. - Tea Bar: tea from an Industrial Coffee Machine and slushies, the nearest the game's goods come to bubble tea, with cupcakes, donuts, ice cream, croissants, soda, coffee and cotton candy on the side. It is busiest from lunch to the early evening. - Tobacconist: cigarettes and cigars on a Tobacco Shelf (large, medium or small), with energy drinks, soda and cheap gifts. It is busiest before and after work. # What the shop needs in BizMan - Ice Cream Parlour and Tea Bar: customers are served, as in a coffee shop. Each needs a Cash Register on cabinets and staff with the Customer Service skill to work it. No course is needed to start one. - Tobacconist: customers serve themselves, as in a liquor store. It needs a Stack Of Shopping Baskets and a point of sale: a Cash Register or a Checkout Counter. As with a liquor store, BizMan lets you start one only once you have the Headquarters course from Manhattan Business School, the third of its courses after Basic HR and Market Demands. - Every kind needs at least one of its main goods on show, paper bags in its point of sale and opening hours set in BizMan. Storage Shelves in the shop receive its deliveries. # Where the goods come from - Ice Cream Parlour and Tea Bar: everything they sell is at the wholesalers, as a coffee shop's is. Buy it at any wholesale store and carry it in, or ask the store's manager for a weekly delivery and order it in BizMan's Deliveries tab. They need no headquarters and no warehouse. - Tobacconist: no wholesaler sells cigarettes or cigars. They come from an importer, as a liquor store's drinks and tobacco and a jewellery store's jewellery do. Its energy drinks, soda, gifts and paper bags can still come from the wholesalers. - Importing is the game's own chain, and every link is needed: - the Headquarters course, then a Headquarters in an office building with a Computer Workstation for each person below; - a Purchasing Agent at the headquarters, who signs a contract with the importer: cigarettes and cigars are at United Ocean Import on the pier; - a Warehouse with Pallet Shelves, which receives the imports on the delivery day BizMan shows for the agent's order; - a Logistics Manager at the headquarters with a delivery plan from the warehouse to the shop, and a Delivery Driver with a vehicle at the warehouse, who brings the goods to the shop's storage shelves overnight. - A Factory can make some goods instead, after the Product Manufacturing course: cigarettes and cigars from tobacco and paper imported at Global Harvest Traders. A jewellery store's expensive jewellery and smartwatches come only from a factory. - The game's help gives each step in full: its Wholesale / Import pages, and the business school's page for the courses. # Customers and prices - Customers come as they do to the game's own shops: by the building's size, the street's traffic and your marketing, by the day and the hour, and by each district's demand for each good. A district that wants ice cream wants it from your parlour as it does from a supermarket. - Prices are the game's market prices, moved by the city's economy as every other shop's are. - The ice cream parlour and the tea bar count as food: they get food inspections and, with Licences and permits on, need a food hygiene licence from the Company app (see Running a business). A tobacconist sells no alcohol, so it needs no alcohol licence. - Like a liquor store, a tobacconist keeps its goods on open shelves, and thieves may take from them. # Ready-made designs - The interior installation firms offer designs for each kind, made from the game's own coffee shops, fast food restaurants and liquor stores without the shelves for goods the shop does not sell. A tea bar's machines are set to pour tea. An ice cream parlour's designs are for the four larger shop sizes, the ones the game has designs with an ice cream counter for. # The option - Off, the {shops_kinds} kinds are not offered when you start a business. Shops already open keep trading. - Prepare this save for removing the mod makes each of these shops the game's own: an ice cream parlour a fast food restaurant, a tea bar a coffee shop and a tobacconist a liquor store.

reallife_shops_help_icecreamparlour:
**Ice Cream Parlour** businesses operate out of retail buildings. This kind of business comes with Real Life Overhaul.

All of this store's items can be ordered from [Wholesalers](wholesalers-locations).

Customers are served by employees, most of them in the afternoon and at weekends.

The business requires the following furniture to function:

* [Cash Register](furniture-cashregister)
* At least one product to sell (see below)

Businesses of this type primarily sell:

* [Ice Cream](products-icecream), from an [Ice Cream Counter](furniture-icecreamcounter)
* [Slushie](products-slushi), from a [Slushie Machine](furniture-slushimachine)

And can also sell:

* [Cotton Candy](products-cottoncandy)
* [Cupcake](products-cupcake)
* [Donut](products-donut)
* [Soda Can](products-sodacan)
* [Popcorn](products-popcorn)
* [Cup of Coffee](products-cupofcoffee)

Employees with the following skills can be assigned:

* [Customer Service](skill-customerservice)
* [Cleaning](skill-cleaning)
