reallife_lic_qh_01: Your truck is 4 metres tall and a sign ahead shows a lower height limit. What do you do?|Stop before it and find another way round|Carry on slowly and hope it fits|Let some air out of the tyres and try
reallife_lic_qh_02: How much longer than a car is a heavy truck like the Freight Truck?|About twice as long or more, so it needs far more room|About the same length|A little shorter, as the cab sits over the wheels
reallife_lic_qh_03: Where is it hardest to see from the seat of a heavy truck?|Close behind it and right beside the cab|Straight ahead through the windscreen|Nowhere: the high seat sees everything
reallife_lic_qh_04: A narrow street has cars parked on both sides. What do you think about first?|Whether the truck fits through with room to spare at both mirrors|How fast you can get through|Nothing: the other drivers will move
reallife_lic_qh_05: Why must you watch overhanging trees, signs and awnings?|The top of the body can strike them even when the cab passes clear|They only matter to buses|They bend out of the way
reallife_lic_qh_06: Where is the best place to park a heavy truck?|A place long and wide enough for it, clear of the traffic lanes|Across two car spaces and the pavement|In a bus stop for a few minutes
reallife_lic_qh_07: Why must a load be secured before you set off?|A load that shifts can tip the truck or fall into the road|It only matters on the motorway|Loose loads make the truck faster
reallife_lic_qh_08: Compared with an empty truck, a loaded one needs what to stop?|More distance|Less distance|The same distance
reallife_lic_qh_09: Where should the heaviest part of a load sit?|Low down and spread evenly over the axles|At the top of the stack|All at the very back
reallife_lic_qh_10: Before driving off after loading, what do you check?|That the doors are shut and the load is tied down|Only the radio|Nothing: the depot checks it
reallife_lic_qh_11: Why does a heavy truck take longer to pick up speed?|It weighs many times what a car does, with not much more engine|Its gearbox is broken|Trucks are limited to 20 km/h
reallife_lic_qh_12: On a long road downhill, what keeps a heavy truck under control?|A lower gear and steady braking, never riding the brakes|Neutral, to save fuel|Full speed, then hard braking at the bottom
reallife_lic_qh_13: How big a gap do you leave to the vehicle ahead in a heavy truck?|A much longer one than in a car|The same as in a car|As small as possible, so nobody cuts in
reallife_lic_qh_14: The road is wet. What happens to the truck's stopping distance?|It grows a great deal: brake earlier and more gently|It stays the same|It shrinks, as the water cools the brakes
reallife_lic_qh_15: Why should you brake early and smoothly in a truck?|A heavy load keeps pushing forwards and harsh braking can unsettle it|It makes no difference|To make the lights change
reallife_lic_qh_16: A light turns amber as you near it in a heavy truck. What is right?|Stop if you can do so safely: the truck needs more room to stop|Speed up: trucks may run amber lights|Sound the horn and carry on
reallife_lic_qh_17: The brakes feel weaker after a long stretch downhill. Why?|They have overheated: slow down in a lower gear and let them cool|The tyres are too new|The load has got lighter
reallife_lic_qh_18: Cars keep pulling in just ahead of your slowing truck. What do you do?|Ease off and open the gap again|Close up so nobody else can do it|Flash and sound the horn at them
reallife_lic_qh_19: Turning right into a narrow street in a heavy truck, what must you do?|Swing wide enough for the rear wheels to clear the kerb, watching the mirrors|Cut the corner tightly|Turn early so the cab gets round first
reallife_lic_qh_20: Why do the rear wheels of a long truck matter on a turn?|They follow a tighter line than the front and can mount the kerb or hit people|They do not: they follow the front exactly|They lift off the road
reallife_lic_qh_21: How often should you check the mirrors in a heavy truck?|All the time, and always before turning, changing lane or stopping|Only when reversing|Only on the motorway
reallife_lic_qh_22: Before reversing a heavy truck, what do you do?|Look all round, use the mirrors and reverse slowly|Reverse quickly so it is over sooner|Rely on the horn alone
reallife_lic_qh_23: Someone on a bicycle is beside the cab while you wait to turn. What do you do?|Wait until they have gone past or are well clear|Turn: they will see the truck|Edge forwards to make them stop
reallife_lic_qh_24: People are crossing just in front of a high cab. Why take extra care?|Someone close to the front can be out of sight below the windscreen|People always see trucks coming|Trucks have priority at crossings

reallife_changes_051_0: Companion tools can read prices, bills and business planning data, and ask which changes the mod allows before making them. The Guide and the Branches tab of Your bank now say why a bank branch looks like a loss every day in the game's statement: only its costs are booked there, while its fees and the business it brings are your bank's income at your headquarters. Lose touch: on a person's page in People, More about them now offers Lose touch. After the game's own question they leave your phone, and somebody new can take their place. Family, your old friend, a partner and anyone you share a home, plans or money with stay, and the page says why. Once your life is full, asking for a number says so instead of maybe next time, and an acquaintance you have not spoken to for 60 days may drift away to make room. A Marketplace app on the phone: buy used goods and cars from the city's people, collect them at their door or have them brought home, fix them up and clean them, and sell them on to buyers who haggle. Clients also ask for freelance visits there, from detailing a car to a move with a van, done at their door on the game's work panel or left to a helper, with a rating from each client. Being a landlord: your tenants now have a satisfaction, report repairs you can send a contractor to or do yourself at the building's door, complain and leave when unhappy, and the city inspects the buildings you let. Send a reminder or offer a payment plan for rent owed, hire a lettings agency or a property manager, and see each building's rent roll and what a sale would leave. Seasons: what your customers buy follows the season of the Calendar, with more coffee, tea, alcohol, gifts and flowers in winter and more ice cream and cold drinks in summer, and on some winter days it snows, forecast the evening before, the ground turns white and traffic and people in the street slow down. People you meet can hold a position: a recruiter, an importer's buyer, a wholesaler's manager, a law firm's partner, an investor, a city official or a landlord. Introductions by family and friends bring them more often, and as you grow closer each does you a favour or two, once: a job lead, freelance work, a supplier's contact, better delivery terms, an investor meeting or a tip about a building for sale. Rival tycoons: a new option sets when the first one comes forward, at 5 million as before or at 10, 20, 30 or 50 million. A new option, Ride fares: easier passengers (off unless you switch it on), has passengers mind hard stops, bumps and speeding less; everything else about a fare is as before. Car tuning: the custom shop has a Gear change slot (quick shift and sequential gearboxes), a Figures page that reads power, torque, 0 to 100 km/h, top speed, gear change, braking, weight, ride height and grip as standard, now and with the work you choose, and its work now counts when you sell the car: the buyer pays part of what it cost on top of the game's price. Household staff: ring the new Household staff contact to take on a cleaner, a cook, a live-in butler or a mobile mechanic for your home, at the city's going wages. They clean the home, cook dinners into the fridge, and wash, repair and service the cars at home, and while you are there you see them at work. Three new kinds of shop to start in BizMan: an ice cream parlour, a tea bar and a tobacconist. They sell the game's own goods from its own furniture and run as its own shops do, each with its icon, busy hours, help page and ready-made designs. A heavy goods licence for the Freight Truck, the game's largest vehicle: on top of the commercial licence, with its own theory test, a lesson and a driven test in the school's truck, and the courier round offers better paid heavy loads with it. Fixed: in a home with an upper floor, a meal is taken to a free seat on the floor you are on, so the seats upstairs no longer hide the table downstairs. With Developer diagnostics on, the log also says why a piece of furniture cannot be picked up to move, or will not go down where you click, and whether the save keeps its new place. Fixed: in a Going Public session, a class or exam now begins at its school desk or university classroom when you get there, as the session hides the game's panel, and a desk with nothing to begin says why in a notice. Work late at a job's desk begins there too. Fixed: a hit-and-run you got away from no longer costs you twice. When a summons follows, the court case takes the traffic camera's bill, so a dismissed case is not followed by a fine, and a conviction's sentence covers it, the damages included. Fixed: a job's working hours now always fall inside its workplace's opening hours, so a shift no longer starts before the place opens (the warehouse job began at 06:00 at places that open at 08:00, and the shut door cost warnings and then the job). A save with such a job has its hours put right and those warnings taken back at load, and a working day whose place is shut at its start, or a rota shift with nobody near open to work for, is excused.

reallife_guide_careers_ladder_about: At a store of one of the city's chains, rise from the floor to shift supervisor, store manager, regional manager and executive, each with its own tools in the Career app.
reallife_guide_careers_ladder:
# Where it runs
- A job on the floor of a store of one of the city's companies, a rival's chain or one of the city's own of one name, puts you on the management ladder there. The company is modelled from the save: its stores in the city (up to {ladder_stores}), the staff the game has at each, and its own managers as people.
- Nothing of the game's own businesses is changed. A member of the game's staff who leaves a store (you poached them, say) leaves the company's model too, a post to fill.
# The ranks
- Frontline employee: your own schedule, wage and requests. Ask your boss for an earlier or later shift, equipment (the work teaches a quarter more) or insurance (the employer pays more into your pension).
- Shift supervisor ({ladder_pay_1} an hour or more): fill a gap on the shift from the staff, answer shift requests, pass the rest up.
- Store manager ({ladder_pay_2}): set the store's schedule within the company's policy, take on staff within the hiring policy, give small raises within the band, meet demands within the store's weekly budget.
- Regional manager ({ladder_pay_3}): several stores. Settle what store managers send up, move staff between stores, appoint a store manager.
- Executive ({ladder_pay_4}): chief operating officer, chief human resources officer or chief financial officer. Set the company's policy in your area: staffing and how soon matters go up, the hiring floor, the most a new hire is paid and the raise band, or each store's budget.
# Promotion
- At each review of your job, with a rating of 3 or better, you move up a rank once you have the time in your rank, the performance score and the points in the rank's two skills, and your name is put forward.
- Shift supervisor: {ladder_days_1} days, a score of {ladder_score_1}, {ladder_need_1} points. Store manager: {ladder_days_2} days, {ladder_score_2}, {ladder_need_2} points. Regional manager: {ladder_days_3} days, {ladder_score_3}, {ladder_need_3} points. Executive: {ladder_days_4} days, {ladder_score_4}, {ladder_need_4} points and a recommendation.
- Your superior recommends you at a review when your score is five over the next rank's and you left no task to lapse. Below the top, a recommendation takes a third off the days.
- A regional manager and an executive need a company with two stores or more.
# The performance score
- On the floor it is your attendance and your store's results. As a manager it is your stores' staffing and morale, and the tasks you decided rather than left.
- It moves a review by up to {ladder_bonus} points either way.
# Tasks
- Each task waits {ladder_task_days} days on the Management tab of the Career app, a gap on the shift until the day's end. One left to lapse is decided for you, and counts against you.
- A full working day at your store as a supervisor or store manager lifts the staff's morale. The desk says how many tasks are waiting.
- One person can have a raise once every {ladder_raise_days} days.

reallife_guide_economy_hierarchy: # What it is - Over your Managers stands one Company policy: the rules every manager obeys when they decide by themselves. It runs while Company hierarchy: policy, regions and executives is on, and needs Managers for your businesses. - Set it for the whole company, then for a region, then for a store. A region or a store may be stricter than the one above it, never looser. - What a manager cannot settle under the policy is escalated: to a regional manager, then an executive, then you. Only real problems reach you, in Waiting for you at the top of the Managers tab, with a notice. # The policy centre - Open Company policy on the Managers tab. Pick a scope at the top: the whole company, a region or a store with a manager. Pick a rule in the list to change it; it applies at once. - Hiring: the least skill a manager hires at, the most a hire is paid, where a gap is filled from (the place's own job board, the region's other boards, or a move from a store with staff to spare), and whether regional managers appoint and replace store managers (both off at the start). - Pay: the pay band, the largest raise at once, the days between two raises, who may agree a raise or an offer past the band (nobody at the start, the regional manager, the people chief or you) and how far past it they may go. - Demands the managers meet: a switch each for raises, rivals' offers, overtime and claims (off, that kind comes to you), the manager's monthly budget for overtime and hires, and the most the finance chief adds to a budget running out. - Performance: a profit target a day, a standing target, the tolerance, the days off target before a place is escalated, and how much of a place's score is its profit. The rest of the score is standing. - Escalation and reports: how long a gap or a request may wait, how much of a budget may go, the standing floor, how many leavers make a wave, and how often the managers report: every evening at {mgr_digest_hour}:00, on Sunday evening with the week, or only what needs you. - Who approves exceptions, the weight of profit and the reports are set for the whole company only. - A step looser than the scope above is kept as you chose it and shown as held. It binds again if the one above loosens. - A band or a budget set on a manager's own panel is that store's rule. - Templates set every rule at once: Starting policy, Careful, Lean and Generous, or {hier_templates_most} of your own saved from any scope. - The starting policy is what the managers did before: a save that never opens the centre is decided exactly as before. # What is escalated - A gap in the staff under the number a manager keeps, after {hier_gap_days} days. - A manager's budget used past {hier_budget_share}. - A request for a raise or a rival's offer left unanswered for {hier_unmet_days} days, or a strike. - The staff's standing under {hier_mood_floor} on average for {hier_mood_days} days. - {hier_wave_count} or more leaving one place within {hier_wave_days} days, counting those working their notice. - A place off its targets past the tolerance ({hier_tolerance} at the start) for {hier_kpi_days} days. There are no targets at the start. - A raise or an offer past the pay band, when the policy names somebody to approve it: it goes to them at {hier_staff_hour}:00 as the requests are answered. - The figures above are the starting policy's. A place with no manager raises nothing: its decisions are yours. - Each goes to the first holder in post who may settle it under the policy: the region's regional manager (at work, not off sick), then the executive of its area, then you. They try once a day; if they cannot, it passes up. What reaches you comes with one notice. # What a holder does - A gap: candidates from other places' job boards are hired inside the place's rules and budget, then, where moves are allowed, the most skilled who fits is moved from a store with staff to spare. - A raise past the band: agreed if it is inside the room past the band. - Requests waiting: answered inside the band. A strike is always left to you. - Low standing or leavers: the underpaid are raised to the going rate inside the band. - A budget running out: the policy's top-up, once a month. - A place off target: reported, and settled only by you. # The levels - The ranks are the career ladder's: L1 a store's manager, L2 a regional manager, L3 an executive, L4 you. - A regional manager is of a district, or of a region you make: on a manager's panel pick its Region, its district's or one of {hier_regions_most} you name A to H. Each region has its own policy within the company's and its own Dashboard on its regional manager's page, with Reallocate staff and Appoint managers beside the store's quick actions. With the option off every store is in its district again, and a regional manager of a region you made keeps the post but decides nothing. - Where the region's policy allows it, a regional manager appoints a manager at a store with staff and none, and replaces one whose place stays off its targets for twice the days set and scores under {hier_replace_score}. - Executives: three seats, operations, people and money, each one of your professionals at senior or above in a profession the seat names (hire them through the Jobs tab of Open Roles, then appoint them on the seat's page). Nobody holds two seats or also manages a place. Operations holds the stores' gaps and targets, people holds pay and staff, and money holds the budgets. - Each executive settles what the policy lets them and reports each week. After a busy week in their area they may propose one company rule of their area a step looser: Approve sets it at once, Reject leaves it. - An executive who leaves or no longer fits is stood down, and what they held comes to you. With Professionals off every seat waits and decides nothing. - The Owner overview opens the Managers tab: only what waits for you and the executives' summaries, with a way to each level. Switch on Deep Mode to see every level's pages and to step in where an escalation is held: Settle it now or Pass it up. The choice is kept in the save. - Everybody above the floor is paid through your money each day as a business cost, on top of their own pay: a manager and a regional manager their allowance, an executive {hier_exec_premium} of a working day at the going rate of their profession. A seat that waits is paid nothing. Every decision of a regional manager or an executive, with what it changed, is in the log of the escalation or the seat it was about. # What you can do - Open an escalation in Waiting for you: Fill the gap now (from every source, whatever the policy), Add a month's budget, Raise the underpaid, Agree or Refuse an exception, Approve or Reject a proposal, or Let it be. It is raised again only if its cause is still there. - Each manager's panel has a Dashboard: the place's staff against what it keeps, the standing, the budget used and its score, what is pending, and two quick actions, Fill gaps and Batch raises, both inside the policy. - A notice each week sums up the company's week: what the managers settled, what is still open and the places' score. - Switch the option off and every manager decides by their own limits again; nothing is escalated, and the policy is kept for later.

reallife_changes_055_0: The most of a company you may hold is an option under the stock market's options: 10% as before, 25%, 50% or all of it. A rival's holding company stops at the quarter its tycoon does not own, and a holding past a lowered figure is kept. Takeaway and plates: food you carry in a bag, and a home dish packed to take from the cooking list, is eaten when you sit down. Click a chair or a bench, rest, and press Eat: the bag becomes the place's tray, a plate on the table or a plate in your lap. Fixed: the first midnight after loading a save no longer stutters from the mod's day. The code every feature runs at midnight was made ready in the very frame the day turned; it is now made ready a little at a time in the first half minute after the load, and nothing the day does changes.

Up to four homes can each have their own cleaner, cook, butler and mechanic, each paid per visit as before. The Guide is rewritten from the mod as it is now: over a hundred pages checked against the code, with every figure taken from it, what each feature needs and where to click, how a job offer's chance and pay are worked out, sleep, the goods a shop needs headquarters and a warehouse for, and install and update steps. reallife_changes_056_1: Fixed: the Family contact is now always made while Family life is on, so a walk with the pushchair, a proposal outdoors and a wedding in the open air can always be asked for. Fixed: asking your partner to move in from People now moves them in for Family life too, if your home has room. Fixed: after a wedding the couple move in together only if your home has room for them. Fixed: outing costs with friends, pocket money, wedding catering, Mom's gifts and what friends lend now follow the price level. Fixed: when you lose touch with someone, the position they held in your network no longer passes to whoever takes their place. Fixed: the council's rent policy now works the right way round for property. Where landlords set their own rents, homes let dearer, and under rent control, cheaper. Fixed: the least you can finance a car or a mortgage for, and the least you can draw on a card, now follow the city's prices. Fixed: the taxi contact names the phone option by its own name when it takes no calls. Fixed: the refusal for too many franchised shops now says the limit counts the shops of all your brands together. Fixed: the City Ledger no longer speaks of newspaper kiosks on its subscriptions line or front page when kiosks are switched off. Fixed: the trading licence renewal no longer comes up as a business event while the Company app's licences are on, so licences are not charged twice. Fixed: the fish you catch are sold at the city's prices, as the bait is. Fixed: the regional manager policy text now gives the score the rule really uses. Fixed: Hire an influencer on an influencer's profile now lets you pick the business to hire for, not always the first. Fixed: a hired influencer now makes as many posts as the deal says and is priced for, not one every day. Fixed: the Flare notifications option now also silences the notices for a booked invitation, a camera that is busy or fails, and a ready selfie. Fixed: a launch deal now counts its fortnight from the day the business opened, not from when Flare first saw it. Fixed: the extra customers where the cleaners go now count inside Flare's cap of six per cent. Fixed: posts about your office now help your approval while you are mayor, as they do on the council. Fixed: Forget the key no longer signs you out of ChatGPT when Ollama, LM Studio or Off is chosen. Fixed: the city's gossip and the net worth read are no longer skipped when time runs fast. Fixed: the RLO Texts test notice for a pack that writes only English no longer says it is only for now. Fixed: the Calendar no longer lists the seasons while they stand down for Alcware Seasons. Fixed: fewer people are out on the street in rain, ice, snow and heat, as the Guide says. Fixed: a Marketplace request whose time has passed can no longer be booked or sent a helper. Fixed: a police report from a station's front desk now does something: the insurer pays a break-in's theft claim in full, and a car's next repair without the excess. Fixed: a warm top now keeps the cold off, so it costs no energy on foot in a cold snap or on ice. Fixed: the presets table and the Guide show a drop-down's choice by name and a slider with its unit, not a bare number. Fixed: preparing a save for removing the mod now says what each kind of business became. Fixed: days in a Going Public session no longer run down the time a buyer has to take over your sold company's businesses. Fixed: the Guide's Character and Navigation pages now list the skin and building-name options. Fixed: the driving school's closed notice names its real hours. Fixed: the note on undoing a preset names the right button. Fixed: the pavement cart's job card shows the day's offer. Fixed: police move a busker on and warn a cart seller under one rule: the police and police presence both on. Fixed: giving up a shift with nothing done now counts as a failed shift, as the Guide says.

reallife_changes_056_2: Fixed: a short stutter the first time some phone and computer panels opened while playing. The game's font is now found again by its name, never by a search of the whole scene. Fixed: the left pane of the apps, the white card beside the tables, drew section heads over the text above them and wrapped lines over the next row, because the card had a fixed height and Unity's layout squeezed every text to fit. The card is now rebuilt and scrolls: the title, its line and its status chips stay at the top, the buttons and the Guide link at the foot, and what lies between scrolls with the mouse wheel. Each section is a card with its own heading, each fact is a label and a value on one line (a long value wraps under itself), and a career ladder is a list of rungs with the pay beside each name, what it asks under it and your own rung marked, whatever the language or the length of the text. Fixed: sitting at a recruitment office's desk without the Basic HR course gave you nothing. The desk now always offers two choices: register with the jobs board, which needs no course, or recruitment, which shows the Basic HR page if that course is not complete. Fixed: a thing bought on the Marketplace now has a clear way to be collected. The route ends on the pickup point at the seller's door, a parcel stands there, and the door's panel offers Collect, also after a load. If you come by car, a notice tells you to get out. The seller holds it for three days, the Yours tab says until when, and after that the money returns to you. Fixed: two people in your company could have the same name. The game checks a new name only against the staff it knew when it first looked, so seekers, candidates waiting and your tech payroll were missed. Every new name in the tech sector is now checked against all names in use, and people who already share a name are given a new one, with a notice. A hire the game turns down no longer leaves a candidate waiting in the staff app, and an applicant who cannot start, because the business is gone or the game will not take them on, is now reported to you. Fixed: a limit on products in tech firms was too low and not explained. Your firms could have only 16 products being built or on sale between them, and withdrawn products piled up in the list. Each firm can now have 12 and all your firms 36, the 12 newest withdrawn products are kept, and the Tech app says how many you have and why another cannot be started. A product holds 24 features at most, and its page and the Guide now say so. Fixed: Alex and Mom now have one fixed look for every player, in a new game and in an old save, and Alex, a woman, is the same at home as your roommate, at gatherings and on the phone. A roommate who is one of your friends keeps that friend's look, and your partner is drawn at the same age at home as when you go out. A save that held two looks for one person is put right on load, with a notice.

reallife_guide_trades_about: Work at the city's works sites in the building trades, design buildings at an architects' practice, and climb three new ladders.
reallife_guide_trades:
# Work at a works site
- Walk up to a works site's notice board and press its key: the site's notice has Work here. It offers the trades the site has on at its stage, one at a time, with the pay and what each asks. Take one and you start where you stand, in the hi-vis.
- Labourer and mason are open to anyone. A labourer's load pays {trades_labourer_pay} and a mason's stretch of wall {trades_mason_pay}, by how well it is done: badly done still pays {trades_floor} of it.
- Each shift is played on the game's own panel and the bar on your shift card: press as the marker crosses the green to lay a brick, dig, tighten a coupler, roll paint or fix a tile; pick the right terminal or fitting before the time runs out; set a crane's load down as it swings over the marker.
- The surveyor walks to each corner the marker shows and reads the level there. Night security walks its rounds after the site shuts and gets to each noise before the thief is gone.
- Let time pass leaves the rest of a shift to the game's clock at a fair unit's pay. Walking off ends the shift.

# The building inspector
- With a degree in construction management, civil engineering or architecture you can inspect any site for the city: {trades_items} items, each a reading against its limit, and you call it sound or a fault.
- When you find faults the contractor may offer you money to sign it off. Refuse and the site fails; an unsafe site is stopped for a working day. Take it and it may come out within {trades_bribe_days} days ({trades_bribe_out} of the time): a fine of twice the money, and City Building Control lets you go.

# The architects' practice
- Vale and Hudson Architects stands on a floor of one of the mod's buildings: choose its floor at the building's door. Its desk has the work: a design, draughting, a frame or a tender.
- A design is a client's building: place the stairs, the lift, the lobby and the flats on the floor plan, scored on fit, light, flow and cost; choose the facade the client will like within the budget, with their satisfaction on the bar; and, if you are an engineer too, place the columns so every span holds. A stage pays {trades_architect_pay} by how near it came to the best.
- Builders send briefs to the practice; your finished design goes in its book, where their projects read the score.

# Courses and careers
- New courses in the Campus app: the bricklaying diploma and the crane operator's ticket at the school, construction management at the university, and the architect's licence, an exam after the architecture degree. The electrician's, plumber's and carpenter's diplomas open those trades too.
- Three employers take you on through the Work contact: Hudson Brick and Build (labourer, mason, foreman, site manager), City Building Control (building inspector up to chief inspector) and Vale and Hudson Architects (draughtsperson, junior architect, architect, partner).
- An apprenticeship: every unit a labourer does teaches {trades_learn} of a point of masonry. The mason's rank asks {trades_mason_points} points or the diploma, a foreman {trades_foreman_points}. A review that earns a promotion you do not yet qualify for says what is missing.

# Going Public
- Your shifts are yours alone: nothing new is sent to the other players. An unsafe site you fail is reported to the city as a report at its notice is, which the session's host decides.

reallife_guide_construction_about: Build in the new district or rebuild your own buildings, with a construction company of your own or by hiring one of the city's builders: get them designed and approved, build them and sell them, and bid against the city's builders for works.
reallife_guide_construction: # What it is - A Construction Company is a business type of its own. Open it in an office with BizMan, as any office business, then found the company in the Construction app on your phone. Hire its staff the game's way: designers and client staff at the office's desks. - The app has eight tabs: Overview, Land, Projects, Tenders, Crews, Company, Rivals and City. - You need no company of your own to build: hire one of the city's builders instead (see Hiring a builder). # Where things are - Show on map, under the title of a lot, a project, a tender or a building in the app, makes it your destination, with the game's marker and arrow. An empty lot or a site with no building yet is marked at its front on its street. - What is under way shows in the game's objectives at the top left, most urgent first: each project's next step and when, a hired builder's next payment, the licence, your tenders and claims. Press a line to open it in the app, or its marker to show it on the map, and press the heading to fold it to its first line. Switch it off under Construction in the options. # The licence - Your company needs the contractor's licence to start works and to bid. Apply at City Hall: on the planning and building control topic of its call, or with Call City Hall in the app. The fee is {bld_licence_fee}, and City Hall decides in {bld_licence_days} days. - It is refused while a conviction counts against you. It holds for a year: renew it in its last days. # Land - The new district's empty lots are for sale on the Land tab, at {bld_land_share} of the value of the building a lot usually holds, at the district's prices. - Each lot is zoned for some uses. The city's council can add one: ask at City Hall for {bld_zone_fee}, and it hears it at its next planning sitting, or at your own meeting if you sit on it. A motion of the council can allow a use on every lot of a kind. - Land tax is {bld_land_tax} of the lot's price a year, and {bld_vacant_tax} more on land kept empty for {bld_vacant_days} days. - No land is sold during a Going Public session. - A building you own can be rebuilt instead: it keeps its businesses and gets a new look of the same size behind the game's scaffolding. # The plans - A project begins with its plans: the use, one of the city's own designs that fits the ground, the architect and the parking. - A practice draws them for {bld_firm_fee_least} to {bld_firm_fee_most} of the estimate, and a dearer practice draws better plans. An architect on your staff draws them for no fee, as well as their skill allows. - Once your own training lets you, design the building yourself at the architects' practice. Your design's score is the plans' quality, its cost against the budget is the build's cost, and for a block of homes its flats are the block's. - The plans write in the fire exits the building needs and the parking its use and size ask for. The new district allows {bld_uptown_limit} storeys, {bld_strict_storeys} under strict permits. - From {bld_engineer_from} storeys, and for every rebuild, an engineer must sign the plans off: an engineer on your staff, you if you are qualified, or an outside one for {bld_engineer_fee} of the estimate. - An estimator on your staff prices the plans, so the estimate comes closer to what the building costs. # Planning permission - Apply at City Hall. The fee is {bld_planning_fee} and {bld_planning_share} of the estimate. The council decides in {bld_planning_days} working days, more for a big building, {bld_planning_most} at most. - The neighbours have their say first, and their objections are in the City Ledger. The council weighs the plans' quality, your reputation, the objections, the requirements met, the zoning and its permits policy. Many objections bring conditions: a contribution to the street. - Refused, appeal to the court for {bld_appeal_fee}, or redraw the plans for a share of the first fee and apply again. A lawyer of your own helps an appeal. # Building - Start with the licence, planning permission and at least one crew on the project. It goes up as one of the city's construction sites, at your crews' pace. Your company runs {bld_sites_most} sites at once at most, and employs {bld_crews_most} crews at most. - A site goes through four stages: groundworks, foundations, the frame, and the shell and fit out. Each stage needs its trades, its materials and its plant. A crew's skill and morale set its pace. - Order each stage's materials from one of three builders' merchants. Their prices follow the raw materials exchange. A delivery comes on its day, and sometimes only part of it does. - Hire plant for each working day, or buy it and keep it at a yard, one of your warehouses. A frame of {bld_crane_from} storeys or more needs a tower crane. - The building inspector comes three times: after the foundations, after the frame and at the end. Book each visit. A failed inspection means rework first. Good crews, a site manager and a walk round the site with the foreman help it pass. - You can offer the inspector money instead. For {bld_bribe_days} days it may come out: a case is opened against you, and your reputation and standing fall. - A site manager on your staff runs a site: books the inspector, orders the materials, gets the plant and puts a free crew on it. - Rain stops the work, a storm can damage a frame, and materials go missing at night. A fault found after the handover brings a claim in court. # Hiring a builder - You need no company of your own to build. Buy a lot or pick a building you own, have the plans drawn by a practice (or by you once qualified), and get planning permission at City Hall yourself. - Then press Hire a builder on the project's page. Each of the city's {bld_rivals} builders quotes a price and a time for the week, priced off the plans' estimate, with its standing and what it is known for beside it. Pick one, or the cheapest or the fastest. - The contract: a deposit of {bld_hire_deposit} now, then {bld_hire_stage_first}, {bld_hire_stage_frame} and {bld_hire_stage_final} of the price as the three inspections pass, and the last {bld_hire_retention} kept back until the handover. - The builder sets the site out in the city's programme and works it at its own pace, with its own crews, materials and plant. It books the inspector itself and puts right what fails at its own cost. - Late, it gives back {bld_hire_penalty} of the price for each day, {bld_hire_penalty_most} at most, out of what is kept back. - The handover, the opening and the ribbon are as for your company's own buildings, and the building stands at once and is yours: use it, let it or sell it. A construction loan and flats sold off plan work the same. - With a company of your own you choose: build it with your crews, or hire a builder. Your own company is never among those who quote. - Or go to a builder's office in Uptown and click the person at the front desk: they give the builder's quote for your building that is ready to start, sign the contract there and then, and say what the builder is known for. In your own company's office, the person at the front desk opens the company's pages. # Money - A construction loan lends up to {bld_loan_share} of the land and the estimate, at the business loan's rate and {bld_loan_points} points more. It pays out in stages, at the start and after each inspection passed, and is repaid over {bld_loan_years} years from the handover. It is on your credit file. - An investor puts in {bld_investor_least} to {bld_investor_most} of the estimate, and is paid back with a share more {bld_investor_days} days after the handover. - The flats of a block of homes can be sold before they are built, at {bld_off_plan} of their value: a deposit of {bld_deposit} now, and the rest at completion. A flat is about {bld_flat_area} m2 of floor. - Insurance pays a share of what is stolen and of a claim for faults, and full cover pays for storm damage too. Its cost each day follows the works under way, and the insurer keeps back the first {bld_cover_excess} of each loss. # Afterwards - A finished building on a lot of yours goes up when the scaffolding comes down (at the next black screen if you are looking at it) and is yours: use it, let it or sell it in BizMan. Or sell a block's flats one by one at the asking price you choose, and the building is its residents'. - The day after the handover is the opening day. Cut the ribbon at the building's front for a moment on Flare, a story in the City Ledger and a lift in standing. # Tenders and rivals - The city's own works, businesses' rebuilds and public buildings go out to tender. Bids close {bld_tender_hours} hours after a tender opens. Bid {bld_bid_least} to {bld_bid_most} of the value, at the usual time or fast. The best mix of price, time and reputation wins. - {bld_rivals} rival builders bid against you, each known for a kind of work. They offer your best crews more pay: match it or lose them. - The city's developers build on the district's lots that nobody has bought, and each building they finish becomes one of the district's. - A speciality makes its kind of work faster, its materials cheaper and its tenders likelier won. It can change once in {bld_speciality_rest} days. # The building code - The building code is the elected government's, set with its permits policy. Fast-track permits allow a third more storeys outside the new district, ask a third fewer parking spaces, take 40% off the planning fee and double the surcharge on land kept empty. Strict permits allow {bld_strict_storeys} storeys in the new district and a third fewer elsewhere, ask half as many parking spaces again, raise the planning fee by half and halve the surcharge. - Candidates promise one or the other and the winner brings it in, the new district's voters leaning to growth. The council votes on it, a petition can put it to the council, and in office you can table it. The City tab and City Hall show the code in force and what changes when. - With a construction company or land in the new district, a vote of yours on the code or on zoning touches your interests: declare it, or it may come out as misconduct. # Crime and the courts - Now and then three of the city's builders agree who wins a tender: one is to win, the others put in high cover bids. They may ask your company to cover too, for {bld_ring_cut} of the winning price. Cover, turn them down, or report it. For {bld_ring_days} days after the award the city's inquiry may find a ring out: its builders are fined, the City Ledger names them, and a company that covered faces a case of bid rigging. - A client or flat buyers may pay late or not at all. Chase the debt with up to {bld_chase_most} letters, then take it to court: after a letter, or once it is {bld_sue_after} days overdue. The court's fee comes back if you win. - Short of cash, a merchant may deliver on account and give you {bld_account_days} days. Leave that, or a crew's wages, unpaid too long and they take you to court. # Building of the year - The City Ledger's critic reviews each new building. In the year's last days the {bld_award_shortlist} best are shortlisted and the city votes on Flare, where your followers count for your own. The winner lifts its builder's reputation and your standing. # Show flats - A block of homes sold off plan can have a show flat while it is built: open it on the block's money page in the Projects tab. Choose one of the game's residential designs, fully dressed or plain, of the size of its flats. - It stands on a floor of one of the mod's buildings. Walk in by that building's door, or press Show me the way. - Buyers come to its viewings, one to {bld_viewings_most} a day. Its quality (its interior and decor, scored as a business's are) against the district's standard sets how many viewings there are, how often a buyer takes a flat, and the price: {bld_show_price_least} to {bld_show_price_most} of the plain off plan price. - Show the buyers round yourself on its floor, or hire a salesperson for {bld_agent_day} a day. With nobody there, fewer of them buy. - Its dressing costs its furniture at market prices and the installation, and each day it is open costs {bld_show_day}. It closes when the block is handed over. # Renovations - Refit a shop or office you run, from its Interior tab in BizMan or from the Land tab of the app. Your company's crews do it as a project, {bld_refit_hours_least} to {bld_refit_hours_most} working hours by its size, or the city's best renovation contractor does it at its quote. - The business closes while the works go on. At the end its wear is gone, and its new fittings add up to {bld_refit_lift_most} to its decor, fading as the finishes wear. - A new look outside is a rebuild of a building you own, and a rebuild can refit the business inside it too. - Businesses put their own refits out to tender. The renovation speciality is the one for them. - Homes and empty units you rent or own can be refitted too. Keep the furniture, or pick one of the game's own interior designs for the unit: at the end the game's own installers clear it and lay the design, paid then at their prices less what the old furniture sells for. Be out of the unit that day, or they come the next. - A business of the city's that refits by tender wears another of the game's own layouts for its kind once the works are done, whoever won them. # Demolition - Knock down a building of yours in Uptown from its page in the Land tab. Ask City Hall for the demolition permit, decided in up to {bld_permit_days_most} working days; the neighbours may object to the dust and noise. Asking gives its tenants and any business there {bld_notice_days} days' notice. - When the notice has run, a business there closes and the tenants are bought out at {bld_buyout_days} days of their rent. Your business, your home or your staff must be out of it first. - Your company's crews knock it down as the demolition works, or the city's demolition contractor does it at its quote. It comes down behind the game's scaffolding and its rubble is hauled away. - Its ground stays yours: a site of the lots it stood on, to build on again. Only Uptown's buildings come down; the city's older districts are rebuilt instead. - Plan a new building on that ground as on any lot: any of the city's designs that fills its spaces, of whatever size does, with plans and planning permission as usual. # Joining and splitting land - Join a site of yours with the one beside it along the block's side, from its page in the Land tab: free spaces you bought, ground you cleared, or both. One building of the city's designs then stands over all of it, up to {bld_site_spaces_most} spaces wide, the widest the city's designs take. - Buy the next free space and join it in one press. Neighbouring buildings are bought one at a time, never a whole block: knock each down, then join their ground. - Split a site back into its lots, each a site with its own address, for smaller buildings; a building that stands over several lots is split by knocking it down. # Extensions and change of use - Plan an extension on a building of yours in Uptown, from its page in the Land tab: storeys on top, up to the building code's limit in force. The plans, an engineer's sign off and planning permission come first; the works go on behind the scaffolding while a business inside stays open. At the handover its floor area grows, and the deed's with it, so its rent from the city's tenants and its tax follow. Its front stays its own. - Plan a change of use: offices, homes, shops or a warehouse, where the building's structure takes it. The council weighs the new use on its lot; its tenants and any business there get notice as for a demolition; the works strip it and fit it out. It ends as an empty unit of yours of the new use, to furnish or to let. # The city redevelops - The city's developers do all of this too, by the same rules: the eight builders' development arms, and a rival tycoon's holding while one is in play. They knock buildings down and build anew, join two neighbours into one bigger building, split a big one into smaller ones, put storeys on, and change uses. Only the city's own buildings, never yours. - When a building of Uptown's is for sale, a developer may make an offer. The Land tab shows it and the day it completes; buy the building in BizMan before then and it is yours. - Each move goes through notice, City Hall and the works, at the same pace as yours. The City Ledger reports them, and a builder's page in the Rivals tab lists its own. How often is in the options, under Construction company: The city redevelops (off, slow, usual, lively). They rest during a Going Public session. # Build mode - Press Build mode in the Construction app, from anywhere. The city map opens over Uptown and stays in full view, and time stops until you leave. You stay where you were. The first time, a short tour of four tips shows the parts; Skip the tour ends it. - The bar at the top always says what to do next, with the step's number from picking land (1) to Build here (5), and in a quieter line a tip and what Esc does now. Esc ends the tour, shuts the design window, lets a design or the squares go, and only then leaves. Leave build mode at the top right leaves at once. - The tools sit at the foot in the order you use them: Buy land, Zone, Place a building, Bulldoze, Join or split and Refurbish. The one in use is blue. A tool you cannot use yet is greyed, and its tooltip says why: Zone needs land, Place needs land that is zoned and free, Join needs a site, Bulldoze and Refurbish need a building of yours. A small panel over the toolbar holds the tool in use: its figures and the one or two buttons to press. - Every block is cut into small zoning squares, about 7 to 9 m, from street to street, each with a thin line round it. The view toggles beside the tools colour them: land and buildings (white for sale, your land light in your colour, your buildings solid, other owners' grey), zoning in the game's own colours for each use, land value, occupancy and what is under construction; a small legend over the views names its colours. A zoned square's line is green, a demolished one's red. Point at a square and the game's tooltip beside it gives its owner, the council's zoning, the height limit and its price or zone. - Buy land: click squares next to a street, or drag along it. The squares between your pick and the street come with it, up to {bld_site_spaces_most} spaces wide. A drag keeps to the street it started on and leaves out land the tool cannot take; the panel says what was left out. Click a picked square or right-click it to drop it, or hold shift and drag to drop a run. The panel gives the street, the price, the land tax a year, the zoning, the height limit and whether it is a corner site, then Buy for the price. A space bought short of its depth costs less; buy deeper later. - Zone: pick homes, shops, offices or warehouses in the panel, each in its colour and marked Allowed here or Needs City Hall with the fee, then click or drag over your land; Remove zone takes a zone away. A use the council allows applies at once; one it does not is asked of City Hall after the game's question box, and heard at the council's next sitting. - Place a building: drag over your zoned squares from the street and the Choose a building window opens in the middle, the only window over the map. Its filters show the designs that fit here, the corner designs and the city's designs; each card gives the name, kind and use, storeys, floor area and cost, and one that cannot be built there is greyed with the reason. Pick one and press Place it on the map: its ghost stands on the plot and the panel gives its cost, time to build and storeys, with red lines for too tall, parking, the wrong zone or too few squares. Build here makes the project; the architect draws the plans and City Hall decides the permission as for any building. - Corner buildings: pick squares at a block's corner, from the avenue back with the corner's own square, and seven buildings made for corners are offered before the city's designs, as the zoned use allows: a bodega with flats, a diner, a bank, an art deco tower, a glass tower, a warehouse loft and a pre-war block of flats. Each faces both streets with its door on the corner, and its ghost is turned to them. Its shop signs are live: the name of the business trading there, For lease while a unit is to let, and its address number; the business's own sign of the game stays at the door. The city's developers build them on corners too. - Bulldoze, Join or split and Refurbish: click a building or land of yours and press the button in the panel. Your sites and the city's show as markers with their stage. - The rest of the city: outside Uptown each of the game's buildings is one plot, outlined and coloured on its roof. The land view shows it for sale, yours, rented by you, a rival's, empty to let, let, or not for sale; the other views show its type in the game's colours, its price a square metre, whether it has room to let, and works under way, a rival's as well as yours. Point at one for its address, type, size, owner, price and state. Click it and the panel offers Buy the building and Rent it (the game's own BizMan page, where the offer and the rent are made), and Refurbish and Redevelop for a building of yours; Bulldoze stays greyed, as the city's older districts are rebuilt, never knocked down. Anything you cannot do says why. Squares, zoning and new buildings are only in Uptown: while the map looks elsewhere, Zone, Place a building and Join or split are greyed and say so. - Over the map the pointer is a cross, as in Cities Skylines; over a panel or a question box it is the game's own. - Demand: the four short bars beside the views (H, S, O and W) show what Uptown wants; point at one for its figure. Homes are wanted where there are jobs, shops where people live and walk, offices where people can work, warehouses where shops need goods. Empty units beyond the share Uptown keeps free to let lower a use's demand; a new building still finding tenants does not. Demand moves Uptown's rents and values a step a day at most, the city's developers start only where their use is wanted, and the council looks more kindly on a request for a use in demand. - Every new building is checked when it stands and at every load: its address, owner, card, BizMan page, the map's filters and search, its door and who moves in. - In a Going Public session build mode only shows the land and the sites: only Buy land opens, to look at prices.

reallife_guide_markets_builders_about: The city's rival builders on the stock market, their shares moved by what they do in the construction game, and futures on building materials to hedge a project's costs.
reallife_guide_markets_builders: # Builders on the market - {bm_listed} of the eight rival builders you bid against are listed in the construction sector: Ostrander Building Co., Dunmore and Pike Civil, Tri-Street Utilities, Hartwell Groundworks, and Ironbridge Contracting as the contracting arm of Ironbridge Civil Works. The family firms, Calloway Brothers Scaffolding, Mercer Shopfitters and Fenwick and Daughters, stay private. - Their shares move on what they do in the construction game. A tender won lifts the winner (about {bm_win} for the city's works, more for a business's building or a public building) and takes a little off every other listed builder; a tender your company wins takes that little off them all. Works handed over on time lift a builder, and late ones cost it about {bm_late}. Each new building of theirs in Uptown lifts its builder, and the others a little. - A bribe of theirs that comes out costs a builder about {bm_bribery} and {bm_bribery_margin} of its usual margin for good, and a strike costs it too. Moves of the market's mood fade over time. - They pay dividends each quarter and trade in the Stocks app like any company. News of a builder you hold or watch comes as a notification, and the City Ledger prints it. # Building materials on the exchange - The game's recipes have no cement, steel, bricks or timber, so the exchange has its own: cement and steel by the tonne, bricks by the thousand and timber by the cubic metre. Each moves at every close with its group and the city's price level. Glass is the game's own. - The builders' merchants price their loads by them. They trade on the Futures tab like any material, settled in cash: they are never delivered to a warehouse. # Hedging a project - In the Construction app, a project that is ready to build or building has Materials and hedge: what it will still buy of each material, from which day, at today's prices. - Hedge buys a future for each material and each Friday before its purchases, sized so the future's gain or loss matches the purchase's dearer or cheaper price. The margin and commission are taken as for any future, and the broker's rules hold, with at most {bm_contracts} contracts at once and {bm_units} units on one material. A purchase before the first Friday on offer is too near to hedge, and one after the last is hedged to the last. - While its futures are open a project cannot be hedged again. Once they have settled, hedge what is left. - At the handover the project says what its hedge saved or cost, and its page keeps the figure. # Your company with a construction business - Your company comes to the market in the construction sector when its largest business is your construction company, and its books count the works' takings and costs, beyond the office's wages and rent.

reallife_guide_landmarks_about: Three landmarks for Uptown: a skyscraper, a mall and a stadium, each a megaproject the city puts out to tender.
reallife_guide_landmarks:
# Uptown's landmarks
The city builds three landmarks in Uptown, each on a block of its own on Uptown Avenue: Summit Tower, its tallest offices; Uptown Galleria, a great shop with shops to let round it; and Crest Field, a stadium of {lmk_capacity} seats for Uptown FC.
# How they are built
- Each is announced in the City Ledger on its day, and its block is held from the start: nobody buys it or builds on it.
- It goes out to tender in the construction game for {lmk_tender_days} days. Your company can bid in the Tenders tab against the city's builders; the best mix of price, time and reputation wins.
- Won, it is a project of yours like any other, with crews, materials and inspections. Lost, a rival builds it. In a Going Public session, or without the construction game, the city's own works build it on their timetable.
- It opens the day after it is handed over, with a ceremony at its front from 10:00 to 18:00. Join the crowd there for a little Standing.
# What they do
- Summit Tower is the city's own project: the council grants it with its tender, so the district's height limit, which binds the plans a company draws, does not hold it to its storeys.
- Once built, the lots round them get busier: up to {lmk_lift_cap} more traffic for the shops near them, which prices the land there higher too.
- Summit Tower gives work to some {lmk_tower_jobs} people, Uptown Galleria to {lmk_mall_jobs} and Crest Field to {lmk_stadium_jobs}. The tower's offices and the galleria's shops are let by the city like any of the district's.
- Uptown FC play at home every Saturday at {lmk_kick_off}. On a match day the crowds stand outside, the shops near the stadium get {lmk_match_lift} more traffic, and {lmk_match_jobs} people work the match. The City Ledger has the score the next morning.

reallife_guide_schools_about: A school campus in Uptown, and the city's schools: buy Birchwood School and run it against the trusts and the council.
reallife_guide_schools:
# Birchwood School
Birchwood School is a school for ages 5 to 17 on Uptown's west square, between Birch and Elm Street, north of Uptown Avenue. Its main school has three floors of classrooms you can walk round, with a hall, a junior block, a basketball court and a green between them, a playing field at the north end and a fence with gates on Uptown Avenue, Elm Street and Summit Avenue. Families gather at the gates for the school run on weekday mornings and afternoons.
# The city's schools
- Twelve schools share the city: Birchwood, four private schools of the education trusts, and the council's free school in each district. Their league table is in the Schools tab of the Campus app.
- Some {school_pool} of the city's children go to a school their families pay for. They choose by each school's name, its fee and its scholarships; a school takes as many as it has places, and the rest wait.
- A school teaches best with a teacher to every {school_ratio} pupils, a good headteacher and skilled teachers.
- Results day comes once a year, at the end of the summer term, and the City Ledger prints the league table. The council's inspectors visit every school every {school_inspect_days} days.
- At the start of each term, a school short of teachers takes them from a school that pays {school_poach}% less. Pay well or lose your staff.
# Running Birchwood School
- The council opens it and, after {school_sale_days} days, sells it to the richest trust, unless you buy it first. Its owner asks {school_asking}% of what it is worth.
- Yours, you set the fee, open or close classes of {school_class} up to its {school_places} places, set the teachers' pay and the scholarships, and hire a headteacher. Its money comes to you each week.
- The trusts run their schools with the same levers and may offer to buy yours; take an offer, or sell to them for {school_sale_part}% of what it is worth.
- Its name lifts the traffic of Uptown's lots within {school_lift} m: their shops see more customers and their rents rise.
# Your children
- A child of school age can go to Birchwood: enrol them in the Schools tab. Its fee replaces the private school's in the family's week (none at your own school), and their reports follow its results.
- Their school run and parents' evenings are at its main gate.
# Going Public
In a session the schools are not bought or sold, and each runs by its owner's rules on every machine.
