reallife_changes_057_0: Some construction sites are now whole buildings being rebuilt: the building is wrapped to its roof in the game's own scaffolding and fabric, crews work on its decks, and after an inspection the scaffolding comes down. The scaffolding fades with the building when it would hide you. The building trades: at a works site's notice board, Work here offers the trades it has on, from labourer and mason to roofer, electrician, plumber, crane operator, surveyor, night security and the city's building inspector, each played in a game of its own on the game's panel and bar. An architects' practice on a floor of one of the mod's buildings: design a client's building (the floor plan, the facade and the frame), draw up plans or price tenders. New courses (bricklaying, a crane ticket, construction management and the architect's licence) and three employers, a builder, the city's building control and the practice, with ladders from labourer to site manager and from draughtsperson to partner. Manhattan now goes on north past 1st Avenue into Uptown, a new district of three rows of eighteen blocks from Willow to Lake Street. 9th to 1st Street run on past their old dead ends, 1st Avenue runs on west and east, and nineteen streets cross Uptown, Summit and Crest Avenue, with pavements you walk straight onto from Manhattan's, street lamps, traffic lights, parking, people on foot, traffic all through it and three bus termini; the city map pans over it and the minimap shows its streets. On the city map the fog round the city's edge no longer hides Uptown: it is cut away over the whole district, with the same soft edge as round Manhattan. Uptown is built up like the city's own districts: most of its lots have buildings from the first day, with businesses, homes and offices to rent or buy in BizMan, the rest are open land for the construction game, and it is listed with the city's districts on the map. It can be switched off under Uptown in the options. Your own construction company: open an office as a Construction Company and run it from the new Construction app. Buy lots in the new district or rebuild a building you own; have the plans drawn by a practice, by an architect on your staff or by you at the architects' practice; meet the fire exits, parking, height limit and an engineer's sign off; get planning permission at City Hall, with the neighbours' objections in the City Ledger and appeals to the court; pass three inspections; order materials from builders' merchants priced by the raw materials exchange; hire plant or keep your own at a yard; and keep your crews paid and happy. Construction loans, investors and flats sold before they are built pay for it. Bid against eight rival builders for the city's works, businesses' rebuilds and public buildings, while the city's developers put up the district's buildings on the lots nobody bought. A finished building stands and is yours the moment it is handed over, and its opening has a ribbon to cut. The city around your construction company: the elected government sets the building code with its permits policy (the height limits, the parking asked, the planning fee and the tax on land kept empty), candidates promise it and the winner brings it in, the city's one council hears zoning and, on it, you can table both; builders now and then agree who wins a tender and may ask you to cover, clients and flat buyers can pay late and be taken to court, crews and merchants left unpaid can sue you, and the City Ledger reviews new buildings and names a building of the year after a vote on Flare. Show flats and renovations: a block of homes sold off plan can open a show flat dressed in one of the game's residential designs, on a floor you walk into, where buyers come to viewings; its quality against the district's standard sets how fast the flats sell and at what price, and a salesperson can be hired. And refit a shop or office you run, by your own company or a contractor: it closes for a few days, its wear goes and its decor rises, while businesses put their own refits out to tender. Uptown's landmarks: the city builds Summit Tower, Uptown Galleria and Crest Field, each on a block of its own on Uptown Avenue. Each is announced in the City Ledger and goes out to tender in the construction game, where your company can bid, or the city builds it itself; it goes up as a building site and opens with a ceremony you can join. The tower's offices and the galleria's shops are let like the district's own, the lots round them get busier, and Crest Field has Uptown FC's home matches every Saturday, with crowds outside and the score in the next morning's paper. The city's builders on the stock market: five of the eight rival builders you bid against are listed in the construction sector, their shares moved by the tenders they win and lose, works handed over on time or late, new buildings in Uptown, bribes that come out and strikes, and they pay dividends as any company does. The raw materials exchange now has cement, steel, bricks and timber, which the builders' merchants price by, and in the Construction app a project's Materials and hedge page shows what it will still buy and hedges it with futures; at the handover it says what the hedge saved or cost. A company of yours with a construction business now comes to the market in the construction sector, its books counting the works. The eight rival builders now have offices in Uptown: each is a Construction Company on the city map's filter and in BizMan, and the Construction app's Rivals tab gives its address and sets it as your destination. Build without a company: a new building on your lot or a rebuild of your own can be put out to the city's eight builders. Each quotes a price and a time, and the one you hire takes a deposit, builds it at its own pace through the three inspections, is paid as each one passes and gives some back if it is late. The building is yours as your company's own builds are, and the Construction app's Land, Projects and Rivals tabs work with no company at all. Uptown's offices are places to work: the law firms, web agencies, design studios, event planners and travel agencies the city opens in them from the first day are employers in the Career app, as Manhattan's are, a post there names Uptown after its address, and travel agencies now take on sales staff. Uptown's shops and offices are open from the first day as Manhattan's are: those the game's generator left empty past the share it keeps to let get businesses of the game's own. Uptown has a wholesale store and a petrol station of its own, each a copy of the city's own: Northgate Wholesale on Uptown Avenue between 7th and 6th Street, with its drive-in, its goods ordered from your phone and delivered, or picked up by car at its garage doors, and Summit Fuel on the corner of 9th Street and Uptown Avenue, with its pumps, car wash and repair bays. Uptown's builders now have someone at the front desk. Walk into a builder's office and click the receptionist to get its quote for your building that is ready to start, hire it there and then through the game's own question, or hear what it builds and how it stands; with nothing ready, they tell you what to do first and can open the app's Land tab. In your own construction company's office, the person at the front desk opens the company's overview, projects and crews. A third of Uptown's shops, offices and homes now stand free for you to rent, and the rest have businesses and residents. Its shops hold a wide mix, with few of one kind on a street, among them ice cream parlours and tobacconists run by the city. Buses now reach every corner of Uptown: two new lines run from beside the subway entrances at 9th and 2nd Street up into the district, round its edges and along Uptown and Crest Avenue, so every block is within 250 m of a stop. Uptown's pavements have benches you can sit on, bins, trees and bicycle docks, spaced as Manhattan's are. Uptown has its own special places, run as the game's own: a branch of Vantander Bank whose loans are the head office's, a recruitment agency, a marketing agency, an interior installation firm, an office supplies store, an appliance store and a furniture store, a supermarket with a cashier's job, a clinic where you wake if you faint nearby, a car dealership and an importer with goods of its own. Each is staffed, on the city map's rows and in BizMan, and works from the phone as its kind does. Uptown is laid out on spaces: each lot holds many buildings side by side, every one on the whole spaces of its own size and filling them, the lots past its outer streets are built too, and the construction game sells a lot's free spaces, one or several side by side, for a building that fills them. The Construction app now shows where things are: Show on map, under the title of a lot, a project, a tender or a building, makes it your destination, an empty lot marked at its front on its street. And what is under way in your construction game shows in the game's objectives at the top left, most urgent first: each project's next step and when, a hired builder's next payment, the licence, your tenders and claims, each line opening the app or showing its place on the map. Birchwood School: a school for ages 5 to 17 on Uptown's west square, between Birch and Elm Street, with three floors of classrooms, a hall, a junior block, a basketball court, a green and a playing field behind its own fence, and families at its gates for the school run. The city's twelve schools compete for families and teachers, with results day, inspections and a league table in the City Ledger: buy Birchwood and run it, setting its fee, classes, pay, scholarships and headteacher, while the education trusts and the council run theirs by the same rules. Your children can go there, from the new Schools tab of the Campus app. Options > Tests has What is this ground?, which names the block, lot and streets where you stand. Refurnish any unit you rent or own, a home or an empty unit as well as a business: your company or a contractor does the works, and at the end the game's own installers clear it and lay one of the game's interior designs, at their prices. A business of the city's that refits by tender wears another of the game's layouts for its kind afterwards. Knock down a building of yours in Uptown: a demolition permit at City Hall, notice to its tenants and any business there, who are bought out when it runs, and the building coming down behind the game's scaffolding, by your crews or the city's demolition contractor; its ground stays yours to build on again. Only Uptown's buildings come down: the city's older districts are rebuilt instead. Build a new building on ground you cleared: any of the city's designs that fills its spaces, of any size, with plans and planning permission as on any lot. Join sites of yours side by side, bought or cleared, into one for a bigger building up to the widest the city's designs take, buy the next free space and join it in one press, or split a site back into its lots for smaller buildings. Put storeys on a building of yours in Uptown, up to the building code's limit, its floor area and its deed growing at the handover while its front stays its own, or make it another use its structure takes, emptied first and fitted out anew. The city's developers do all of this too, by the same rules, to the city's own buildings and never yours: they make offers for Uptown's buildings for sale that you can beat in BizMan before their day, knock down and build anew, join, split, extend and convert, as often as the options say. Birchwood School has its own look. The main school, the hall and the junior block are modelled by hand in red brick and limestone, and stand where the city's borrowed designs stood. They are drawn with the game's own brick, roof and glass, so they cost the frame rate next to nothing. The main school keeps its door, classrooms and floors. Build mode, from the Construction app: the city map opens over Uptown with time paused and every block is cut into small zoning squares, as in Cities Skylines. Buy squares, paint a use on your own land (a use the council does not allow goes to City Hall as a request), place one of the city's designs with a ghost and its warnings, and bulldoze, join, split or refit from the same window. Bars show Uptown's demand for homes, shops, offices and warehouses; it moves the district's rents and values, and the city's developers build where a use is wanted. Every new building is checked as a whole building of the game when it stands and at every load. The Contacts app has groups: the game's row of category buttons now holds Family, Friends and people, Work and careers, Services and trades, Money and banks, City and government, and Other beside the game's own, so the mod's contacts are no longer one long list under General. Each button shows its unread messages, and its tooltip says how many contacts it holds. Search looks through every group. It can be switched off with Groups in the Contacts app, under Phone in the options. Corner buildings in build mode: seven buildings made for a block's corner, a bodega with flats, a diner, a bank, an art deco tower, a glass tower, a warehouse loft and a pre-war block of flats, each facing both streets with its door on the corner. Pick squares at a corner and they are offered before the city's designs for the use zoned there, with a ghost turned to the two streets. Their shop signs are live: the name of the business trading there, For lease while a unit is to let, and the address number. The city's developers build them on corners too. Uptown's two other squares are parks now, one between 6th and 5th Street and one between Grove and Park Street: lawns with the game's own trees and bushes, paths from avenue to avenue and from street to street, a fountain in one and a statue in the other, benches to sit on, lamps and bins, and people walking and sitting there. What is this ground? calls them parks. Fixed: the mod's police stations, hotels, tech towers, university and other places kept losing their buildings. Each night the game opened new businesses, the rivals' among them, in the empty units they stand in, and a police station or a tower then had to move. The game now leaves the mod's buildings alone, so they stay where they are. The two offices kept for you stay free for you once the businesses in them close, and empty shops in the office districts now become offices to let as the mod meant, where before almost none could. Fixed: scaffolding and hoarding are now set up at buildings whose door stands out on the pavement, such as 36 5th Avenue, where the site used to be given up. Fixed: building sites, your company's own and a builder's you hire, no longer stand still at the end of a stage (a new building stopped at 40%, after its groundworks), and a failed inspection is put right and booked again. A hired builder tells you as each stage begins, as it books each inspection and when it runs late, and a site that stood still picks up from where it stands. Its quote counts the inspections' waits and the city's working hours, and its due day comes from its site's own schedule. Fixed: Birchwood School's hall and junior block were missing from its campus, and so were the benches round its green. Both buildings now stand every time the city loads, and the benches are found where the game keeps them. Fixed: a finished building now stands the moment it is handed over, as the scaffolding comes down, where before the lot stayed empty until you reloaded. It stands at once when nobody is looking at its ground, or at the next black screen when you are, and your deed is written then. An opening day now has a notice the evening before and another on the morning, shows as urgent in the objectives from the handover, and an opening you miss tells you once what it cost. Fixed: Birchwood School's building card now says what it is, a school, with its name, who runs it (the council, a trust or you) and whether it is open by the school's own hours, where before it showed a closed office on a Friday afternoon. Its basketball court was drawn under the lawn and now shows, two half courts back to back with a hoop and a net at each end and the game's fence round them. The empty lawns are dressed with the game's own paths, trees, benches, table groups, bins and climbing frames, with planters at the main door and the junior block, the playing field keeps its distance from the fence, the windows are a darker, reflective glass, and pupils and families walk the campus by the school's clock: at the gates and the door at the school run, in the courtyard, on the court, on the green and in the yards at break and lunch, and on the court and the field after classes. Fixed: Birchwood School's page in BizMan said the building was owned by Undefined, offered the form to start a business there and called it an office building. It now names the owner (the city council, a trust or you), says who runs the school in place of the form, points you to the Schools tab of the Campus app when the school is yours, and reads School. Fixed: nobody walked Birchwood School's campus, because the pedestrians' walking ground stopped at its edge. Families and pupils now come in at the gates and walk the courtyard, the court, the green and the field. Fixed: a black slab stood on the campus lawn (the game's bike-share dock), so the campus has no bicycle stands. Fixed: a building the construction game finishes now registers with the city map's filters the moment it stands, as a load registers it. A building you own shows under Rented by you with its marker, one to let shows under its own type, one whose use you change moves to the new type, and one you knock down leaves the map at once instead of leaving its marker where it stood. Fixed: no benches stood on Uptown's pavements, in its parks or on the campus, because the game renames its benches when it wakes them and the mod looked for the old name. They now stand there and can be sat on. Uptown's street furniture no longer lays the bike-share dock either, which drew as a black slab. Fixed: a building you own or rent also shows under its own type row on the city map, as well as under Rented by you, so an empty warehouse you own now shows under Warehouse. The map's search now finds any building by its address, empty or not. Fixed: build mode's squares now show on empty land too. They showed only where a building hid them, as the map draws its district colours. Each square has a thin line round it: land for sale is white with a bright line, your land and your buildings read apart, a zoned square's line is green and a demolished one's red. Views as in Cities Skylines colour the squares by zoning in the game's own colours, land value, occupancy or what is under construction, each with a legend, and the square under the pointer says its zoning, height limit, price and owner. Build mode opens in a big window in the middle that steps aside while you pick squares; a picked square clicked again or right-clicked is let go, and Esc clears what is picked before it leaves. Uptown's demand no longer sits at 0: the third of its units kept free to let counts as normal, a new building still being let is not oversupply, and rents move ten in a thousand a day at most from the first day. Fixed: build mode was hard to find your way in. The map now stays in full view: a bar at the top always says what to do next, the tools sit at the foot in the order you use them, greyed with the reason until you can use them, with the views and demand bars beside them and a small panel for the tool in use. A window in the middle opens only to choose a building, and a short tour shows the way the first time. Fixed: Fire engines, ambulances, patrol cars and tow trucks on a call no longer wait behind a stopped bus or car for ever. A bus at a stop with no bay pulls away, and a bus held up behind something goes round it at once, when one of them comes up behind it. Standing cars in the way are moved on, and the unit looks two lanes over for a way past. A fire engine that is held up for good stops where it is and its crew walks the rest of the way to the fire. Fixed: in build mode the hint bar no longer covers the game's top bar and needs, and keeps to one line; the tour's tips have room inside their cards and stand clear of the tool panel; the zone rows are buttons with each zone's colour; the legend is short and sits over the views; Clear is a button, and a pick that makes no site says how to put it right; a drag picks along its street, leaving out squares it cannot take, and Zone tells you to buy land for sale first; the game's FPS and address lines no longer cover the toolbar.

reallife_changes_057_2: Fixed: when the business you work for closes, is bought or loses its building, you are now laid off at once with redundancy pay and a good reference, with no quit, sacking or missed day against you and no wait before you apply again; if it moves, your job moves with it. A quit or sacking that followed a closing is put right as a redundancy when you load. Fixed: an invitation in the Planner, such as an evening with investors, did not say where to go. Every invitation from Standing is now a video call. The Planner says so, and you join it from the Standing page in the Finance app while it runs, instead of it starting by itself wherever you stand. Fixed: the road in Uptown flickered in places, 7th Street among them. A block's ground lay at the same height as the pavements it overlapped, and the picture jumped between the two. Each block now has one ground, a hair lower than the pavements, and each avenue sits a hair higher than its crossings. Fixed: the driving school's car could be left standing with the drive unable to begin. If the examiner cannot walk to the car they are now taken to be aboard once you are at the wheel; a game left paused, or with its time controls locked, says so and is freed; and a car that does not move with the accelerator held is looked over and mended where it can be, and the drive is called off with the fee returned if it still will not go. Fixed: employers were hard to find. The Career app has Show on map for each employer at a help-wanted board, with the address of its board, and for every vacancy, application and job; the city map has an Employers hiring row; and the map's search finds an employer such as Fairway Markets by its name.
